examples.en: Local farmers produce fresh organic mangoes and guavas.
examples.zh: 在地農民生產新鮮的有機芒果與芭樂。

examples.en: This high-efficiency automated assembly line can produce a thousand units daily.
examples.zh: 這條高效能的全自動化組裝流水線每日可生產製造一千台成品裝置。

examples.en: Supermarkets place crisp, colorful fresh produce right near the store entrance.
examples.zh: 超市通常將色澤鮮艷、清脆可口的生鮮蔬果擺設在最靠近大門入口處。

explains: This verb means to make or grow something. It can also mean to show or bring something forward. As a noun in plural form, it can name fruits and vegetables grown for food.
A farm may grow carrots and apples to sell at a market. A factory makes toys from wood and plastic. A person may also show a ticket when asked.
The word has several meanings, so the sentence gives clues. Farms grow food, while factories make goods. In the noun use, it usually means fresh food from plants.

examples.en: The geothermal production well produces two hundred tons of superheated steam and boiling water per hour.
examples.zh: 這口高性能地熱「生產井」（Production Well），每小時穩定產出兩百公噸的超高溫過熱蒸汽與沸水。

examples.en: Automation assembly lines boosted electric vehicle factory production by thirty percent this quarter.
examples.zh: 大量導入全自動化機械手臂產線，使這座現代化智慧工廠本季度的電動車整車組裝產量成長了三成。

examples.en: Broadway theater companies rehearsed daily to prepare their new musical production for premier night.
examples.zh: 百老匯音樂劇劇團全體演員與樂隊每日在劇場閉門高強度彩排，全力備戰即將迎來全球首演之夜的全新大戲。

entries.definition: 抽取高溫高壓蒸汽與熱水之生產井；生產
explains: This noun means the act of making something or the total amount made. It may describe a movie, a play, or goods from a factory. People work together to create the finished result.
Workers may build toys on an assembly line. Actors and crew may make a film for theaters. Both tasks create something people can use or watch.
This term describes how something is made as well as the amount finished. A product is one item that has been made. The word is common in factories and entertainment.

examples.en: The class made good progress on the science project.
examples.zh: 全班的科學計畫有了很好的進展。

examples.en: Her reading improved with steady progress each week.
examples.zh: 她每週穩定進步，閱讀能力提升了。

examples.en: The work is progressing faster than we expected.
examples.zh: 工作進展得比我們預期快。

explains: This noun means movement toward a goal or improvement over time. As a verb, it means to move forward or get better. It may describe schoolwork, a project, or growth.
A student may learn more words each week. A garden project can move from planning to planting. Small steps show that things are moving ahead.
Moving ahead often happens slowly, not all at once. It differs from reaching a goal, which means finishing what someone tried to do. The verb can also describe moving forward in space.

examples.en: Our group completed the science project ahead of time.
examples.zh: 我們小組提前完成了自然科學專題計畫。

examples.en: She is currently managing a major software project.
examples.zh: 她目前正在負責管理一個大型軟體專案。

examples.en: The government announced a new housing project for low-income families.
examples.zh: 政府宣布了一項針對低收入家庭的新住宅計畫。

examples.en: Our software development project will launch in the fourth quarter.
examples.zh: 我們的軟體開發專案將於第四季度正式上線。

examples.en: Financial analysts project a ten percent growth in smartphone exports next year.
examples.zh: 財務分析師樂觀預測，明年智慧型手機的出口總量將迎來百分之十的顯著成長。

examples.en: The projector beam projected the architectural blueprint onto the conference wall.
examples.zh: 投影機的光束將這份精密的建築施工設計藍圖清晰投影在會議室大白牆上。

entries.definition: 專案；計畫；投射；項目；預測；投影
explains: This noun means a planned piece of work with a goal and an end. It may be done by one student or a whole team. As a verb, it can mean to guess what may happen or send an image onto a surface.
Students may make a poster about planets for science class. A builder plans a new playground. A movie screen shows images sent from a small machine.
This planned piece of work usually takes several steps and may take days or weeks. It differs from a single task, which can be finished quickly. Other uses appear in math and light.

examples.en: I promise to return your book by Friday.
examples.zh: 我保證在週五前歸還你的書。

examples.en: A person of integrity always strives to keep every promise made.
examples.zh: 一個有誠信的人總是努力恪守許下的每一項承諾。

examples.en: The talented young violinist shows great artistic promise for the future.
examples.zh: 這位富有天賦的年輕小提琴家展現了光明遠大的藝術前程。

examples.en: The green hydrogen revolution carries a bright promise of clean blue skies and lasting prosperity for all mankind.
examples.zh: 綠色氫能革命為全球人類帶來了重現萬里蔚藍天空與生生不息繁榮的「美好崇高承諾」（Promise）。

examples.en: The dedicated father made a solemn heartfelt promise to take his family camping in the national park.
examples.zh: 這位慈愛的父親向孩子們許下了一個無比鄭重的溫暖承諾，約定暑假一定帶全家前往高山國家公園搭帳棚露營觀星。

examples.en: The young robotics prodigy shows immense artistic and engineering promise in her international science fair project.
examples.zh: 這位年僅十五歲的機器人天才少女，在其國際青年科學展覽作品中展現出了令人驚艷、無可限量的藝術美感與工程才華潛力。

entries.definition: 承諾；答應；前途；點亮湛藍天空、迎向繁榮生機之零碳氫能美好承諾
explains: This noun means words or actions showing that someone will do something. As a verb, it means to say that you will do it. Keeping your word can help people trust one another.
A child may say they will feed the pet each morning. A friend may agree to return a borrowed book. Keeping your word matters.

A commitment is stronger than a wish because it includes an agreement to act. People should only make commitments they can keep. The noun can also describe someone who seems likely to do well in the future.

examples.en: Please use the proper door to enter the building.
examples.zh: 請走正確的門進入大樓。

examples.en: He wore proper shoes for the rainy hike.
examples.zh: 他穿了適合雨天健行的鞋子。

examples.en: The teacher showed us the proper way to hold the brush.
examples.zh: 老師示範了正確握畫筆的方法。

explains: This adjective means suitable or correct for a situation. It can describe clothes, behavior, or the way a task is done. What is suitable may change from place to place.
A student wears clean shoes for a school concert. A person speaks quietly in a library. These choices fit the setting.

This adjective can mean correct or fitting, while “perfect” means without any flaws. Adults may teach children fitting ways to behave in different places. It can also mean belonging to a particular thing.

examples.en: I propose that we meet after lunch.
examples.zh: 我提議我們午餐後見面。

examples.en: She proposed a new way to organize the books.
examples.zh: 她提出了一種整理書籍的新方法。

examples.en: He proposed to his partner beside the lake.
examples.zh: 他在湖邊向伴侶求婚。

explains: This verb means to suggest a plan or idea for others to consider. It can also mean to ask someone to marry you. The meaning depends on what is being suggested.
A student may suggest a new game for recess. A couple may decide to marry and one person asks the other. Both uses begin with an idea offered to someone.
A proposal is the noun form. The verb is more formal than “suggest” in some situations. People can accept, reject, or discuss an idea.

examples.en: We must protect coral reef ecosystems from oceanic warming.
examples.zh: 我們必須保護珊瑚礁生態系統免受海水升溫危害。

examples.en: Always wear a helmet to protect your head while riding a YouBike.
examples.zh: 騎乘 YouBike 自行車時務必配戴安全帽以保護頭部安全。

examples.en: New environmental legislation aims to protect natural wetlands from overdevelopment.
examples.zh: 新頒布的環保法規旨在保護天然濕地免於過度開發破壞。

explains: This verb means to keep someone or something safe from harm. People can care for animals, belongings, or the environment. It can also mean defending someone from blame or attack.
A helmet helps keep a rider safe during a fall. A fence can keep a garden away from hungry rabbits. These actions reduce danger.
Taking steps before harm happens can keep someone or something safe. “Save” can mean help someone from immediate danger. The verb is often followed by “from.”

examples.en: Protective gloves kept her hands warm.
examples.zh: 防護手套讓她的雙手保持溫暖。

examples.en: The case has a protective cover for the tablet.
examples.zh: 平板電腦的保護殼有防護蓋。

examples.en: His big sister felt protective of the toddler.
examples.zh: 他的姊姊很想保護那個幼兒。

explains: This adjective describes something made to keep a person or thing safe. It may describe clothing, equipment, or a rule. It can also describe someone who tries to care for another person.
A worker may wear gloves to keep hands safe. A sunscreen lotion helps skin during sunny hours. Parents often watch young children near a road.
Safety gear is made to reduce harm, but it cannot remove every danger. A caring adult may act in a way that keeps a child safe. The adjective describes a purpose or behavior.

examples.en: She used the map to prove that the road was closed.
examples.zh: 她用地圖證明那條路已封閉。

examples.en: The test will prove whether the battery works.
examples.zh: 這項測試將證明電池是否能運作。

examples.en: The baker let the dough prove beside the warm oven.
examples.zh: 麵包師把麵糰放在溫暖的烤箱旁發酵。

explains: This verb means to show that something is true by giving facts or evidence. It can also mean to test food dough and let it rise. People may use the word when checking an idea.
A student can use math steps to show an answer is correct. A scientist collects evidence before reaching a conclusion. A baker lets dough rise before baking.
This verb is stronger than “suggest,” because it aims to show that an idea is true. The baking meaning is different and used in cooking. Nearby words show which meaning is intended.

examples.en: The school will provide lunch for the field trip.
examples.zh: 學校會為校外教學提供午餐。

examples.en: Her notes provided useful information for the class.
examples.zh: 她的筆記為全班提供了有用的資訊。

examples.en: The hotel provides guests with clean towels.
examples.zh: 旅館為房客提供乾淨的毛巾。

explains: This verb means to give or make something available. A person may give help, food, or information. It can also mean arranging for a need to be met.
A library gives books for people to borrow. A host may bring water to a guest. A school can share supplies with students.
“Give” is a simpler verb with a similar meaning. It is often followed by “with” or “for.” The formal verb can describe services as well as objects.

examples.en: We ate chocolate pudding after dinner.
examples.zh: 我們晚餐後吃了巧克力布丁。

examples.en: The warm pudding smelled like cinnamon.
examples.zh: 熱布丁聞起來有肉桂香。

examples.en: She made rice pudding for the family.
examples.zh: 她為家人做了米布丁。

explains: This noun names a soft sweet food often eaten after a meal. It may be baked, steamed, or chilled. Recipes vary from place to place.
A family might serve a creamy cup after dinner. Another cook may bake a warm dish with fruit and spices. People often eat it as a treat.
In some countries, this word can mean many kinds of sweet dishes. In others, it often means a soft baked dessert. The recipe tells what ingredients it contains.

examples.en: We carved a funny face into the pumpkin.
examples.zh: 我們在南瓜上刻了一張有趣的臉。

examples.en: The pumpkin soup was warm and smooth.
examples.zh: 南瓜湯溫暖又滑順。

examples.en: Grandma baked a pumpkin pie for the picnic.
examples.zh: 奶奶為野餐烤了南瓜派。

explains: This noun names a large round orange vegetable with a thick skin. People often carve a face into one for an autumn holiday. Its flesh and seeds can be used in cooking.
A farmer may grow many of these in a field. A family might bake one into a pie. The seeds can be roasted for a crunchy snack.
This vegetable belongs to the squash family. It is often orange, but some kinds are green or white. A carved one should be kept cool.

examples.en: The teacher punished the class for throwing paper.
examples.zh: 老師因為全班丟紙而處罰他們。

examples.en: The punishment was to clean the art tables.
examples.zh: 處罰是清理美術桌。

examples.en: Parents should choose a fair punishment for breaking the rule.
examples.zh: 父母應為違規行為選擇公平的處罰。

explains: This word means to make someone face a consequence for breaking a rule. It can also name the consequence itself. Adults may use fair consequences to teach children about choices.
A student who runs in the hall may lose a few minutes of playtime. A referee may send a player off after a serious rule break. The consequence should match the action.
The verb describes giving a consequence, while the noun names it. This consequence can sound severe, so people often talk about fair rules and results. The goal should be safety and learning.

examples.en: The bright light made her pupils grow smaller.
examples.zh: 強光讓她的瞳孔縮小。

examples.en: Each pupil received a new reading book.
examples.zh: 每位學生都拿到一本新的讀本。

examples.en: The teacher spoke to her pupils after lunch.
examples.zh: 老師午餐後和學生們談話。

explains: This noun can mean the dark center of the eye that lets light in. It can also mean a student, especially a young learner in British English. The plural can refer to the children in a classroom.
A young learner may be called by this word in British English. The plural can refer to children in a classroom. Nearby words reveal whether it means a student or an eye part.
The eye part changes size in bright or dim light. The student meaning is common in school language in some countries. Teachers may use it for a group of learners.

examples.en: The puppy chased a ball across the yard.
examples.zh: 小狗在院子裡追著球跑。

examples.en: Our puppy sleeps in a soft basket.
examples.zh: 我們的小狗睡在柔軟的籃子裡。

examples.en: The puppy learned to sit for a treat.
examples.zh: 小狗學會坐下來換取零食。

explains: This noun names a young dog. It usually has small paws, soft fur, and playful behavior. As it grows, it becomes an adult dog.
A family may bring a young dog home and teach it where to sleep. It needs food, water, play, and care. Children should treat it gently.
A kitten is a young cat, while this term is used for a young dog. It can also be used affectionately for a person who is new at something. Young animals need kind care.

examples.en: Lavender flowers have a nice purple color.
examples.zh: 薰衣草花朵擁有美麗的紫色。

examples.en: The evening sky slowly faded into deep purple before nightfall.
examples.zh: 傍晚的天空在入夜前逐漸轉變為深紫色。

examples.en: She picked a bunch of ripe purple grapes from the vineyard.
examples.zh: 她從葡萄園摘了一串熟成的紫葡萄。

explains: This word names a color made by mixing red and blue. It can describe flowers, clothes, or the sky at sunset. As a noun, it names the color itself.
A child may choose a violet crayon to color a flower. Some grapes have dark skins of this color. It can look light or deep.
This color sits between red and blue on a color wheel. Lavender is a light shade, while plum is darker. The word can describe either a thing or the color.

examples.en: When machines handle tedious manual labor, humans can dedicate their lives to noble creative purpose.
examples.zh: 當繁瑣重複的勞動全數交由智慧機器分擔，人類終於能將寶貴的生命時光全心投入崇高的創造性意義。

examples.en: Volunteering at the local animal shelter gave the retired schoolteacher a newfound sense of joy and life purpose.
examples.zh: 退休後定期在流浪動物之家擔任愛心志工，為這位奉獻半生的高中老教師帶來了重獲新生般的充實快樂與生命意義。

examples.en: The primary purpose of this meeting is to finalize budget allocations for the upcoming fiscal quarter.
examples.zh: 本次專案跨部門協調會議的首要核心目的，在於正式定案並確認即將到來的下個會計年度各項研發預算分配。

examples.en: Living with a clear sense of noble purpose infuses every daily struggle with courage and joy.
examples.zh: 懷抱著清晰堅定的崇高人生使命（Purpose）而活，能讓生命中的每一場艱辛奮鬥皆化為滿懷勇氣與喜悅的試煉。

examples.en: The non-profit foundation was established with the explicit purpose of building libraries in underserved rural schools.
examples.zh: 這家民間非營利慈善基金會自創立之初，其最明確純粹的宗旨使命就在於為偏鄉教育資源匱乏的小學打造現代化圖書館。

examples.en: Finding meaningful life purpose often begins with identifying how your unique strengths can serve others.
examples.zh: 探尋人生的真正意義與崇高使命，往往始於沉靜覺察自己獨一無二的才能如何能為這個世界與他人帶來實質貢獻。

entries.definition: 生命熱情與崇高人生意義；目的；崇高人生使命與存在意義
explains: This noun means the reason someone does something. It can also mean an aim or plan. People may talk about why a tool or activity is used.
A ruler helps measure length, so that is one reason to use it. A student may study to learn a new skill. Knowing the aim helps people decide what steps to take.
An aim is more specific than a hope. It explains why an action is done or what result is wanted. The word is often used with “for.”

examples.en: We solved the puzzle before dinner.
examples.zh: 我們在晚餐前解開了謎題。

examples.en: The last piece of the puzzle was under the table.
examples.zh: 拼圖最後一片在桌子底下。

examples.en: Her strange answer puzzled the class.
examples.zh: 她奇怪的回答讓全班困惑。

explains: This noun names a game or problem that is difficult to understand or solve. It can also mean a toy with pieces that fit together. As a verb, it means to confuse someone.
A child may put together picture pieces to show a finished scene. A tricky question can make the class think carefully. Both uses challenge the mind.
A riddle is a kind of word problem, while a jigsaw has separate pieces. The verb form describes making someone confused. The word is often used for fun challenges.

examples.en: Taiwanese manufactured goods are famous for high quality and reliability.
examples.zh: 台灣製造的產品以高品質與高可靠度聞名。

examples.en: We aim to improve the overall quality of patient healthcare services.
examples.zh: 我們的目標是提升病患醫療照護服務的整體品質。

examples.en: Leadership, empathy, and integrity are essential qualities of a good mentor.
examples.zh: 領導力、同理心與誠信是身為優秀導師必備的特質。

explains: This noun means how good or useful something is. It can describe a product, a person’s work, or a material. As an adjective, it can mean high grade.
A strong backpack may last for many years. A teacher can check how well a student completed a project. People often compare items before buying them.
How good or useful something is differs from how many or how much there is. A small amount can still be excellent. The adjective form describes something especially good.

examples.en: Mindful fashion enthusiasts prioritize exceptional fabric quality over sheer cheap quantity.
examples.zh: 懂穿搭的品味人士始終堅持「質量重於數量」（Quality Over Quantity），買少買好。

examples.en: Reducing the quantity of fast-fashion purchases frees up budget for enduring staple pieces.
examples.zh: 大幅減少購買廉價快時尚衣服的數量，能騰出更多充裕預算投資在經久耐穿的傳世單品。

examples.en: Warehouses track the exact quantity of incoming fabric bolts before factory manufacturing starts.
examples.zh: 服裝倉儲物流中心在服裝工廠正式裁片開工前，會嚴密清點到庫布匹的精確批次與數量。

explains: This noun means how many things there are or how much of something is present. It is used for things that can be counted and for materials measured by amount. A large amount does not always mean something is good.
A shop counts the number of apples in a basket. A cook measures how much flour is needed. These amounts help people plan.
One noun asks “how much” or “how many,” while another asks “how good.” Some things are counted one by one, and others are measured by weight or volume. It can also mean a set amount.

examples.en: The teacher gave us a ten-word vocabulary pop quiz today.
examples.zh: 老師今天給我們考了十個單字的隨堂單字小考。

examples.en: You can take an online interactive quiz to test your grammar proficiency.
examples.zh: 您可以參加線上互動測驗以檢測自身的文法精熟度。

examples.en: The pub hosts a lively trivia quiz night every Wednesday evening.
examples.zh: 這家酒館每週三晚上都會舉辦氣氛熱烈的常識問答測驗之夜。

explains: This noun names a short test that checks what someone remembers. It can also be used as a verb for giving someone such a test. Teachers may ask a few questions at the start of class.
Students might answer questions about a story they read. A teacher can use the results to see what needs more practice. The test is usually shorter than a major exam.
This short classroom test often checks a small part of a subject. A larger test may cover more material and take longer. The verb can mean asking someone questions informally.

examples.en: The railroad runs through the valley.
examples.zh: 鐵路穿過山谷。

examples.en: We traveled by railway to the coast.
examples.zh: 我們搭火車前往海岸。

examples.en: Workers repaired the railroad after the storm.
examples.zh: 暴風雨後，工人修理了鐵路。

explains: These words name a track system used by trains and the companies or routes connected with it. One spelling is more common in American English, and the other is more common in British English. Trains carry people and goods along the tracks.
A passenger may ride between two cities on a train. Freight trains move supplies from factories to stores. Both use long tracks that connect places.
The spellings differ by region but refer to the same general system. A subway is an urban train network, often underground. The words can also refer to the track itself.

examples.en: I wore my raincoat on the walk to school.
examples.zh: 我走路上學時穿了雨衣。

examples.en: Her yellow raincoat has a hood.
examples.zh: 她的黃色雨衣有連帽。

examples.en: Please hang your wet raincoat by the door.
examples.zh: 請把濕雨衣掛在門邊。

explains: This outer coat keeps rain off a person’s clothes. Its fabric is made to stop water from passing through. Some have a hood.
A child may wear one to school in a storm. It can be folded into a bag when the sky clears. It helps keep clothes dry.
An umbrella covers the head, while this clothing covers the body. It is useful in wet weather. Bright colors help people see the wearer.

examples.en: GPS points plotted on maps defined a five-square-kilometer home range for the dominant male cat.
examples.zh: 將 GPS 定位座標點標繪於地圖上，繪製出成熟成年公石虎高達五平方公里的「家域活動範圍」（Home Range）。

examples.en: Female leopard cats maintain a significantly smaller home range centered on safe denning hollows.
examples.zh: 母石虎的活動範圍相對精巧集中，通常以隱密安全的育幼樹洞或土穴為核心。

examples.en: Habitat fragmentation forces wild carnivores to expand their range dangerously close to human settlements.
examples.zh: 棲地破碎化迫使野生肉食動物不得不擴大覓食活動範圍，冒險逼近人類村落聚落。

examples.en: Carrying sixty kilograms of compressed hydrogen provides an exceptional driving range of over one thousand kilometers.
examples.zh: 搭載六十公斤高壓氫氣，即可賦予大型卡車超過一千公里的「超長續航里程」（Driving Range）。

examples.en: The bookstore carries an impressive range of publications spanning classical philosophy, cooking, and architecture.
examples.zh: 這家獨立人文書店陳列販售極為豐富齊全的各類圖書，涵蓋古典哲學思辨、國際廚藝美學與現代建築設計。

examples.en: The majestic Central Mountain Range spans the spine of Taiwan, boasting dozens of peaks over three thousand meters.
examples.zh: 巍峨雄偉的中央山脈橫亙台灣本島縱貫脊樑，孕育了數十座海拔突破三千公尺大關、壯闊起伏的高山百岳群峰。

entries.definition: 公石虎與母石虎活動領域核心活動範圍；範圍；單次加氫一千公里超長續航里程 (告別里程焦慮)
explains: This word can mean the area or distance covered by something. It can also mean a group of choices. As a verb, it means to spread over an area.
A map may show where a certain bird lives. A store may sell many sizes of shoes. A car can travel far before needing fuel.
It has several uses in travel and shopping. As a verb, it can describe things reaching across a large area. Nearby words show its meaning.

examples.en: The rapid stream carried leaves downstream.
examples.zh: 湍急的溪流把葉子沖向下游。

examples.en: A rapid change in the weather surprised us.
examples.zh: 天氣迅速改變，讓我們很驚訝。

examples.en: The runner made rapid progress during practice.
examples.zh: 那名跑者在練習期間進步很快。

explains: This adjective means happening or moving very quickly. It can describe a change, animal, trip, or response. It often suggests little waiting.
A rabbit can run across a field in a short time. Weather can change before lunch. People may need to act fast.
“Fast” is a simpler word with a close meaning. A slow process takes more time. This adjective can describe speed or how quickly something happens.

examples.en: We saw a rare bird near the lake.
examples.zh: 我們在湖邊看到一種罕見的鳥。

examples.en: That old stamp is rare and hard to find.
examples.zh: 那張舊郵票很稀有，不容易找到。

examples.en: He ordered his steak rare.
examples.zh: 他點的牛排要煎得偏生。

explains: This adjective means not common or not often seen. It can describe an unusual animal, event, or object. It can also mean valuable because there are few of it.
A wildlife guide may be excited to spot a bird that lives in few places. A shop may sell a hard-to-find old coin. These things are unusual to come across.
“Common” is the opposite. Some unusual things are valuable, but not all are. The adjective can also describe meat cooked only a little.

examples.en: Keep food sealed so rats won't get inside.
examples.zh: 把食物密封好，老鼠才不會跑進來。

examples.en: City sanitation teams set bait traps to control the rat population in sewers.
examples.zh: 城市環境衛生小組設置餌劑陷阱，以控制下水道的大老鼠數量。

examples.en: Rats are remarkably intelligent creatures capable of navigating intricate mazes.
examples.zh: 大老鼠是非常聰明的生物，能夠走出複雜的迷宮。

explains: A small animal with a long tail and sharp front teeth often lives near people and searches for food. It can squeeze through small openings. The same short word can insult a person who cheats.
A farmer may find marks from one in a grain shed. A cat may try to catch one in a barn. It can hide in a tiny hole.
A mouse is usually smaller than this animal. Wild ones can carry germs, so people should not touch them. In slang, the name may be an insult.

examples.en: It was rather cold, so we wore our coats.
examples.zh: 天氣相當冷，所以我們穿上外套。

examples.en: I would rather walk than wait for the bus.
examples.zh: 我寧願走路也不等公車。

examples.en: The story was rather funny.
examples.zh: 這個故事相當有趣。

explains: This word can mean somewhat or to a certain degree. It can also show that someone likes one choice more than another. It is often followed by “than.”
A person may feel somewhat tired after a long walk. Someone may choose tea instead of coffee. The word can soften what a speaker says.
When choosing one action instead of another, this word can introduce the choice. It can also mean quite or somewhat, as in feeling quite cold. Nearby words help explain its role.

examples.en: Reality can be different from what we imagine.
examples.zh: 現實可能和我們想像的不同。

examples.en: It took him a moment to face reality after losing the game.
examples.zh: 輸掉比賽後，他花了一點時間才面對現實。

examples.en: The story mixes fantasy with reality.
examples.zh: 這個故事把幻想和現實交織在一起。

explains: This noun means what is true or actually happening. It can contrast with a dream, story, or wish. People sometimes need time to accept a difficult situation.
A child may learn that a movie dragon is pretend, but a pet dog is real. A family may face the truth about a broken window. Facts help people understand what happened.
Imagination creates things in the mind, while this word describes what exists or happens. A story can be based on real events or made up. It can also mean the way life is.

examples.en: I suddenly realized that I had left my EasyCard at home.
examples.zh: 我突然意識到我把悠遊卡忘在家裡了。

examples.en: It took decades of persistent dedication for the visionary baker to realize his dream.
examples.zh: 歷經數十年如一日的堅定奉獻，這位充滿抱負的烘焙大師終於實現了自己的夢想。

examples.en: Only when you live completely alone do you realize how much your parents sacrificed.
examples.zh: 唯有當你真正完全獨立在異鄉生活時，你才會深刻意識到父母當年的無私付出。

explains: This verb means to understand something or become aware of it. It can also mean to make a hope or plan come true. A person may notice a mistake only after looking again.
A student may suddenly understand why an answer was wrong. A family may work hard to make their dream of a garden come true. Both involve a change from before.
The verb can describe understanding or achieving. A goal is not achieved just by wishing for it. People may also use it to mean “notice.”

examples.en: I received a notification on my smartphone.
examples.zh: 我的智慧型手機收到了一則推播通知。

examples.en: She received a scholarship to study abroad next semester.
examples.zh: 她獲得了下學期赴海外留學的獎學金。

examples.en: The company received hundreds of inquiries after the product launch.
examples.zh: 產品發表會後，該公司收到了數百件詢問。

explains: This verb means to get or be given something. It can describe a letter, gift, message, or visitor. It can also mean welcoming a person.
A child may get a birthday card in the mail. A coach may welcome new players to the team. In both cases, something comes to the person.
“Get” is a simpler word with a close meaning. It often takes an object, such as a package or message. It can also describe signals arriving at a device.

examples.en: We read a recent article about sea turtles.
examples.zh: 我們讀了一篇最近有關海龜的文章。

examples.en: Her recent visit made Grandma very happy.
examples.zh: 她最近的拜訪讓奶奶很開心。

examples.en: A recent storm knocked leaves from the trees.
examples.zh: 最近的一場暴風雨把樹葉吹落了。

explains: This adjective means happening not long ago. It can describe news, a change, or a memory. The exact time depends on the topic.
A student may tell a friend about a trip from last week. Rain from yesterday may leave puddles in the playground. These events happened close to now.
This adjective is the opposite of old or long ago. It does not tell an exact date. People often use it with “in” or “over the.”

examples.en: Integrated Electronic Health Records (EHR) eliminate redundant blood tests across different clinics.
examples.zh: 跨院整合的電子健康病歷（EHR）能讓轉診醫師一目了然過往檢查報告，免去病患重複抽血之苦。

examples.en: The Olympic sprinter shattered the 100-meter world record by crossing the finish line in 9.58 seconds.
examples.zh: 這位傳奇牙買加短跑名將以九秒五八的驚人神速率先衝過終點線，一舉粉碎打破了塵封已久的一百公尺世界紀錄。

examples.en: Vinyl record collectors spend weekends scouring vintage music shops for rare original jazz pressings.
examples.zh: 黑膠唱片發燒收藏家每逢週末便流連於老街二手黑膠唱片行，興奮尋寶發掘早已絕版的初版經典爵士名盤。

entries.definition: 跨院共享之電子健康病歷 (EHR)
explains: This noun can mean a written account of events or information. It can also mean a best achievement, such as the fastest time in a race. As a verb, it means to capture sound or information.
A doctor writes notes about a visit. A runner may set a new best time. A phone can capture a voice message for later.
The word can name a document, a best result, or saving information. Music artists save songs so people can listen later. Nearby words tell the meaning.

examples.en: Get plenty of sleep to help your body recover rapidly.
examples.zh: 保持充足睡眠以幫助你的身體迅速康復。

examples.en: She managed to fully recover from pneumonia after two weeks of rest.
examples.zh: 經過兩週的充分休息，她從肺炎中完全康復。

examples.en: Police officers worked hard to recover the stolen museum artifacts.
examples.zh: 警方全力追查以找回博物館失竊的古董文物。

examples.en: Drink warm water, rest well, and you will recover from the cold soon.
examples.zh: 多喝溫開水、好好充分休息，你的感冒很快就會康復痊癒了。

examples.en: Police managed to recover stolen valuable jewelry and return it to the owner.
examples.zh: 警方抽絲剝繭迅速破案，成功找回追回了遭竊取的貴重珠寶並原物歸還失主。

examples.en: The tourism sector began to recover rapidly once international flight borders reopened.
examples.zh: 國際航班邊境大門重新敞開後，各地觀光旅遊業景氣便開始強勁復甦反彈。

explains: This verb means to become well again after being sick or hurt. It can also mean to get back something that was lost. People may need time and care.
A child may rest at home until a cold goes away. A swimmer might find a lost toy in a pool. Both cases involve getting back to a better state.
It can describe health, strength, or a lost item. Getting better is not always quick. People may also get over a disappointment.

examples.en: Keep the milk in the refrigerator so it stays fresh.
examples.zh: 把牛奶放進冰箱以保持新鮮。

examples.en: She posted our weekly class timetable on the door of the refrigerator.
examples.zh: 她把我們每週的課表貼在冰箱門上。

examples.en: Put leftover soup into a sealed container before placing it in the refrigerator.
examples.zh: 將吃剩的湯放入密封保鮮盒後再放進冰箱保存。

explains: This large kitchen appliance keeps food cold. It usually has shelves and a door that opens and closes. Cold storage helps food stay fresh longer.
A family puts milk and fruit inside after shopping. Ice trays can freeze water in a small compartment. The appliance uses electricity to stay cool.
A freezer makes food much colder and keeps it frozen. This machine keeps most food cold but not solid. People often use a shorter name in casual speech.

examples.en: He politely refused the extra piece of chocolate cake.
examples.zh: 他禮貌地婉拒了額外的巧克力蛋糕。

examples.en: The brave firefighter refused to give up searching for survivors.
examples.zh: 英勇的消防員拒絕放棄搜救任何生還者。

examples.en: It is perfectly fine to refuse requests that compromise your personal values.
examples.zh: 拒絕違背自己個人原則與價值觀的請求是完全合理的。

explains: This verb means to say no to something offered or requested. It can also mean deciding not to do something. The word can sound polite or firm.
A child may say no to another cookie because they are full. A person may turn down an invitation when busy. The choice is theirs.
“Decline” is a close word in some situations. A door that will not open may be described as not working. The object after this verb tells what is turned down.

examples.en: I regard my cousin as a good friend.
examples.zh: 我把表親視為好朋友。

examples.en: The teacher regarded the answer as correct.
examples.zh: 老師認為答案正確。

examples.en: We regard kindness as important.
examples.zh: 我們認為善良很重要。

explains: This verb can mean to think about someone in a certain way. It can also mean looking at or considering an idea. A phrase using it may introduce a topic.
A student may think of a classmate as a good helper. A teacher may consider how a rule affects everyone. People use the word when sharing a view.
In some sentences it means respect. It can also introduce a topic when talking about a trip. The meaning changes with the sentence pattern.

examples.en: This region gets a lot of rain in summer.
examples.zh: 這個地區夏天雨量很多。

examples.en: We explored the mountain region during our holiday.
examples.zh: 我們假期時探索了山區。

examples.en: The region is known for its fresh apples.
examples.zh: 這個地區以新鮮蘋果聞名。

explains: This noun means an area of a country or the world. It may have its own weather, landscape, or local customs. Maps divide large places into smaller areas.
An area near a mountain may be colder than land by the sea. People there may grow special crops. The word helps describe where something is.
Such an area can be larger than a town but smaller than a whole country. It does not always have official borders. Scientists and travelers often use the term.

examples.en: We have a regular meeting every Monday.
examples.zh: 我們每週一固定開會。

examples.en: She visits the library on a regular schedule.
examples.zh: 她定期去圖書館。

examples.en: The shop has regular customers who come each week.
examples.zh: 這家店有每週都來的常客。

explains: This adjective means usual or happening at steady times. It can describe a routine, size, or member of a group. It can also mean following a rule.
A child may have a usual bedtime on school nights. A bus may come at the same time each day. These events follow a familiar schedule.
Buses and trains often follow a set schedule. This word can also describe a shape with equal sides and angles. Nearby words show the intended meaning.

examples.en: The club rejected the plan because it cost too much.
examples.zh: 社團因為計畫花費太高而否決了它。

examples.en: She felt sad when her drawing was rejected.
examples.zh: 她的畫被退回時，她感到難過。

examples.en: Please reject any fruit that is moldy.
examples.zh: 請丟掉任何發霉的水果。

explains: This verb means to say no to an idea, request, or person. It can also mean to throw something away because it is not wanted. People may turn down a plan they think will not work.
A group may turn down a suggestion that costs too much. A recycling center sorts items it cannot use. In both cases, something is not accepted.
This verb is often stronger than “refuse,” especially for an idea or application. People can turn down a plan without turning away its author. The body can also fail to accept a transplant.

examples.en: I can relate to how nervous you felt before the show.
examples.zh: 我能體會你演出前緊張的心情。

examples.en: She related the story of her first day at school.
examples.zh: 她講述了自己上學第一天的故事。

examples.en: These two ideas relate to the same question.
examples.zh: 這兩個想法都和同一個問題有關。

explains: This verb means to connect one thing with another. It can also mean to tell a story or experience. People use it when they see a link between ideas.
A student may connect a book’s story to something that happened at home. A witness may tell what they saw. Both meanings bring information together.
This phrase can mean understanding another person’s feelings or experience. A family link can also be described with a similar word. The verb has several uses.

examples.en: My relation from Canada is visiting this summer.
examples.zh: 我在加拿大的親戚今年夏天要來訪。

examples.en: There is a clear relation between sleep and energy.
examples.zh: 睡眠和精力之間有明顯的關係。

examples.en: The two events have no relation to each other.
examples.zh: 這兩件事彼此沒有關聯。

explains: This noun names a connection between people or things. It can also mean a family member. A person may talk about how two ideas are connected.
A brother and sister have a family connection. A student may compare two stories and notice they share an idea. The same word can describe both links.
This word can name someone in a family, though “relative” is more common. It can also mean how one thing connects with another. Nearby words show the intended meaning.

examples.en: Their relationship grew stronger over the years.
examples.zh: 他們的關係多年來變得更親密。

examples.en: The book explores the relationship between sisters.
examples.zh: 這本書探討姊妹之間的關係。

examples.en: Good communication helps a relationship last.
examples.zh: 良好的溝通有助於維持一段關係。

explains: This noun means the way two people, groups, or things are connected. It can describe friendship, family, or work. A good connection often needs care and communication.
Two friends may talk through a problem and make up. A teacher and student work together toward learning. These are different kinds of connections.
A relation can be a family member, while this word is the connection itself. People may have many kinds of connections. It can also describe links between ideas or objects.

examples.en: The museum has an exhibit about religion around the world.
examples.zh: 博物館有一個介紹世界各地宗教的展覽。

examples.en: They learned about a new religion in history class.
examples.zh: 他們在歷史課上學到一種新的宗教。

examples.en: Her religion teaches kindness to strangers.
examples.zh: 她的宗教教導人們善待陌生人。

explains: This noun means belief and worship connected with a god or gods. Different groups have their own stories, customs, and ceremonies. Some people follow a faith, while others do not.
A family may celebrate a holiday with special food and songs. A place of worship may bring people together. These traditions can be important to a community.

These beliefs and practices differ from culture, which includes many parts of how people live. People should speak respectfully about different faiths. The word can also mean a strong personal belief.

examples.en: Please remove your shoes before entering the room.
examples.zh: 進入房間前請脫掉鞋子。

examples.en: Dad removed the old sticker from the window.
examples.zh: 爸爸把舊貼紙從窗戶上撕下來。

examples.en: The teacher removed one question from the quiz.
examples.zh: 老師從小考中刪去了一題。

explains: This verb means to take something away from a place. It can also mean to take off clothing or delete information. A person may clear a table after a meal.
A worker may take a box out of the hallway. A child may take off muddy shoes before entering the house. A computer user can erase an old file.
This word is more formal than “take away.” It can describe moving a stain, item, or person. The thing being taken away usually follows the verb.

examples.en: How much is the monthly rent for this two-bedroom suite?
examples.zh: 這間兩房套房每個月的租金是多少？

examples.en: We decided to rent a compact car to explore the coastal highway.
examples.zh: 我們決定租一輛小型掀背車來暢遊濱海公路。

examples.en: The sudden rent increase forced the small bakery to relocate to another street.
examples.zh: 突如其來的租金調漲迫使這家小烘焙坊搬遷至其他街道。

explains: This word can mean paying to use a home, car, or other thing for a while. It can also name the money paid for that use. As a verb, it means to let someone use something for payment.
A family may pay each month to live in an apartment. A visitor may borrow a bicycle from a shop for a day. The owner receives money for the use.
Buying means paying to own something, while paying for temporary use means having it for a limited time. The noun can refer to payment or an agreement. Read the terms before signing.

examples.en: The mechanic repaired my punctured bicycle tire quickly.
examples.zh: 技師迅速修補了我被刺破的腳踏車輪胎。

examples.en: Road repair work caused minor traffic delays during rush hour.
examples.zh: 道路修繕工程在尖峰時段造成了輕微的交通延誤。

examples.en: It will cost several hundred dollars to repair the broken smartphone screen.
examples.zh: 修理破碎的手機螢幕需要花費數百美元。

examples.en: Supplying a donor template directs the cell's natural homology repair machinery to fix the mutation.
examples.zh: 提供一段健康修復模板，能引導細胞內部的「同源重組修復機制」（Repair），將致病突變完美修正。

examples.en: The city maintenance crew worked through the night to repair the burst underground water main.
examples.zh: 市府工務搶修隊頂著夜色徹夜施工，在破曉前順利修復了爆裂的地下主要自來水幹管。

examples.en: Open and honest communication helps repair wounded trust between long-time business partners.
examples.zh: 坦誠不公的真摯溝通與交流，有助於重新修復長期商業合作夥伴之間受損的互信基礎。

entries.definition: 修理；修補；修復；同源重組修復 (HDR 精準插入修復基因片段)
explains: This verb means to fix something that is broken or damaged. It can also mean to make an idea or relationship better. People may mend a toy, bike, or fence.
A parent may mend a torn backpack strap. A worker may fix a hole in a wall. Careful work can make the item useful again.
This word often refers to things, while “fix” is a simple word with a similar meaning. It can also describe making up after an argument. The noun form names the work done.

examples.en: I will reply to your email as soon as possible.
examples.zh: 我會盡快回覆您的電子郵件。

examples.en: She received no reply to her letter for two whole weeks.
examples.zh: 她整整兩週都沒有收到對那封信的回覆。

examples.en: He replied politely that he was unable to attend the party.
examples.zh: 他禮貌地回覆表示自己無法出席該派對。

explains: This verb means to answer someone who has spoken or written to you. It can also name the answer itself. A quick response may be spoken, typed, or sent by mail.
A child may answer a question in class. A friend may send a message back after reading a note. The response shows that the person received the first message.
A noun can name the answer sent back. It usually comes after an earlier message. In a letter, the written words may be sent by mail.

examples.en: Fluent English communication is an essential job requirement.
examples.zh: 流利的英語溝通能力是一項必要的基本職務要求。

examples.en: Fulfilling ninety credit hours is a mandatory academic requirement for graduation.
examples.zh: 修畢取得九十個學分，是這所大學取得學士學位必備的核心修業規章要求。

examples.en: Wearing non-slip shoes and ear protection is a strict factory safety requirement.
examples.zh: 進入廠區工作時穿戴防滑安全鞋與抗噪防護耳罩，是一項不可妥協的工安強制規定。

explains: This verb means to need something or make it necessary. A rule may say what people must do. The noun names something that is needed.
A school trip may need a signed form. A game may need two teams before it can begin. These things must be ready first.
Something needed can be a rule, condition, or item. People should check instructions carefully. It is stronger than a wish because it must be done.

examples.en: Treat your elders and teachers with genuine respect.
examples.zh: 以真誠尊重的態度對待長輩與師長。

examples.en: I hold immense respect for frontline healthcare workers who serve selflessly.
examples.zh: 我對在第一線無私奉獻照護病患的醫護工作人員抱持著無比崇高的敬意。

examples.en: In many respects, studying abroad transforms a young person’s worldview permanently.
examples.zh: 在許多層面與維度上，赴海外留學會永久性地拓展重塑年輕人的世界觀。

explains: This word means treating someone or something as important and worthy of care. It can also mean admiration for a person’s actions. As a verb, it means to show this feeling.
A student may admire a coach who works hard. Good manners help people feel valued. Listening carefully is one way to show care.
The word can describe a feeling or an action. Following a rule shows that feeling. People may show it through words, choices, and behavior.

examples.en: She responded to the question with a smile.
examples.zh: 她微笑著回答了問題。

examples.en: The dog responded when I called its name.
examples.zh: 我叫狗狗的名字時，牠有了反應。

examples.en: He responded quickly to the message.
examples.zh: 他很快回覆了訊息。

explains: This verb means to answer or react to something. A person may speak after hearing a question. A body or machine may also react to a change.
A student answers when the teacher calls their name. A flower may open when sunlight reaches it. Both are reactions to something.
The verb can describe a spoken answer or an action. “Reply” is often used for words or messages. A response may also be a feeling or movement.

examples.en: Ken is responsible for managing customer relations.
examples.zh: 肯恩負責管理客戶關係事務。

examples.en: Parents should teach their children to be responsible citizens.
examples.zh: 父母應當教導孩子成為負責任的公民。

examples.en: Who is responsible for the broken window in the hallway?
examples.zh: 走廊上那扇破掉的窗戶是誰該負責？

explains: This adjective describes someone who can be trusted to do what they should. It can also mean being the cause of something. The word often appears with “for.”
A child may remember to feed the family pet. A broken window may be caused by a ball. These examples show two uses.
Taking care of a duty is one meaning. It does not mean being blamed for everything. A person can admit a mistake and help fix it.

examples.en: Where is the restroom in this store?
examples.zh: 這間店的洗手間在哪裡？

examples.en: The restroom has a sink and two stalls.
examples.zh: 洗手間裡有一個洗手台和兩間廁所。

examples.en: Please wash your hands in the restroom.
examples.zh: 請在洗手間洗手。

explains: This noun names a room with a toilet and sink that people can use in a public place. Signs often show where it is. Other countries may use different names.
A shopper may look for one in a large store. A traveler may stop at one during a long trip. It usually has separate areas for different users.
At home, people often call this room a bathroom. Public buildings have signs to help visitors find it. People should leave it clean for the next person.

examples.en: Hard work brings positive exam results.
examples.zh: 努力付出會帶來良好的考試成果。

examples.en: Heavy torrential rain caused flash flooding as a result of poor drainage.
examples.zh: 由於排水不良，豪大雨最終導致了瞬間積淹水的結果。

examples.en: The clinical experiment produced unexpected scientific results that surprised researchers.
examples.zh: 這項臨床實驗產生了令研究人員大感意外的科學成果。

explains: This noun means what happens because of an action or event. It can also mean a score or answer. As a verb, it means to happen because of something.
A student studies and gets a good score. Heavy rain may cause puddles in the street. The final outcome follows an earlier action.
A cause happens first, and what follows comes after. This word can be used for schoolwork, games, or events. It may be good, bad, or unexpected.

examples.en: You can return unworn items within seven days.
examples.zh: 您可在七天內將未穿過的商品辦理退貨。

examples.en: He returned the borrowed library books on his way home from school.
examples.zh: 他在放學回家的路上順道歸還了向圖書館借閱的書籍。

examples.en: In return for your kind help, I would like to treat you to dinner.
examples.zh: 為了答謝你的熱心幫忙，我想請你吃頓晚餐。

examples.en: E-commerce platforms offer hassle-free seven-day merchandise return services.
examples.zh: 電商平台提供七天鑑賞期內輕鬆便捷的無條件退換貨服務。

examples.en: The investor expects a substantial financial return on this renewable energy project.
examples.zh: 該名投資者殷切期望這項大型再生能源投資專案能帶來豐厚且穩健的投資報酬率。

examples.en: She promised to return the borrowed library books before the weekend due date.
examples.zh: 她信守承諾，在週末到期日截止前親自將所有向公立圖書館借閱的藏書歸還。

explains: This word can mean to come or go back to a place. It can also mean giving something back or exchanging a purchase. As a noun, it can name the trip back.
A child may go back home after school. A shopper may bring an unwanted shirt back to the store. Both actions bring something back.
A trip back goes to where it began. The word can also mean an answer or money earned from an investment. Nearby words show the meaning.

examples.en: Check customer reviews and photos before booking the seaside hotel.
examples.zh: 預訂海景飯店前先查看住客的真實評論與照片。

examples.en: Students should review their vocabulary flashcards every evening before bedtime.
examples.zh: 學生們每天晚上就寢前都應該將單字記憶卡拿出來認真複習一遍。

examples.en: The medical committee met to conduct a thorough review of clinical trial results.
examples.zh: 醫學倫理審查委員會召開會議，對新藥臨床試驗的完整數據進行嚴格審查。

examples.en: Read honest gadget reviews before deciding which tablet to buy.
examples.zh: 在決定購買哪款平板電腦之前，先閱讀客觀真實的評測心得。

examples.en: The academic committee conducted a thorough review of the research proposal.
examples.zh: 學術委員會對該項專題研究企劃書進行了極其嚴謹的審查評估。

examples.en: Students gathered at the library to review vocabulary notes before the midterm.
examples.zh: 學生們期中考前聚集在圖書館內溫習複習單字筆記。

examples.en: Prepare quantifiable business metric achievements before your year-end performance review meeting.
examples.zh: 在參加年終績效考核面談前，請提早備妥量化客觀的營收貢獻、專案進度與 KPI 達標數據。

examples.en: Supervisors conduct quarterly review sessions to track progress on key strategic OKRs.
examples.zh: 部門主管每季定期召開一對一工作績效檢討考核會議，嚴格追蹤各項關鍵戰略 OKR 的推進落實。

examples.en: The client submitted a glowing review praising our quick turnaround and meticulous code quality.
examples.zh: 跨國企業客戶在專案結案報告中給予滿分五星好評審查，盛讚我們極速的交付效率與嚴謹的程式碼品質。

examples.en: The Institutional Review Board reviewed the patient consent forms to protect human dignity.
examples.zh: 醫院「人體試驗倫理審查委員會」（Institutional Review Board IRB），嚴格審查知情同意書以捍衛人權尊嚴。

examples.en: Peer review by external domain specialists caught methodological errors before the journal published the paper.
examples.zh: 在學術期刊正式刊登論文前，由外部同行專家進行的嚴格審查成功挑出了研究方法中的微小瑕疵。

examples.en: The manager conducted a comprehensive annual performance review with every software engineer on the team.
examples.zh: 部門主管與團隊中每一位軟體工程師展開一對一深入懇談，進行全面客觀的年度工作績效考評回顧。

entries.definition: 評論；評價；複習；審查；評測；開箱評價；年度績效考核面談；醫院人體試驗倫理審查委員會 (IRB 審查)
explains: This word can mean looking at something again to check or remember it. It can also be an opinion about a book, show, or product. As a verb, it means to examine.
A student may look over spelling words before a test. A reader may write what they thought about a new book. Both involve thinking carefully.
Looking something over can help someone remember facts or decide what to buy. A written opinion may praise or criticize. The word can also name an official check of work or plans.

examples.en: The king’s riches filled a room with gold.
examples.zh: 國王的財富讓一整個房間都堆滿了黃金。

examples.en: The story tells of riches hidden under the old tree.
examples.zh: 故事講述藏在老樹下的財寶。

examples.en: He dreamed of finding riches in the mountains.
examples.zh: 他夢想在山中找到寶藏。

explains: This plural noun means a great amount of money or valuable things. It can also describe great natural resources. Stories often show characters searching for treasure.
A pirate tale may tell of gold hidden on an island. A land with fertile soil and forests may be rich in natural resources. These things have high value.
Wealth is a similar idea. Money is only one kind of valuable thing. The plural form is common when talking about treasure or great wealth.

examples.en: The rocky beach was hard to walk across.
examples.zh: 多岩石的海灘很難走。

examples.en: We drove along a rocky road in the hills.
examples.zh: 我們沿著山中的崎嶇道路開車。

examples.en: They had a rocky start but soon became friends.
examples.zh: 他們一開始相處不順，但很快就成了朋友。

explains: This adjective means covered with rocks or made of stone. It can also describe a difficult or unsteady situation. The word may describe land, a road, or a relationship.
A hiker may walk slowly over a rough path with many stones. A boat may move unsteadily in a storm. Both situations can be hard to manage.
A smooth road has few bumps or stones. This adjective can also describe a hard time between friends. Its meaning depends on what it describes.

examples.en: She played the role of a brave explorer.
examples.zh: 她扮演一位勇敢的探險家。

examples.en: My role in the project is to draw the map.
examples.zh: 我在這個計畫中的工作是畫地圖。

examples.en: Everyone has a role to play on the team.
examples.zh: 每個人在隊伍中都有自己的角色。

explains: This noun means the part a person has in a play, group, or situation. It can also mean a duty or job. People may have different duties at home and school.
An actor may pretend to be a king on stage. A class leader may help organize a project. Each person has a part to play.
A job title names work, while this word can include duties beyond a title. It may refer to a character in a story. The word is often used with “play.”

examples.en: Birds are resting on the red tile roof.
examples.zh: 鳥兒正棲息在紅瓦屋頂上。

examples.en: We stood on the rooftop viewing platform to admire the night skyline.
examples.zh: 我們站在頂樓觀景台上欣賞迷人的夜間城市天際線。

examples.en: The old house roof leaked rainwater during the torrential typhoon.
examples.zh: 老屋的屋頂在傾盆颱風雨期間發生了滲水。

examples.en: A living green roof blanketed with drought-tolerant succulents reduces building cooling demands by 20%.
examples.zh: 在頂樓鋪設耐旱景天科植物的立體綠化綠屋頂，能阻隔烈日暴曬並為頂樓降溫三到五度。

examples.en: Sedum mats planted on the flat roof create an insulating buffer against midday tropical radiation.
examples.zh: 平屋頂上鋪滿的佛甲草與景天科植物植生毯，為頂樓住戶築起了一道阻絕熱浪輻射的隔熱緩衝屏障。

examples.en: Green roof installations capture stormwater before it overflows municipal drainage systems.
examples.zh: 全面普及的立體綠屋頂能在第一時間攔截吸納暴雨雨水，避免雨水瞬間灌爆市區下水道系統。

entries.definition: 屋頂；頂部；景天科隔熱降溫立體綠化空中花園
explains: This noun names the top covering of a building. It protects the rooms below from rain, sun, and snow. The word can also mean the highest part of something.
A family listens to rain tapping overhead. Workers may climb up to fix a broken tile. The covering keeps the inside dry.
A ceiling is the inside surface above a room, while this part is outside. Some homes have flat tops and others slope. The word can also refer to the top of a car.

examples.en: The rooster crowed before sunrise.
examples.zh: 公雞在日出前啼叫。

examples.en: A red rooster walked across the farmyard.
examples.zh: 一隻紅公雞走過農場庭院。

examples.en: The rooster woke us early on the farm.
examples.zh: 農場裡的公雞很早就把我們叫醒了。

explains: This noun names an adult male chicken. It often has a red crest and makes a loud call at dawn. It lives on a farm or in a yard.
A farmer may hear one crow early in the morning. Hens lay eggs, while this bird does not. It may have bright feathers and a curved tail.
A young chicken is called a chick. The female adult is a hen. This bird is known for its early morning call.

examples.en: The royal family waved to the crowd.
examples.zh: 王室向群眾揮手。

examples.en: They visited a royal palace during their trip.
examples.zh: 他們旅行時參觀了一座王宮。

examples.en: A royal blue scarf hung by the door.
examples.zh: 門邊掛著一條寶藍色圍巾。

explains: This adjective describes a king, queen, or their family. It can also describe something very grand or impressive. Some countries have such a family as part of their traditions.
A palace may have rooms used by a king and queen. A family may visit a grand celebration with special clothes. The word suggests a connection to rulers.
A president is elected in many countries, while a king or queen may inherit the role. The adjective can also describe a deep blue color. Nearby words show which sense fits.

examples.en: Rub the table gently with a clean cloth.
examples.zh: 用乾淨的布輕輕擦桌子。

examples.en: He rubbed his hands together to warm them.
examples.zh: 他搓搓雙手讓它們暖和起來。

examples.en: The dog rubbed its head against my leg.
examples.zh: 狗狗把頭靠著我的腿磨蹭。

explains: This verb means to move one thing back and forth against another. It can warm, clean, or polish a surface. It can also mean applying a substance with the hand.
A child may move both hands together on a cold day. A person can use a cloth to clean a dusty table. Repeated movement can create warmth or remove dirt.
Scrubbing uses stronger back-and-forth movement. The action may be gentle or firm. The word can also describe friction between surfaces.

examples.en: The ball is made of soft rubber.
examples.zh: 這顆球是用柔軟的橡膠做的。

examples.en: She used a rubber to erase the pencil mark.
examples.zh: 她用橡皮擦擦掉鉛筆痕。

examples.en: Rubber boots kept his feet dry in the rain.
examples.zh: 橡膠雨鞋讓他的腳在雨中保持乾爽。

explains: This noun names a stretchy material used to make tires, bands, and boots. In British English, it can also mean an eraser. The adjective can describe something made from this material.
A child may use a stretchy band to hold papers together. A car tire is made partly from this flexible substance. It can bend without breaking easily.
Plastic is a different material and may not stretch in the same way. In some places, people call an eraser by this name. The sentence helps show the meaning.

examples.en: It is rude to interrupt someone when they speak.
examples.zh: 在別人說話時插嘴是不禮貌的。

examples.en: The waiter received complaints because of his rude attitude.
examples.zh: 那位服務生因為粗魯無禮的態度而遭到投訴。

examples.en: It is rude to stare pointedly at strangers on the subway.
examples.zh: 在捷運上盯著陌生人看是非常不禮貌的。

explains: This adjective describes behavior that is not polite or kind. It can describe words, actions, or a person’s manner. Speaking over someone may seem this way.
A person may interrupt a friend and refuse to listen. A child can learn to say “please” and “thank you.” Polite words help people get along.
This behavior is stronger than simply being quiet or shy. It often means someone has ignored good manners. A direct comment can sound unkind even if it is true.

examples.en: The runner crossed the finish line first.
examples.zh: 那名跑者第一個越過終點線。

examples.en: A runner brought the note to the office.
examples.zh: 一名傳送員把便條送到辦公室。

examples.en: The table runner has blue flowers.
examples.zh: 桌旗上有藍色花朵。

explains: This noun names a person who runs as a sport or for exercise. It can also mean a long narrow carpet or a person who delivers things. The context shows which meaning is intended.
A child may race around a track during practice. A long strip of cloth can protect a table. Someone may also carry messages between rooms.
A jogger runs for exercise, while a person in a race may train for speed. The noun can also name a plant stem that grows along the ground. It has several everyday uses.

examples.en: Strict traffic lights and pedestrian crossings enhance road safety.
examples.zh: 完善嚴格的交通號誌與行人穿越道能增進道路安全。

examples.en: Construction workers must wear protective hard hats and safety boots on site.
examples.zh: 營建施工現場工人工作時必須全程配戴防護工程安全帽與防刺安全鞋。

examples.en: Food safety inspectors check restaurant kitchens regularly to prevent food poisoning.
examples.zh: 食品安全衛生稽查員定期抽檢餐廳廚房衛生，以防範食物中毒發生。

examples.en: Rigorous multi-tier farm inspections ensure strict national food safety compliance.
examples.zh: 產官學多方攜手落實多重產地抽驗與源頭控管，為全體國人的每日三餐食品安全嚴格把關。

examples.en: Always wear protective helmet and steel-toed boots to ensure personal safety on construction sites.
examples.zh: 在進出工務建設工地現場時，請務必全程規範佩戴工程安全帽與防穿刺鋼頭工作鞋以確保人身安全。

examples.en: Strict food safety protocols protect public health against harmful bacterial contamination outbreaks.
examples.zh: 全面落實嚴謹標準的食品安全作業規範，能有效築牢公共衛生防線，防堵致病細菌交叉污染。

examples.en: Advanced active and passive safety features make modern vehicles protective fortresses on wheels.
examples.zh: 先進的主動預警防護與被動高剛性車體結構，將現代汽車打造為守護全家人生命安全的移動堡壘。

examples.en: Construction workers must wear hard hats and reflective safety vests at all times on job sites.
examples.zh: 勞檢所嚴格規範，營建工地現場的工程人員任何時刻皆必須確實配戴安全帽並穿著反光安全背心。

examples.en: Food safety inspectors conducted surprise inspections across night market stalls to test cooking oil quality.
examples.zh: 衛生局食品安全稽查員深入各大觀光夜市小吃攤展開無預警突擊抽檢，嚴格檢測油炸食用油的總極性物質。

examples.en: Centimeter-level lane-level positioning is a fundamental requirement for full autonomous driving safety.
examples.zh: 達成公分級的「車道級精準定位」，是確保全自動無人駕駛車輛上路營運「功能安全」（Safety）的核心基石。

examples.en: Factory workers must wear hard hats, steel-toed boots, and high-visibility vests for workplace safety.
examples.zh: 工廠現場作業人員進入廠區時，必須依工安規定全程佩戴工程安全帽、鋼頭防護鞋與高反光反光背心。

examples.en: Airline flight attendants review aircraft safety instructions and emergency exit procedures before takeoff.
examples.zh: 民航客機空服員在班機後推起飛前，依例向全體登機乘客詳細示範救生衣操作與客艙緊急逃生門安全指引。

examples.en: Decades of testing demonstrate that hydrogen vehicles achieve superior crash safety compared to gasoline cars.
examples.zh: 數十年的嚴格撞擊測試證實，現代氫能車輛在各項事故中展現出優於傳統汽油車的「極致安全性能」（Safety）。

examples.en: Chemical laboratory regulations mandate wearing protective goggles and coats to ensure student laboratory safety.
examples.zh: 學校化學實驗室守則明文規定所有進入實驗室人員皆必須配戴防護護目鏡與實驗白袍，嚴格確保學員人身實驗安全。

examples.en: The kindergarten classroom underwent safety modifications, installing cushioned foam guards on all sharp table edges.
examples.zh: 幼兒園小班教室在開學前全面進行兒童居家安全防護改造，在所有桌椅尖銳邊角皆仔細加裝加厚防撞泡棉防護條。

entries.definition: 安全；平安；治安；食品安全；嚴格把關；全方位的行車防護安全；確保無人自駕載具萬無一失之功能安全最高認證；嚴格符合 ISO 與全球車輛法規之全方位安全防護
explains: This noun means being protected from danger or harm. It can also mean a device or rule that helps prevent accidents. People should follow safe practices at home and outside.
A helmet helps protect a cyclist’s head. A guardrail can keep people from stepping off a high platform. These things lower risk.
Rules help people know what to do. They cannot prevent every accident, but they reduce danger. The word can also mean a secure place or condition.

examples.en: We watched the boat sail across the bay.
examples.zh: 我們看著船航行穿過海灣。

examples.en: The white sail caught the wind.
examples.zh: 白色的船帆迎風鼓起。

examples.en: The ship will sail at dawn.
examples.zh: 船將在黎明時出航。

explains: This verb means to travel on water in a boat, often using wind. As a noun, it names the large cloth that catches wind. The word can also mean moving smoothly.
A family may ride in a small boat across a lake. The wind pushes against the cloth and moves the boat forward. A captain steers around rocks.
A motorboat uses an engine, while a sailboat can use wind. The noun names the cloth, and the verb names the trip. A bird can glide through the air.

examples.en: The sailor tied the boat to the dock.
examples.zh: 水手把船繫在碼頭上。

examples.en: A sailor waved from the deck.
examples.zh: 一名水手在甲板上揮手。

examples.en: The sailor checked the ropes before leaving.
examples.zh: 水手離開前檢查了繩索。

explains: This noun names a person who works or travels on a ship. Crew members help steer, care for equipment, or move cargo. Some serve in a navy.
A person on a ship may spend weeks at sea with a crew. Another might guide a small boat along the coast. The job requires learning how to stay safe on the water.
A passenger rides on a ship but does not work there. A captain leads the crew. The word can describe people on many kinds of ships.

examples.en: The salesperson showed us three coats.
examples.zh: 那位銷售員拿了三件外套給我們看。

examples.en: A salesman helped Dad choose a new lamp.
examples.zh: 一名男銷售員幫爸爸挑了一盞新燈。

examples.en: The saleswoman answered my question about the shoes.
examples.zh: 那位女銷售員回答了我關於鞋子的問題。

explains: This noun names someone whose job is helping customers choose and buy things. They may work in a store or contact people about a service. The word has several gender forms.
A man may help a customer choose a coat. A customer can ask about sizes, colors, or prices. Helpful workers answer questions before a purchase.
A cashier takes payment, while this worker may help people choose an item. The gender-neutral form is common. The role may involve products or services.

examples.en: Salted crispy chicken is a must-try night market snack.
examples.zh: 鹹酥雞是必嚐的夜市小吃。

examples.en: This seaweed soup tastes a little bit too salty; please add some water.
examples.zh: 這碗海帶湯喝起來有點太鹹了，請加點水。

examples.en: Sea water is salty because it contains dissolved minerals and salts.
examples.zh: 海水之所以是鹹的，是因為含有溶解的礦物質與鹽分。

explains: This adjective means tasting of salt. It can also describe a person who feels annoyed, especially after losing. Food may need only a little salt to taste this way.
A cook may add a pinch to soup. A person may taste a chip and notice its salt flavor. Too much can make food hard to enjoy.
Sweet is a different taste. The word can also be informal slang for being angry or annoyed. The sentence shows which meaning is used.

examples.en: The Mars Sample Return campaign aims to bring pristine rock cores back to Earth for ultra-precise lab testing.
examples.zh: 火星樣本採樣返回計畫，旨在將密封的原始岩芯帶回地球進行頂級化驗。

examples.en: Titanium sample tubes are dropped along the rover’s path, waiting for a future retrieval lander.
examples.zh: 封存著沉積岩芯的純鈦樣本儲存管被整齊放置在探測車行經路徑上，靜候未來的取樣登陸器前來回收。

examples.en: Analyzing a tiny soil sample using synchrotron radiation could reveal definitive proof of past alien microbiology.
examples.zh: 使用同步輻射光源化驗微小的火星土壤樣本，將能為火星遠古是否存在地外微生物提供決定性鐵證。

entries.definition: 火星密封岩芯樣本採樣返回地球計畫；樣品
explains: This noun means a small part taken from a larger amount to show what it is like. It can also mean a piece used for testing. As a verb, it means to try a little.
A shopper may taste a tiny piece of cheese before buying it. A scientist may test a small amount of water. These parts give information about the whole.
A small part is less than the full amount. Stores sometimes offer free tastes of food. The verb can mean trying or testing a little.

examples.en: The sand felt warm under our feet.
examples.zh: 沙子在我們腳下摸起來暖暖的。

examples.en: We built a small castle in the sand.
examples.zh: 我們用沙子堆了一座小城堡。

examples.en: The wind blew sand across the path.
examples.zh: 風吹著沙子越過小路。

explains: Tiny grains of rock or shells are often found on beaches and deserts. They feel rough between the fingers. Wind and water move them around.
Children may fill a bucket beside the sea. Builders mix it with other materials to make concrete. It can be light or dark in color.
Gravel has larger pieces than this material. A beach may have a soft layer beside the water. People should not throw it at others.

examples.en: Mom packed a ham and egg sandwich for my lunch.
examples.zh: 媽媽為我的午餐準備了火腿蛋三明治。

examples.en: He ordered a toasted chicken club sandwich with a cup of black coffee.
examples.zh: 他點了一份烤雞肉總匯三明治搭配一杯黑咖啡。

examples.en: Sandwiches are convenient snacks to pack for outdoor hiking trips.
examples.zh: 三明治是外出健行旅行時便於攜帶的點心。

explains: Food placed between pieces of bread or inside a cut roll makes an easy lunch. Fillings may include cheese, vegetables, eggs, or meat. People carry it to school or work.
A child may spread peanut butter on bread and add banana slices. A shop may sell warm bread with cheese inside. People choose many fillings.
A wrap holds its filling in flatbread. This meal usually uses sliced bread or a roll. It can be eaten cold or toasted.

examples.en: The warm soup satisfied my hunger.
examples.zh: 熱湯讓我不再餓了。

examples.en: Her answer satisfied the teacher.
examples.zh: 她的回答讓老師滿意。

examples.en: This toy satisfies the safety rules.
examples.zh: 這個玩具符合安全規定。

explains: This verb means to give someone what they need or want. It can also mean meeting a rule or condition. A good answer may make a curious person content.
A snack may stop someone from feeling hungry. A student may complete all parts of an assignment. Both meet a need or expectation.
It is often followed by a person or need. A pleasing result can make someone happy. The word can describe feelings, rules, or conditions.

examples.en: Japanese pull saws cut cleanly on the pull stroke, producing razor-thin kerfs with minimal tear-out.
examples.zh: 日式細工拉鋸在向內拉動時俐落施力鋸切，切口平整光滑且不留毛邊木屑。

examples.en: He used a sharp hand saw to prune dead branches off the fruit trees in the backyard orchard.
examples.zh: 他手持一把鋒利的手工園藝鋸，俐落地將後院果園果樹上的枯萎枝椏一一修剪鋸除。

examples.en: Through the binoculars, she clearly saw a pair of migratory black-faced spoonbills wading in the wetland.
examples.zh: 透過高倍率雙筒望遠鏡，她清晰看見了一對珍貴的保育類黑面琵鷺正在濕地淺灘悠閒漫步。

entries.definition: 日式細工拉鋸 (Dozuki 鋸)；鋸開
explains: A tool with a sharp toothed edge cuts wood or other material. The same spelling is also the past form of “see.” Sentence clues show which meaning fits.
A carpenter moves the toothed tool back and forth through a board. Yesterday, a child noticed a rainbow after the rain. These uses have different meanings.
A knife has a smooth edge, while this tool has teeth. As a past verb, it tells what someone viewed earlier. The same spelling has two common uses.

examples.en: The sudden noise scared the cat.
examples.zh: 突如其來的聲音嚇到了貓。

examples.en: The mask did not scare the baby.
examples.zh: 那個面具沒有嚇到寶寶。

examples.en: The dark tunnel gave us a scare.
examples.zh: 黑暗的隧道讓我們受到驚嚇。

explains: This verb means to make someone feel afraid. A loud sound or sudden surprise can do this. The noun can name a short time of fear.
A mask may frighten a friend during a game. A sudden bark can startle someone walking by. People should stop if the other person feels upset.
“Frighten” is a close word. A story about ghosts may cause fear without real danger. A sudden noise can also make someone worry about a possible problem.

examples.en: The scared child held her mother’s hand.
examples.zh: 那個害怕的孩子握著媽媽的手。

examples.en: I felt scared before the first lesson.
examples.zh: 第一堂課前我感到害怕。

examples.en: The scared puppy hid under the chair.
examples.zh: 那隻受驚的小狗躲在椅子底下。

explains: This adjective describes feeling afraid or worried. A person may feel this way in the dark or before trying something new. The feeling can pass when they feel safe.
A child may hold a parent’s hand during a loud storm. A student may feel worried before speaking to the class. Kind support can help.
This adjective describes the person’s feeling, while “scary” describes what causes fear. People can feel afraid and still do a brave thing. Support from a friend can help.

examples.en: The opening sunset scene by the beach was breathtakingly beautiful.
examples.zh: 海灘邊的日落開場場景美得令人屏息。

examples.en: Police and forensic detectives arrived quickly at the crime scene.
examples.zh: 警方與鑑識小組探員迅速抵達了犯罪現場。

examples.en: Taipei boasts a vibrant underground indie music scene with weekly live shows.
examples.zh: 台北擁有蓬勃發展的地下獨立音樂圈，每週都有現場演出。

examples.en: Patrol officers immediately cordoned off the indoor crime scene with bright yellow caution tape.
examples.zh: 巡邏員警第一時間拉起鮮黃色警戒封鎖線，嚴格管制並保全犯罪現場完整跡證。

examples.en: Forensic technicians spent eight hours systematically photographing and dusting the entire scene.
examples.zh: 鑑識小組人員耗費了整整八個小時，對整個犯罪現場展開地毯式的照相存證與粉末採證。

examples.en: Unauthorized personnel were strictly barred from walking across the wet murder scene.
examples.zh: 所有未經授權的無關人員一律被嚴格隔離在外，嚴禁踩踏尚未勘驗完成的命案現場。

entries.definition: 場景；一幕；現場；犯罪現場黃色警戒封鎖線
explains: This noun can mean the place where something happens. It can also name a part of a play or movie. It may describe what people see around them.
A police officer may ask what happened at a street corner. In a play, actors perform one part before the next begins. The word has several uses.
A setting tells where a story takes place. One part is only a piece of the whole story. The word can also mean a noisy public argument.

examples.en: Check your daily schedule to see if you are free.
examples.zh: 查看你的每日行程表，看看是否有空。

examples.en: The train arrived twenty minutes behind schedule.
examples.zh: 火車比預定時間晚到了二十分鐘。

examples.en: We need to schedule an appointment with the dentist.
examples.zh: 我們需要和牙醫預約門診時間。

examples.en: Check the weekly flight schedule before planning your business trip.
examples.zh: 在規劃商務出差前先核對每週航班時刻表。

examples.en: Despite heavy monsoon rains, the bridge construction remained strictly on schedule.
examples.zh: 儘管遭遇連綿豪雨侵襲，跨海大橋的橋樑鋼構興建工程依然嚴格維持在預定進度上。

examples.en: Let's schedule a Zoom call for tomorrow morning to review the draft contract.
examples.zh: 咱們安排在明天早晨進行一場 Zoom 視訊會議，逐條審查合約初稿條款細節。

entries.definition: 行程表；時刻表；排定；進度表；行程；排程
explains: This noun is a plan showing when things will happen. It can list classes, meetings, or trips. As a verb, it means to choose a time.
A student checks a list of class times to find the next lesson. A family may plan a visit for Saturday. The list helps everyone know what comes next.
A calendar shows dates, while this plan may include exact times too. Plans can change when something unexpected happens. The verb is often used with “for.”

examples.en: Many people ride scooters to work in Taiwan.
examples.zh: 在台灣許多人騎機車上班。

examples.en: Always wear a safety helmet when riding a scooter.
examples.zh: 騎機車時一定要配戴安全帽。

examples.en: Scooters make it easy to weave through busy city traffic.
examples.zh: 機車讓人很容易穿梭在繁忙的市區車流中。

examples.en: Scooters are the most common mode of transport in Taiwan.
examples.zh: 機車是台灣最普遍的代步交通工具。

examples.en: She commutes to work on her electric scooter every morning.
examples.zh: 她每天早晨騎著電動機車通勤上班。

examples.en: Renting a scooter is a convenient way to explore the island.
examples.zh: 租一輛機車是探索這座島嶼的便利方式。

explains: This small two-wheeled vehicle has a low place for the feet. Some have a motor, while others are pushed with one foot. A helmet helps protect riders.
A child may push along a path in the park. A grown-up may ride a motorized one through city streets. Riders should follow traffic rules.
A bicycle has pedals and a seat, while many of these have a standing platform. Larger motor models may have seats. The word describes several small vehicles.

examples.en: What is the final score of the baseball game?
examples.zh: 這場棒球比賽的最終比分是多少？

examples.en: The young striker scored the winning goal in the final ninety seconds.
examples.zh: 年輕前鋒在最後九十秒踢進了致勝得分球。

examples.en: The composer wrote a haunting orchestral score for the movie soundtrack.
examples.zh: 作曲家為電影原聲帶編寫了一首扣人心弦的管弦樂配樂。

examples.en: The Tony Award-winning musical score blends jazzy brass riffs with symphonic strings.
examples.zh: 勇奪東尼獎最佳配樂大獎的原創音樂總譜，巧妙揉合了奔放的爵士銅管搖擺與磅礡的大編制管弦交響。

examples.en: The composer sat at the piano for six straight months to craft the emotional orchestral score for the film.
examples.zh: 這位電影配樂大師在鋼琴前閉關創作長達半年，為這部史詩鉅片譜寫出賺人熱淚的壯麗管弦樂總譜。

examples.en: Striking in the final ninety seconds, the local football team managed to score the winning goal.
examples.zh: 在終場前最後九十秒讀秒階段，地主足球隊抓住角球機會頭槌破網，奇蹟般射入鎖定勝局的致勝分。

entries.definition: 得分；比分；進球；記分；百老匯原創音樂總譜
explains: This noun means the number of points earned in a game. It can also mean music written for a film or show. As a verb, it means to earn points.
A team may put the ball in the net during a soccer match. The board shows how many points each side has. A composer writes music for a movie.
Putting the ball in the net is one way to earn points in soccer. The total tells who is ahead. In music, it shows which notes performers should play.

examples.en: Staring at the screen for too long hurts your eyes.
examples.zh: 盯著螢幕太久會傷害你的眼睛。

examples.en: Modern smartphone screens adjust brightness automatically according to room lighting.
examples.zh: 現代智慧型手機螢幕會依據室內光線自動調整亮度。

examples.en: He installed a protective glass film over the tablet screen.
examples.zh: 他在平板螢幕上貼了一層玻璃保護貼。

explains: This noun names the flat surface showing pictures on a phone, computer, or television. It can also mean the cloth used to show a movie. As a verb, it means to check or test.
A student reads a story on a tablet display. People watch a film on a large wall at a theater. A doctor may check for a health problem.
A display shows images but does not create them by itself. A curtain can hide the view. Checking people or things for a reason is another use of the verb.

examples.en: We ordered seafood soup for lunch.
examples.zh: 我們午餐點了海鮮湯。

examples.en: Fresh seafood needs to stay cold.
examples.zh: 新鮮海鮮需要保持低溫。

examples.en: The seafood market opens early.
examples.zh: 海鮮市場很早就開門。

explains: This noun means food from the sea, such as fish, shrimp, or clams. People cook it in many ways. Some people cannot eat it because of allergies.
A family may order fish at a seaside restaurant. A cook can add shrimp to noodles. Fresh food should be kept cold until prepared.
Meat comes from land animals, while this food comes from water animals. Not every ocean animal is eaten. Different cultures use different spices.

examples.en: Search for English tutorials on YouTube.
examples.zh: 在 YouTube 上搜尋英語教學影片。

examples.en: Police launched an extensive search for the missing hiker in the mountains.
examples.zh: 警方在山區對失蹤的登山客展開了全面搜救。

examples.en: Use specific keywords to search the university database efficiently.
examples.zh: 使用具體關鍵字可以有效率地檢索大學資料庫。

examples.en: Grover’s search algorithm accelerates unstructured database queries with a quadratic mathematical speedup.
examples.zh: 格羅弗搜尋演算法，為龐大無序的非結構化資料庫檢索帶來平方根級的驚人數學加速。

examples.en: Searching through an unsorted phonebook of N entries takes only the square root of N quantum iterations.
examples.zh: 在一本包含 N 筆隨機雜亂資料的電話簿中搜尋特定號碼，格羅弗演算法僅需開根號 N 次的量子迭代。

examples.en: Cryptanalysts evaluate Grover’s search when determining symmetric key lengths like AES-256.
examples.zh: 現代密碼分析學家在評估 AES-256 對稱加密金鑰強度時，皆會將格羅弗搜尋演算法的威脅納入考量。

entries.definition: 搜尋；尋找；搜查；格羅弗演算法 (平方根級非結構化資料庫搜尋)
explains: This verb means to look carefully for someone or something. It can also mean examining a place. As a noun, it names the act of looking.
A child may look under the bed for a missing shoe. A librarian can help someone find a book. Careful looking may take time.
The phrase “look for” is used when something is missing. “Look” can be quicker or less careful. A computer can find words or information.

examples.en: Her secondary school is across the river.
examples.zh: 她的中學在河的另一邊。

examples.en: When mixing paints, secondary colors include green, orange, and purple.
examples.zh: 混合顏料時，綠色、橘色和紫色屬於二次色。

examples.en: The color of the bag was a secondary concern.
examples.zh: 袋子的顏色是次要考量。

explains: This adjective means coming after the first or being less important. It can also name a school level for older children. It often contrasts with “primary.”
A student may move to a school for older children after several years. In a plan, one goal may matter less than the main goal. Both uses suggest second place.
It may mean second in order or not the main thing. It does not mean unimportant in every case. Nearby words help show the meaning.

examples.en: Can you keep a secret between the two of us?
examples.zh: 你能保守我們兩人之間的秘密嗎？

examples.en: The chef refuses to reveal the secret ingredient behind the award-winning sauce.
examples.zh: 主廚拒絕透露這款獲獎特調醬汁背後的獨門秘密食材。

examples.en: Government intelligence archives keep top-secret files protected under high security.
examples.zh: 政府情報檔案庫在高度嚴密戒備下保管著絕密機密文件。

explains: This noun means information kept from other people. As an adjective, it describes something not meant to be known by everyone. It can also mean a special way to do something.
A child may plan a birthday party and keep it quiet. A hidden code can help friends send a message. Trust matters when sharing personal information.
A surprise is often hidden only for a short time. Some information should stay private for safety. The adjective can describe a hidden place or plan.

examples.en: Please read the first section before class.
examples.zh: 請在上課前閱讀第一個部分。

examples.en: The sports section is in the back of the newspaper.
examples.zh: 體育版在報紙後面。

examples.en: This section of the road is closed today.
examples.zh: 這段道路今天封閉。

explains: This noun means one part of a larger thing. A book, store, or road may be divided into parts. It can also name a group within an organization.
A reader may turn to the sports pages of a newspaper. A store keeps toys in one area and food in another. Dividing things makes them easier to find.
A chapter is one part of a book, while a larger part may be shorter or longer. This word helps show how something is organized. It can also mean a piece cut from a whole.

examples.en: They seek a safe place to rest.
examples.zh: 他們尋找安全的地方休息。

examples.en: Many students seek help with hard math problems.
examples.zh: 許多學生尋求協助解決困難的數學題。

examples.en: She sought her lost keys in the garden.
examples.zh: 她在花園裡找尋遺失的鑰匙。

explains: This verb means to look for or try to get something. It often appears in careful or formal writing. People may look for help, advice, or a solution.
A lost hiker may look for a safe path. A student may ask a teacher for help. The person is trying to find something needed.
It is more formal than “look for.” It can also mean trying to achieve a goal. Its past form changes completely.
