examples.en: Automated climate-controlled greenhouses regulate temperature, shade curtains, and humidity seamlessly.
examples.zh: 配備智慧感測器的科技溫室，能全自動調節內外遮陰網、通風風扇與微霧降溫系統。

examples.en: The massive release of greenhouse gases from fossil fuel combustion drives global atmospheric warming.
examples.zh: 化石燃料燃燒大量釋放到大氣中的溫室氣體，是加劇全球氣候暖化與極端氣候的核心主因。

examples.en: Fragile Phalaenopsis orchids are cultivated inside sterile, temperature-regulated commercial greenhouses.
examples.zh: 嬌貴嬌艷的蝴蝶蘭植株，被悉心安置在具備無菌微氣候調節與自動恆溫控制的商業生產溫室中細心培育。

entries.definition: 溫室；花房；溫室效應；智慧溫室；溫室大棚；智慧環控防蟲科技溫室
explains: A glass or plastic building lets sunlight in and helps plants grow in a warm place. Gardeners can control the heat and water inside. It is useful in cold weather.
People grow vegetables and flowers there. The clear walls trap warmth from the sun. Vents can let hot air escape.
A plant shelter is designed for growing plants, while a house is made for people to live in. It can extend the growing season. Gardeners still need to water and care for each plant.

examples.en: He gave a wide grin when he saw the puppy.
examples.zh: 看到小狗時，他露出了燦爛的笑容。

examples.en: She grinned at her friend across the classroom.
examples.zh: 她隔著教室對朋友咧嘴一笑。

examples.en: The boy could not hide his grin after winning the race.
examples.zh: 男孩贏得賽跑後，藏不住臉上的笑容。

explains: A broad smile showing happiness or amusement can be called this. A child may make one after telling a funny joke. Friends can tell the joke was enjoyed.
As a verb, it means to smile widely. Someone might do so when opening a birthday gift. The smile can show pleasure or excitement.
A small smile may be quiet, while this expression is usually wide and easy to notice. A person can also smile nervously. The face and situation give clues about the feeling.

examples.en: Mom stopped at the grocery store for apples and rice.
examples.zh: 媽媽到雜貨店買蘋果和米。

examples.en: We put the grocery bags on the kitchen table.
examples.zh: 我們把食品袋放在廚房桌上。

examples.en: The grocery near our home closes at nine.
examples.zh: 我們家附近的食品雜貨店九點關門。

explains: A shop that sells food and household items is often called this. People go there to buy fruit, bread, and milk. A shopping list helps them remember what they need.
The word can also describe food items bought for home. A family may carry bags from the store into the kitchen. Some people shop once a week.
A bakery sells mostly baked goods, while this kind of store offers many types of food. Some locations are small and some are large. Prices and choices can vary.

examples.en: Ships navigate through dense ocean fog guided safely by the invisible electronic guidance of orbital satellites.
examples.zh: 遠洋貨輪在濃密海霧中破浪前行，全程受到來自兩萬公里太空衛星的無聲守護與「精準導引」（Guidance）。

examples.en: High school counselors provide valuable career guidance to help graduating seniors choose college majors.
examples.zh: 高中輔導室資深輔導老師熱心提供豐富的升學選組職涯諮詢導引，協助高三畢業生適性選擇大學科系。

examples.en: Guided by his grandfather's gentle moral guidance, he grew into an honest and compassionate community leader.
examples.zh: 在外祖父耳提面命、溫厚正直的品德教誨指引下，他長大成人後成為一位誠懇踏實且深具同理心的社區領袖。

entries.definition: 來自兩萬公里太空深處無聲守護之星光導引；引導
explains: Help or advice that points someone toward a good choice is called this. A teacher can help a student plan a project. Listening carefully can make the next steps clearer.
A map points out which way to go. A coach can also guide a player during practice. Both kinds of help can build confidence.
An order tells someone exactly what to do, while advice helps a person decide. Asking a trusted adult can be useful when a choice feels difficult. People can learn to make decisions over time.

examples.en: Please put your gum in the trash when you are done.
examples.zh: 嚼完口香糖後，請把它丟進垃圾桶。

examples.en: The dentist checked my gums during the visit.
examples.zh: 看診時，牙醫檢查了我的牙齦。

examples.en: A piece of gum stuck to the bottom of his shoe.
examples.zh: 一塊口香糖黏在他的鞋底。

explains: A chewy candy can be called this. People chew it for flavor, but should throw it away when finished. It can stick to shoes or furniture.
This short noun can also name the soft tissue around the teeth. Brushing gently helps keep it healthy. A dentist can answer questions about mouth care.
Candy is something people eat, while the tissue around teeth is part of the mouth. Context tells us which meaning fits. Both can be discussed in a dental office.

examples.en: The hairdresser trimmed my bangs before picture day.
examples.zh: 拍照日之前，髮型師幫我修剪了瀏海。

examples.en: Her hairdresser suggested a shorter style for summer.
examples.zh: 她的髮型師建議她夏天剪短一點。

examples.en: The hairdresser cleaned the comb after each customer.
examples.zh: 髮型師每服務一位客人後都會清潔梳子。

explains: A person who cuts and styles people's hair for work has this job. Customers may visit a salon for a trim. They can explain the style they want.
This worker may wash, color, or arrange hair. Clean tools help keep each visit safe. People can ask questions before choosing a style.
A barber often cuts hair too, while this title is commonly used for someone working in a salon. Job duties can overlap. Training helps workers learn their craft.

examples.en: Do not leave shoes and personal clutter in the shared public hallway.
examples.zh: 請勿將鞋子與私人雜物堆放在公共走廊上。

examples.en: Students gathered in the school hallway chatting excitedly between periods.
examples.zh: 學生們在下課時間齊聚在學校走廊上熱烈聊天。

examples.en: The motion-sensor lights illuminate the hotel hallway as you walk past.
examples.zh: 當你走過時，感應式吸頂燈會自動照亮飯店長廊。

explains: A long passage inside a building connects rooms. People walk through it to reach a classroom or bedroom. Doors often open along its sides.
Schools may have lockers along this space. Students should walk calmly and keep it clear. Running there can cause accidents.
A room is used for an activity, while this narrow space helps people move between rooms. Some homes have pictures on its walls. Good lighting makes it safer.

examples.en: The computer-controlled hydraulic hammer delivers thousands of tons of impact force to drive underwater piles.
examples.zh: 電腦精密控制的水下液壓打樁錘，輸出數千噸衝擊力將基樁打入堅硬岩層。

examples.en: Soft-start procedures ramp up hammer power gradually to allow nearby marine life to swim away safely.
examples.zh: 打樁作業嚴格實施軟啟動程序，逐步緩慢調升衝擊錘敲擊力道，好讓周遭海洋生物有充裕時間游離遠避。

examples.en: The heavy hydraulic hammer was lowered from the crane vessel boom down to the ocean floor.
examples.zh: 重達數百噸的水下液壓大打樁錘，由起重船的主吊臂緩緩垂直下放吊至海床表面就位。

examples.en: Two tiny, black-polished steel hammers strike the ringing gongs with rapid, precise mechanical force.
examples.zh: 兩枚經過黑色鏡面拋光的「微型精鋼音錘」（Hammers），以精準力道快速敲擊音簧演奏時間。

examples.en: The carpenter used a claw hammer to drive sturdy galvanized nails into the wooden roof joists.
examples.zh: 木工師傅熟練地揮動手中的羊角鐵鎚，將一顆顆堅固耐用的防鏽熱浸鍍鋅鋼釘釘入木造屋頂大梁。

examples.en: The auctioneer brought down his wooden hammer, declaring the rare impressionist painting sold for millions.
examples.zh: 拍賣官在一片屏息肅穆中重重敲下手中的木質拍賣槌，莊嚴宣布這幅法國印象派稀世名畫以數億天價落槌成交。

entries.definition: 氣泡幕減噪水下高衝擊液壓打樁錘；鏡面拋光微型精鋼音錘 (每秒敲擊音簧)；鐵錘
explains: A hand tool with a heavy head is used to drive nails into wood. The handle gives the user a firm grip. Wear safety glasses when doing this work.
A person can also use the tool to pull out certain nails. The claw at the back helps with that job. An adult should supervise children using tools.
A screwdriver turns screws, while this tool is mainly used for nails. Choose the right size for the job. Store it safely after use.

examples.en: She picked a handful of daisies for her mother.
examples.zh: 她摘了一把雛菊送給媽媽。

examples.en: Only a handful of students stayed after class.
examples.zh: 只有少數幾位學生留在課後。

examples.en: He added a handful of nuts to the salad.
examples.zh: 他在沙拉裡加了一把堅果。

explains: An amount that can fit in one hand is called this. A child might pick up a small amount of berries. The size depends on the person's hand.
The word can mean a small number of things. A teacher may have a small number of students helping with a project. The group is easy to count.
A full bowl can hold much more than this small amount. Someone may grab a little snack. The context shows whether it means a quantity or a few people.

examples.en: He carried a clean handkerchief in his jacket pocket.
examples.zh: 他在外套口袋裡放了一條乾淨的手帕。

examples.en: Grandma waved her handkerchief as the train left.
examples.zh: 火車開走時，奶奶揮了揮手帕。

examples.en: I used a handkerchief to wipe the water from my face.
examples.zh: 我用手帕擦掉臉上的水。

explains: A small square of cloth can be carried in a pocket and used to wipe the nose or face. It can be washed and used again. Some people prefer paper tissues.
People sometimes wave one to say goodbye. It may be made of cotton or another soft material. A clean one is ready for use.
A towel is larger and used for drying after a bath, while this cloth is small enough to carry. Keeping it clean is important. Do not share one when someone is sick.

examples.en: A pocket map is handy when we visit a new town.
examples.zh: 到新城鎮遊覽時，口袋地圖很方便。

examples.en: My aunt is handy with tools and repaired the chair.
examples.zh: 我阿姨很會用工具，修好了椅子。

examples.en: Keep a pen handy to write down the address.
examples.zh: 把筆放在手邊，方便記下地址。

explains: Something easy to use or helpful nearby can be described this way. A small flashlight is useful during a power cut. Keeping it in a drawer makes it easy to find.
A person who is good at fixing things may be described with this adjective. They can repair a loose shelf or mend a toy. Care and practice build that ability.
Convenient describes something that saves effort, while skilled describes a person's ability. This word can refer to either usefulness or practical skill. The sentence shows which meaning applies.

examples.en: She put her wet jacket on a hanger to dry.
examples.zh: 她把濕外套掛在衣架上晾乾。

examples.en: The closet was full of empty hangers.
examples.zh: 衣櫥裡滿是空衣架。

examples.en: He chose a wooden hanger for his best shirt.
examples.zh: 他為最好的襯衫挑了一個木衣架。

explains: A shaped frame with a hook is used to hang clothes in a closet. It helps keep shirts from becoming wrinkled. Some are made of wood, wire, or plastic.
A hook or support can hold other things too. A hooked frame keeps a jacket off the floor. Put it away after taking clothes off.
A shelf supports items from below, while this object usually holds clothes from above. A hook lets it hang from a rail. Choose a strong one for a heavy coat.

examples.en: The fishing boats returned to the harbor before sunset.
examples.zh: 漁船在日落前返回港口。

examples.en: We watched the sailboats leave the harbor.
examples.zh: 我們看著帆船駛離港口。

examples.en: The harbor was calm after the storm passed.
examples.zh: 暴風雨過後，港灣恢復了平靜。

explains: A sheltered area of water where boats can stay safely is called this. A breakwater may protect it from strong waves. Fishing boats often return there at night.
A town beside this place may have docks, shops, and homes. Travelers can watch boats come and go. The water is usually calmer than the open sea.
An open coast is exposed to waves, while this sheltered place gives ships protection. A port may include buildings and services for trade. Both can be busy with boats.

examples.en: The helmet protected his head from harm.
examples.zh: 安全帽保護他的頭部免於受傷。

examples.en: Careless words can harm a friendship.
examples.zh: 不經意的話可能傷害友誼。

examples.en: The storm did little harm to the garden.
examples.zh: 暴風雨沒有對花園造成太大損害。

explains: Damage or injury to a person, animal, or thing is called this. A sharp object can cause a cut. Put it away safely after use.
As a verb, it means to hurt or damage something. Loud sounds may bother pets. Keeping the noise low protects their comfort.
A problem may be annoying without causing real damage. People should take care not to injure others with their words or actions. An apology can help after someone is hurt.

examples.en: Too much screen time can be harmful to your eyes.
examples.zh: 看螢幕太久可能對眼睛有害。

examples.en: The harmful smoke made everyone leave the room.
examples.zh: 有害的煙霧讓大家離開房間。

examples.en: Litter can be harmful to animals in the sea.
examples.zh: 垃圾可能會傷害海洋中的動物。

explains: Something that can hurt a person, animal, or the environment is described this way. Smoke can make breathing difficult. Fresh air is better for the lungs.
Some chemicals can damage plants or animals if used carelessly. Read labels and ask an adult before touching unknown products. Safe storage matters.
Helpful actions make things better, while this adjective warns that damage may result. Too much sun can harm skin. Shade and protective clothing can help.

examples.en: Golden rice fields in Chishang are ready for autumn harvest.
examples.zh: 台東池上金黃燦爛的稻田已迎來秋收割稻的豐收時節。

examples.en: Villagers held a grand festive thanksgiving banquet to celebrate the bumper crop harvest.
examples.zh: 村民們盛大舉辦感恩祭典盛宴，共同熱烈慶祝這一季農作物的豐收滿載。

examples.en: Farmers work long hours during the summer fruit harvest before typhoons hit.
examples.zh: 在颱風警報發布前夕，果農們頂著烈日超時搶收熟成水果以減少農損。

examples.en: The family enjoyed a bumper harvest of sweet, sun-ripened cherry tomatoes this summer.
examples.zh: 全家人在今年盛夏歡喜採收了一大籃在烈日下自然熟透、甜美多汁的有機紅寶石小番茄。

examples.en: Farmers work tirelessly from dawn to dusk during the busy autumn wheat harvest.
examples.zh: 農夫們在金秋忙碌的小麥採收季節從清晨破曉辛勤勞作至日落黃昏。

examples.en: Harvest leafy greens early in the morning while their leaves remain crisp and full of moisture.
examples.zh: 建議在清晨露水未乾時及時採摘綠葉蔬菜，此時葉片水份最為飽滿脆嫩、口感最佳。

examples.en: Bringing in the annual sweet potato harvest fills the entire village with joyful laughter and shared pride.
examples.zh: 揮汗迎來一年一度沉甸甸的無毒甘藷大豐收採收，讓整座村莊的曬穀場飄滿歡聲笑語與欣慰驕傲。

examples.en: Vineyards employ extra seasonal workers during the crisp autumn grape harvest season.
examples.zh: 在金風送爽的秋收葡萄採收採摘旺季期間，各大觀光葡萄酒莊紛紛加聘大量季節性採收人手前來助陣。

examples.en: After decades of relentless academic research, the dedicated botanist began to harvest widespread global acclaim.
examples.zh: 在歷經數十年心無旁騖的嚴謹植物學基礎科學研究後，這位甘於寂寞的植物學家終於開始在國際學術舞台上收穫如潮的盛讚。

entries.definition: 收割；採收；豐收成果；採收採摘；大豐收；收穫；慶賀一年辛勤耕耘的豐碩收穫
explains: The crops gathered from fields at the end of a growing season are called this. Farmers may collect apples, corn, or wheat. The work can take many days.
As a verb, it means to gather crops when they are ready. Farmers use machines or hand tools. Weather can affect the amount they collect.
Planting happens at the start of growing, while gathering the ripe food happens later. A good season may provide plenty to sell or store. Some communities celebrate the work with a festival.

examples.en: He made a hasty drawing before the bell rang.
examples.zh: 鐘聲響起前，他匆匆畫了一張圖。

examples.en: Do not make a hasty choice without reading the rules.
examples.zh: 沒有讀清楚規則前，不要匆忙做決定。

examples.en: Her hasty reply caused a small misunderstanding.
examples.zh: 她匆忙的回答造成了一點誤會。

explains: An action done too quickly, without enough thought, can be described this way. A rushed choice may lead to a mistake. Taking time to check is often wiser.
A person may move quickly because there is little time. They should still watch where they are going. Rushing can cause accidents.
Careful means taking time to think, while this adjective suggests speed and little planning. A quick decision is not always a bad one. The situation determines whether it was wise.

examples.en: The ducklings began to hatch just before sunrise.
examples.zh: 小鴨在日出前開始孵化。

examples.en: A tiny chick hatched from the speckled egg.
examples.zh: 一隻小雞從斑點蛋裡孵了出來。

examples.en: The crew opened the hatch to reach the lower deck.
examples.zh: 船員打開艙口前往下層甲板。

explains: A baby bird comes out of an egg by doing this. The parent may sit on the eggs to keep them warm. Soon the young birds need food and care.
As a noun, it can mean a small door or opening in a floor, roof, or ship. It allows people to reach another space. The context shows which meaning applies.
Eggs must stay warm for a certain time before young animals emerge. Not every egg will do so. People should leave nests alone and observe from a distance.

examples.en: The hateful note upset the children.
examples.zh: 那張充滿惡意的字條讓孩子們很難過。

examples.en: He apologized for making a hateful comment.
examples.zh: 他為自己說出充滿仇恨的話而道歉。

examples.en: They refused to repeat the hateful rumor.
examples.zh: 他們拒絕再散播那個惡意謠言。

explains: A person or action full of strong dislike can be described this way. Mean words may show that feeling. Choosing respectful language helps people get along.
An unpleasant experience may also be described with this adjective. A very bad day of rain might spoil an outdoor event. The word expresses strong negative feelings.
Dislike can be mild, but this word suggests a much stronger feeling. People can disagree without being cruel. Kind behavior makes a safer community.

examples.en: The farmer stacked hay in the barn for winter.
examples.zh: 農夫把乾草堆在穀倉裡留到冬天。

examples.en: The horse ate hay from a wooden feeder.
examples.zh: 馬從木製飼料槽裡吃乾草。

examples.en: A bale of hay fell off the wagon.
examples.zh: 一捆乾草從馬車上掉了下來。

explains: Dried grass is stored as food for farm animals. Farmers cut it and let it dry before stacking it. Horses and cows may eat it.
A large stack can be kept in a barn. Animals need other food and clean water too. The dry plants should be protected from rain.
Fresh grass grows in a field, while this dried material is saved for feeding animals later. Straw comes from the leftover stems of grain plants. The two materials are not always the same.

examples.en: The economic growth report made front-page news headlines today.
examples.zh: 經濟成長報告成為今天各大報紙的頭版頭條新聞。

examples.en: Eye-catching headlines on the web often lure readers into clickbait articles.
examples.zh: 網路上搶眼吸睛的標題經常吸引讀者點擊誘導性文章。

examples.en: The famous rock band will headline the music festival this coming weekend.
examples.zh: 這支知名搖滾樂團將於即將到來的週末擔任音樂節壓軸主唱。

examples.en: The trade agreement made front-page headlines across major global newspapers.
examples.zh: 該項具里程碑意義的經貿協定強勢榮登全球各大主流報章的頭版頭條新聞。

examples.en: Dramatic environmental crises continue to grab headlines worldwide.
examples.zh: 震撼性的環境危機持續佔據全球各大新聞媒體的頭條版面。

examples.en: Editors spend considerable time crafting an accurate and eye-catching headline.
examples.zh: 編輯們花費大量心思與時間來琢磨既準確又吸睛的新聞標題。

entries.definition: 頭條新聞；標題；報紙標題
explains: The title at the top of a news story is called this. It tells readers the main subject. A short title may catch their attention.
A newspaper or website uses large print for important stories. The words summarize what happened. Readers can decide whether to read the full report.
A caption describes a picture, while this title introduces a whole story. Good titles are clear and accurate. They should not trick readers.

examples.en: The company moved its headquarters to a larger building.
examples.zh: 公司把總部搬到一棟更大的建築裡。

examples.en: The rescue team shared updates from its headquarters.
examples.zh: 救援隊從總部分享最新消息。

examples.en: Their headquarters is near the train station.
examples.zh: 他們的總部在火車站附近。

explains: The main office of an organization is called this. Leaders and workers may make important plans there. A company can have smaller offices in other places.
An army or group may also direct its work from a central building. Maps and reports may be kept there. The people inside help coordinate many activities.
A local branch serves one area, while this central place guides the larger organization. It may be in a large city. The exact location depends on the group.

examples.en: The scrape began to heal after Mom cleaned it.
examples.zh: 媽媽清潔傷口後，擦傷開始癒合。

examples.en: Time helped heal the hurt feelings between the friends.
examples.zh: 時間幫助兩位朋友修復受傷的感情。

examples.en: The cut will heal faster if you keep it clean.
examples.zh: 保持傷口清潔有助於它更快癒合。

explains: To become well again after an injury or illness is to do this. A small scrape may improve after it is cleaned and covered. Rest can help the body recover.
A hurt feeling can also improve with time and care. Talking with a trusted person may help someone feel better. Kindness can make a difficult day easier.
A doctor may treat an injury, while the body does much of the recovery. Recovery takes different amounts of time. Get help from an adult when you are hurt.

examples.en: A heap of leaves covered the garden path.
examples.zh: 一大堆落葉蓋住了花園小徑。

examples.en: The children piled a heap of sand beside the play area.
examples.zh: 孩子們在遊戲區旁堆了一大堆沙。

examples.en: I have a heap of books to return to the library.
examples.zh: 我有一大堆書要還給圖書館。

explains: A large, untidy pile of things can be called this. Leaves may gather in one after a windy day. A rake helps spread them out or collect them.
People may use this noun for a great amount of something. A large amount of homework means many assignments. The word often suggests a messy arrangement.
A neat stack has items placed in order, while this pile may be uneven. A large pile of toys can make a room hard to walk through. Putting things away keeps a clear path.

examples.en: We turned on the heater when the room grew cold.
examples.zh: 房間變冷時，我們打開了暖氣。

examples.en: The water heater made the shower warm.
examples.zh: 熱水器讓淋浴水變暖了。

examples.en: Keep the curtains away from the portable heater.
examples.zh: 窗簾要遠離這台移動式暖爐。

explains: A machine or device that makes a room or water warmer is called this. A home may use one during cold weather. Keep clothes and paper away from it.
A small portable model can warm one room. Adults should follow its safety directions. Turning it off before leaving can prevent accidents.
A fan moves air, while this appliance adds warmth. Some systems heat an entire building. Others warm only a small area.

examples.en: My heel hurt after I wore tight shoes all day.
examples.zh: 我穿了一整天太緊的鞋子後，腳跟很痛。

examples.en: The heel of her boot had a small tear.
examples.zh: 她靴子的後跟有一道小裂痕。

examples.en: He stood on his heels while stretching his toes.
examples.zh: 他踮起腳跟伸展腳趾。

explains: The back part of a foot is called this. It rests on the ground when a person stands. Shoes often have a raised part underneath it.
This word also names the back section of a shoe or sock. A hole there can make footwear uncomfortable. Repairing it may help the shoe last longer.
The toes are at the front of the foot, while this part is at the back. Walking uses both ends. The back of the foot can feel sore after wearing shoes that do not fit.

examples.en: The old story described a frightening journey through hell.
examples.zh: 古老故事描寫了一段穿越地獄的可怕旅程。

examples.en: The campers said the stormy night was hell.
examples.zh: 露營者說那個暴風雨之夜糟透了。

examples.en: Different faiths have different ideas about hell.
examples.zh: 不同信仰對地獄有不同的觀念。

explains: In some religions, this word names a place where very bad people may be punished after death. Beliefs about it differ among religions. Stories and traditions describe it in many ways.
People also use it informally to describe a very unpleasant experience. A day with many problems may feel terrible. This casual use can sound strong or rude.
A religious idea and an everyday expression are not the same use. Reading the surrounding sentence helps identify the meaning. Choose gentler words in polite conversation.

examples.en: Always strap your safety helmet securely before riding.
examples.zh: 騎車前請務必將安全帽確實扣緊。

examples.en: Construction workers must wear hard helmets on the building site.
examples.zh: 工地工人必須在建築工地上佩戴安全帽。

examples.en: The bicycle helmet protected his head during the fall.
examples.zh: 自行車安全帽在他摔倒時保護了他的頭部。

explains: A hard protective covering worn on the head is called this. People use one when riding a bicycle or playing some sports. It can help protect against injury.
Different activities need different designs. A construction worker's version is not the same as a bicycle rider's. It should fit properly and be fastened.
A hat may keep the sun off, but this gear is made to protect the head. Replace it if it has been badly damaged. Follow safety rules every time.

examples.en: Do not hesitate to ask the teacher for help.
examples.zh: 需要幫忙時，別猶豫，儘管去問老師。

examples.en: She hesitated before stepping onto the wobbly bridge.
examples.zh: 她踏上搖晃的橋前猶豫了一下。

examples.en: He hesitated because he was not sure which answer was correct.
examples.zh: 他不確定哪個答案正確，所以遲疑了。

explains: To pause before doing or saying something because you are unsure is to do this. A student may wait before answering a hard question. Taking a moment can help the student think.
Someone may feel uncertain about joining a new activity. Asking a question can make the choice clearer. A friend can offer support without pressure.
Acting right away is different from stopping to consider what to do. A short pause can be wise. Too much delay may cause someone to miss an opportunity.

examples.en: The map gave us a hint about where the treasure was buried.
examples.zh: 地圖給了我們一個提示，指出寶藏埋藏的位置。

examples.en: She hinted that a surprise was waiting at home.
examples.zh: 她暗示家裡有個驚喜正等著我們。

examples.en: Can you give me a hint for this riddle?
examples.zh: 你可以給我一點解這個謎語的提示嗎？

explains: A small clue that helps someone solve a problem is called this. A detective may notice a muddy footprint. It can point toward an answer.
The word can also mean a small suggestion. A teacher might offer one when a student feels stuck. The student still works out the solution.
A full answer gives everything away, while a clue leaves some thinking to do. A game may give players a small clue. It helps without solving the whole puzzle.

examples.en: The startup decided to hire three full-stack developers.
examples.zh: 這家新創公司決定聘請三位全端工程師。

examples.en: Tourists can hire bicycles near the lake shore for a scenic cycling ride.
examples.zh: 造訪湖畔的觀光遊客可以在環湖步道起點租賃自行車，享受沿途愜意的湖光山色。

examples.en: Our newest hire in the accounting department demonstrated exceptional financial modeling skills.
examples.zh: 會計財務部剛報到的新員工展現了令人驚豔的高水準財務建模與數據分析實力。

explains: To pay someone to do a job is to do this. A shop may bring in extra workers before a busy holiday. The worker agrees to do the tasks for pay.
A person can also rent something for a period of time. A family might pay to use a bicycle while on vacation. Context shows whether a worker or an item is involved.
Buy means to own something, while this action may only provide its use for a while. An employer chooses a worker for a role. Both sides should understand the agreement.

examples.en: The historian found an old diary in the town archive.
examples.zh: 歷史學家在鎮上的檔案室找到一本舊日記。

examples.en: A historian visited our class to talk about ancient trade.
examples.zh: 一位歷史學家到我們班上談古代貿易。

examples.en: The historian compared two letters from the same year.
examples.zh: 歷史學家比較了同一年寫的兩封信。

explains: A person who studies and writes about events from the past is called this. They use letters, records, and objects as evidence. Careful research helps them tell accurate stories.
This scholar may compare different accounts of the same event. One source may leave out important details. Checking several sources can reveal more.
An archaeologist studies objects from earlier times, while this researcher often studies written records too. The jobs can overlap. Both help people learn about the past.

examples.en: Our class visited a historic fort by the river.
examples.zh: 我們班參觀了河邊一座具有歷史意義的堡壘。

examples.en: The team made a historic record at the games.
examples.zh: 這支隊伍在比賽中創下了歷史紀錄。

examples.en: They restored the historic theater downtown.
examples.zh: 他們修復了市中心那座具有歷史意義的劇院。

explains: An important event or place from the past can be described this way. A building where a major agreement was signed may be preserved. Visitors can learn what happened there.
The adjective can describe something that makes history because it is significant. A first flight across an ocean was an important achievement. People may remember it for many years.
Historical often means related to the past in general, while this word stresses importance. An old shoe is not always special. A famous place may be both old and important.

examples.en: The phone holder kept the screen steady on the desk.
examples.zh: 手機架讓桌上的螢幕保持穩定。

examples.en: Each ticket holder received a small program.
examples.zh: 每位持票者都拿到一本小節目冊。

examples.en: Please use the cup holder during the ride.
examples.zh: 乘車時請使用杯架。

explains: A person or object that keeps something in place may be described this way. A cup stand keeps a drink upright in a car. It helps prevent spills.
A person may own a card or carry a ticket for an event. The noun can refer to a person or a support for an object. The surrounding sentence makes the meaning clear.
A container stores things inside, while a support may simply keep an item steady. A towel rack keeps a towel easy to reach. The object being supported gives a clue to the meaning.

examples.en: The rabbit hid in a hollow tree trunk.
examples.zh: 兔子躲在中空的樹幹裡。

examples.en: The metal pipe is hollow inside.
examples.zh: 這根金屬管內部是空心的。

examples.en: We heard a hollow sound when he tapped the box.
examples.zh: 他敲盒子時，我們聽見空洞的聲音。

explains: An object that is empty inside can be described this way. A tube has an open space through its center. A heavy solid block has no such space.
A tree trunk may become empty inside as it grows old. Small animals might make a home there. The outside can still look strong.

Solid means filled throughout, while this adjective describes a space inside. An empty-sounding note may seem echoing because it comes from an empty space. The sentence determines whether it describes shape or sound.

examples.en: Pilgrims traveled to the holy site to pray.
examples.zh: 朝聖者前往聖地祈禱。

examples.en: The book tells a story about a holy teacher.
examples.zh: 這本書講述一位聖者的故事。

examples.en: They removed their shoes before entering the holy place.
examples.zh: 進入聖地前，他們脫下鞋子。

explains: A person, place, or object treated as sacred in a religion can be described this way. Different faiths have their own important places. Visitors should show respect there.
People may use this adjective when speaking about a special religious idea or figure. Customs vary among communities. Learning about them helps people be considerate.
Ordinary describes everyday things, while this word points to religious importance. A building can be special because people gather there to pray. The meaning depends on a community's beliefs.

examples.en: The camper felt homesick on her first night away.
examples.zh: 露營者離家的第一晚感到想家。

examples.en: A photo of his family helped him when he felt homesick.
examples.zh: 他想家時，看著家人的照片讓他好過一些。

examples.en: After a week abroad, I began to feel homesick.
examples.zh: 在國外待了一週後，我開始想家。

explains: A person who misses home while away can be described this way. A child at a new camp may miss family and familiar rooms. Calling home can bring comfort.
Being in a new country or school can feel lonely at first. Familiar music or a favorite photo may help. Making a new friend can also ease the feeling.
Excitement about travel can happen at the same time as missing home. Both feelings are normal. People can talk with someone they trust about them.

examples.en: She returned to her hometown for the summer festival.
examples.zh: 她回到家鄉參加夏日慶典。

examples.en: My hometown has a small library beside the river.
examples.zh: 我的家鄉有一間河邊的小圖書館。

examples.en: He misses the friends he made in his hometown.
examples.zh: 他想念在家鄉結交的朋友。

explains: The town or city where a person grew up is called this. They may have gone to school there. Old friends and familiar streets can bring back memories.
Someone can still feel attached to this place after moving away. A visit may include seeing family or walking past a childhood home. People sometimes return for holidays.
A current home may be in a different place from where someone was raised. The first place can still feel special. Asking where someone grew up may invite a story.

examples.en: The teacher thanked Eli for his honesty about the broken ruler.
examples.zh: 老師感謝伊萊誠實說明尺子是他弄壞的。

examples.en: Honesty helps friends trust one another.
examples.zh: 誠實有助於朋友彼此信任。

examples.en: She showed honesty by returning the extra change.
examples.zh: 她把多找的錢還回去，展現了誠實。

explains: Telling the truth and not trying to deceive others is called this quality. People trust someone who speaks honestly. Admitting a mistake can be difficult but helpful.
This quality also means being fair and sincere in one's actions. Returning a lost wallet shows good character. Others may feel safe asking for help.
A lie hides what is true, while this virtue lets people know what really happened. Everyone can make mistakes. Speaking truthfully helps people solve problems.

examples.en: The town held a ceremony to honor the firefighters.
examples.zh: 鎮上舉辦典禮向消防員致敬。

examples.en: She felt honored to receive the art prize.
examples.zh: 她很榮幸獲得藝術獎。

examples.en: We honor our promise by helping on Saturday.
examples.zh: 我們遵守承諾，星期六會去幫忙。

explains: Respect and admiration for someone's actions can be called this. A community may give an award to a brave helper. The award shows appreciation.
As a verb, it can mean to keep a promise or show respect. People can keep a promise by doing what they said. The action matters more than words.
Praise may be spoken, while this can also involve a lasting sign of respect. A school might name a room after a kind teacher. Families may remember people in their own ways.

examples.en: We are hopeful that the rain will stop before the picnic.
examples.zh: 我們希望野餐前雨會停。

examples.en: The young player felt hopeful after practicing every day.
examples.zh: 每天練習後，這位年輕選手感到充滿希望。

examples.en: Her hopeful smile encouraged the whole team.
examples.zh: 她充滿希望的笑容鼓舞了整個隊伍。

explains: A person who believes something good may happen can be described this way. A student may expect to do well after studying. Positive thoughts can give courage.
The adjective can also describe a situation that seems likely to improve. Dark clouds may clear by afternoon. Looking at the weather report gives more information.
Hopeless means seeing no chance of improvement, while this word suggests a good possibility. Hope does not guarantee success. It can help someone keep trying.

examples.en: The goat scratched its horn against the fence.
examples.zh: 山羊用角磨了磨圍欄。

examples.en: She played a bright note on the French horn.
examples.zh: 她用法國號吹出明亮的音符。

examples.en: The driver sounded the horn to warn the cyclist.
examples.zh: 駕駛人按喇叭提醒騎腳踏車的人。

explains: A hard pointed part grows on the head of some animals, such as a goat. It can help protect the animal. Some animals have two of them.
A brass instrument with a curled tube can also be called this. A musician blows into it to make sound. It is used in bands and orchestras.
A vehicle uses a loud warning sound to alert people nearby. Drivers press a button to make that sound. It should be used only when needed.

examples.en: The horrible smell came from the old lunch box.
examples.zh: 難聞的氣味是從舊便當盒傳出來的。

examples.en: We had horrible weather during the boat trip.
examples.zh: 我們搭船旅行時遇上很糟的天氣。

examples.en: The child felt horrible after losing his favorite toy.
examples.zh: 弄丟最喜歡的玩具後，孩子心情很差。

explains: Something extremely unpleasant or frightening can be described this way. A terrible smell may come from spoiled food. Throw it away safely.
A person may use this adjective to describe a very bad experience. Losing a favorite toy can feel upsetting. Someone kind may help them feel better.
Bad can describe many things, but this word is stronger. A scary movie may upset young viewers. Choose entertainment that feels comfortable.

examples.en: The children watched a gentle story instead of a horror movie.
examples.zh: 孩子們沒有看恐怖片，而是看了一個溫馨的故事。

examples.en: She stared at the broken vase in horror.
examples.zh: 她驚恐地盯著摔破的花瓶。

examples.en: The book tells a horror story about a haunted house.
examples.zh: 這本書講述一個鬼屋恐怖故事。

explains: A strong feeling of fear and shock is called this. Someone may feel it after seeing a serious accident. They should get help from a trusted adult.
Stories and movies made to frighten people belong to this kind of entertainment. They often include danger or mysterious events. Some are too scary for young children.
Fear can be mild, while this feeling is intense. A person may also feel shock when something very bad happens. Calm support can help them recover.

examples.en: The nurse checked the patient hourly during the night.
examples.zh: 護士在夜間每小時檢查病人一次。

examples.en: She earns an hourly wage at the bookshop.
examples.zh: 她在書店領取時薪。

examples.en: The hourly bus service stops after midnight.
examples.zh: 每小時一班的公車在午夜後停止行駛。

explains: Something that happens every hour can be described this way. A clock may chime once each hour. The repeated sound helps mark time.
A worker can be paid for each hour of work. The amount is called a pay rate for each hour worked. The total depends on how long the person works.
Daily means once each day or related to a day, while this word focuses on one hour at a time. A bus may arrive every hour. Check the schedule for exact times.

examples.en: The housekeeper changed the sheets in the guest room.
examples.zh: 客房清潔人員更換了客房裡的床單。

examples.en: Our housekeeper helped keep the kitchen tidy.
examples.zh: 我們家的管家幫忙保持廚房整潔。

examples.en: The hotel housekeeper brought fresh towels.
examples.zh: 飯店客房清潔人員送來乾淨的毛巾。

explains: A person whose job is to clean and care for a home or hotel room is called this. They may make beds and tidy rooms. Their work helps keep spaces comfortable.
Some homes employ a worker to help with daily chores. The family and worker should agree clearly on the tasks. Respectful treatment matters.
A hotel cleaner may care for guest rooms, while a private household worker may have other duties. The job can differ from place to place. Asking about responsibilities avoids confusion.

examples.en: Grandma gave me a hug when I arrived.
examples.zh: 我抵達時，奶奶抱了抱我。

examples.en: The child hugged his teddy bear at bedtime.
examples.zh: 孩子睡前抱著他的泰迪熊。

examples.en: She asked her friend before giving her a hug.
examples.zh: 她先詢問朋友，才抱了抱她。

explains: To put your arms around someone in a friendly way is to do this. It can show love, comfort, or welcome. Ask first if the other person is comfortable.
People also hold an object close to themselves. A child may hold a stuffed toy while resting. The verb can describe either kind of action.
A handshake uses hands only, while this gesture brings people close together. Some people prefer not to be touched. Respect their choice.

examples.en: She hummed a tune while watering the plants.
examples.zh: 她一邊替植物澆水，一邊哼著曲子。

examples.en: The old fan began to hum softly.
examples.zh: 舊電扇開始發出輕微的嗡嗡聲。

examples.en: He hummed along with the song on the radio.
examples.zh: 他跟著收音機裡的歌曲哼唱。

explains: To make a low, steady sound with a closed mouth is to do this. A person may do it while working. The tune can be hard for others to hear.
A machine can also make a soft buzzing noise. A refrigerator may make one as it runs. The sound can help someone notice that it is working.
Singing uses clear words or open notes, while this action often keeps the lips closed. A bee makes a similar low sound with its wings. The source may be a person or a machine.

examples.en: It felt humid after the summer rain.
examples.zh: 夏雨過後，空氣感覺很潮濕。

examples.en: The humid air made my hair curl.
examples.zh: 潮濕的空氣讓我的頭髮捲了起來。

examples.en: We turned on a fan during the humid afternoon.
examples.zh: 潮濕的午後，我們打開了電風扇。

explains: Air that contains a lot of water vapor can be described this way. On such a day, people may feel sticky. Drinking water and resting in the shade can help.
Tropical places often have this kind of weather. Clothes may take longer to dry outside. A weather report can tell how damp the air is.
Dry air has little moisture, while this adjective describes air with much more. Rain can make the air damp. A fan may make a room feel more comfortable.

examples.en: Her gentle humor made the class smile.
examples.zh: 她溫和的幽默感讓全班露出笑容。

examples.en: The book is full of silly humor for young readers.
examples.zh: 這本書充滿適合年輕讀者的滑稽幽默。

examples.en: He used humor to help his nervous friend relax.
examples.zh: 他用幽默讓緊張的朋友放鬆下來。

explains: The ability to notice or create things that make people laugh is called this. A funny story can cheer up a group. Laughter should not come from hurting someone.
People may use this word for a playful way of seeing a situation. A person can make a gentle joke about a small mistake. Kindness makes the joke safe.
A joke is one short funny idea, while this noun can mean the broader quality of being funny. Different people enjoy different kinds of jokes. It is good to stop if someone feels hurt.

examples.en: The humorous cartoon made us laugh at lunch.
examples.zh: 那幅滑稽漫畫讓我們午餐時笑了出來。

examples.en: Grandpa told a humorous story about his dog.
examples.zh: 爺爺講了一個關於他家狗狗的有趣故事。

examples.en: The humorous play had a silly ending.
examples.zh: 那齣滑稽戲以一個可笑的結局收尾。

explains: Something that makes people laugh can be described this way. A playful story may have an unexpected ending. The reader may smile at the surprise.
A person can tell a joke in a lively way. The listener should enjoy it too. Good humor does not make fun of someone unfairly.
Funny is a common word for causing laughter, while this adjective is a little more formal. A comic drawing can be amusing. The main goal is to bring harmless fun.

examples.en: The hikers felt hunger after walking all morning.
examples.zh: 健行者走了一整個早上後感到飢餓。

examples.en: Her hunger for adventure led her to explore new trails.
examples.zh: 她對冒險的渴望帶領她探索新的步道。

examples.en: A warm bowl of soup eased his hunger.
examples.zh: 一碗熱湯減輕了他的飢餓感。

explains: The body's need for food is called this. A person may feel it after running or waiting a long time to eat. A healthy meal can satisfy it.
A strong desire for something can also be described with this noun. Someone may have a strong desire to learn new things. This meaning is not about food.
Thirst is the need for water, while this feeling is the need for food. People notice it differently. Eating regular meals can help them feel well.

examples.en: The guide rested in a small hut near the trail.
examples.zh: 嚮導在步道旁的小屋休息。

examples.en: A thatched hut stood beside the tropical beach.
examples.zh: 熱帶海灘旁有一間茅草小屋。

examples.en: The hikers found an empty hut before the rain began.
examples.zh: 雨開始下之前，健行者找到了一間空的小屋。

explains: A small, simple shelter is called this. It may be built from wood, leaves, or other local materials. A person can stay inside to rest.
Some people use one as a cabin near a beach or in the mountains. It usually has fewer rooms than a house. Its design depends on the place.
A large home has many rooms, while this shelter is usually small. It can protect people from rain and sun. Strong materials help it stand safely.

examples.en: The icy sidewalk was hard to cross safely.
examples.zh: 結冰的人行道很難安全通過。

examples.en: An icy wind blew across the field.
examples.zh: 一陣刺骨的冷風吹過田野。

examples.en: She put on gloves before touching the icy gate.
examples.zh: 她戴上手套才去碰冰冷的門。

explains: A surface covered with ice can be described this way. A road may become slippery after freezing rain. Walk carefully and watch your step.
Very cold weather can also be described with this adjective. A freezing wind may make people shiver. Warm clothing helps keep them comfortable.
Cool weather is mild, while this word suggests ice or very low temperatures. Water can freeze when the temperature drops. Check conditions before going outside.

examples.en: Great fiction novelists use vivid imagination to craft entire fantasy universes.
examples.zh: 偉大的虛構小說家運用豐沛生動的想像力構建出瑰麗的奇幻世界。

examples.en: Playing pretend games stimulates a toddler's cognitive growth and active imagination.
examples.zh: 角色扮演假想扮家家酒遊戲能有效刺激幼童的大腦認知發育並豐富其想像力。

examples.en: The visual special effects in the movie were beyond anything our imagination could conceive.
examples.zh: 這部科幻史詩鉅作中所呈現的震撼視覺特效，徹底超越了人類過往的一切想像極限。

examples.en: Artists sketch glowing neon sculptures in thin air, bounded only by the limits of their imagination.
examples.zh: 藝術家在虛擬空氣中揮毫繪製發光的立體雕塑，唯一的極限就是人類無拘無束的「想像力」（Imagination）。

examples.en: Children possess vivid imagination, turning cardboard shipping boxes into fantastical space rockets.
examples.zh: 孩童擁有無窮無盡的生動想像力，能將尋常的瓦楞紙箱幻化為奔向星際的奇幻太空火箭。

examples.en: Solving complex environmental challenges requires bold scientific imagination paired with disciplined execution.
examples.zh: 克服複雜棘手的全球環境變遷挑戰，既需要大膽的科學想像力，也離不開務實嚴謹的執行力。

entries.definition: 想像力；幻想力；在三維空間中自由揮灑之無窮建築設計想像力
explains: The ability to picture things in the mind is called this. A child can imagine a castle on the moon. Drawing can help show the idea.
Writers use this ability to create characters and events. The story may include things that do not exist in real life. Readers picture the scenes as they read.
Memory recalls things that happened, while this power can create new ideas. Pretend games let children practice it. It can help with art, writing, and problem solving.

examples.en: The nurse gave immediate help to the injured child.
examples.zh: 護士立即協助受傷的孩子。

examples.en: Please send an immediate reply if you can come.
examples.zh: 如果你能來，請立刻回覆。

examples.en: Our immediate neighbors brought us fresh oranges.
examples.zh: 我們的隔壁鄰居送來新鮮柳橙。

explains: Something that happens now, without waiting, can be described this way. A reply with no delay comes right away. The speaker does not wait until later.
A nearby family member is in a direct relationship to you, not many steps away. The word can describe close connection too. The meaning depends on the noun it describes.
Soon means after a short time, while this adjective stresses no delay. A teacher may need an answer at once. Pay attention to the situation.

examples.en: The country imports raw energy materials like crude oil and gas.
examples.zh: 該國進口原油與天然氣等能源原料。

examples.en: Imported Japanese matcha powder is used in their specialty pastry creations.
examples.zh: 他們的特色甜點創作特別嚴選自日本原裝進口的頂級抹茶粉。

examples.en: Rising customs tariffs may increase the retail price of imported cars.
examples.zh: 調高關稅稅率可能會進一步推升進口進口車輛的終端零售價格。

explains: To bring goods into a country from another country is to do this. Stores may sell fruit grown far away. The goods travel across borders.
A computer user can bring information from one file or program into another. A button may load a list of names. The action adds the material to the new place.
Exporting sends goods outward, while this verb describes bringing them inward. Countries trade many products. A label may tell where an item was made.

examples.en: Her piano solo impressed the audience.
examples.zh: 她的鋼琴獨奏讓觀眾印象深刻。

examples.en: The clean model impressed the science judges.
examples.zh: 那個整潔的模型讓科學評審留下深刻印象。

examples.en: He hoped to impress his coach by arriving early.
examples.zh: 他希望藉由提早到場讓教練留下好印象。

explains: To make someone admire or remember something is to do this. A student may amaze the class with a careful science project. Hard work can lead to a strong result.
A person may try to show a skill in order to gain approval. Being kind and prepared can leave a good feeling. Bragging is not necessary.
To earn someone’s admiration is not the same as forcing them to agree. A beautiful performance may make a lasting mark. People can admire effort as well as talent.

examples.en: The school has an indoor pool for winter lessons.
examples.zh: 學校有一座室內游泳池，供冬季課程使用。

examples.en: We planned an indoor game in case it rained.
examples.zh: 我們安排了室內遊戲，以防下雨。

examples.en: The indoor plants need water every few days.
examples.zh: 這些室內植物每隔幾天需要澆水。

explains: An activity or object meant for use inside a building can be described this way. A table game is often played inside. Rain will not bother the players.
A plant kept inside may need enough light and water. Some kinds grow well near a window. Check what each plant needs.
Outdoor things are used outside, while this adjective points to rooms and buildings. A swimming pool may be either kind. Look at the place where it is built.

examples.en: We stayed indoors during the thunderstorm.
examples.zh: 雷雨期間我們待在室內。

examples.en: The children played indoors until the snow stopped.
examples.zh: 孩子們在室內玩耍，直到雪停了。

examples.en: It was too hot to work outdoors, so we moved indoors.
examples.zh: 天氣太熱，不適合在戶外工作，所以我們移到室內。

explains: Inside a building is described by this adverb. Children stayed in when the rain began. They played board games at home.
People may go inside when the weather is too hot or cold. A library offers a cool place to read. Staying inside can be pleasant for a while.
Outside means in the open air, while this word means within a room or building. A person can exercise in either place. The weather may affect the choice.

examples.en: The industrial building made metal parts for bicycles.
examples.zh: 這座工業建築生產腳踏車的金屬零件。

examples.en: A new industrial park opened outside the city.
examples.zh: 一座新的工業園區在市郊啟用。

examples.en: The museum showed an industrial machine from the past.
examples.zh: 博物館展示了一台昔日的工業機器。

explains: Factories and the making of goods are related to this adjective. A factory district may have large buildings and trucks. It can be far from homes.
A machine used for making products can be described this way. Workers follow safety rules around it. It may be much larger than a home machine.
Agricultural work grows food, while this field often makes goods in factories. Both are important to communities. Some places have both kinds of work.

examples.en: This paper is inferior to the thicker kind for painting.
examples.zh: 這種紙不如較厚的紙適合繪畫。

examples.en: She worried that her work was inferior to her classmates’.
examples.zh: 她擔心自己的作品不如同學的。

examples.en: The old battery was inferior to the new one.
examples.zh: 舊電池的品質不如新電池。

explains: Something of lower quality or rank compared with another thing can be described this way. One toy may break sooner than a stronger one. The comparison tells us which is less good.
A person who feels less capable may believe they are not as good as others. Everyone has different strengths. Encouragement can help people value themselves.
Superior describes a higher level, while this word describes a lower one. It should compare things fairly. It does not mean a person has no worth.

examples.en: Please inform the coach if you will miss practice.
examples.zh: 如果你無法參加練習，請通知教練。

examples.en: The sign informed visitors about the museum hours.
examples.zh: 告示牌告訴遊客博物館的開放時間。

examples.en: Dad informed us that dinner was ready.
examples.zh: 爸爸告訴我們晚餐準備好了。

explains: To tell someone facts or news is to do this. A teacher may tell families about a change in the school schedule. A message shares the details.
A sign can let visitors know where to go. Clear directions help people choose the right path. The information should be easy to understand.
Ask means requesting an answer, while this verb means giving someone useful facts. A weather report tells people about rain. It can help them plan.

examples.en: The guide gave us information about the old castle.
examples.zh: 導覽員提供了關於古堡的資訊。

examples.en: Please write your contact information on the form.
examples.zh: 請在表格上填寫你的聯絡資訊。

examples.en: We found useful information about frogs in the library.
examples.zh: 我們在圖書館找到青蛙的實用資料。

explains: Facts or details about a subject are called this. A library book may tell about whales. Readers can learn new things from it.
A form may ask someone to write a name and address. Those details help another person contact them. Keep private details safe.
An opinion is what someone thinks, while this noun refers to facts or useful details. Maps show useful details about roads. It is important to check that it is correct.

examples.en: The player rested at home after a knee injury.
examples.zh: 膝蓋受傷後，這位選手在家休息。

examples.en: Wearing a helmet can help prevent a head injury.
examples.zh: 戴安全帽有助於預防頭部受傷。

examples.en: The nurse checked the injury on his hand.
examples.zh: 護士檢查了他手上的傷。

explains: Physical damage to the body is called this. A fall may hurt an arm or leg. Rest and care can help, but serious problems need an adult's help.
A sports player may need time away from practice after getting hurt. Following a coach's safety directions can lower the chance of trouble. Warm-ups help prepare the body.
A bruise is one kind of minor damage, while a broken bone is more serious. Different problems need different care. Tell an adult whenever someone gets hurt.

examples.en: We stayed at a quiet inn near the lake.
examples.zh: 我們住在湖邊一間安靜的小旅館。

examples.en: The inn served warm bread at breakfast.
examples.zh: 這間旅店早餐供應熱麵包。

examples.en: A traveler asked for a room at the inn.
examples.zh: 一位旅客在小旅館詢問房間。

explains: A small place where travelers can stay overnight is called this. It may offer a bed and breakfast. Some are found in villages or along roads.
Many of these places have fewer rooms than a large hotel. The owner may welcome guests personally. Travelers should check what services are included.
A home is where people live, while this business provides short stays for visitors. It can be old or modern. Reading reviews may help travelers choose one.

examples.en: The inner pocket of his coat held the key.
examples.zh: 他外套的內袋裡放著鑰匙。

examples.en: She listened to her inner thoughts before answering.
examples.zh: 回答前，她先傾聽自己內心的想法。

examples.en: The inner walls of the box were lined with soft cloth.
examples.zh: 盒子的內壁襯有柔軟的布。

explains: Something located inside or closer to the center can be described this way. The room deep inside had no windows. A hallway connected it to the outside rooms.
A person's thoughts and feelings can also be called their private world. Friends may not know every feeling. It can help to talk with someone trusted.
Outer describes the surface or outside, while this adjective refers to what is within. The layer on the inside of a jacket may feel soft. Look at the noun it describes.

examples.en: Under the rule of law, every defendant is presumed innocent until proven guilty.
examples.zh: 在現代法治精神下，任何被告在未經判決確定有罪前均推定為無罪。

examples.en: DNA testing decades after the trial proved that the imprisoned man was completely innocent.
examples.zh: 在判決入獄數十年後所採用的現代高科技 DNA 重新鑑定，鐵證如山地證明了該名服刑男子是完全清白無罪的。

examples.en: Don't be so naive and innocent as to believe every investment promise you read on social media.
examples.zh: 切莫過於天真無邪，千萬不要傻傻輕信在社群網路上所看到的高報酬零風險各類虛假投資謊言。

entries.definition: 清白的；無罪的；天真無邪的
explains: Someone who has not done something wrong can be described this way. A child may be blamed for a mess they did not make. Asking what happened can reveal the truth.
The word can also describe a harmless action or object. A friendly joke may cause no damage. The situation helps show the meaning.
Guilty means responsible for a wrong act, while this word means not responsible for it. People should not blame others without evidence. Fair questions help find out what occurred.

examples.en: The mechanic will inspect the brakes before our trip.
examples.zh: 技師會在我們出發前檢查煞車。

examples.en: We inspected the shells we found on the beach.
examples.zh: 我們仔細查看在海灘上找到的貝殼。

examples.en: The teacher inspected each model for loose parts.
examples.zh: 老師檢查每個模型是否有鬆脫的零件。

explains: To look at something carefully to check its condition is to do this. A mechanic may examine a bicycle before a race. Finding a loose part early can prevent a problem.
People may check a room for safety. A worker can look at the equipment before using it. Careful checking protects everyone.
A quick glance may miss small details, while this verb suggests close attention. A student can check an answer before handing in a test. Taking time can catch mistakes.

examples.en: The inspector checked the playground equipment for safety.
examples.zh: 檢查員檢查遊樂場設備是否安全。

examples.en: A food inspector visited the school kitchen.
examples.zh: 食品檢查員到學校廚房查看。

examples.en: The building inspector approved the new stairs.
examples.zh: 建築檢查員核准了新樓梯。

explains: A person whose job is to check whether rules or standards are followed is called this. A building safety checker may look at stairs and doors. Safety is the main concern.
This worker may examine food, equipment, or a school. They write down what they find. The report can help fix problems.
A repair worker fixes something, while this official checks its condition. Both roles can help keep people safe. The place being checked tells what kind of worker it is.

examples.en: The intelligent crow learned how to open the box.
examples.zh: 聰明的烏鴉學會了如何打開盒子。

examples.en: She made an intelligent choice after comparing the two plans.
examples.zh: 比較兩個方案後，她做出了明智的選擇。

examples.en: The intelligent students solved the puzzle together.
examples.zh: 聰明的學生們一起解開了謎題。

explains: A person who learns, understands, and solves problems well can be described this way. Practice can strengthen these abilities. People may be clever in different ways.
An animal can also learn and remember useful actions. A dog may understand many commands. Training and patience help it improve.
Knowledge is what someone has learned, while this adjective describes the ability to learn and reason. Everyone can develop skills. Asking questions is one way to grow.

examples.en: Please do not interrupt while your sister is reading.
examples.zh: 妹妹正在閱讀時，請不要打斷她。

examples.en: The phone interrupted our dinner.
examples.zh: 電話打斷了我們的晚餐。

examples.en: He raised his hand so he would not interrupt the lesson.
examples.zh: 他舉手發言，以免打斷課程。

explains: To stop someone while they are speaking or doing something is to do this. A person may speak before the other has finished. Waiting for a pause is more polite.
A phone call can stop a meeting for a short time. The meeting may continue afterward. Some interruptions are important, but others can wait.
Listening quietly lets a speaker finish a thought. This verb describes breaking into that moment. Raising a hand can show you wish to speak.

examples.en: The students invented a game using paper cups.
examples.zh: 學生們用紙杯發明了一種遊戲。

examples.en: She hopes to invent a better way to recycle bottles.
examples.zh: 她希望發明更好的瓶子回收方式。

examples.en: The young engineer invented a small garden tool.
examples.zh: 這位年輕工程師發明了一種小型園藝工具。

explains: To create something new that did not exist before is to do this. A person might make a tool that solves a problem. Testing helps improve the design.
People can create a new game or way of doing a task too. A clever idea may begin with a simple question. Drawing a plan can help explain it.
Discover means finding something that already exists, while this verb means making something new. Many useful objects began as ideas. Patience and practice help turn them into real things.

examples.en: The inventor showed us a model of her water-saving device.
examples.zh: 發明家向我們展示了她的節水裝置模型。

examples.en: A young inventor designed a holder for his bicycle helmet.
examples.zh: 一位年輕發明家設計了安全帽架。

examples.en: The inventor tested each version before choosing the best one.
examples.zh: 發明家測試了每個版本，才選出最好的。

explains: A person who creates a new tool, machine, or idea is called this. They notice a problem and try to solve it. Their work may take many attempts.
Some people build a model before making the full object. They test it and make changes. Careful notes can help them remember what worked.
A scientist may study how nature works, while this person focuses on creating something new. One person can do both kinds of work. Their discoveries may help many people.

examples.en: The class investigated why the plant leaves turned yellow.
examples.zh: 全班調查植物葉子變黃的原因。

examples.en: The police investigated the missing bicycle.
examples.zh: 警方調查了腳踏車失竊案。

examples.en: We investigated how shadows change during the day.
examples.zh: 我們探究影子如何隨著一天的時間改變。

explains: To try to discover the facts about something is to do this. A detective may ask questions and look for clues. Careful work can reveal what happened.
A scientist may study a question by making observations. They write down results and compare them. This helps them reach a fair conclusion.
Guessing gives an idea without proof, while this action checks evidence. People should be patient when learning the truth. Different clues may point in different directions.

examples.en: Thank you for the wedding invitation card!
examples.zh: 感謝你的婚禮喜帖邀請函！

examples.en: She graciously accepted the formal invitation to keynote the international conference.
examples.zh: 她欣然接受了在國際會議上發表主題演講的正式邀請。

examples.en: Send out party invitations at least two weeks ahead of time.
examples.zh: 請至少提前兩週發出派對的邀請函。

explains: A message asking someone to come to an event is called this. It may give the date, time, and place. The guest can reply to say whether they will come.
It can also be a spoken request to join an activity. A friend may ask someone to play a game. Accepting or declining politely is helpful.
An announcement tells a group about something, while this message is meant to welcome a person. It can be sent on paper or by phone. The wording can be formal or friendly.

examples.en: The old piano had ivory-colored keys.
examples.zh: 那架舊鋼琴的琴鍵是象牙白色的。

examples.en: The museum explained why ivory trade harms elephants.
examples.zh: 博物館說明了象牙貿易為何會傷害大象。

examples.en: She chose an ivory scarf instead of a bright white one.
examples.zh: 她選了一條象牙白色的圍巾，而不是亮白色的。

explains: A hard, pale material from the tusks of elephants is called this. Buying it can harm animals. Many places restrict trade to help protect them.
People may use this word for a creamy white color. A shirt or wall can be painted in that shade. It looks softer than bright white.
The natural material comes from animal tusks, while the color can be made safely with paint or fabric. Choose alternatives that do not come from wildlife. Protecting animals matters.

examples.en: The old jail had thick stone walls.
examples.zh: 那座舊監獄有厚厚的石牆。

examples.en: A guard opened the jail door for the visitor.
examples.zh: 警衛為訪客打開了監獄的門。

examples.en: The town turned its former jail into a museum.
examples.zh: 鎮上把舊監獄改建成博物館。

explains: A place where people are kept after being arrested or sentenced is called this. They cannot leave freely. Laws govern how people there are treated.
A person may be held in this place for a short time while waiting for a hearing or serving a sentence. Rules and routines control daily life there. The details depend on the place.
A school is open for lessons, but this building keeps people who are not free to leave. It may have locked doors and guarded rooms. The word can appear in history books and stories.

examples.en: She filled a glass jar with homemade jam.
examples.zh: 她在玻璃罐裡裝滿自製果醬。

examples.en: The sudden crash jarred everyone in the quiet room.
examples.zh: 寧靜的房間裡突然一聲巨響，讓大家都嚇了一跳。

examples.en: Put the buttons in the small jar on the shelf.
examples.zh: 把鈕扣放進架子上的小罐子裡。

explains: A container with a wide opening and usually a lid is called this. People store jam or pickles inside. Glass versions let you see what is within.
The verb can mean to shake or shock someone. A sudden loud noise may disturb a person. The feeling can be uncomfortable.
A bottle often has a narrow neck, while this container has a wider mouth. Both can hold liquids or food. Choose one that closes tightly for storage.

examples.en: He yawned and stretched his jaw.
examples.zh: 他打了個哈欠，伸展下顎。

examples.en: The dog held the toy gently in its jaws.
examples.zh: 狗用嘴輕輕咬著玩具。

examples.en: Her jaw hurt after she chewed the tough candy.
examples.zh: 她嚼了很硬的糖果後，下顎感到疼痛。

explains: The bones around the mouth that help a person chew are called this. Teeth are attached to them. Opening the mouth moves the lower part.
Some animals have strong mouth bones for biting or chewing. A turtle uses them to eat plants or other food. Different animals have different shapes.
These bones support the teeth used for biting and chewing. The lower one moves when the mouth opens. In some animals, they are very strong and help crush hard food.

examples.en: The band played jazz at the summer festival.
examples.zh: 樂團在夏日節慶演奏爵士樂。

examples.en: My uncle listens to jazz while cooking dinner.
examples.zh: 叔叔做晚餐時會聽爵士樂。

examples.en: The saxophone solo gave the jazz song a lively sound.
examples.zh: 薩克斯風獨奏讓這首爵士樂聽起來很有活力。

explains: A kind of music often uses instruments such as saxophones, drums, and trumpets. Musicians may make up new melodies while playing. Its rhythms can be lively.
Different players take turns with short musical parts. They listen closely to one another. The music can sound different each time.
A song played from written notes may follow a set pattern, while this style often allows improvising. Many styles have grown from it. People enjoy listening or dancing to its beat.

examples.en: He felt jealous when his sister received a new bicycle.
examples.zh: 妹妹收到新腳踏車時，他感到嫉妒。

examples.en: The jealous cat pushed between its owner and the puppy.
examples.zh: 那隻吃醋的貓擠到主人和小狗中間。

examples.en: She felt jealous of a friend’s beautiful painting.
examples.zh: 她羨慕朋友畫得漂亮。

explains: A person who feels unhappy because someone has what they want may be described this way. A child may feel this when a sibling gets a new toy. Talking kindly about the feeling can help.
Someone may worry that a friend likes another person more. Trust and honest conversation can ease that worry. People can have many friends.
Admiration is liking what another person can do, while this feeling can include worry or resentment. Noticing the difference helps someone respond well. Sharing and gratitude can improve a situation.

examples.en: The jeep carried our camping gear along the rocky road.
examples.zh: 吉普車載著我們的露營裝備行駛在石子路上。

examples.en: A green jeep waited outside the museum.
examples.zh: 一輛綠色吉普車停在博物館外。

examples.en: They drove a jeep across the sandy trail.
examples.zh: 他們開著吉普車穿越沙地小徑。

explains: A strong vehicle made for driving over rough ground is often called this. It may have four-wheel drive. People use it on some country roads.
The word is also the name of a vehicle brand. Many models have an open top or space for outdoor gear. Drivers should follow road rules everywhere.
A small city car is built mainly for smooth streets, while this kind of vehicle can travel on uneven paths. It still needs a trained driver. Seat belts keep passengers safer.

examples.en: Royal jelly is a nutrient-dense secretion fed exclusively to the queen bee, promoting her vitality.
examples.zh: 珍貴純天然的蜂王乳是女王蜂終生專屬享用的天然高活性營養聖品。

examples.en: Spreading homemade strawberry jelly over warm sourdough toast makes a delicious breakfast treat.
examples.zh: 將親手手工熬製的手作草莓果凍果醬均勻抹在剛出爐的烤酸種吐司上，是一道極致美味的元氣早餐。

examples.en: The pastry chef created an exquisite dessert layered with mango jelly and white chocolate mousse.
examples.zh: 法式甜點主廚精心打造了一款層次分明的精緻甜點，底層是酸甜芒果凍，上層覆蓋著白巧克力慕斯。

entries.definition: 珍貴滋補蜂王乳 (蜂王漿)；果凍
explains: A soft, wobbly food made from fruit juice and gelatin is called this. It can be served as a dessert. Some people call a similar spread by this name too.
The word can also name a sea animal with a soft body and long trailing parts. Some kinds sting, so people should not touch them. Watch them from a safe distance.
Jam usually contains pieces of fruit, while this spread is often smooth. A sea creature with the same name is very different from food. Context tells the meaning.

examples.en: The jet landed safely after its long flight.
examples.zh: 這架噴射客機在長途飛行後安全降落。

examples.en: A jet of water sprayed from the broken hose.
examples.zh: 水從破掉的水管中噴射而出。

examples.en: We watched a jet climb above the clouds.
examples.zh: 我們看著一架噴射機爬升到雲層上方。

explains: A fast aircraft powered by engines that push air backward is called this. It can carry passengers over long distances. Airports have special runways for it.
A narrow stream of liquid or gas can also be called this. Water may shoot from a hose in a strong stream. The surrounding words show the meaning.
A propeller plane has blades that turn outside, while this aircraft uses engines with no propeller blades. Both can fly. Passengers should follow crew instructions.

examples.en: Synthetic ruby jewels pressed into chatons provide frictionless bearings for fast-spinning steel pivots.
examples.zh: 鑲嵌於黃金套筒中的「人造紅寶石軸承」（Jewels），為高速旋轉的精鋼齒輪軸尖提供近乎零摩擦的旋轉支撐。

examples.en: The crown jewels kept inside the fortified royal tower include diamond tiaras and jewel-encrusted scepters.
examples.zh: 嚴密珍藏在倫敦塔要塞深處的英國皇室加冕珠寶皇冠珠寶，包括璀璨奪目的鑽石皇冠與鑲滿紅寶石的黃金權杖。

examples.en: An experienced watchmaker uses brass tweezers to press each synthetic jewel into its recessed setting.
examples.zh: 經驗老到的高級製錶師手持黃銅鑷子，小心翼翼地將每一顆微米紅寶石寶石軸承精密壓入夾板凹槽中。

entries.definition: 機芯齒輪微型軸承人造紅寶石軸承 (減阻)；珠寶
explains: A valuable stone, such as a ruby or diamond, is called this. It may be set into a ring or necklace. Some are cut to make them shine.
People may use the word for a precious and beautiful object. A family might keep one as a special keepsake. The value can come from memories as well as price.
A piece of jewelry can hold a stone, while this word refers to the stone itself. Not all stones are precious. Careful handling keeps them from being lost.

examples.en: Delicate sterling silver jewelry adds a subtle sparkle without feeling gaudy.
examples.zh: 精緻小巧的 925 純銀極簡鎖骨鏈與小耳環能為整體造型點綴低調奢華的微光，絕不落俗套。

examples.en: She keeps her heirlooms and delicate gold jewelry neatly organized in a velvet jewelry box.
examples.zh: 她將祖傳傳家首飾與細緻純金項鍊分門別類、井然有序地收納在絲絨珠寶盒中。

examples.en: Artisanal handcrafted jewelry often features recycled metals and ethically mined gemstones.
examples.zh: 獨立手作職人金工珠寶飾品往往大量採用再生貴金屬與符合人道採礦標準的天然寶石。

explains: Decorative items such as rings, necklaces, and bracelets are called this. People wear them to make an outfit special. Some are made from metal or stones.
A small box can keep these items safe. They may be given as gifts for birthdays or weddings. Store them carefully so they do not tangle.
A jewel is one precious stone, while this noun refers to wearable decorations. Some pieces are simple and others are ornate. People choose what suits them.

examples.en: A swift, seamless journey across the island transforms business meetings and family reunions alike.
examples.zh: 僅需一個半小時即可橫跨全島的「快捷舒適旅程」（Journey），徹底改變了全台商務出差與家庭團聚的面貌。

examples.en: Learning a foreign language is a lifelong personal journey of discovery, patience, and cultural empathy.
examples.zh: 學習一門全新的外國語言是一段終身探索的個人心靈旅程，需要無比的恆心耐心與跨文化同理包容力。

examples.en: The young backpacker documented every step of her six-month solo journey across Southeast Asia on her vlog.
examples.zh: 這位勇敢的年輕背包客用自媒體影音日誌，生動記錄了自己獨自背起行囊橫跨東南亞六個月壯遊的每一個足跡。

entries.definition: 台北到高雄僅需九十分鐘快捷安全的城際旅程；旅程
explains: A trip from one place to another can be called this. It may take a few hours or several days. Travelers plan what to bring.
People can also use the word for a long process of learning or change. Growing up includes many new experiences. Each step brings something to learn.
A short walk may be a simple outing, while this word often suggests a longer trip or process. A map can help travelers plan. Unexpected events may happen along the way.

examples.en: The joyful children danced around the birthday cake.
examples.zh: 快樂的孩子們圍著生日蛋糕跳舞。

examples.en: A joyful song played during the parade.
examples.zh: 遊行時播放著歡樂的歌曲。

examples.en: We felt joyful when our team won the final.
examples.zh: 隊伍贏得決賽時，我們感到非常喜悅。

explains: A person or event full of great happiness can be described this way. A family reunion may bring smiles and laughter. People enjoy being together.
Music can have a bright, happy feeling. It may make listeners want to clap or dance. The sound can match a celebration.
Glad describes being pleased, while this adjective suggests a stronger, open happiness. A happy day may include good news and friends. The feeling can be shared.

examples.en: Premium grilled Taiwanese sausages are bursting with sweet, juicy flavors.
examples.zh: 現烤出爐的高粱酒黑豬肉香腸咬下去瞬間在嘴裡迸發出微甜又多汁的飽滿肉汁。

examples.en: Freshly picked watermelons in summer are sweet, cold, and remarkably juicy.
examples.zh: 盛夏現摘的花蓮大西瓜汁水飽滿、甘甜多汁，冰鎮過後更是清甜可口。

examples.en: The chef seared the ribeye steak on high heat to lock in all the rich, juicy goodness.
examples.zh: 大廚以大火高溫快速炙烤肋眼牛排表面，將豐盈醇厚且多汁的肉汁完全鎖在牛排中。

explains: Fruit with plenty of liquid inside can be described this way. A ripe orange may taste fresh and sweet. Its juice can run down your fingers.
Food can be moist when it contains a lot of moisture. Cooking meat too long may make it dry instead. Careful cooking keeps it tender.
Dry describes food with little moisture, while this adjective suggests a wet, flavorful bite. Watermelon is often refreshing. The texture depends on how ripe it is.

examples.en: A tiger moved quietly through the jungle.
examples.zh: 老虎悄悄地穿過叢林。

examples.en: The explorers followed a narrow path in the jungle.
examples.zh: 探險者沿著叢林中的狹窄小徑前進。

examples.en: Vines covered the old stone wall like a jungle.
examples.zh: 藤蔓爬滿了舊石牆，像叢林一樣茂密。

explains: A thick forest in a warm, wet region can be called this. Many kinds of plants grow there. Animals may live among the trees and vines.
The word can describe a place that feels tangled or crowded. A messy garden may seem hard to walk through. Clearing a path can help.
A desert is dry and has little rainfall, while this kind of forest gets much more water. It can have dense plants and rich animal life. Visitors should follow guides and stay safe.

examples.en: My junior teammate asked me to explain the drill.
examples.zh: 我的年輕隊友請我說明這項練習。

examples.en: She is a junior at the high school.
examples.zh: 她是這所高中的三年級學生。

examples.en: The race has a junior group for younger runners.
examples.zh: 這場賽跑設有年紀較小的參賽組別。

explains: A person younger or less experienced than another may be described this way. In school, it can name a student in a lower grade. The exact use depends on the country.
The word can also be part of a person's name when they share a name with a parent. It does not always describe age. The sentence gives the clue.
Senior often refers to an older or more experienced person, while this word can refer to someone younger. Teams may use it for age groups. Rules vary by activity.

examples.en: We cleared the junk from the garage and recycled the metal.
examples.zh: 我們清理了車庫裡的廢物，並回收金屬。

examples.en: He ate too much junk food before dinner.
examples.zh: 晚餐前他吃了太多垃圾食物。

examples.en: The children made a robot from junk parts.
examples.zh: 孩子們用廢棄零件做了一個機器人。

explains: Old or unwanted things that are no longer useful can be called this. A broken toy may be thrown away or recycled. Sorting items helps reduce waste.
Some food with little nutrition is casually described this way. Eating too much of it may not be healthy. Balanced meals give the body what it needs.

A useful object should be kept or repaired, while this word describes things people do not need. One person's old item may still be useful to someone else. Donating can be better than throwing it out.

examples.en: A kangaroo hopped across the grassy field.
examples.zh: 一隻袋鼠跳過長滿草的田野。

examples.en: The baby kangaroo rested in its mother’s pouch.
examples.zh: 小袋鼠待在媽媽的育兒袋裡休息。

examples.en: We saw a kangaroo at the wildlife park.
examples.zh: 我們在野生動物園看到一隻袋鼠。

explains: A large animal from Australia has powerful back legs for jumping. It carries its young in a pouch. Its long tail helps it balance.
These animals eat plants and often live in groups. They can move quickly across open land. People should watch them from a safe distance.
A wallaby is a smaller relative, while this animal is often much larger. Both have pouches for their young. Their strong legs make them good jumpers.

examples.en: Clean your computer keyboard regularly to remove dust.
examples.zh: 定期清潔電腦鍵盤以清除灰塵。

examples.en: Mechanical keyboards offer satisfying tactile feedback while typing code.
examples.zh: 機械式鍵盤在敲寫程式碼時能提供令人滿意的段落觸感。

examples.en: Wireless keyboards connect seamlessly via Bluetooth to laptops.
examples.zh: 無線鍵盤可透過藍牙無縫連接至筆記型電腦。

explains: A set of keys used for typing letters and numbers is called this. It connects to a computer or tablet. Pressing each key sends a signal.
A musical instrument with black and white keys can also have this name. Players press them to make notes. A piano has a large one.
A screen can show letters without physical keys, while this device has buttons you press. Some instruments also use keys. Context shows whether typing or music is meant.

examples.en: The doctor drew a picture of a kidney for the class.
examples.zh: 醫生為全班畫了一張腎臟的圖。

examples.en: A pair of kidneys helps clean the blood.
examples.zh: 一對腎臟有助於淨化血液。

examples.en: The lesson explained how a kidney works.
examples.zh: 這堂課說明了腎臟如何運作。

explains: An organ in the body filters waste from the blood and helps make urine. Most people have two. Drinking water supports normal body functions.
Doctors can check how well this organ works with medical tests. It has an important job in keeping the body balanced. A trusted adult can explain health questions.
The heart pumps blood, while this organ cleans it. Different body parts have different tasks. Keeping healthy habits supports them all.

examples.en: The village is about one kilometer from the station.
examples.zh: 村莊距離車站大約一公里。

examples.en: We walked two kilometers along the river.
examples.zh: 我們沿著河走了兩公里。

examples.en: The sign said the beach was five kilometers ahead.
examples.zh: 標誌寫著海灘在前方五公里處。

explains: A unit for measuring distance equals one thousand meters. Road signs may show how many of these remain to a town. It is longer than a meter.
Many countries use this unit on maps and road signs. A short walk may cover only part of one. A car can travel several in a few minutes.
A mile is another distance unit used in some places. Maps show which unit they use. Knowing the scale helps estimate a trip.

examples.en: My little brother started kindergarten this week.
examples.zh: 我弟弟這週開始上幼兒園。

examples.en: The kindergarten class planted beans in small cups.
examples.zh: 幼兒園班級把豆子種在小杯子裡。

examples.en: She learned to tie her shoes in kindergarten.
examples.zh: 她在幼兒園學會了綁鞋帶。

explains: A school or class for very young children before primary school is called this. Children learn through play and simple lessons. They practice sharing and following routines.
A child may learn letters, numbers, songs, and art there. Teachers help children feel comfortable in a group. The daily schedule includes rest and play.
Primary school usually has more formal lessons, while this early program helps children get ready. Different places set different ages. Families can ask a school about its rules.

examples.en: The story takes place in a kingdom beside the sea.
examples.zh: 故事發生在海邊的一個王國。

examples.en: The young king ruled the kingdom wisely.
examples.zh: 年輕的國王明智地統治王國。

examples.en: In science class, we studied the plant kingdom.
examples.zh: 自然課上，我們學習了植物界。

explains: A country or land ruled by a king or queen can be called this. It may have castles and royal laws. Stories often describe such places.
Scientists also use this word for one of the largest groups of living things. Animals and plants belong to different groups. The meaning depends on the subject.
This place can be real or imaginary in a story. A republic has a different kind of government. In science, the same word has a separate meaning.

examples.en: The art kit had paint, brushes, and thick paper.
examples.zh: 美術材料組裡有顏料、畫筆和厚紙。

examples.en: Dad packed a first-aid kit for the hike.
examples.zh: 爸爸為健行準備了一個急救包。

examples.en: The robot kit came with clear instructions.
examples.zh: 機器人套件附有清楚的說明。

explains: A set of tools or supplies packed together for a particular task is called this. A first-aid version contains items for small emergencies. Keep it where adults can find it.
People can buy a craft version with materials for making one project. The pieces and directions are usually included. It is fun to follow the steps.
A single tool is only one item, while this set includes several things used together. A repair box may have many pieces. Check that nothing important is missing.

examples.en: The brave knight guarded the bridge in the tale.
examples.zh: 故事中，勇敢的騎士守護著橋梁。
