examples.en: The teacher asked us to classify each shape on the worksheet.
examples.zh: 老師請我們把學習單上的每個形狀分類。

explains: To put things into groups based on shared details is to sort them. A person first decides which feature matters. Labels make each group easy to recognize.
Ravi sorted his cards by the animals shown on them. He placed birds together and fish in another pile. Then he counted each group.
Putting items in a random pile does not show how they are alike. Choosing a clear feature makes sorting useful. People can group the same items in different ways.

examples.en: The eagle grabbed a fish with its strong claws.
examples.zh: 老鷹用強壯的爪子抓住一條魚。

examples.en: The cat's claw caught on the soft blanket.
examples.zh: 貓爪勾住了柔軟的毯子。

examples.en: A crab lifted one claw as it moved across the sand.
examples.zh: 螃蟹在沙地上移動時舉起一隻螯。

explains: A sharp curved nail on an animal's foot can help it grip, climb, or catch food. Birds and cats have different kinds. The shape fits what each animal does.
The kitten used its small nails to hold onto a soft toy. Its owner gave it a scratching post instead of furniture. The kitten learned where to play.
A flat human fingernail is not shaped like the sharp curved nails of some animals. Different animals use them in different ways. People should watch wild creatures from a safe distance.

examples.en: The Qingshui Cliff drops steeply straight down into the Pacific Ocean.
examples.zh: 清水斷崖險峻峭拔，垂直俯瞰直插入太平洋中。

examples.en: Seabirds build secure nests on narrow rocky ledges along the coastal cliff.
examples.zh: 海鳥在沿海懸崖陡峭狹窄的岩石岩架上構築安全的巢穴。

examples.en: Warning fences prevent adventurous sightseers from stepping too close to the cliff edge.
examples.zh: 警告護欄能防範好奇冒險的觀光客過於逼近危險的懸崖邊緣。

examples.en: Towering vertical limestone cliffs drop hundreds of meters straight into the roaring Taroko Gorge.
examples.zh: 太魯閣國家公園兩側高聳入雲的千仞大理石絕壁懸崖，筆直向下直插轟鳴的立霧溪谷。

examples.en: Warning signs caution hikers to stay well away from the crumbling edge of the ocean cliff.
examples.zh: 警示牌告誡健行登山客務必遠離容易風化崩落的海崖邊緣。

examples.en: Rock climbers inspected safety anchors before repelling down the granite cliff face.
examples.zh: 攀岩者在沿著花崗岩峭壁垂降前，仔細檢查了岩壁上的固定錨點與安全吊帶。

entries.definition: 懸崖；峭壁；千仞絕壁大斷崖；懸崖峭壁
explains: A steep high face of rock rises sharply above land or water. The edge can be dangerous, so people should stay behind safety barriers. Some birds build nests on ledges.
The family stopped at a marked lookout above the sea. They stayed behind the fence and watched waves hit the rocks below. A sign warned visitors not to climb.
A hill rises gradually and is often easy to walk up. A steep rock face drops sharply. Both are landforms, but one needs greater care.

examples.en: I felt clumsy while trying to skate for the first time.
examples.zh: 第一次溜冰時，我覺得自己動作笨拙。

examples.en: The clumsy puppy knocked over the water bowl.
examples.zh: 那隻笨手笨腳的小狗撞翻了水碗。

examples.en: He made a clumsy attempt to carry all the boxes at once.
examples.zh: 他笨拙地試著一次搬起所有箱子。

explains: Someone who often drops things or bumps into objects may move without much control. This can happen when a person is tired or learning a new skill. Practice can help movements become smoother.
While carrying a stack of books, Finn tripped over his backpack. He picked them up and moved the bag out of the way. Then he carried fewer books at a time.
Careful movement can be smooth and steady. Uncoordinated movement may cause small accidents. Everyone has moments when they are not careful.

examples.en: French press and cold brew methods require a coarse coffee grind size.
examples.zh: 法式濾壓壺與冷萃咖啡沖泡法皆需要使用顆粒較大如粗海鹽般的粗研磨咖啡粉。

examples.en: The texture of the sandpaper was too coarse for fine furniture polishing.
examples.zh: 這款砂紙的顆粒過於粗糙，不太適合用來做高級實木家具的精細拋光作業。

examples.en: Season the steak with coarse sea salt and cracked black pepper before grilling.
examples.zh: 在將厚切牛排送上烤網碳烤之前，先均勻撒上天然粗海鹽與現磨黑胡椒碎醃漬入味。

explains: A surface made of large rough pieces can feel uneven when touched. Sand or cloth may have this texture. Fine material feels smoother and smaller.
Mina rubbed two kinds of paper between her fingers. One felt smooth, while the other had a rough grain. She chose the smoother sheet for drawing.
A polished stone is smooth, but an unfinished one may have a rough surface. Texture helps people describe what they touch. Words can also have other meanings depending on context.

examples.en: For the first time in history, humanity has learned not just to read, but to write the sacred code of life.
examples.zh: 在漫長演化史上人類首次學會了不僅能閱讀、更能親筆書寫並編程神聖的「生命遺傳程式碼」（Code of Life）。

examples.en: The hotel room safe requires guests to enter a four-digit numeric security code to unlock the door.
examples.zh: 飯店客房專用保險箱要求入住旅客自行設定輸入一組四位數的數位安全防護密碼以解鎖保險箱門。

examples.en: Talented teenage students learn how to code mobile apps using Python and JavaScript in after-school workshops.
examples.zh: 充滿天賦的國高中青少年學生在課後研習工作坊中，熱情學習運用 Python 與 JavaScript 撰寫手機應用程式代碼。

entries.definition: 謙卑解讀並重寫演化三十八億年之神聖生命程式碼；代碼
explains: A set of instructions written for a computer tells it what steps to follow. People use special symbols and rules to create those instructions. The computer carries them out.
Jin wrote simple instructions to make a screen character move. When he pressed a key, the character walked across the screen. He changed the steps to make it turn.
A recipe gives steps for cooking, and computer instructions give steps for a machine. Each follows rules. Careful checking can fix mistakes.

examples.en: The old tent collapsed when strong winds hit it.
examples.zh: 強風吹來時，那頂舊帳篷倒塌了。

examples.en: The tired runner collapsed onto the grass after the race.
examples.zh: 疲憊的跑者在比賽後倒在草地上。

examples.en: The sandcastle collapsed when a wave washed over it.
examples.zh: 海浪沖過時，沙堡塌了。

explains: A building or structure can suddenly fall down when it loses support. People should move away from an unsafe place and tell an adult. A weak frame may need repair.
The old cardboard tower leaned to one side as the children added blocks. It fell onto the soft mat. They rebuilt it with a wider base.
A stable structure stands firmly, while a weak one may fall. A person can also fall down from tiredness or illness. The surrounding words explain the meaning.

examples.en: I had lunch with my colleagues at the canteen.
examples.zh: 我和同事們在員工餐廳一起吃午餐。

examples.en: Trust between colleagues is vital for efficient team project collaboration.
examples.zh: 同事之間的信任對於高效率的團隊專案合作至關重要。

examples.en: We organized a farewell party for our esteemed colleague who is retiring next week.
examples.zh: 我們為即將於下週光榮榮退的敬重同事籌辦了一場溫馨的歡送會。

explains: A person who works with someone at the same place or in a similar job is part of that person's work team. They can share ideas and help with tasks. Good teamwork makes work easier.
At the bakery, Rosa prepared dough while her coworker decorated cakes. They checked each other's work before opening the shop. Customers enjoyed the fresh treats.
A customer visits a business, while a worker helps run it. People on the same team may have different jobs. Respectful talk helps them cooperate.

examples.en: The combination of sunshine and rain helped the garden grow.
examples.zh: 陽光和雨水的結合幫助花園裡的植物生長。

examples.en: Her outfit is a combination of blue jeans and a yellow shirt.
examples.zh: 她的穿搭是藍色牛仔褲和黃色上衣的組合。

examples.en: We tried a new combination of fruit in the smoothie.
examples.zh: 我們在冰沙裡試了新的水果組合。

explains: Several things brought together can make a new whole. They may keep their own qualities while working together. The result depends on what is included.
Leo mixed oats, berries, and yogurt in a bowl. Each food tasted different, but together they made a filling breakfast. He added honey on top.
A single color stands alone, while mixing colors can create another shade. Items can also be grouped without being changed. The situation shows which sense fits.

examples.en: Watching a lighthearted romantic comedy always cheers me up.
examples.zh: 看一部輕鬆浪漫的喜劇片總是能讓我心情大好。

examples.en: The stand-up comedy club was packed with people laughing hysterically.
examples.zh: 單口喜劇脫口秀俱樂部裡擠滿了捧腹大笑的觀眾。

examples.en: The theatrical production balanced slapstick comedy with poignant drama.
examples.zh: 這部舞台劇製作巧妙平衡了肢體鬧劇幽默與動人深刻的情感。

explains: A story or show made to make people laugh is meant to be funny. It may use silly events, jokes, or amusing characters. People enjoy different kinds of humor.
The family watched a movie about a clumsy chef who kept mixing up orders. The silly mistakes made them laugh. At the end, the chef learned to slow down.
A serious story may focus on danger or sadness. A funny one tries to bring smiles. Both can tell a story about people and their choices.

examples.en: The commander gave the crew instructions before takeoff.
examples.zh: 指揮官在起飛前向機組人員下達指示。

examples.en: A brave commander led the rescue team through the storm.
examples.zh: 一位勇敢的指揮官帶領救援隊穿過暴風雨。

examples.en: The commander checked that every soldier was ready.
examples.zh: 指揮官確認每位士兵都已準備就緒。

explains: A person who leads a group of soldiers or directs a mission gives orders and makes plans. The group follows instructions to work together. This role carries responsibility.
During the training exercise, the leader explained where each team should go. Everyone listened and checked their equipment. They finished the task safely.
A follower carries out a plan, while a leader helps decide what to do. People in charge must communicate clearly. The title is often used in military settings.

examples.en: Leave a friendly comment below if you enjoyed the vlog!
examples.zh: 如果你喜歡這部生活 Vlog，請在下方留下友善的留言！

examples.en: The government minister declined to comment on the ongoing investigation.
examples.zh: 政府部會首長對目前正在進行中的調查案婉拒置評發表評論。

examples.en: Her constructive comments helped the author polish the book chapter.
examples.zh: 她富有建設性的點評意見幫助作者潤飾了書稿章節。

examples.en: Don't forget to like, share, and leave a comment below!
examples.zh: 別忘了按讚、分享，並在下方留言處留下您的看法！

examples.en: The spokesperson declined to make any comment regarding the rumors.
examples.zh: 發言人拒絕對外界的謠傳發表任何評論。

examples.en: Her critical comments helped improve the team's research paper.
examples.zh: 她切中要點的評論建議幫助團隊改進了研究論文品質。

explains: A spoken or written remark shares what someone thinks about something. It may give information, praise, or a question. A respectful tone helps others listen.
After reading the class story, May wrote a short note about her favorite character. She explained why she liked the ending. Her teacher read it aloud.
A question asks for an answer, while a remark may simply share an idea. Both can start a conversation. People should choose words carefully online.

examples.en: Commerce between the two towns grew after the new bridge opened.
examples.zh: 新橋開通後，兩個城鎮之間的商業往來增加了。

examples.en: The internet has changed how people do commerce.
examples.zh: 網際網路改變了人們進行商業活動的方式。

examples.en: The port is an important center of commerce.
examples.zh: 這座港口是重要的商業中心。

explains: The buying and selling of goods and services is part of business activity. Shops, farms, and companies take part. This activity helps people get what they need.
A farmer sent apples to a market in town. The shop paid for the fruit and sold it to families. Both sides took part in trade.
A person may grow food at home without selling it. When goods are exchanged for money, business activity takes place. Many people help goods travel to buyers.

examples.en: He committed to helping at the animal shelter each week.
examples.zh: 他承諾每週都到動物收容所幫忙。

examples.en: They committed themselves to finishing the garden project.
examples.zh: 他們承諾完成花園專題。

examples.en: She committed to reading every night before bed.
examples.zh: 她承諾每晚睡前閱讀。

explains: To promise to do something and keep working at it shows a person is serious about the plan. It may take time and effort. A clear goal can help someone stay on track.
Maya promised to practice the piano every afternoon. She put a reminder by the keyboard and followed her plan. After a month, she could play a new song.
A quick wish may fade, while a firm promise includes action. People should choose tasks they can manage. Keeping a promise helps others trust them.

examples.en: Good communication helped the team solve the problem.
examples.zh: 良好的溝通幫助團隊解決了問題。

examples.en: We use hand signs for communication during the noisy game.
examples.zh: 在吵鬧的遊戲中，我們用手勢溝通。

examples.en: Clear communication is important when planning a trip.
examples.zh: 規劃旅行時，清楚的溝通很重要。

explains: People share ideas or information by speaking, writing, drawing, or using signs. Listening is an important part of sharing messages. Clear messages help people understand one another.
The group planned a class party by writing ideas on a board. Each student listened before adding a suggestion. They agreed on games and snacks.
A message sent without listening may be misunderstood. Asking questions can check that everyone understands. People use many ways to share information.

examples.en: Our local neighborhood community organized a weekend park cleanup.
examples.zh: 我們在地的社區鄰里組織了一場週末公園大掃除活動。

examples.en: A friendly community center provides dance classes and meals for seniors.
examples.zh: 友善親切的社區活動中心為銀髮長輩提供舞蹈課程與營養共餐。

examples.en: Neighbors foster a warm sense of community by looking out for one another.
examples.zh: 街坊鄰里守望相助、互相關照，營造出溫馨濃厚的社區凝聚力。

examples.en: Cultivating a supportive fan community is essential for long-term creator success.
examples.zh: 經營一個溫馨互助的粉絲社群是創作者維持長期成功的重要基石。

examples.en: The neighborhood community banded together to clean up the coastal beach.
examples.zh: 社區鄰里團結一心，攜手同心投入清理沿海沙灘垃圾的環保行動。

examples.en: Developers contribute code openly to benefit the global open-source community.
examples.zh: 開發者們無私公開貢獻程式碼，造福全球廣大的開源軟體社群。

examples.en: Fostering an active Discord community strengthens bonds between creator and fans.
examples.zh: 悉心經營充滿活力的官方 Discord 專屬社群能極大拉近創作者與廣大粉絲的情感連結。

examples.en: The local community center organizes weekend workshops and sports events for residents.
examples.zh: 社區活動中心每逢週末皆會為附近居民策劃豐富的專題手作工作坊與運動球賽。

examples.en: Online gaming communities provide a supportive space where players can make lasting friendships.
examples.zh: 線上遊戲玩家社群為各國玩家提供了一個溫暖互助的避風港，讓大家結交長久摯友。

examples.en: Community-based integrated care models ensure medical, social, and meal services reach every rural alley.
examples.zh: 社區整合型長照照顧網絡，將醫療照護、日間托老與愛心送餐服務無縫送達每一條偏鄉巷弄。

examples.en: Neighborhood volunteers organized a festive weekend clean-up day to revitalize the local community park.
examples.zh: 鄰里熱心志工舉辦了歡樂的週末大掃除活動，齊心協力讓社區小公園煥然一新。

examples.en: Living in a close-knit apartment community provides wonderful mutual support when neighbors travel abroad.
examples.zh: 居住在守望相助、關係緊密的公寓大樓社區中，當鄰居出國旅行時能互相照應並代收包裹。

examples.en: Local community volunteers organize historic walking tours to share their ancestral neighborhood stories.
examples.zh: 在地社區志工主動發起文化走讀導覽，帶領年輕學子深入老街巷弄探索家族歷史記憶。

examples.en: Active community involvement is essential for keeping restored historic districts vibrant and lived-in.
examples.zh: 在地社區居民的主動參與，是讓活化修復後的歷史街區保持生機盎然與生活氣息的活水。

examples.en: The old port community mobilized swiftly to prevent the demolition of the century-old grain warehouse.
examples.zh: 老港口社區全體鄉親迅速串聯集結，成功搶救了面臨怪手拆除危機的百年老穀倉。

entries.definition: 社區；共同體；粉絲社群；社群互動；社群平台；社區整合型 ABC 級長照服務網；在地鄉親守護家鄉古蹟文化聚落
explains: People who live in the same area or share an interest can form a group. They may help each other and work on shared goals. Each person can contribute something.
Neighbors planted flowers beside the local library. Some brought tools, and others watered the new plants. The street looked brighter after they worked together.
A single household is small, while a whole neighborhood includes many families. People may also connect through a shared hobby. Working together can make a place stronger.

examples.en: Dogs and cats are beloved companion animals, cherished as genuine family members.
examples.zh: 狗狗與貓咪是現代人生活中不可或缺的摯愛伴侶動物，被視為如家人般珍貴的毛小孩。

examples.en: For many elderly people living alone, a loyal canine companion provides comfort and safety.
examples.zh: 對許多獨居長輩而言，忠誠的犬類伴侶能帶來無比的安慰與安全感。

examples.en: She chose a calm, mature dog as her travel companion during weekend hikes.
examples.zh: 她選擇了一隻沉穩的成犬，作為週末健行時的隨行同伴。

examples.en: Treat English as a loyal lifelong companion that will accompany and empower you on every future journey.
examples.zh: 將英語當作一位忠實的「終身摯友伴侶」（Companion），它將在未來的每一次旅程中陪伴並賦予你強大力量。

examples.en: A good pocket dictionary and a spiral notebook make excellent companions for solo backpackers.
examples.zh: 一本隨身精緻小字典與一本線圈筆記本，是獨自背起行囊踏上征途的旅人身邊最好的知心同伴。

examples.en: Her rescue dog proved to be an affectionate and faithful companion throughout the years.
examples.zh: 她領養回家的搜救米克斯小狗，在漫長歲月中成為了她生活中最深情貼心且忠誠不渝的良伴。

entries.definition: 伴侶動物；同伴；隨行者；讓英語成為一生相伴、拓展視野之忠實摯友
explains: A person or animal that stays with someone can make a journey or activity less lonely. They may share time and offer comfort. Close friends enjoy spending time together.
During the long train ride, Ana's friend played word games with her. They watched the scenery pass and shared snacks. The trip felt shorter.
A stranger may only meet someone once. A close friend often spends time with that person. Animals can also provide friendship.

examples.en: She won first prize in the English speech competition.
examples.zh: 她在英語演講比賽中榮獲第一名。

examples.en: Fierce market competition led to significant price cuts for consumers.
examples.zh: 激烈的市場競爭為消費者帶來了大幅的價格折扣。

examples.en: Entry into the prestigious design competition is completely free of charge.
examples.zh: 報名參加這項負有盛名的設計競賽是完全免費的。

explains: A contest gives people a chance to try to do better than others at a task or sport. Everyone follows the same rules. Practice can help each person improve.
The school held a drawing contest in the gym. Children showed their pictures and voted for their favorites. Every artist received a kind note.
Playing for fun does not always involve a prize. A contest may have winners, but trying and learning also matter. Fair play makes it enjoyable.

examples.en: Table tennis is a highly competitive sport in Asia.
examples.zh: 桌球在亞洲是一項競爭非常激烈的運動。

examples.en: To stay competitive, businesses must innovate and adopt modern technologies.
examples.zh: 為了保持競爭力，企業必須持續創新並採用現代科技。

examples.en: He has an intensely competitive spirit and always strives to win.
examples.zh: 他擁有極強的好勝心，總是全力爭取勝利。

explains: A person or activity focused on trying to win can be described this way. Players may work hard to improve their skills. They should still treat others fairly.
Noah practiced his serve before the tennis match. He wanted to win, but he shook hands with his opponent afterward. Both players enjoyed the game.
A relaxed game may have no score or prize. A serious contest can make players work harder. Good sportsmanship matters in either case.

examples.en: Every competitor received a ribbon after the race.
examples.zh: 比賽後，每位參賽者都收到一條緞帶。

examples.en: The young competitor practiced for the swimming contest.
examples.zh: 這位年輕的參賽者為游泳比賽練習。

examples.en: Each competitor showed respect for the other players.
examples.zh: 每位競爭者都尊重其他選手。

explains: A person or team taking part in a contest is trying to reach the same goal as others. Each one follows the rules and shows their skill. Some contests have prizes.
Four runners lined up at the track. They waited for the signal and raced toward the finish. Each runner congratulated the others afterward.
A spectator watches a contest, while a participant takes part in it. Several participants may try to win. Fair rules give everyone a chance.

examples.en: Adding too many rules can complicate the game.
examples.zh: 加入太多規則可能使遊戲變複雜。

examples.en: The missing key complicated our search for the room.
examples.zh: 鑰匙不見了，使我們找房間的事情變得更麻煩。

examples.en: Try not to complicate the instructions with extra details.
examples.zh: 盡量不要用額外細節把說明弄得太複雜。

explains: To make a task harder by adding extra parts or problems is to make it less simple. Too many directions can confuse people. Removing unnecessary steps can help.
The recipe was easy until Leo added several extra ingredients. He lost track of what went into the bowl. His sister helped him follow the original steps.
A simple plan has only a few clear steps. A more difficult plan may have many parts to manage. Organizing the work can make it easier.

examples.en: He composed a short song for the school concert.
examples.zh: 他為校園音樂會創作了一首短歌。

examples.en: The student composed a letter to thank her coach.
examples.zh: 學生寫了一封信感謝教練。

examples.en: She composed a melody on the piano after dinner.
examples.zh: 晚餐後，她在鋼琴上譜出一段旋律。

explains: To create a piece of music or writing is to put ideas together in an organized way. A person chooses notes or words to express something. Careful changes can improve the result.
Rina sat at the piano and tried several melodies. She wrote down the notes she liked and added a gentle ending. Her family listened to the new tune.
A song has notes and rhythm, while a letter has words and sentences. Both can be made by choosing and arranging parts. Practice helps a creator improve.

examples.en: The acclaimed composer created a sweeping orchestral soundtrack that moved audiences.
examples.zh: 榮獲多座國際大獎的電影配樂大師譜寫出氣勢恢宏的交響樂原聲配樂，深深觸動了全場觀眾。

examples.en: Film director Christopher Nolan collaborated closely with composer Hans Zimmer on mind-bending scores.
examples.zh: 名導克里斯多福諾蘭與配樂巨擘漢斯季默深度合作，打造出多部震撼寰宇、顛覆感官的經典神曲。

examples.en: The versatile composer blended traditional Taiwanese folk instruments with modern electronic synthesizers.
examples.zh: 這位才華洋溢的配樂作曲大師巧妙將台灣傳統北管嗩吶等民俗樂器，與前衛現代電子合成器完美揉合。

explains: A person who creates music chooses notes and rhythms to make a piece. The music may be written for singers, instruments, or both. Performers later play it for listeners.
A woman wrote a tune for a school play. She tried different notes until the song matched the scene. The children practiced it together.
A singer performs a song, while the music creator makes it. Sometimes one person does both jobs. Music can be written in many styles.

examples.en: The rule of thirds is a foundational composition guideline for visual balance.
examples.zh: 經典的三分法則（九宮格構圖）是構建畫面視覺平衡感與呼吸感最扎實的核心基礎。

examples.en: Creative composition guides the viewer's eye directly to the emotional focal point.
examples.zh: 充滿創意的畫面構圖安排，能巧妙引導觀賞者的視覺視線自然聚焦於核心情感主體。

examples.en: Experimenting with low ground-level perspectives revitalized his urban architectural composition.
examples.zh: 嘗試貼近地面的超低視角貼地拍攝，為他的都會現代建築攝影構圖注入了嶄新活力。

examples.en: Monthly InBody scans track body composition changes in visceral fat and muscle mass.
examples.zh: 每個月定期站上 InBody 身體組成分析儀檢測，能精準掌握內臟脂肪等級與肌肉增長趨勢。

examples.en: Tracking body composition is far more informative than simply staring at numbers on a bathroom scale.
examples.zh: 追蹤身體組成比例的實質變化，遠比每天死盯著體重計上的單純數字更有參考價值。

examples.en: Body recomposition allows beginners to lose stubborn fat while building new muscle tissue at the same time.
examples.zh: 身體組成重組（Recomp）讓重訓新手能夠在減去頑固脂肪的同時同步合成增長新肌肉。

examples.en: Balanced triangular composition draws the viewer's focal eye directly toward the Madonna's serene smile.
examples.zh: 經典穩固的三角形畫面構圖美學，巧妙引導觀賞者的視覺焦點自然凝視在聖母安詳溫柔的微笑上。

examples.en: Photographers practice the rule of thirds to establish compelling composition across landscape horizons.
examples.zh: 專業攝影師熟練運用三分法則（Rule of Thirds）來進行黃金構圖，使壯闊山海地平線更顯張力。

examples.en: The professor praised the high school student's imaginative musical composition for string quartet.
examples.zh: 音樂系教授對這位高中青年學子為弦樂四重奏所譜寫的原創室內樂編制與靈動旋律讚不絕口。

entries.definition: 構圖美學；畫面佈局；作文；身體組成分析 (InBody)；成分構圖；畫面構圖美學；作品成分
explains: Parts arranged together can make a complete piece of writing, music, or art. The order of the parts affects how the whole feels. Creators make choices about what to include.
Lily wrote three paragraphs about her summer trip. She placed the events in order and added a clear ending. Her teacher enjoyed reading it.
A list of ideas is not always a finished piece. Arranging them gives the work a shape. Different arts use different ways to organize parts.

examples.en: Find a quiet corner in the library so you can concentrate.
examples.zh: 在圖書館找個安靜的角落，這樣你才能專注讀書。

examples.en: It is dangerous to text on your smartphone while driving because you cannot concentrate.
examples.zh: 開車行進間低頭滑手機傳訊息極其危險，因為這會使駕駛完全無法集中注意力。

examples.en: Elite athletes concentrate completely on their breathing before the starting pistol fires.
examples.zh: 頂尖運動員在起跑發令槍鳴響前的那一刻，會全神貫注於自己平穩深沉的呼吸。

explains: To give careful attention to one task is to focus on it. Turning off noise can make this easier. Taking a short break may help when someone feels tired.
Eli moved to a quiet table to finish his puzzle. He studied each piece and matched its colors. Soon the picture was complete.
Doing many things at once can make mistakes more likely. Giving attention to one job helps a person notice details. A calm place can support careful work.

examples.en: Studying in short intervals helps maintain sharp mental concentration.
examples.zh: 分段讀書有助於維持敏銳高度的專注力。

examples.en: A sudden loud honk from a truck shattered his concentration during the online exam.
examples.zh: 線上遠距考試進行中，窗外卡車突然傳來的刺耳大喇叭聲打斷了他的高度專注。

examples.en: The chemist measured the exact salt concentration of the saltwater solution.
examples.zh: 化學分析實驗員精確量測並記錄了該鹽水配方溶液中的確切食鹽百分比濃度。

explains: The ability to keep attention on one thing helps a person finish careful work. A quiet place and enough rest can support it. Interruptions may make it harder.
Maya wanted to finish a difficult puzzle. She turned off the television and spread the pieces on a table. After some time, she found where each one fit.
A short glance gives little attention, while steady focus lasts longer. People can build this skill with practice. Breaks help the mind rest.

examples.en: The concept of sharing was easy for the children to understand.
examples.zh: 孩子們很容易理解分享這個概念。

examples.en: We learned a new concept in math today.
examples.zh: 我們今天學了一個新的數學概念。

examples.en: The book explains the concept with simple pictures.
examples.zh: 這本書用簡單的圖片解釋這個概念。

explains: A general idea helps people understand a topic or explain how something works. It may connect many smaller facts. Pictures and examples can make it easier to learn.
The teacher explained the idea of gravity by dropping a ball. The children watched it fall to the floor. They then talked about why objects move downward.
A detail is one small piece of information. A broad idea brings several details together. Examples can show how the idea works in real life.

examples.en: I have a question concerning tomorrow's field trip.
examples.zh: 我有一個關於明天校外教學的問題。

examples.en: The teacher sent a note concerning the homework.
examples.zh: 老師寄了一張關於家庭作業的通知。

examples.en: We read a story concerning a lost puppy.
examples.zh: 我們讀了一個關於迷路小狗的故事。

explains: This word can introduce information about a subject. It tells readers what the next details relate to. A sentence around it helps make the meaning clear.
A note about the school trip listed the bus time and what to bring. Parents read the details before signing the form. Everyone knew where to find the information.
A message may cover several subjects. One phrase can point to the subject being discussed. Clear headings help readers follow the topic.

examples.en: Green concrete made from industrial blast furnace slag cuts manufacturing carbon emissions by forty percent.
examples.zh: 利用高爐爐石粉與飛灰替代部分水泥燒製的低碳綠混凝土，能將建材生產碳排放一口氣大減四成。

examples.en: Construction workers poured fresh concrete into foundational wooden molds to build retaining walls.
examples.zh: 營造工地泥作師傅手持震動棒，將剛出預拌車的均勻泥漿灌漿澆置於地下基礎擋土牆模板之中。

examples.en: The team leader demanded concrete proposals with specific timelines rather than vague conceptual promises.
examples.zh: 專案總監嚴格要求各業務小組提出附帶明確查核里程碑的具體可執行提案，而非空泛抽象的口頭承諾。

examples.en: Specifying low-carbon slag concrete replaces limestone with industrial byproducts, cutting kiln emissions.
examples.zh: 採用添加高爐熟料與飛灰的低碳綠混凝土，能減少石灰石高溫煅燒，大幅降低生產碳排。

examples.en: Curing concrete with captured carbon dioxide permanently mineralizes carbon inside the structural slabs.
examples.zh: 將工廠捕捉的二氧化碳注入混凝土攪拌養護，能將溫室氣體永久礦化封存於建築結構樓板之中。

examples.en: The architect combined low-carbon concrete cores with wooden frames to achieve optimal seismic safety.
examples.zh: 建築大師巧妙將低碳混凝土抗震核心筒與外圍溫潤木構骨架結合，兼顧極致環保與耐震安全。

entries.definition: 低碳環保綠混凝土；混凝土；爐石飛灰低碳環保綠混凝土；具體的
explains: A hard building material is made by mixing cement, water, and other materials. It becomes solid and is used for paths or walls. Workers shape it before it dries.
The builders poured a wet mixture into wooden forms for the new walkway. They smoothed the top and left it to harden. Soon people could walk there.
A wooden path is made from boards, while this material hardens into a solid surface. The word can also mean clear and specific. Nearby words reveal the meaning.

examples.en: The train conductor inspected tickets during the ride.
examples.zh: 列車長在列車行駛途中進行查票。

examples.en: The orchestra conductor raised his baton and the music began.
examples.zh: 管弦樂團指揮揚起指揮棒，美妙的樂音隨即奏響。

examples.en: Copper is widely recognized as an excellent electrical conductor.
examples.zh: 銅被公認為極為優良的導電體。

examples.en: The charismatic orchestra conductor raised the baton and music swelled.
examples.zh: 魅力非凡的樂團指揮家輕輕舉起指揮棒，雄渾樂音隨之奔騰而起。

examples.en: Copper is widely used in electrical cables because it is an excellent conductor.
examples.zh: 金屬銅之所以被廣泛應用於製造電纜導線，是因為它是一種極為優良的導電體。

examples.en: The friendly train conductor punched tickets as the carriage rattled through scenic mountains.
examples.zh: 親切和藹的火車列車長在車廂搖曳穿梭於秀麗青山峽谷時，逐一為旅客驗票剪票。

entries.definition: 列車長；車長；指揮家；導體
explains: A person who leads musicians during a performance shows them when to play and how fast to go. The leader uses hand movements or a small stick. Musicians watch carefully.
At the concert, a woman stood in front of the orchestra. She raised her hands and guided the players through the song. The music ended together.
A train worker who checks tickets and helps passengers can have this title too. The sentence shows which job is meant. Both roles guide others.

examples.en: Scientists met at a conference to share their discoveries.
examples.zh: 科學家在研討會上分享他們的發現。

examples.en: The school conference begins at nine in the morning.
examples.zh: 學校的會議早上九點開始。

examples.en: She gave a talk at the children's book conference.
examples.zh: 她在兒童書籍研討會上發表演講。

explains: A formal meeting brings people together to discuss a subject or share information. It may last for a few hours or several days. Speakers and listeners can learn from one another.
Teachers met in the school hall to talk about reading ideas. Each person shared an activity that worked well. They brought new plans back to their classes.
A casual chat may happen between two friends. A formal meeting often has an agenda and many participants. Clear notes help people remember decisions.

examples.en: She confessed that she had eaten the last cookie.
examples.zh: 她承認自己吃掉了最後一塊餅乾。

examples.en: The boy confessed his mistake to the teacher.
examples.zh: 男孩向老師承認了自己的錯誤。

examples.en: He confessed that he was afraid of the dark.
examples.zh: 他坦承自己怕黑。

explains: To admit that something is true, especially a mistake, is to speak honestly about it. The person may feel nervous but wants to tell what happened. Honesty can help solve a problem.
Owen broke a cup while playing indoors. He told his mother what he had done and offered to help clean up. She thanked him for being truthful.
Hiding a mistake can make it harder to fix. Telling the truth gives others a chance to understand. People can learn from what happened.

examples.en: Scoring high on the English mock test boosted my confidence.
examples.zh: 英文模擬考拿下高分大大提振了我的自信心。

examples.en: Supportive words from her violin mentor restored her shaken artistic confidence.
examples.zh: 小提琴名師由衷的溫暖鼓勵與指點，重新喚醒並重建了她一度動搖的藝術自信。

examples.en: The team gained immense confidence after defeating the reigning city champions.
examples.zh: 在爆冷力克衛冕全市冠軍強隊之後，全體隊員的士氣與信心獲得了空前提升。

examples.en: Speaking with genuine confidence opens international doors that once seemed completely out of reach.
examples.zh: 帶著由衷的「溝通自信」（Confidence）勇敢開口，將為你推開過去看似遙不可及的國際大門。

examples.en: Preparing thoroughly before each presentation will significantly boost your professional confidence.
examples.zh: 在每次上台簡報前做好周全準備，能大幅增強你在專業場合中的表達自信心。

examples.en: Her quiet confidence reassured the entire project team during high-stakes contract discussions.
examples.zh: 她那從容沉穩的自信，在緊要關頭的合約商議中給了整個專案團隊無比的定心丸。

entries.definition: 信心；自信心；勇於開口、無懼出錯之強大英語溝通自信心；自信
explains: Believing that you can do something gives you courage to try. Practice and support from others can help build this feeling. It does not mean every attempt will be perfect.
Before the spelling bee, Rosa practiced each word with her father. She took a deep breath and walked to the front. She felt ready to begin.
Fear may make a person hesitate, while belief in their ability helps them try. Mistakes are part of learning. Encouraging words can help someone keep going.

examples.en: The confusing map caused confusion among the hikers.
examples.zh: 這張令人困惑的地圖讓健行者不知所措。

examples.en: A clear sign helped end the confusion at the station.
examples.zh: 一個清楚的標誌消除了車站裡的混亂。

examples.en: There was confusion about which door to use.
examples.zh: 大家不清楚該走哪一扇門。

explains: When details are hard to understand, a person may not know what to do. Unclear directions can cause this feeling. Asking questions can help make things clear.
The class received two different times for the field trip. Students asked their teacher which one was correct. She checked the note and gave them the right time.
Clear instructions are easy to follow. Mixed or missing information can leave people unsure. Checking the facts can solve the problem.

examples.en: We congratulated Maya on winning the art prize.
examples.zh: 我們祝賀瑪雅贏得美術獎。

examples.en: Please congratulate your brother on his graduation.
examples.zh: 請祝賀你哥哥畢業。

examples.en: The coach congratulated the team after a close game.
examples.zh: 一場激烈的比賽後，教練向隊伍道賀。

explains: To tell someone that you are happy about their success is to offer kind praise. A few warm words can show that you noticed their hard work. People may also give a card or handshake.
After Jamie finished the race, his classmates cheered and told him they were proud. He smiled and thanked them. Their words made the day special.
A complaint points out a problem, while praise recognizes something good. People can celebrate large wins or small steps. Sincere words make others feel valued.

examples.en: Congress met to discuss a new plan for the country.
examples.zh: 國會召開會議，討論一項新的國家計畫。

examples.en: The members of Congress voted on the bill.
examples.zh: 國會議員對這項法案進行表決。

examples.en: She watched a report about Congress on television.
examples.zh: 她在電視上觀看了一則關於國會的報導。

explains: A group of elected people may meet to discuss and make laws for a country. Members speak, ask questions, and vote on ideas. The work can take time.
The news showed leaders meeting in a large hall. They talked about a plan to improve roads and schools. People watched to learn what would happen.
A town council makes decisions for a local area. A national lawmaking group works on rules for the whole country. The name and duties depend on the place.

examples.en: The explorers worked together to conquer the steep mountain trail.
examples.zh: 探險家們合作克服了陡峭的山路。

examples.en: The army tried to conquer the neighboring land.
examples.zh: 軍隊試圖征服鄰近的土地。

examples.en: She conquered her fear of speaking in front of the class.
examples.zh: 她克服了在全班面前說話的恐懼。

explains: To win control over a place or group after a struggle is to defeat its defenders. The word can also describe overcoming a difficult fear or challenge. Effort and courage may be needed.
The story's hero crossed a mountain and reached the castle. After a long battle, the army took control of the fortress. The villagers were finally safe.
A challenge can feel difficult, but practice may help someone overcome it. A contest has a winner and a loser. The context tells which meaning fits.

examples.en: Guided by a clear conscience, the whistleblower exposed corporate corruption despite immense personal risk.
examples.zh: 在清明無愧的內在良心（Conscience）指引下，吹哨者無懼龐大壓力毅然揭發企業高層的貪腐黑幕。

examples.en: He tossed and turned in bed, unable to sleep because a guilty conscience weighed heavily on his chest.
examples.zh: 他整夜在床上輾轉反側無法入眠，因為內心深處那份因說謊而產生的沉重內疚良知折磨著他的良心。

examples.en: Prisoners of conscience are non-violent individuals jailed simply for expressing their peaceful beliefs.
examples.zh: 所謂「良心犯」（Prisoners of Conscience），是指僅因和平表達自身政治理念或信仰而無辜遭極權黑牢監禁的公民。

examples.en: Leaving the abyssal seafloor undisturbed is an urgent moral test of humanity's global ecological conscience.
examples.zh: 讓深海海床維持萬古靜謐不受破壞，是對全體人類守護地球「全球生態道德良知」（Conscience）的重大考驗。

examples.en: He could not in good conscience accept corporate profits earned by exploiting underpaid factory workers.
examples.zh: 他本著自己的道德良心，斷然拒絕接受任何藉由殘酷剝削低薪血汗勞工所賺取的骯髒企業利潤。

examples.en: After confessing his youthful wrongdoing to his parents, he finally felt a clear conscience and peaceful mind.
examples.zh: 在勇敢向父母坦白承認年少時犯下的過錯後，他如釋重負，心中終於恢復了無愧良知的寧靜坦然。

entries.definition: 內在良心良知；道德自覺；守護深海黑暗無聲世界之人類道德生態良知；良心
explains: An inner sense can help a person judge whether an action is right or wrong. It may make someone feel uneasy after doing something unkind. Listening to that feeling can guide better choices.
After taking a toy without asking, Ben felt bad about it. He returned it and told his friend the truth. He decided to ask before borrowing next time.
A rule is written down for everyone to follow. A personal moral sense comes from thinking about fairness and care. Both can guide behavior.

examples.en: One consequence of staying up late was feeling tired at school.
examples.zh: 熬夜的一個後果是上學時感到疲倦。

examples.en: The broken window was a consequence of the wild game indoors.
examples.zh: 窗戶破裂是在室內玩鬧造成的後果。

examples.en: Think about the consequences before you make a choice.
examples.zh: 做決定前要想想可能的後果。

explains: A result that follows an action or event can be expected or surprising. Choices often lead to outcomes. Thinking ahead can help people make wise decisions.
When Lily forgot to water the plant for many days, its leaves drooped. She gave it water and moved it near a window. She learned to follow the care chart.
An action happens first, and an outcome comes afterward. Some outcomes are helpful, and others cause trouble. People can learn from what happens.

examples.en: The consequent delay made us miss the first part of the show.
examples.zh: 因此造成的延誤讓我們錯過了表演的前半段。

examples.en: A power cut and its consequent darkness surprised the campers.
examples.zh: 停電及其隨後而來的黑暗讓露營者很驚訝。

examples.en: The team changed its plan and the consequent result was a win.
examples.zh: 隊伍改變計畫，隨之而來的結果是獲勝。

explains: A result that follows an earlier event happens because something came before it. One change can lead to another. The order of events helps explain the link.
The heavy rain filled the path with puddles. As a result, the children walked through the grass instead. The wet weather changed their route.
A cause happens first, and an effect comes after it. Sometimes several events are connected. Looking closely can show which event led to the next.

examples.en: My conservative grandfather prefers the old family recipes.
examples.zh: 我思想較保守的祖父偏好家族的老食譜。

examples.en: The conservative plan avoided spending too much money.
examples.zh: 這項保守的計畫避免花費太多錢。

examples.en: She holds conservative views about changing the school rules.
examples.zh: 她對修改校規抱持保守看法。

explains: Someone who prefers to keep familiar ways and make changes slowly may be described this way. The word can also name a political view. Context helps show the intended sense.
When the class chose a new game, Mark wanted to keep the rules they already knew. He was careful about trying a different version. His friends explained it first.
Some people enjoy quick changes, while others feel safer with well-known routines. Both can share useful ideas. Listening helps a group decide what works.

examples.en: The team consists of five players and one coach.
examples.zh: 這支隊伍由五位球員和一位教練組成。

examples.en: A healthy breakfast can consist of fruit, bread, and milk.
examples.zh: 健康的早餐可以由水果、麵包和牛奶組成。

examples.en: The story consists of three short chapters.
examples.zh: 這個故事由三個短章節組成。

explains: To be made up of certain parts means those parts form the whole. A team, meal, or story can have several pieces. The parts together create it.
The picnic lunch had bread, fruit, and cheese. Each item was different, but together they made a meal. The family ate beside the lake.
A part belongs to a larger whole. Many parts can be joined to make one thing. A list can show what is included.

examples.en: His consistent practice helped him become a better swimmer.
examples.zh: 他持續穩定的練習幫助他成為更好的游泳選手。

examples.en: The teacher gives consistent instructions every morning.
examples.zh: 老師每天早上都給予一致的指示。

examples.en: Rainfall has been consistent throughout the week.
examples.zh: 這一週的降雨量一直很穩定。

explains: Something that stays the same over time is steady and dependable. A person may follow the same routine each day. Repeating good habits can help someone improve.
Nina practiced her spelling for ten minutes every evening. She kept going even when the words were hard. Soon she made fewer mistakes.
A changing schedule can be hard to predict. A steady pattern is easier to rely on. Regular practice often brings gradual progress.

examples.en: These five chapters constitute the first part of the book.
examples.zh: 這五個章節構成了本書的第一部分。

examples.en: The students constitute half of the audience.
examples.zh: 學生占了觀眾的一半。

examples.en: Small acts of kindness constitute a thoughtful gift.
examples.zh: 一個個小小的善舉構成了一份貼心的禮物。

explains: Several things can together make up a whole group or amount. Each part contributes to what the whole becomes. Counting the parts can show the total.
Three red balls and two blue balls made five balls altogether. The colors were different, but all belonged to the collection. The children counted them twice.
A piece by itself is only part of a set. Several pieces together can form a complete group. The sentence often tells what the parts create.

examples.en: The national constitution guarantees fundamental human rights and freedoms.
examples.zh: 國家根本大法憲法保障全體國民享有基本人權與各項自由權利。

examples.en: Any newly enacted parliamentary law that conflicts with the constitution is deemed void.
examples.zh: 任何由立法機關制定通過之法律若與憲法最高位階原則發生牴觸，依法自始宣告無效。

examples.en: Engaging in regular physical exercise and eating a balanced diet helps strengthen your bodily constitution.
examples.zh: 堅持養成規律運動的良好習慣並攝取營養均衡的原型食物，有助於從根本上強健個人的生理體質。

explains: A country's highest set of laws describes how its government works and what rights people have. Leaders must follow its rules. It can be changed only through special steps.
The class learned that a country's leaders cannot make every rule they want. A founding document sets limits and protects people's rights. The teacher showed a simple example.
An ordinary law covers one issue, while a country's basic legal document guides many laws. Each country may have a different one. It helps organize government.

examples.en: Workers constructed a sturdy steel pedestrian footbridge over the river.
examples.zh: 工人們在河面上修建了一座堅固的鋼骨行人景觀陸橋。

examples.en: Engineers used precast modular blocks to construct the hospital in just three months.
examples.zh: 工程團隊採用預鑄模組化工法，在短短三個月內便迅速建造完成了這間急救醫院。

examples.en: The philosopher tried to construct a coherent theory of social justice.
examples.zh: 這位哲學大師試圖構建出一套自圓其說且邏輯嚴密的社會公平正義理論體系。

explains: To build something by joining materials is to make a structure. People plan the parts and put them together carefully. A strong base can help it stand.
The children used blocks to make a tall tower. They placed wide blocks at the bottom and smaller ones above. Their careful work kept it upright.
Drawing a plan shows what a builder hopes to make. The finished structure comes after the materials are joined. Tools should be used safely.

examples.en: MRT line construction requires careful urban traffic planning.
examples.zh: 捷運新路線的施工興建需要周詳細緻的都市交通維持計畫。

examples.en: The bridge has been closed for repairs and major seismic construction work.
examples.zh: 該座跨海大橋因進行維修檢測與重大耐震補強施工工程而暫時封閉通行。

examples.en: Heavy machinery and cranes operated around the clock during highway construction.
examples.zh: 在高速公路施工期間，各類大型重型機具與起重吊車二十四小時全天候作業運轉。

explains: The work of building or repairing something uses materials and tools. Workers follow a plan to make roads, houses, or bridges. Safety gear protects them on the job.
A crew closed one sidewalk while fixing a broken step. They put up signs to guide people around the work. Soon the path was safe again.
A finished building is the result, while the work of making it takes place over time. Plans show what needs to be done. Many workers may share the tasks.

examples.en: The coach gave constructive advice after the practice game.
examples.zh: 練習賽後，教練提出了有助改進的建議。

examples.en: Their constructive discussion helped improve the project.
examples.zh: 他們具建設性的討論幫助改善了專題。

examples.en: Please offer constructive feedback about my drawing.
examples.zh: 請針對我的畫作提出有助改進的意見。

explains: Helpful ideas can show how to improve a plan or fix a problem. Kind suggestions point to a next step. They help a person learn without being hurtful.
After reading Eli's story, his friend said the ending was fun and suggested adding one more detail. Eli tried the idea and made the story clearer. He thanked his friend.
A rude remark may only make someone feel bad. Useful feedback explains what could work better. Respectful words make it easier to listen.

examples.en: We consulted the map before choosing a hiking trail.
examples.zh: 選擇健行步道前，我們查閱了地圖。

examples.en: You should consult a teacher if the directions are unclear.
examples.zh: 如果指示不清楚，你應該詢問老師。

examples.en: The chef consulted a cookbook to find a new recipe.
examples.zh: 廚師查閱食譜書來尋找新食譜。

explains: To ask someone knowledgeable for advice is to talk with that person before deciding. They may explain choices or answer questions. The person who asks still needs to choose what to do.
Before planting a tree, Maya spoke with a gardener about the sunny side of the yard. The gardener suggested a place with more room. Maya followed the advice.
A quick guess may not be enough for a difficult question. An expert can share useful information. Asking someone does not mean they make every choice.

examples.en: The school hired a consultant to help improve its library.
examples.zh: 學校聘請顧問協助改善圖書館。

examples.en: A food consultant suggested healthier lunch choices.
examples.zh: 一位飲食顧問建議了更健康的午餐選擇。

examples.en: The consultant met with the team to discuss its plans.
examples.zh: 顧問與團隊會面，討論他們的計畫。

explains: A person with special knowledge can give advice to a business or another group. The person studies a problem and suggests possible steps. The group decides what to do next.
A small shop wanted to make its entrance easier to use. It asked a building expert to look at the doorway and suggest changes. The owner chose which ideas to follow.
A regular employee may work on daily tasks in one place. An outside expert may visit to share advice. Both roles can help a group.

examples.en: The family consumed all the soup at dinner.
examples.zh: 全家晚餐時把湯喝光了。

examples.en: A large truck consumes more fuel than a small car.
examples.zh: 大型卡車比小型汽車消耗更多燃料。

examples.en: These lights consume less energy than the old ones.
examples.zh: 這些燈比舊燈消耗更少的能源。

explains: To eat or drink something is to take it into the body. People also use energy or supplies as they do activities. The sentence shows what is being used.
After the long walk, the children ate sandwiches and drank water. The food helped them feel ready to keep exploring. They rested under a tree.
A plant takes in water and light as it grows. A person eats food for energy. Both use things from their surroundings.

examples.en: Smart consumers compare prices across platforms before purchasing.
examples.zh: 聰明的消費者在購物前會在各大平台比價。

examples.en: Consumer protection agencies protect shoppers against deceptive false advertising.
examples.zh: 消費者保護機構全力捍衛消費權益，防範誤導性的虛偽誇大不實廣告。

examples.en: Modern consumers increasingly prefer brands that practice environmental sustainability.
examples.zh: 現代消費者日益偏好選擇落實環境友善與企業永續發展的良心品牌。

explains: A person who buys or uses goods and services chooses what to spend money on. Reading labels can help someone compare products. Careful choices can save money and reduce waste.
At the store, Ben compared two kinds of cereal. He checked the price and read the ingredients before choosing. His parent helped him understand the label.
A maker produces an item, while a buyer takes it home to use. People can also share items instead of buying new ones. Each choice affects what stores offer.

examples.en: Standardized shipping containers revolutionized modern international ocean trade.
examples.zh: 標準化海運貨櫃徹底革新了現代國際遠洋貿易史。

examples.en: Put the leftover food in an airtight plastic container before placing it in the fridge.
examples.zh: 請在將剩菜剩飯放入冰箱保鮮之前，先裝進密封保鮮容器中。

examples.en: Port workers operated giant gantry cranes to stack hundreds of steel containers.
examples.zh: 港口碼頭工人熟練操作巨型門式起重機，將數百只鋼製貨櫃整齊堆疊。

examples.en: Thousands of forty-foot steel containers are loaded onto mega container ships by giant gantry cranes.
examples.zh: 碼頭巨型岸邊橋式起重機以驚人效率將數千只四十呎標準鋼製貨櫃吊裝至兩萬箱級超大型貨櫃輪上。

examples.en: Shipping lines inspect each empty container for floor damage or waterproof leaks prior to releasing it.
examples.zh: 船運航商在放行空貨櫃給出口工廠提領裝貨前，均會仔細檢查櫃底木板完整度與水密密封性。

examples.en: Refrigerated containers, or reefers, maintain precise sub-zero temperatures throughout tropical voyages.
examples.zh: 冷藏冷凍專用貨櫃（Reefer）即便航行於酷熱的熱帶赤道海域，也能一路維持精準零下的保鮮低溫。

examples.en: Standardized steel intermodal shipping containers revolutionized global trade by slashing unloading times.
examples.zh: 標準化鋼製海運貨櫃，大幅縮短了碼頭裝卸時間，徹底掀起全球貿易革命。

examples.en: Over twenty thousand metal containers were stacked on the open deck of the freighter.
examples.zh: 超過兩萬只彩色鋼製貨櫃整齊碼放在這艘巨型遠洋貨輪的開闊甲板上。

examples.en: Customs officials selected thirty import containers for thorough X-ray contraband inspection.
examples.zh: 海關查緝關員抽點了三十只特定進口貨櫃，引導進入高能 X 光大型貨櫃檢驗儀進行掃描查驗。

entries.definition: 貨櫃；集裝箱；容器；標準海運貨櫃；二十呎與四十呎標準海運貨櫃
explains: A box, jar, or other object can hold items inside it. Some keep food fresh, while others carry supplies. A lid can help protect what is stored.
Ava put leftover soup into a glass jar and closed the top tightly. She wrote the date on a label and placed it in the fridge. It stayed covered.
A tray holds objects but may leave them open to air. A closed vessel protects what is inside. Different shapes fit different uses.

examples.en: The contents of the box were wrapped in blue paper.
examples.zh: 盒子裡的物品用藍色紙包著。

examples.en: The website lists the content of each lesson.
examples.zh: 網站列出了每堂課的內容。

examples.en: Please check the contents before closing the bag.
examples.zh: 把袋子關起來前，請檢查裡面的物品。

explains: The things included inside a book, box, or message are what it contains. A list at the beginning of a book can show its sections. The details help readers know what to expect.
The box held crayons, paper, and a small ruler. Mia checked each item before taking it to class. Everything she needed was there.
The outside gives a box its shape, while what is inside makes up its inner items. A book also has ideas and information within its pages. Context guides the meaning.

examples.en: Finding contentment in simple pleasures brings enduring inner tranquility.
examples.zh: 在生活微小的單純美好中尋得由衷的知足，能帶來恆久安詳的內心寧靜。

examples.en: A life of genuine contentment is rarely achieved through material wealth alone.
examples.zh: 真正知足常樂的人生心境，絕非單純依靠累積物質財富便能輕易獲得。

examples.en: The retired artisan sat in his garden, a look of profound contentment on his face.
examples.zh: 退休的老工匠悠然坐在花園裡，臉上洋溢著無比知足平靜的神采。

explains: A calm feeling comes when someone is pleased with what they have. It does not require having everything they want. Enjoying a simple moment can bring peace.
After finishing her drawing, Mira sat by the window and watched the rain. She felt happy with her quiet afternoon. She did not need a new toy to enjoy herself.
Excitement can be loud and brief, while calm satisfaction may last quietly. People find happiness in different ways. Gratitude can help them notice what is good.

examples.en: She entered a contest to design the school mascot.
examples.zh: 她參加了設計校園吉祥物的比賽。

examples.en: The baking contest begins at ten o'clock.
examples.zh: 烘焙比賽十點開始。

examples.en: He won the contest with a clever science project.
examples.zh: 他以巧妙的科學專題贏得比賽。

explains: An organized event lets people try to do something well and see how they compare. There may be judges, rules, and a prize. Taking part can be fun even without winning.
The library held a drawing event for children. They made pictures of their favorite animals, and a panel chose a winner. Everyone's art went on display.
A casual game may have no judges or prize. A formal event can compare people's work. Clear rules help make it fair.

examples.en: Use the context of the story to guess the new word.
examples.zh: 利用故事的上下文來猜新單字。

examples.en: The context makes it clear that she means the river bank.
examples.zh: 上下文清楚表明她指的是河岸。

examples.en: Without context, the short message was hard to understand.
examples.zh: 沒有上下文，這則簡短訊息很難理解。

explains: The words and details around a sentence help show what it means. They can tell who is speaking and what is happening. Readers use them to understand unfamiliar words.
A story said that Sam went to the bank to sit by the water. The nearby words showed it was a riverbank, not a money office. Reading the whole sentence helped.
A single word may have several meanings. The surrounding information points to the intended one. Looking at the whole passage can prevent mistakes.

examples.en: The continual ringing of the phone made it hard to study.
examples.zh: 電話一再響起，讓人很難專心讀書。

examples.en: Continual practice helped the singer improve.
examples.zh: 持續反覆練習幫助歌手進步。

examples.en: The continual rain kept us indoors for several days.
examples.zh: 雨下個不停，讓我們連續好幾天待在室內。

explains: Something that happens again and again may return many times, with breaks in between. The repeated events can be easy to notice. A pattern helps people describe them.
The dog barked every time a delivery truck passed. It became quiet between visits. The family knew when to expect the sound.
A single event happens once. Repeated events happen over and over, often with pauses. A steady pattern can be helpful or annoying.

examples.en: Continuously welded rail eliminates rail joints, banishing click-clack clatter and extending rolling stock life.
examples.zh: 全線鋪設「無縫長焊鋼軌」（Continuously Welded Rail），徹底消除了傳統鐵軌縫隙的喀噠噪音與磨損。

examples.en: Achieving personal mastery in any specialized technical craft demands years of continuous disciplined practice.
examples.zh: 想要在任何特定專業領域達到登峰造極的造詣，皆需要長年累月持之以恆、不間斷的刻苦磨練。

examples.en: The hospital emergency ward operates under continuous twenty-four-hour clinical supervision.
examples.zh: 醫學中心急診重症監護病房始終處於全天候二十四小時不間斷的專業醫師護理團隊監控照護下。

entries.definition: 數百公里無接縫長焊鋼軌 (徹底消除喀噠聲) 的
explains: Something that keeps going without a break is uninterrupted. A line may stretch across a page, or music may play without stopping. The activity continues the whole time.
The river flowed steadily past the bridge all afternoon. It did not stop between the rocks. The children watched it from the bank.
Repeated events may pause between times. An uninterrupted event has no gaps while it lasts. The length depends on the situation.

examples.en: Contrary to our guess, the small team won the match.
examples.zh: 和我們的猜測相反，小隊贏得了比賽。

examples.en: The two reports gave contrary information about the storm.
examples.zh: 兩份報告對暴風雨提供了相反的資訊。

examples.en: Contrary to the sign, the museum was open on Sunday.
examples.zh: 和標示相反，博物館星期日有開放。

explains: An idea that is opposite to another goes in a different direction. People may use it to show a disagreement. Details around the sentence reveal what is being compared.
One sign said the trail was open, but another sign gave the opposite message. The hikers checked with a ranger before choosing a path. They wanted correct information.
Similar ideas point the same way, while opposing ideas differ. People can compare them calmly. More facts may help settle a disagreement.

examples.en: The bright orange sunset forms a dramatic contrast with dark blue mountains.
examples.zh: 明亮的橙色日落與深藍色山巒形成鮮明的對比。

examples.en: In stark contrast to his noisy brother, Mark is soft-spoken and contemplative.
examples.zh: 與吵鬧外向的哥哥形成強烈對比的是，馬克為人說話輕柔且深思熟慮。

examples.en: The essay contrasts life in a crowded metropolis with life in a peaceful farming village.
examples.zh: 這篇專題短文深入對比了繁華擁擠的大都會生活與寧靜質樸的鄉村農莊歲月。

examples.en: Caravaggio mastered dramatic chiaroscuro contrast between piercing stage lights and pitch-black backgrounds.
examples.zh: 義大利巴洛克畫家卡拉瓦喬以大膽極致的明暗對比（Chiaroscuro）技法聞名，宛如舞台聚光燈穿透深邃黑夜。

examples.en: The pure white marble columns formed a breathtaking contrast against the brilliant azure Aegean Sea.
examples.zh: 潔白無瑕的希臘大理石柱雕像群，在湛藍澄澈的愛琴海天幕映襯下形成了令人屏息的鮮明對比。

examples.en: In sharp contrast to yesterday's chilly downpours, today's weather across Taipei turned sunny and crisp.
examples.zh: 與昨日整天淒冷連綿的傾盆大雨形成鮮明反差對照，今日大台北盆地迎來了晴空萬里、微風徐徐的宜人秋意。

entries.definition: 對比；對照；形成對照；明暗強烈對比 (Chiaroscuro)
explains: A clear difference between two things can help people notice how they are unlike. Comparing their colors, sizes, or ideas can show that difference. A picture may use light and dark areas.
One side of the painting was bright yellow, while the other was deep blue. The colors looked very different beside each other. The artist wanted both areas to stand out.
A comparison can show what is alike and what is different. Looking closely focuses on the differences. Both ways of looking can help people understand.

examples.en: Everyone contributed an idea to the class project.
examples.zh: 每個人都為班級專題提供了一個想法。

examples.en: She contributed old books to the library sale.
examples.zh: 她捐出舊書給圖書館義賣。

examples.en: Good sleep can contribute to a student's health.
examples.zh: 良好的睡眠有助於學生的健康。

explains: To give something useful toward a shared effort is to help it succeed. A person may offer time, ideas, or supplies. Many small efforts can make a big difference.
For the class garden, each child brought a seed packet or helped dig. They worked together to plant the flowers. Soon the yard looked colorful.
Keeping everything to yourself does not help a group project. Sharing skills can move the work forward. Each person can help in a different way.

examples.en: Her contribution helped the team finish the poster.
examples.zh: 她的貢獻幫助團隊完成了海報。

examples.en: The library thanked him for his generous contribution of books.
examples.zh: 圖書館感謝他慷慨捐贈書籍。

examples.en: Each contribution made the community garden better.
examples.zh: 每一份付出都讓社區花園變得更好。

explains: Something given to help a group or project is a useful part of the effort. It can be a gift, an idea, or time spent working. Every person's part may be different.
The neighbors repaired the playground together. One person brought paint, another fixed a bench, and others cleaned. Each gift helped improve the space.
A project is made stronger by the parts people share. A large gift is not always more helpful than a small one. What matters is how it meets the need.

examples.en: The store's location is a convenience for busy families.
examples.zh: 這家商店的位置為忙碌的家庭帶來方便。

examples.en: For your convenience, the library has a return box outside.
examples.zh: 為了方便大家，圖書館在外面設置了還書箱。

examples.en: Online maps add convenience to planning a trip.
examples.zh: 線上地圖讓規劃旅行更方便。

explains: A feature that saves time or effort makes something easy to use. People may choose it because it fits their schedule. This can be helpful when life is busy.
A small shop near the bus stop made it easy for Rosa to buy milk on her way home. She did not need to walk far. The location saved time.
A nearby place may be easy to reach, while a distant one takes longer. People compare ease and cost before choosing. A convenient option may not always be the best one.

examples.en: Taipei Comic Exhibition attracts over half a million enthusiastic attendees annually.
examples.zh: 一年一度的台北漫畫博覽會每年皆吸引了超過五十萬名熱血動漫迷朝聖。

examples.en: Comic conventions offer a vibrant meeting place where creators and fans interact.
examples.zh: 各地盛大舉辦的動漫大展為二次元創作者與廣大粉絲搭建起活力四射的交流橋樑。

examples.en: By convention, participants stand during the opening national anthem ceremony.
examples.zh: 依照傳統慣例，全體與會來賓在典禮開場播放國歌的莊嚴時刻皆起立致敬。

examples.en: The UN Convention on the Law of the Sea declares that the international seabed is the common heritage of humanity.
examples.zh: 「聯合國海洋法公約」（Convention），莊嚴宣告公海海底及其礦產資源屬於全人類共同繼承財產。

examples.en: Thousands of software engineers gathered in Taipei for the annual open-source developer convention.
examples.zh: 數千名軟體工程師齊聚台北國際會議中心，盛大參與一年一度的開源軟體開發者技術年會。

examples.en: Defying social convention, she chose to embark on a solo bicycle journey around the globe.
examples.zh: 她毅然打破世俗保守眼光與傳統成見，隻身展開為期兩年的環球單車壯遊冒險。

entries.definition: 動漫大展；大型博覽年會；常規；聯合國海洋法公約 (定義海底為人類共同財產)；公約
explains: A large gathering brings people with a shared interest together to learn and meet. It may include talks, displays, and activities. People often travel to attend.
Fans of comic books met at a city hall for a weekend event. They dressed as favorite characters and visited art tables. Everyone shared stories about the books.
A small meeting may include only a few people. A large gathering can fill a whole building. It may focus on hobbies, business, or shared rules between countries.

examples.en: She chose a conventional white dress for the wedding.
examples.zh: 她為婚禮選了一件傳統的白色洋裝。

examples.en: The shop uses a conventional cash register.
examples.zh: 這家商店使用傳統的收銀機。

examples.en: His conventional approach followed the usual steps.
examples.zh: 他採用傳統的方法，依循一般步驟進行。

explains: A usual or commonly accepted way of doing something follows familiar rules. It may be different from a new or unusual approach. People often recognize it quickly.
The school used the familiar method of raising hands before speaking. A new teacher tried a different signal, but students needed time to learn it. Both approaches helped organize discussion.
An unusual idea may surprise people. A familiar method follows what many expect. The best choice depends on the task.

examples.en: The neighbors conversed while waiting for the bus.
examples.zh: 鄰居們等公車時交談起來。

examples.en: We conversed about our favorite books during lunch.
examples.zh: 午餐時，我們聊起最喜歡的書。

examples.en: She likes to converse with visitors at the museum.
examples.zh: 她喜歡和博物館的訪客交談。

explains: To talk with someone by sharing ideas and listening to replies is to have a conversation. People take turns speaking. Friendly questions can keep the talk going.
Two cousins sat on the porch and talked about their summer plans. One asked questions while the other answered. They learned what each hoped to do.
A speech is mostly one person talking to a group. A conversation lets people respond to one another. Listening is just as important as speaking.

examples.en: Her smile conveyed how happy she felt.
examples.zh: 她的笑容傳達了她有多開心。

examples.en: The sign conveys an important message to drivers.
examples.zh: 這個標誌向駕駛傳達重要訊息。

examples.en: He used a drawing to convey his idea to the class.
examples.zh: 他用一張圖向全班表達自己的想法。

explains: To carry a message or feeling from one person to another is to communicate it. Words, pictures, or actions can share the idea. Clear signals help people understand.
The coach drew arrows on a board to show the new play. The players looked at the picture and asked questions. They understood where to move.
A listener receives a message, while a speaker sends it. A smile may show happiness without words. Different ways of sharing can work together.

examples.en: The scientist presented solid data to convince the committee.
examples.zh: 科學家提出了扎實確鑿的數據以讓委員會信服。

examples.en: I tried hard to convince him that daily exercise boosts mental clarity.
examples.zh: 我費盡唇舌努力想使他確信，維持規律的每日運動能大幅提升大腦思緒清晰度。

examples.en: The jury was fully convinced of the defendant's complete innocence after hearing the alibi.
examples.zh: 在聽取了無可辯駁的不在場證明後，陪審團完全確信被告在法律上是毫無罪責的。

explains: To help someone believe an idea is true, a person can give reasons and evidence. The listener thinks about what is said before deciding. A strong reason can change someone's mind.
Nora wanted her family to visit the science museum. She showed them a page about the planet show and explained why she liked it. They agreed to go.
An opinion shares what someone thinks, while evidence supports a claim. People may still disagree after listening. Respectful talk lets them compare ideas.

examples.en: The children cooperated to clean up the classroom.
examples.zh: 孩子們合作整理教室。

examples.en: Please cooperate with your partner during the science activity.
examples.zh: 科學活動期間，請和夥伴合作。

examples.en: The two teams cooperated to rescue the lost dog.
examples.zh: 兩支隊伍合作救回了迷路的小狗。

explains: To work together toward the same goal means people share tasks and help one another. They listen and follow agreed rules. Teamwork can make a hard job easier.
The students wanted to build a paper bridge. Some folded the paper, and others tested how many coins it could hold. They improved it together.
Doing a task alone gives one person all the work. Sharing jobs lets a group use different skills. Clear talk helps everyone know what to do.

examples.en: Cooperation between the students made the project successful.
examples.zh: 學生之間的合作讓專題順利完成。

examples.en: The rescue required cooperation from many neighbors.
examples.zh: 這次救援需要許多鄰居合作。

examples.en: Good cooperation helps a team solve problems.
examples.zh: 良好的合作有助於團隊解決問題。

explains: When people work together and help one another, they share effort toward a common goal. Each person may do a different task. Respect helps the group succeed.
The neighbors planned a block party. One family brought tables, another set up games, and others made snacks. Everyone enjoyed the event.
Working against one another can slow a task down. Sharing jobs and listening can help a group finish. A common goal brings people together.

examples.en: Local fruit cooperatives bundle harvest volumes to negotiate better wholesale market prices.
examples.zh: 地區頂級芒果產銷合作社集結全體產銷班社員產能，在台北第一果菜批發市場爭取最佳拍賣拍價。

examples.en: Joining an agricultural cooperative gives smallholders shared access to expensive sorting machinery.
examples.zh: 加入農業產銷合作社讓資源有限的小農得以共同出資使用高科技光波甜度篩選與自動分級機。

examples.en: The students formed a cooperative study group to tackle challenging calculus assignments together.
examples.zh: 大學同學們自發組成了一個互助合作讀書會，同心協力攻克艱澀繁複的微積分作業習題。

entries.definition: 農業產銷合作社；合作的
explains: People who are willing to work together and share tasks are ready to help the group. They listen to others and do their part. Such teamwork can reach a shared goal.
The class made a large map of the town. Each student drew one street and added its name. They joined the pages together.
Someone who refuses to help may slow a group down. A willing teammate shares ideas and effort. Everyone can take a turn leading.

examples.en: He learned to cope with homesickness by calling his family.
examples.zh: 他透過打電話給家人，學會應對思鄉之情。

examples.en: She coped with the long wait by reading a book.
examples.zh: 她靠讀書來打發漫長的等待。

examples.en: The team found a way to cope with the sudden rain.
examples.zh: 隊伍找到應付突然降雨的方法。

explains: To manage a difficult feeling or situation is to find a way to get through it. People may ask for help or take one step at a time. Useful strategies differ for each person.
Before her first day at a new school, Ana felt nervous. She packed her bag the night before and talked with her mother. Having a plan helped her feel ready.
A problem may not disappear right away. Small actions can make it easier to face. Trusted people can offer support.

examples.en: The copper wire carried electricity to the small lamp.
examples.zh: 銅線把電力傳到小燈泡。

examples.en: The old pot was made of copper.
examples.zh: 那只舊鍋是用銅製成的。

examples.en: A copper coin fell from his pocket.
examples.zh: 一枚銅幣從他的口袋掉了出來。

explains: A reddish-brown metal is used for wires, pipes, and some coins. It can carry electricity well. Over time, air and water may change its color.
The old roof had a greenish layer in some places. The teacher explained that the metal underneath had changed after many years outside. The roof still kept the rain out.
Wood does not carry electric current in the same way this metal does. Different materials have different uses. Workers choose them for the job.

examples.en: He tied the package with a red cord.
examples.zh: 他用紅色細繩綁好包裹。

examples.en: The lamp's cord reached the wall outlet.
examples.zh: 燈具的電線延伸到牆上的插座。

examples.en: A strong cord held the tent in place during the wind.
examples.zh: 強韌的繩索在起風時固定住帳篷。

explains: A thick string made of several strands twisted together can tie or connect things. It may hold a tent or carry power to a device. People should keep it neat and safe.
The camper tied a strong rope around the tent pole. It kept the fabric steady in the wind. She checked the knot before going to sleep.
Thin thread can sew a button, while a thicker line can hold a heavier object. Some lines are made of cloth, and others contain wires. The purpose tells which kind is meant.

examples.en: The pen pals correspond by email every week.
examples.zh: 這兩位筆友每週都用電子郵件通信。

examples.en: The numbers on the map correspond to the names in the key.
examples.zh: 地圖上的數字和圖例中的名稱相對應。

examples.en: We corresponded with the museum to ask about its hours.
examples.zh: 我們寫信給博物館詢問開放時間。

explains: To write letters or messages back and forth with someone is to stay in touch over time. The people may live far apart. Each reply continues the exchange.
Mia wrote to her cousin in another country every month. Her cousin sent photos and stories in return. They learned about each other's lives.
A quick greeting may happen once. A regular exchange continues through many messages. People can also share ideas by email.

examples.en: Indigenous dancers wore vibrant, handcrafted traditional tribal costumes.
examples.zh: 原住民舞者身著色彩鮮豔純手工製作的傳統族服。

examples.en: Elementary kids dressed up in superhero and wizard costumes for Halloween.
examples.zh: 國小學童在萬聖節派對上紛紛換上超級英雄與神秘巫師的趣味裝扮。

examples.en: Hand-embroidered silk costumes used in Taiwanese opera are dazzling works of textile art.
examples.zh: 歌仔戲表演所穿著的手工刺繡真絲戲服，是令人賞心悅目的刺繡藝術品。

examples.en: Custom-tailored cosplay costumes require meticulous sewing and lightweight foam crafting.
examples.zh: 量身訂製的高還原度 Cosplay 服裝需要極為細膩精密的裁縫工藝與輕量泡棉剪裁。

examples.en: Children dressed in spooky Halloween costumes knocked on doors asking for sweet candy.
examples.zh: 小朋友們換上搞怪逗趣的萬聖節戲服，成群結隊挨家挨戶敲門高喊不給糖就搗蛋。

examples.en: The theater production hired award-winning designers to create period-accurate stage costumes.
examples.zh: 這部百老匯舞台劇特聘頂級獲獎設計師，為全體演員量身打造貼合時代背景的精緻戲服。

entries.definition: 傳統服飾；戲服；化裝舞會服；角色扮演戲服；全套裝扮
explains: Special clothes can help someone look like a character or fit a performance. They may be worn on stage or at a party. Some outfits show a tradition or time period.
For the school play, Eli wore a long coat and a paper crown. He practiced his lines while dressed as the king. His friends helped adjust the sleeves.
Everyday clothes are chosen for comfort and daily tasks. Special outfits can help tell a story or celebrate an event. People should treat cultural clothing respectfully.

examples.en: They rented a cottage beside the lake for the weekend.
examples.zh: 他們週末租了一間湖邊的小屋。

examples.en: The stone cottage had a bright garden outside.
examples.zh: 那間石造小屋外有一座明亮的花園。

examples.en: Grandma's cottage is surrounded by tall trees.
examples.zh: 奶奶的小屋四周都是高大的樹木。

explains: A small simple house, often found in the countryside, may have a garden and a cozy feel. It can be used as a home or a holiday place. The exact style varies.
The family stayed in a little house beside a field of flowers. They ate breakfast on the porch and watched birds in the trees. The village was quiet.
A large city building may hold many families in separate homes. A small country home usually has fewer rooms. Both provide shelter.

examples.en: The city council approved the new metro construction budget.
examples.zh: 市議會審議通過了全新捷運建設的預算案。

examples.en: Members of the student council organized the annual autumn campus festival.
examples.zh: 學生自治會幹部一手籌劃並組織了一年一度熱鬧的秋季校園祭。

examples.en: The local advisory council meets every month to discuss urban zoning.
examples.zh: 地方都市諮詢委員會每月定期集會，深入探討市區土地重劃規劃。

explains: A group of people chosen to make decisions for a town, school, or organization meets to discuss shared issues. Members listen and vote. Their choices affect the group.
The student leaders met after class to plan a dance. They discussed music, snacks, and a safe place to hold it. Each person shared an idea.
One leader makes decisions alone, while a group can consider many views. Rules guide how members take turns. Meetings help them plan together.

examples.en: Please place your chosen items on the checkout counter.
examples.zh: 請將挑選好的商品放置於結帳櫃檯上。

examples.en: We sat at the kitchen counter enjoying hot fresh pancakes.
examples.zh: 我們坐在廚房吧檯享受熱騰騰的現做鬆餅。

examples.en: The defense lawyer presented strong evidence to counter the prosecution's claim.
examples.zh: 辯護律師提出了有力證據來反駁檢方的指控。

examples.en: Passengers queued politely at the airline check-in counter to drop baggage.
examples.zh: 準備出國的旅客在航空公司劃位報到櫃檯前井然有序排隊，辦理託運行李手續。

examples.en: The customer service counter is on the ground floor next to the information desk.
examples.zh: 客服諮詢服務櫃檯位於一樓大廳，緊鄰旅客服務中心服務台。

examples.en: He leaned against the kitchen counter while sipping his freshly brewed morning coffee.
examples.zh: 他一邊放鬆地靠在廚房流理台料理吧檯邊，一邊細細品味剛沖泡好的熱咖啡。

entries.definition: 櫃檯；相反方向地；報到櫃檯；反駁
explains: A long flat surface in a shop or kitchen can be used to serve people or prepare food. A worker may stand behind it. The setting helps show which kind it is.
At the bakery, Mia placed a loaf on the wooden surface near the cashier. The worker wrapped it and took her payment. She thanked him before leaving.
A table can stand in the middle of a room, while a service surface often sits near a wall. In a contest, this word can also mean something that opposes another action. Context matters.

examples.en: The courageous firefighter rescued a puppy from the smoke.
examples.zh: 勇敢的消防員從煙霧中救出一隻小狗。

examples.en: It was courageous of her to speak up for her friend.
examples.zh: 她勇敢地為朋友挺身而出。

examples.en: The courageous climber kept going despite the cold wind.
examples.zh: 勇敢的登山者不畏寒風，繼續前進。

explains: Someone who faces danger or fear with strength can be brave. Being brave does not mean feeling no fear. A person may act carefully while still feeling nervous.
A child heard a kitten crying under a porch. She told an adult, who helped lift the loose board safely. Together they brought the kitten out.
Running into danger without thinking can be unsafe. Taking a careful step to help someone can show bravery. Asking for help is also a strong choice.

examples.en: As a courtesy, she held the door for the person behind her.
examples.zh: 出於禮貌，她替身後的人扶住門。

examples.en: The waiter treated every guest with courtesy.
examples.zh: 服務生有禮貌地對待每位客人。

examples.en: Please show courtesy to others while waiting in line.
examples.zh: 排隊時請有禮貌地對待他人。

explains: Polite behavior shows care and respect for other people. Saying please, holding a door, or taking turns are examples. Small acts can make shared spaces pleasant.
At the library, Owen waited while another child finished using the computer. He thanked the librarian when it was his turn. Everyone had a chance to use it.
Rude actions can make others uncomfortable. Thoughtful manners show that people notice one another. Different places may have different customs.

examples.en: The story's coward ran away when his friends needed help.
examples.zh: 故事中的懦夫在朋友需要幫助時逃跑了。

examples.en: He called the bully a coward for picking on smaller children.
examples.zh: 他罵那個霸凌者是懦夫，因為他欺負較小的孩子。

examples.en: The coward finally admitted that he was afraid.
examples.zh: 那個膽小鬼最後承認自己害怕。

explains: A person who lets fear stop them from doing what is right may be called this unkind name. It is better to describe the action than insult the person. Everyone feels afraid sometimes.
In the story, a boy hid when his friend needed help. Later he felt sorry and went back with an adult. He learned that asking for help was possible.
Bravery does not mean never feeling fear. It means choosing a careful helpful action even when nervous. People can practice courage in small ways.

examples.en: The sudden burst of first crack signals that internal moisture steam is fracturing the bean's cellular walls.
examples.zh: 烘豆鍋爐內傳來劈啪清脆的第一爆，宣告內部水蒸氣撐破細胞壁釋放迷人芳香。

examples.en: The roaster reduced burner power right at the start of first crack to extend the caramel development phase.
examples.zh: 烘豆師在一爆初響的黃金瞬間精準關小瓦斯火力，以平穩延長焦糖化反應的風味發展期。

examples.en: Listening for the distinct pops of first crack guides decisions on when to drop light-roast specialty lots.
examples.zh: 屏氣凝神聆聽第一爆密集爆鳴聲的起伏節奏，是決定淺焙精品豆何時出鍋下豆的最關鍵聲學指引。

entries.definition: 烘焙一爆密集聲 (First Crack 芳香爆發)；裂紋
explains: A thin line can appear when something hard splits but does not break all the way through. A loud sharp sound can also be described this way. The context shows which meaning is intended.
A ball hit the window and left a narrow line in the glass. The family kept away from it and called someone to repair it. They did not touch the broken area.
A whole surface has no split line. A broken object may fall into pieces. A sharp noise is heard rather than seen.

examples.en: We made a paper craft for the holiday fair.
examples.zh: 我們為節慶園遊會做了一件紙藝作品。

examples.en: The craft of weaving baskets takes patience.
examples.zh: 編織籃子的手藝需要耐心。

examples.en: She enjoys craft activities like sewing and painting.
examples.zh: 她喜歡縫紉和繪畫等手工活動。

explains: Making something by hand with skill can use paper, clay, cloth, or wood. People may create decorations, toys, or useful items. Careful work makes each piece special.
The children cut colored paper and folded it into stars. They hung the stars across the classroom for the winter party. Each one looked a little different.
A factory machine can make many copies quickly. Hand work often takes more time and includes personal choices. Both can create useful things.

examples.en: The clay bowl was her first creation in art class.
examples.zh: 這個陶碗是她在美術課上的第一件作品。

examples.en: His latest creation is a song about friendship.
examples.zh: 他最新創作的是一首關於友誼的歌。

examples.en: The artist displayed her creations in the town hall.
examples.zh: 藝術家在市政廳展出她的作品。

explains: Something newly made by a person can be an object, story, song, or picture. It begins as an idea and takes shape through work. Each maker has their own style.
After drawing several sketches, Leo painted a picture of a dragon. He added bright scales and a long tail. His new artwork hung in the hallway.
A natural object grows without being made by a person. A handmade item comes from someone's effort. Both can be beautiful in different ways.

examples.en: Hands-on art activities spark children's unbounded imagination and creativity.
examples.zh: 動手做的美術勞作活動能激發孩子們無限的想像力與創造力。

examples.en: Solving intricate engineering challenges requires both technical rigor and boundless creativity.
examples.zh: 破解複雜棘手的工程技術瓶頸，既需要嚴謹的科學推導，亦仰賴無窮的創新創造力。

examples.en: The advertising firm values divergent thinking and boundless artistic creativity.
examples.zh: 這家知名頂尖廣告公司極為重視發散思維與員工源源不絕的原創藝術創造力。
