A diver sees a large structure under the sea. Many tiny animals built it over a long time. Fish swim around it.
A shirt has a soft pink-orange shade. The color resembles some sea growth. The same noun can name this color.

examples.en: The detectives found a corpse near the river.
examples.zh: 偵探在河邊發現一具屍體。

examples.en: The novel begins when a corpse is discovered.
examples.zh: 這本小說從發現一具屍體開始。

examples.en: The corpse was taken to the hospital for an examination.
examples.zh: 屍體被送到醫院進行檢查。

explains: This noun means the body of a dead person or animal. It is most often used in serious or formal situations. News and crime stories may use it.
Police find a dead body after a crime. They keep the area closed while they investigate. The noun names the body.
A large animal dies in the forest. Other animals may come near it. The same word can refer to a dead animal’s body.

examples.en: Their correspondence continued for many years.
examples.zh: 他們的通信持續了許多年。

examples.en: The file contains correspondence between the two offices.
examples.zh: 檔案裡有兩個辦公室之間的往來信件。

examples.en: There is a close correspondence between the map and the road.
examples.zh: 地圖和道路之間高度吻合。

explains: This noun means letters or messages exchanged between people. It can also mean a close match between two things. The word often sounds formal.
A student writes to a pen pal in another country. They send letters to each other every month. Their written messages form an exchange.
A map shows a line that matches a road on the ground. The two lines agree closely. The noun can describe this match.

examples.en: She made a cosmetic change to the room.
examples.zh: 她稍微改變了房間的外觀。

examples.en: The doctor explained the cosmetic procedure.
examples.zh: 醫師說明了這項美容療程。

examples.en: He bought a cosmetic to cover a small mark.
examples.zh: 他買了一件化妝品來遮住小斑點。

explains: This adjective describes something used to improve appearance rather than treat a serious problem. It can also describe a small change that affects how something looks. As a noun, it can mean a beauty product.
A person uses cream to make skin look smoother. It changes the appearance for a while. It does not cure an illness.
A company changes the color of its website but keeps its services the same. The change is only about how it looks. The adjective describes this kind of change.

examples.en: The store sells cosmetics from many brands.
examples.zh: 這家商店販售許多品牌的化妝品。

examples.en: She packed her cosmetics in a small bag.
examples.zh: 她把化妝品裝進一個小包裡。

examples.en: Some cosmetics are made for sensitive skin.
examples.zh: 有些化妝品是為敏感肌膚設計的。

explains: This plural noun means products used to improve or change the appearance of the face or body. It includes items such as lipstick and face powder. People choose them for different reasons.
A person puts colored cream on the lips before going out. Another uses powder to reduce shine. These products are sold in a beauty shop.
A store keeps brushes, eye color, and skin products on one shelf. Customers can test some items. The plural noun names this group of products.

examples.en: The manager spoke with her counterpart in the other office.
examples.zh: 經理和另一間辦公室的同職位主管交談。

examples.en: The local law has no exact counterpart abroad.
examples.zh: 國外沒有完全對應的當地法律。

examples.en: He met his counterpart at the conference.
examples.zh: 他在會議上見到了職務相同的人。

explains: This noun means a person or thing with the same role in another place or group. It can also mean something that matches another item. The two sides are similar in function.
A teacher visits a school in another city. She meets the teacher who has the same job there. The two workers share a role.
A phone model has a matching version made by another company. The products serve the same purpose. The noun can name the matching item.

examples.en: You can redeem this electronic discount coupon on your app.
examples.zh: 您可以在手機 App 上兌換這張電子折價券。

examples.en: Clip the paper coupons from the weekly grocery circular to save money.
examples.zh: 剪下每週超市促銷傳單上的紙本折價券以節省開銷。

examples.en: The restaurant gave each diner a buy-one-get-one-free dessert coupon.
examples.zh: 餐廳贈送每位用餐客人一張甜點買一送一優惠券。

explains: This noun means a paper or digital ticket that gives a lower price or special offer. A store may set a date or limit for its use. It can help a customer save money.
A shopper shows a code on a phone at checkout. The price of soap goes down. The offer only works this week.
A magazine includes a small paper slip for a discount. The customer cuts it out and takes it to a shop. The noun names this offer.

examples.en: Generations of families gather under the open courtyard of the brick Sanheyuan during festivals.
examples.zh: 逢年過節全家族老少齊聚在閩南紅磚三合院開闊的門前埕斗（Courtyard）擺設流水席，共享天倫之樂。

examples.en: Cool mountain breezes circulate naturally through the central courtyard, keeping the rooms fresh in summer.
examples.zh: 夏日傍晚清涼的山風在傳統院落的三合院中庭天井間自然對流穿梭，讓各個廂房即便不開冷氣也十分涼爽。

examples.en: We set up banquet tables across the brick courtyard to celebrate Grandma's ninetieth birthday.
examples.zh: 我們在紅磚合院開闊的門埕上擺開數十張總鋪師大紅辦桌，全庄熱鬧歡慶阿嬤的九十大壽。

entries.definition: 傳統三合院埕斗天井；中庭
explains: This noun means an open area surrounded by buildings or walls. It may be found inside a home, school, or public building. People use it to rest or walk outside.
A house has a small open space in the middle. Rooms face toward it. Sunlight reaches the plants there.
Students sit outside between classes. The area is surrounded by school buildings. The noun names this outdoor space.

examples.en: It was cowardly to blame someone who could not answer.
examples.zh: 把責任推給無法回應的人是懦弱的行為。

examples.en: The cowardly thief ran when the lights came on.
examples.zh: 燈亮起時，懦弱的小偷逃跑了。

examples.en: She called the attack cowardly and unfair.
examples.zh: 她稱這次攻擊既懦弱又不公平。

explains: This adjective describes someone who lacks courage when facing danger or difficulty. It can also describe an action that is unfair because a person avoids a direct fight. The word criticizes behavior.
A person leaves a friend behind when danger appears. The friend expected help. Others may call this action weak and unfair.
A bully hurts someone when no one is watching and then hides. The behavior avoids taking responsibility. The adjective describes this kind of action.

examples.en: The small bedroom feels warm, quiet, and cozy during winter.
examples.zh: 這間小臥室在冬天讓人感到溫暖、寧靜且溫馨愜意。

examples.en: We sat in a cozy corner of the vintage cafe reading novels and sipping tea.
examples.zh: 我們坐在這家復古咖啡館溫馨的一角看小說、喝熱茶。

examples.en: Put on a pair of cozy fleece slippers after kicking off your work boots.
examples.zh: 脫下工作皮靴後，換上一雙暖和舒適的刷毛室內拖鞋。

explains: This adjective describes a place that feels warm, comfortable, and pleasant. It can also describe a close and friendly feeling. The word is common for rooms and small homes.
A small room has soft chairs, warm light, and a blanket. A person enjoys reading there on a rainy day. The room feels comfortable.
Friends sit close together around a table and talk quietly. The setting feels welcoming. The adjective describes this warm atmosphere.

examples.en: The city announced a crackdown on illegal parking.
examples.zh: 市政府宣布嚴格取締違法停車。

examples.en: The crackdown led to several arrests.
examples.zh: 這波強力打擊行動造成數人被捕。

examples.en: Officials began a crackdown on fake medicine.
examples.zh: 官員開始嚴厲打擊假藥。

explains: This noun means a strong effort by authorities to stop illegal or unwanted behavior. It often includes stricter rules, checks, or punishments. The action may target crime or rule breaking.
Police inspect cars after many unsafe races occur. Drivers who break the law receive tickets. The enforcement becomes much stricter.
A school begins checking bags after students bring banned items. The new checks aim to stop the behavior. The noun names this strong action.

examples.en: She ate a cracker with a slice of cheese.
examples.zh: 她吃了一片餅乾，配上一片起司。

examples.en: The children pulled a party cracker together.
examples.zh: 孩子們一起拉開了派對拉炮。

examples.en: He used a nut cracker to open the shell.
examples.zh: 他用堅果夾打開外殼。

explains: This noun can mean a thin, dry, crisp food often eaten with cheese or soup. It can also mean a device that makes a loud noise or something that breaks a hard shell. Context shows the meaning.
A child eats a small flat snack with cheese. It breaks with a dry sound. The food is simple and not sweet.
A holiday party uses a paper tube that pops when pulled. A nut tool can also open a hard shell. The noun has several uses.

examples.en: He tried to cram all the clothes into one suitcase.
examples.zh: 他試著把所有衣服塞進一個行李箱。

examples.en: I had to cram for the test last night.
examples.zh: 我昨晚只好臨時抱佛腳準備考試。

examples.en: The small bus was crammed with passengers.
examples.zh: 小巴士裡擠滿了乘客。

explains: This verb means to push many things into a small space. It can also mean to study a lot in a short time, often before a test. The action is rushed or crowded.
A student puts too many books into one bag. The zipper barely closes. The items have been forced into the small space.
A learner reads notes late the night before an exam. There is little time to review. The verb describes this hurried study.

examples.en: A cramp in my leg woke me up.
examples.zh: 我腿部的抽筋把我痛醒了。

examples.en: The tight shoes cramped her toes.
examples.zh: 太緊的鞋子擠壓了她的腳趾。

examples.en: He stopped running because of a cramp.
examples.zh: 他因為抽筋而停止跑步。

explains: This noun means a sudden painful tightening in a muscle. It can make movement difficult for a short time. As a verb, it can mean to limit space or freedom.
A runner stops and holds one leg after a race. The muscle feels tight and painful. It may take a few minutes to relax.
A crowded desk leaves little room for a person to write. The lack of space makes work harder. The verb can describe this limitation.

examples.en: The hikers stood near the edge of the crater.
examples.zh: 健行者站在火山口邊緣附近。

examples.en: A meteor made a crater on the moon.
examples.zh: 隕石在月球上撞出了一個坑洞。

examples.en: The old volcano has a broad crater.
examples.zh: 這座古老火山有一個寬闊的火山口。

explains: This noun means a large bowl-shaped hole in the ground. It may be made by a volcano or by an object from space hitting the earth. The surface around it can be rough.
A volcano erupts and leaves a deep round hole at its top. Steam rises from the opening. Visitors can see the rim from far away.
A space rock strikes the moon and leaves a wide hollow mark. There is no water inside it. The noun names this kind of hole.

examples.en: The witness gave a credible account of the event.
examples.zh: 證人對事件提出了可信的說明。

examples.en: Her explanation sounded credible to the group.
examples.zh: 她的解釋聽起來讓大家信服。

examples.en: The report offered credible evidence.
examples.zh: 這份報告提供了可信的證據。

explains: This adjective describes something that seems likely to be true or believable. A person may be trusted because of knowledge or honesty. Evidence can make an account seem stronger.
A witness gives a clear account and has no reason to lie. The details match what others saw. People believe the story.
A news report names its sources and shows proof. Readers can check the facts. The adjective describes information that seems trustworthy.

examples.en: A crocodile rested on the riverbank.
examples.zh: 一隻鱷魚在河岸上休息。

examples.en: The guide warned us to stay away from the crocodile.
examples.zh: 導遊提醒我們遠離那隻鱷魚。

examples.en: A crocodile can swim with its tail.
examples.zh: 鱷魚能用尾巴游泳。

explains: This noun names a large reptile with a long body, strong tail, and powerful jaws. It lives in rivers and wetlands in warm parts of the world. It often waits quietly near water.
A large animal lies still beside a river. Only its eyes and nose show above the water. It can move quickly to catch prey.
A young one leaves the nest and follows its mother toward a pond. Its skin is covered with hard scales. The reptile grows very large.

examples.en: Use the crossing to reach the other side of the street.
examples.zh: 請走行人穿越道到街道另一側。

examples.en: The ferry crossing took twenty minutes.
examples.zh: 渡輪航程花了二十分鐘。

examples.en: A crossing guard helped the children cross safely.
examples.zh: 導護人員協助孩子們安全過馬路。

explains: This noun means a place where people or vehicles can go from one side to another. It often refers to a marked area on a road or a route over water. It can also name the act of moving across.
A person waits for the light before walking across a busy street. White lines show where to go. Cars stop to let people pass.
A boat carries people from one side of a river to the other. The trip takes a few minutes. The noun can name this journey.

examples.en: He used crutches while his ankle healed.
examples.zh: 腳踝復原期間，他使用拐杖行走。

examples.en: She placed one crutch beside the chair.
examples.zh: 她把一支拐杖放在椅子旁。

examples.en: The speaker used his notes as a crutch.
examples.zh: 那位講者過度依賴筆記。

explains: This is a support that helps someone walk when a leg is hurt. The person holds it while taking steps. It carries some of their weight.
A person with a broken leg may use two long supports to move around. Each has a handle for the hand. The supports help the person keep weight off the injured leg.
The word can also mean something a person relies on too much. A student may always read from notes instead of learning to speak freely. The notes become a way to avoid doing the harder task.

examples.en: The bear cub slept beside its mother.
examples.zh: 小熊睡在媽媽身旁。

examples.en: Two lion cubs played in the grass.
examples.zh: 兩隻小獅子在草地上玩耍。

examples.en: A fox cub peered out of the den.
examples.zh: 一隻小狐狸從洞穴裡向外張望。

explains: This is a young animal such as a bear, lion, or fox. It is smaller than its parents. Its mother may feed and protect it.
A baby bear may stay close to its mother in the forest. It plays and learns how to find food. This word names the young animal.
A young lion may play with others of its own age. Its soft fur may have spots. It grows into a large cat as it gets older.

examples.en: She sliced a cucumber for the salad.
examples.zh: 她切了一條小黃瓜做沙拉。

examples.en: We grow cucumbers beside the fence.
examples.zh: 我們在圍籬旁種小黃瓜。

examples.en: The sandwich had thin cucumber slices inside.
examples.zh: 三明治裡夾著薄薄的小黃瓜片。

explains: This is a long vegetable with green skin and a pale inside. It contains a lot of water. People often slice it into salads.
You can cut this green food into thin rounds. The inside has small seeds. It tastes mild and feels crisp when fresh.
This plant grows along the ground or climbs a support. Its long fruits can be eaten fresh. Some are kept in salty or sour liquid to make pickles.

examples.en: Organic tea growers cultivate heirloom bushes using natural compost and mountain spring irrigation.
examples.zh: 堅持友善大地的有機茶農以天然堆肥與甘冽山泉水悉心灌溉茶樹，在天地滋養下涵育頂級茶菁。

examples.en: Reading classic literature from around the world helps cultivate critical thinking and emotional depth.
examples.zh: 廣泛閱讀世界古典文學與哲學經典名作，有助於涵養青年的獨立批判性思維與深厚的人文同理心。

examples.en: Forward-thinking companies actively cultivate collaborative working cultures where constructive dissent is welcomed.
examples.zh: 具備前瞻遠見的跨國企業主動培育包容開放的協作文化，由衷鼓勵員工提出多元具建設性的不同聲音。

entries.definition: 細心栽種茶樹；涵養品味
explains: This means to prepare land and grow plants on it. A farmer may loosen the soil and plant seeds. The work helps crops grow.
Someone can care for plants over a long period. They may give the plants water and remove unwanted growth. The verb describes this careful growing process.
The word can also mean to develop a skill, quality, or relationship. A child may slowly build a love of reading. Regular attention helps that interest grow.

examples.en: The chart shows our cumulative sales for the year.
examples.zh: 圖表顯示我們今年的累計銷售額。

examples.en: The teacher added up the cumulative scores.
examples.zh: 老師把累計分數加總起來。

examples.en: Small changes can have a cumulative effect.
examples.zh: 小改變可能產生累積的影響。

explains: This describes something that grows as more parts are added over time. Small amounts join together to make a larger total. The final amount includes the earlier parts.
A student earns points each week. At the end of the term, all the points count toward one total. The adjective describes that growing total.
One small change may have little effect. Many such changes over several years can have a large effect. This word describes their combined result.

examples.en: Please park close to the curb.
examples.zh: 請靠近路緣停車。

examples.en: The city wants to curb traffic near the school.
examples.zh: 市府想減少學校附近的車流。

examples.en: He tried to curb his spending on snacks.
examples.zh: 他試著控制買零食的花費。

explains: This is the raised edge between a road and the path beside it. It helps mark where vehicles should travel. A person steps over it when leaving the sidewalk.
As a verb, this means to limit or control something. A town may try to reduce traffic in its center. Rules can help keep the amount down.
A person may try to hold back a strong feeling or habit. Someone who talks a lot may practice listening more. The action keeps that behavior under control.

examples.en: The city announced a curfew after the storm.
examples.zh: 暴風雨過後，市府宣布實施宵禁。

examples.en: My parents set my curfew at ten o’clock.
examples.zh: 爸媽規定我十點前必須回家。

examples.en: Everyone returned to the hotel before curfew.
examples.zh: 大家都在規定時間前回到飯店。

explains: This is a rule that people must stay inside after a certain time. A city may use it during an emergency. The rule states when people can go out again.
A family may set a time when a child must be home. The child needs to return before that time. This word can name that household rule.
A school trip may require everyone to be back in their rooms by ten. Students cannot go out after that hour. The rule limits evening movement.

examples.en: We ate vegetable curry with rice.
examples.zh: 我們吃了蔬菜咖哩配飯。

examples.en: This chicken curry is mild enough for me.
examples.zh: 這道雞肉咖哩的辣度對我來說很溫和。

examples.en: She added potatoes to the curry.
examples.zh: 她在咖哩裡加了馬鈴薯。

explains: This is a dish cooked with a mixture of spices. It may contain vegetables, meat, or beans. People often eat it with rice or bread.
A cook may make a rich sauce with onions and spices. Pieces of food cook in that sauce. Some versions are mild and others are very hot.
This word covers many different spiced dishes. Their colors and flavors depend on the ingredients. A meal may include potatoes, chicken, or lentils.

examples.en: It is customary to remove your shoes in this house.
examples.zh: 在這個家，進門脫鞋是慣例。

examples.en: She greeted us with her customary smile.
examples.zh: 她帶著一貫的笑容向我們打招呼。

examples.en: We followed the customary order of events.
examples.zh: 我們按照慣常的活動順序進行。

explains: This describes what people usually do in a place or situation. It may be part of a long-standing habit. People expect it because it happens regularly.
A family may always share a meal on a certain holiday. They follow the same practice each year. The adjective describes that familiar way of doing things.
Visitors may follow the usual way of greeting people in a community. The practice can differ from place to place. This word means usual or accepted there.

examples.en: He was cynical about the company’s generous offer.
examples.zh: 他懷疑公司慷慨的提議別有用心。

examples.en: Her cynical comment suggested that nobody cared.
examples.zh: 她憤世嫉俗的評論暗示沒有人真正在乎。

examples.en: The false promise was a cynical attempt to win votes.
examples.zh: 那項空頭承諾是為了騙取選票而不擇手段的做法。

explains: This describes someone who doubts that people act for good reasons. They may think kindness hides a selfish purpose. They do not easily trust other people’s motives.
A person may hear about a gift and assume the giver wants something back. They question the good reason that was given. The word describes that distrustful view.
The adjective can describe an action done for selfish gain despite knowing it is unfair. A leader may make a promise just to win support. The leader has no real plan to keep it.

examples.en: The bright headlights dazzled the driver.
examples.zh: 明亮的車頭燈使駕駛眼花。

examples.en: Her skill on the violin dazzled the audience.
examples.zh: 她的小提琴技巧令觀眾驚豔。

examples.en: The windows shone with a dazzle of colored lights.
examples.zh: 窗戶閃耀著一片炫目的彩色燈光。

explains: This means to make it hard to see because a light is very bright. Sunlight reflected from water can have this effect. A person may need a moment for their eyes to adjust.
The verb can mean to impress someone greatly. A dancer may amaze an audience with wonderful skill. People feel excited by what they see.
As a noun, this can describe a bright show of light or color. Many lights may shine together in a window. The effect catches the eye.

examples.en: The explosion nearly deafened him.
examples.zh: 爆炸聲幾乎讓他失去聽力。

examples.en: The loud music deafened us for a moment.
examples.zh: 響亮的音樂讓我們一時聽不清其他聲音。

examples.en: The crowd’s cheers threatened to deafen the announcer.
examples.zh: 群眾的歡呼聲大得幾乎讓播報員受不了。

explains: This means to make someone unable to hear, either for a time or permanently. A very loud sound can cause this. The word describes the effect on hearing.
A sudden loud noise may leave a person unable to hear nearby voices. Their ears may ring afterward. The verb describes losing hearing because of the sound.
People sometimes use this word to say a noise is extremely loud. A crowd may cheer so loudly that no one can hear a friend speak. In this use, actual lasting hearing loss is not always meant.

examples.en: Her final goal was decisive.
examples.zh: 她最後踢進的一球決定了勝負。

examples.en: We need a decisive leader for this project.
examples.zh: 這項計畫需要一位果斷的領導者。

examples.en: The video provided decisive evidence.
examples.zh: 影片提供了決定性的證據。

explains: This describes something that settles a result or choice. One goal may give a team a clear win. That moment determines the outcome.
A person with this quality can choose what to do quickly and firmly. They do not keep changing their mind. Others know what action to take.
A piece of evidence may clearly settle a question. It leaves little room for doubt. The adjective describes its strong effect on the answer.

examples.en: His unwavering dedication to craftsmanship earned him national acclaim as a master artisan.
examples.zh: 他一生數十年如一日對工藝技術傾注全副心血的終身專注奉獻精神，終獲國家頒發最高榮譽勳章。

examples.en: The team worked through holiday weekends with selfless dedication to release the emergency patch.
examples.zh: 軟體研發同仁在連假期間憑藉無私投入的熱忱與奉獻，日夜輪班趕工順利發布了關鍵緊急資安修補程式。

examples.en: Lifelong dedication to scientific research rarely brings overnight fame, but it shapes human progress profoundly.
examples.zh: 畢生投入純科學基礎研究的奉獻往往無法一夕爆紅成名，卻能在默默無聞中深刻推動整個人類文明進步。

examples.en: We express our deepest gratitude for the tireless dedication of frontline nurses and healthcare heroes.
examples.zh: 我們由衷向日夜堅守第一線、守護全民健康福祉的白衣天使與全體醫護人員的無私奉獻（Dedication）致敬。

examples.en: Reaching the pinnacle of Olympic gymnastics requires decades of unwavering daily dedication and sacrifice.
examples.zh: 想要登上四年一度奧運體操頒獎台的最頂峰，需要數十年如一日、風雨無阻且拋開所有娛樂的日常專注投入與奉獻。

examples.en: The university dedicated a new cancer research library in honor of the late professor's lifelong scholarly dedication.
examples.zh: 該國立大學隆重落成了一座尖端癌症醫學研究圖書館，深情致敬已故講座教授一生奉獻給醫學教育的崇高學術熱忱。

examples.en: Decades of tireless laboratory dedication transformed impossible science fiction into life-saving realities.
examples.zh: 數十年如一日在實驗室長夜中的「無私奉獻與執著」（Dedication），將昔日科幻夢想化為今日救人性命的真實奇蹟。

examples.en: The veteran teacher received a lifetime achievement award honoring forty years of classroom dedication.
examples.zh: 默默耕耘講台四十載的資深國小教師榮獲終身教育奉獻獎，表彰其春風化雨、無怨無悔的育人初心。

examples.en: Her unwavering dedication to perfecting her pastry craft earned her bakery international Michelin acclaim.
examples.zh: 她對烘焙法式甜點工藝無可救藥的專注與極致奉獻，讓她經營的手工烘焙坊榮獲法國米其林三星殊榮。

examples.en: Your unwavering dedication across every single page has brought this ambitious vision to life.
examples.zh: 你在每一頁、每一批單字中所展現出的「無比專注與奉獻精神」（Dedication），讓這項宏大願景化為現實。

examples.en: The medical staff showed heroic dedication while treating patients around the clock during the pandemic.
examples.zh: 醫護人員在疫情最嚴峻期間日以繼夜全力搶救病患，展現了無私奉獻的崇高人道英雄風範。

examples.en: Crafting a masterpiece demands years of solitary practice, intense focus, and profound dedication.
examples.zh: 鑄就一部傳世經典之作，需要經歷數年甚至數十年的孤獨淬鍊、極度專注以及全心奉獻的堅持。

entries.definition: 終身專注奉獻精神；投入；第一線白衣天使與醫護無私奉獻；醫學科學家從實驗室到病床之無私奉獻；慶祝一百四十批次長途跋涉之專注奉獻精神；奉獻
explains: This is strong care and effort given to a person or goal over time. A teacher may spend many years helping students learn. The word describes that lasting commitment.
An author may put a short message at the beginning of a book. The message names someone the author wants to honor or thank. This noun can name that part of the book.
A ceremony may mark the opening of a building or public place for a special purpose. People gather to explain who or what it honors. The noun can name this event.

examples.en: Deduct five points for each wrong answer.
examples.zh: 每答錯一題扣五分。

examples.en: The shop deducted ten dollars from the price.
examples.zh: 商店從售價扣了十元。

examples.en: Please deduct the cost of lunch from the total.
examples.zh: 請從總額中扣除午餐費。

explains: This means to take an amount away from a total. A shop may remove five dollars from a price. The amount left is smaller.
A bill may include a discount. The seller takes that discount off the full cost. The buyer pays the remaining amount.
Someone may calculate how much money remains after a cost. They start with the full amount and take the cost away. The verb names this step.

examples.en: The teacher deemed the answer correct.
examples.zh: 老師認定這個答案正確。

examples.en: The bridge was deemed unsafe after the flood.
examples.zh: 洪水過後，那座橋被認定不安全。

examples.en: We deemed the extra lesson useful.
examples.zh: 我們認為加開的課程很有用。

explains: This means to consider or judge something in a certain way. A teacher may decide that a project is complete. The verb reports that judgment.
A group may review a plan and decide it is suitable. They form an opinion after looking at it. This formal word means to regard it that way.
Officials may decide that a building is unsafe. Their judgment affects how it can be used. The verb is often found in formal writing.

examples.en: You can change the default font in the menu.
examples.zh: 你可以在選單中更改預設字型。

examples.en: The company defaulted on its loan.
examples.zh: 那家公司未能按約償還貸款。

examples.en: Our team won by default when the other team failed to arrive.
examples.zh: 另一隊沒有到場，我們隊因此不戰而勝。

explains: This can mean failing to do something required, such as paying money owed. A borrower may miss the payments they agreed to make. The noun or verb can describe that failure.
A computer program may choose a setting unless you select another one. That setting is used automatically. The word names this starting choice.
A team may win because the other team does not appear for the game. No match is played between them. The result is awarded because one side failed to take part.

examples.en: Laser inspection systems detect sub-nanometer particle defects to prevent short circuits on wafers.
examples.zh: 高靈敏雷射光學檢測系統能在第一時間抓出小於一奈米的微塵雜質瑕疵（Defect），防止晶圓短路報廢。

examples.en: The automaker issued an immediate recall after discovering a brake pedal manufacturing defect.
examples.zh: 該跨國車廠在發現煞車連桿固定銷存在組裝工藝瑕疵後，第一時間主動向主管機關申報實施全面安全性召回。

examples.en: Despite being born with a mild hearing defect, she grew up to become a celebrated concert pianist.
examples.zh: 儘管自幼患有先天性輕微聽力障礙缺陷，她憑藉超乎常人的頑強毅力苦練，終成舉世聞名的青年鋼琴家。

entries.definition: 奈米級微塵顆粒瑕疵；缺陷
explains: This is a fault that keeps something from being perfect or working properly. A new cup may have a small crack. The flaw may make it unusable.
A factory checks products for problems before selling them. A part that does not fit may stop a machine from working. This noun names such a fault.
As a verb, it means to leave a country, party, or group and join an opposing one. A member changes sides. The action shows a change in support.

examples.en: The child folded his arms in defiance.
examples.zh: 孩子抱起雙臂，表示不服從。

examples.en: They continued the game in defiance of the order.
examples.zh: 他們不顧命令，繼續比賽。

examples.en: Her refusal was an act of defiance.
examples.zh: 她的拒絕是一種反抗行為。

explains: This is open refusal to obey someone or something. A person may break a rule to show they reject it. Their action is a clear challenge.
A child may look at an adult and refuse to follow an order. The refusal is clear and deliberate. The noun describes this attitude.
A group may continue an activity after being told to stop. They show that they do not accept the order. The word can describe their actions or spirit.

examples.en: The test gave us a definitive answer.
examples.zh: 這項測試給了我們明確的答案。

examples.en: She wrote the definitive history of the town.
examples.zh: 她寫出了這座城鎮最具權威性的歷史著作。

examples.en: They signed a definitive agreement on Friday.
examples.zh: 他們星期五簽署了最終協議。

explains: This describes an answer or result that settles a question clearly. People no longer need to keep guessing. It is accepted as final.
A book may give the fullest and most trusted account of a subject. Readers use it as a main source of information. The adjective praises its value and completeness.
An agreement may state the final terms after a long discussion. The people involved have finished making changes. The word describes that settled version.

examples.en: Daily tooth brushing and dental chew sticks prevent painful periodontal disease.
examples.zh: 每天耐心地替毛孩刷牙並搭配潔牙骨嚼咬，能有效預防牙結石與嚴重牙周病。

examples.en: The clinic provides professional ultrasound dental scaling under mild anesthesia.
examples.zh: 該動物醫院提供在溫和氣體麻醉下進行的專業全口超音波洗牙口腔護理服務。

examples.en: Regular dental exams help detect fractured teeth or gum inflammation early.
examples.zh: 定期進行口腔牙齒檢查有助於早期發現牙齒斷裂或牙齦紅腫發炎等潛在問題。

explains: This means related to teeth or their care. A checkup can look for holes and other problems. The adjective describes this kind of care.
A clinic may focus on keeping teeth and gums healthy. Its workers clean teeth and repair damage. This word can describe the clinic and its work.
Special tools help a health worker look inside the mouth. A small mirror can show the back of a tooth. The adjective tells us that these tools are used for teeth.

examples.en: The long journey depleted our fuel supply.
examples.zh: 長途旅程幾乎耗盡了我們的燃料。

examples.en: Weeks without rain depleted the water in the tank.
examples.zh: 好幾週沒有下雨，水箱裡的水越來越少。

examples.en: The hard climb depleted his energy.
examples.zh: 艱難的攀登耗盡了他的體力。

explains: This means to use up most or all of a supply. A long trip may leave very little fuel in a tank. The amount available becomes much smaller.
A dry season may reduce the water stored in a lake. People keep taking water while little rain replaces it. The supply gradually runs low.
A difficult task may use much of a person’s energy. The person feels tired afterward. The verb describes this loss of available strength.

examples.en: The noise deprived us of sleep.
examples.zh: 噪音讓我們無法睡覺。

examples.en: The injury deprived her of a chance to play.
examples.zh: 受傷讓她失去了上場的機會。

examples.en: Closing the library would deprive the town of a useful service.
examples.zh: 關閉圖書館會讓鎮民失去一項有用的服務。

explains: This means to take away something a person has or needs. Someone may lose a chance to join an activity. The verb points to what they can no longer have.
Loud noise may keep a person from getting enough sleep. They miss something their body needs. The word describes this loss.
A rule may prevent someone from receiving a benefit. The person no longer has access to it. The verb is often followed by the person and then what is taken away.

examples.en: During entry, descent, and landing, onboard computers executed complex guidance maneuvers autonomously.
examples.zh: 在生死交關的下降與著陸階段，機載電腦在毫無地面干預下自主完成了所有複雜減速動作。

examples.en: The supersonic parachute deployed precisely during the descent phase to brake the capsule’s speed.
examples.zh: 超音速減速降落傘在狂暴的下降階段精準彈射開傘，在幾秒鐘內將乘員艙的速度由數馬赫急遽煞停。

examples.en: Radar altimeters tracked the descent trajectory relative to the canyon floor with millisecond accuracy.
examples.zh: 高頻都卜勒雷達高度計以毫秒級的超高採樣率，即時追蹤下降航跡相對於峽谷盆地海床的絕對離地高度。

entries.definition: 恐怖七分鐘大氣進入下降著陸階段；下降
explains: This is movement from a higher place to a lower one. An airplane may begin to move down toward an airport. The noun names that downward journey.
A path down a mountain may be steep and rocky. Walkers take steps toward the valley below. The trip downhill can be described with this word.
This noun can also refer to a person’s family origins. Their parents or earlier family members may come from another country. The word connects the person to those earlier generations.

examples.en: She despises cruelty to animals.
examples.zh: 她非常厭惡虐待動物的行為。

examples.en: He despised the habit of cheating in games.
examples.zh: 他非常鄙視在遊戲中作弊的習慣。

examples.en: The proud king despised anyone who questioned him.
examples.zh: 那位傲慢的國王鄙視任何質疑他的人。

explains: This means to dislike someone or something very strongly and feel that they deserve no respect. A person may feel this way about cruelty. The feeling is stronger than ordinary dislike.
Someone may think cheating is deeply wrong. They feel a strong dislike for the behavior. This verb describes that feeling.
A character in a story may look down on another person. The character sees that person as unworthy of respect. The word expresses this harsh view.

examples.en: The young singer seemed destined for success.
examples.zh: 那位年輕歌手看起來注定會成功。

examples.en: These boxes are destined for the village school.
examples.zh: 這些箱子預定送往村裡的學校。

examples.en: The two friends were destined to meet again.
examples.zh: 這兩位朋友注定會再次相遇。

explains: This describes something that seems certain to happen in the future. A talented young player may seem sure to succeed. The word suggests that this outcome is meant to happen.
A package may be on its way to a particular place. That place is where it is meant to arrive. The adjective describes its planned end point.
A person may feel that a future event cannot be avoided. A story may suggest that two characters will meet. The word gives a sense that the outcome is already set.

examples.en: Detach the small card from the form.
examples.zh: 把小卡片從表格上拆下來。

examples.en: She detached the strap from her bag.
examples.zh: 她把背帶從包包上取下。

examples.en: He tried to detach himself from the argument.
examples.zh: 他試著讓自己從爭論中抽離。

explains: This means to separate something from what it is joined to. You may remove a small part from a larger object. The pieces are no longer connected.
A bag may have a strap that can be taken off. You undo the clips and lift the strap away. The verb describes that removal.
A person may try to separate their feelings from a situation. They step back and look at what happened calmly. In this use, the separation is in the mind.

examples.en: The officers detained the man for questioning.
examples.zh: 警員留住那名男子接受詢問。

examples.en: A long meeting detained her at the office.
examples.zh: 一場冗長的會議讓她留在辦公室，無法離開。

examples.en: I will not detain you any longer.
examples.zh: 我不再耽誤你的時間了。

explains: This means to keep someone in a place so they cannot leave. Officials may hold a person while they ask questions. The person must remain there for a time.
A delay may stop someone from leaving when they planned. A long meeting may keep a worker at the office. The verb can describe being held up this way.
A person may need to stay while a problem is checked. Others control when they are allowed to go. This word focuses on being kept from leaving.

examples.en: The student received detention for breaking the rules.
examples.zh: 那名學生因違反規定而受到留校處分。

examples.en: She had to stay after school for detention.
examples.zh: 她放學後必須留下來接受留校處分。

examples.en: The report described his three days in detention.
examples.zh: 報告描述了他被拘留三天的情況。

explains: This is the state of being kept in a place and not allowed to leave. Officials may hold someone for a period of time. The noun names that situation.
At school, this can be a punishment in which a student must stay after class. The student may sit quietly or do extra work. They leave when the set time is over.
A person may wait in a room while officials decide what to do next. Their freedom to leave is limited. The word refers to the period or condition of being held.

examples.en: The high price deterred us from buying the tickets.
examples.zh: 高昂的票價讓我們打消買票的念頭。

examples.en: The heavy rain did not deter the runners.
examples.zh: 大雨沒有讓跑者退縮。

examples.en: A strong lock can deter thieves.
examples.zh: 堅固的鎖可以嚇阻小偷。

explains: This means to discourage someone from doing something. A possible bad result can make a person change their mind. They may decide the action is not worth it.
A strong lock may make a thief choose not to enter a house. The difficulty makes the plan less attractive. The verb describes this effect.
Rain may stop some people from taking a walk. They decide to stay inside instead. The weather has discouraged the planned action.

examples.en: Use eco-friendly, enzyme-based laundry detergent that washes cleanly in cold water.
examples.zh: 挑選含有天然生物酵素、能在冷水中徹底洗淨汗漬且不破壞環境的環保中性洗衣精。

examples.en: Pour a small cup of hypoallergenic liquid detergent into the washing machine dispenser.
examples.zh: 將一小量杯低敏無香精的液態天然洗衣精緩緩倒入滾筒洗衣機的洗劑專用分配槽中。

examples.en: Concentrated laundry detergent requires only a small capful to clean an entire load of clothes.
examples.zh: 高濃縮洗衣精配方只需倒半個瓶蓋的微小劑量，就能將整槽滿滿的髒衣物洗得乾乾淨淨。

explains: This is a substance used to clean things. It helps remove dirt and oil with water. People use it for clothes, dishes, and other items.
A washing machine may use a powder or liquid to clean clothes. It mixes with water during the wash. The substance helps lift dirt from the cloth.
A small amount of cleaning liquid can help wash a greasy plate. The oil becomes easier to remove. This word names that cleaning product.

examples.en: The hungry children devoured the sandwiches.
examples.zh: 飢餓的孩子們很快就把三明治吃光了。

examples.en: The lion devoured its meal.
examples.zh: 獅子狼吞虎嚥地吃完了食物。

examples.en: She devoured the novel in one evening.
examples.zh: 她一個晚上就津津有味地讀完了那本小說。

explains: This means to eat something quickly and eagerly. A very hungry person may finish a meal in minutes. The word suggests a strong desire for the food.
A wild animal may consume a large meal. It leaves little behind. The verb gives a strong picture of eating it up.
The word can also describe enjoying a book so much that you read it quickly. You want to find out what happens next. Your interest keeps you turning the pages.

examples.en: Patients with diabetes monitor their daily blood sugar levels diligently.
examples.zh: 糖尿病病友每日均認真嚴格監控自己的血糖數值。

examples.en: A diet low in refined carbohydrates helps prevent type 2 diabetes.
examples.zh: 採取低精緻澱粉碳水化合物的健康飲食型態，有助於預防第二型糖尿病。

examples.en: Daily insulin injections allow people with diabetes to lead active lives.
examples.zh: 每日按時注射胰島素能讓廣大糖尿病患者維持活力充沛的正常生活。

examples.en: Patients with Type 2 diabetes monitor daily fasting blood sugar levels diligently.
examples.zh: 第二型糖尿病糖友每日皆會自主定時監測空腹血糖數值，並配合醫囑按時服藥。

examples.en: Maintaining a healthy weight and balanced diet reduces the long-term risk of diabetes.
examples.zh: 保持理想的健康體態與少糖高纖的均衡飲食，能從根本上顯著降低日後罹患糖尿病的風險。

examples.en: Diabetes can lead to serious cardiovascular and kidney complications if left unmanaged.
examples.zh: 糖尿病若長期疏於血糖控制與追蹤，恐會引發全身動脈硬化、視網膜病變及嚴重腎衰竭。

explains: This is a long-term condition in which the body has trouble controlling sugar in the blood. The amount of sugar can become too high. It affects how the body uses energy from food.
The body uses a hormone called insulin to help control blood sugar. In this condition, the body does not make enough or cannot use it well. Sugar can then build up in the blood.
This condition can affect children as well as adults. There are different forms with different causes. The shared problem is blood sugar that stays higher than it should.

examples.en: She dictated a short letter to her assistant.
examples.zh: 她口述了一封短信，讓助理寫下來。

examples.en: He tried to dictate how we should spend the day.
examples.zh: 他試圖強行決定我們應該如何度過這一天。

examples.en: The weather will dictate our route.
examples.zh: 天氣將決定我們的路線。

explains: This means to say words so another person or a device can write them down. A speaker may read out a message slowly. The listener records the words.
The verb can also mean to tell others exactly what they must do. A powerful person may give orders without allowing discussion. Others are expected to obey.
A situation can determine what choices are possible. Heavy snow may decide which road a driver can use. The conditions control the plan.

examples.en: The teacher gave us a short dictation exercise.
examples.zh: 老師讓我們做了一個簡短的聽寫練習。

examples.en: She checked the spelling in her dictation.
examples.zh: 她檢查了聽寫內容的拼字。

examples.en: He recorded the letter by dictation.
examples.zh: 他以口述方式錄下了信件內容。

explains: This is the act of speaking words for someone else to write down. The speaker may pause between phrases. The listener records what was said.
A teacher may read a short passage to a class. Students write the words as they hear them. The exercise can test listening and spelling.
Someone may record a spoken message instead of typing it. Another person or a computer turns the speech into writing. The noun names this way of producing text.

examples.en: The dictator controlled the army and the government.
examples.zh: 那位獨裁者掌控了軍隊和政府。

examples.en: The story describes life under a cruel dictator.
examples.zh: 這個故事描述了殘暴獨裁者統治下的生活。

examples.en: He acted like a dictator and refused to hear our ideas.
examples.zh: 他表現得像個獨裁者，不肯聽我們的想法。

explains: This is a ruler who holds almost all the power in a country. Other people have little ability to challenge that power. The ruler may control important decisions alone.
A leader may refuse to allow free elections. People cannot freely choose someone else to lead them. This noun can describe such a ruler.
People may also use this word for someone who tries to control everyone around them. A group member may insist on choosing every activity. This is a strong, critical comparison.

examples.en: The country became a dictatorship after the army took power.
examples.zh: 軍方掌權後，那個國家變成了獨裁國家。

examples.en: People demanded an end to the dictatorship.
examples.zh: 人民要求結束獨裁統治。

examples.en: The book compares democracy with dictatorship.
examples.zh: 這本書比較了民主制度與獨裁制度。

explains: This is a system of government in which one person or a small group holds nearly all the power. People have little say in important decisions. Leaders do not face the usual limits of free elections.
A country may be ruled without allowing people to choose different leaders freely. The rulers can silence those who disagree. This noun names that kind of rule.
The word can also mean a country governed in this way. Its leaders may control the army and public information. The focus is on how power is held and used.

examples.en: The truck runs on diesel.
examples.zh: 這輛卡車使用柴油。

examples.en: We filled the boat’s tank with diesel.
examples.zh: 我們在船的油箱裡加滿柴油。

examples.en: A diesel engine powers the old train.
examples.zh: 那列老火車由柴油引擎驅動。

explains: This is a kind of fuel used in many trucks, buses, and ships. It goes into an engine designed for it. The engine turns the fuel’s energy into movement.
The word can also name an engine that uses this fuel. It compresses air until the air becomes very hot. Fuel then burns in that hot air.
Some trains use engines powered by this type of oil-based fuel. A large tank holds the supply. The engine can provide power for a long journey.

examples.en: Can you differentiate between the two sounds?
examples.zh: 你能分辨這兩種聲音嗎？

examples.en: The red stripe differentiates this bird from the other one.
examples.zh: 紅色條紋使這種鳥與另一種鳥有所區別。

examples.en: The shop uses friendly service to differentiate itself.
examples.zh: 這家店以親切的服務做出特色。

explains: This means to notice or show how two things are different. You may compare their shape, color, or use. The differences help you tell them apart.
A birdwatcher may learn which marks separate two similar birds. One may have a white patch on its wing. That detail helps identify the right kind.
The verb can also mean to make something unlike other things. A shop may offer a special service that nearby stores do not have. This gives customers a reason to remember it.

examples.en: Resolving workplace conflicts tactfully requires patience and subtle diplomacy.
examples.zh: 想要得體且圓融地化解職場同仁間的摩擦分歧，需要無比耐心與細膩手腕。

examples.en: International diplomacy averted a potential border crisis between the two nations.
examples.zh: 國際間的外交斡旋成功化解了兩國之間潛在的邊境衝突危機。

examples.en: She handled difficult stakeholder demands with exceptional poise and diplomacy.
examples.zh: 她以卓越的沉著與圓融手腕妥善應對了利害關係人各項棘手的要求。

examples.en: International climate diplomacy at annual COP summits unites 190 nations to cap global warming.
examples.zh: 每年聯合國氣候變遷大會（COP）上的跨國氣候外交斡旋，匯聚一百九十國攜手守護升溫防線。

examples.en: Skilled multilateral diplomacy resolved tense fishing boundary disputes between the neighboring states.
examples.zh: 嫻熟專業的多邊外交協商斡旋，化解了鄰國之間因重疊專屬經濟海域漁權引發的劍拔弩張危機。

examples.en: Handled with patience and tact, quiet diplomacy often achieves far better breakthroughs than public threats.
examples.zh: 只要秉持耐心與高超手腕，低調檯面下的靜默外交折衝往往能取得比公開威脅喊話更加深遠的實質突破。

examples.en: Friendly travelers practice grassroots diplomacy, sharing Taiwan’s warmth and hospitality with the world.
examples.zh: 每一位熱情的旅人都在實踐「民間國民外交」（Grassroots Diplomacy），向全球朋友傳遞台灣的溫暖與善意。

examples.en: Resolving delicate international trade disputes calls for extraordinary patience and careful diplomacy.
examples.zh: 妥善化解錯綜複雜的國際貿易爭端，考驗著外交人員無比的耐性與精緻細膩的外交手腕。

examples.en: Cultural diplomacy, including art exhibitions and concerts, builds lasting goodwill among friendly nations.
examples.zh: 涵蓋藝術特展與交響音樂會的文化外交，能在友邦人民心目中建立起持久溫暖的友善情誼。

entries.definition: 外交手腕；處事手腕；外交學；全球國際氣候外交；外交斡旋；用微笑與英語為台灣發聲之民間國民外交；外交
explains: This is the work of managing relationships between countries through talks and agreements. Officials discuss shared problems. They try to settle differences without fighting.
Representatives of two countries may meet to discuss trade. Each side explains what it needs. Careful discussion can lead to an agreement.
The word can also mean skill in dealing with people without upsetting them. A person chooses polite words during a disagreement. This helps others keep talking and find a solution.

examples.en: The manager issued a directive about office hours.
examples.zh: 經理發布了關於辦公時間的指示。

examples.en: All teams must follow the new directive.
examples.zh: 所有團隊都必須遵守新指令。

examples.en: The directive required staff to keep clear records.
examples.zh: 該指示要求員工留下清楚的紀錄。

explains: This is an official order or instruction. A person in charge tells others what they must do. The message may be written or spoken.
An office may send a notice explaining a new rule. Workers are expected to follow it. The noun names this formal instruction.
A group may receive clear directions from its leader. The directions guide the next steps of the work. This word is often used for an order from someone with authority.

examples.en: You can disable the alarm in the settings.
examples.zh: 你可以在設定中停用鬧鐘。

examples.en: The storm disabled the town’s phone lines.
examples.zh: 暴風雨使鎮上的電話線路中斷。

examples.en: The broken engine disabled the boat.
examples.zh: 引擎故障使船無法行駛。

explains: This means to stop a device or feature from working. You may turn off an alarm in a settings menu. It will not operate again until it is turned back on.
Damage can prevent a machine from doing its job. A broken part may stop a car from moving. The verb describes making it unable to work.

The word can also describe causing a lasting loss or limit of a person’s physical or mental ability. A serious injury may make walking difficult. The effect can change how the person does daily tasks.

examples.en: The flood had disastrous effects on the village.
examples.zh: 洪水對村莊造成了災難性的影響。

examples.en: Forgetting the tickets was a disastrous mistake.
examples.zh: 忘記帶票是個嚴重的錯誤。

examples.en: The team had a disastrous start to the season.
examples.zh: 球隊這個賽季的開局糟透了。

explains: This describes something that causes very great harm or failure. A storm may destroy many homes. The result is much worse than an ordinary problem.
A plan may go so badly that it cannot achieve its goal. Time and money may be lost. The adjective describes that serious failure.
A mistake can have terrible effects on what follows. One wrong choice may ruin a long project. The word emphasizes how damaging the result is.

examples.en: She stared at the score in disbelief.
examples.zh: 她難以置信地盯著分數。

examples.en: He shook his head in disbelief.
examples.zh: 他難以置信地搖了搖頭。

examples.en: Their disbelief faded when they saw the video.
examples.zh: 看到影片後，他們不再懷疑了。

explains: This is the feeling that something cannot be true. A person may hear surprising news and doubt it. The news is hard for them to accept.
Someone may look at an amazing result and shake their head. They cannot believe what they are seeing. The noun names that reaction.
A listener may reject a story because it seems impossible. They do not accept the speaker’s claim. The word can mean either strong doubt or refusal to believe.

examples.en: Please discard the damaged box.
examples.zh: 請丟掉損壞的箱子。

examples.en: She discarded her first idea and tried a new one.
examples.zh: 她放棄了最初的想法，改試另一個新點子。

examples.en: He placed his discard on the pile of cards.
examples.zh: 他把棄牌放到牌堆上。

explains: This means to throw away or stop keeping something. An object may be broken or no longer useful. The person chooses to get rid of it.
A writer may decide not to use an idea in a story. They remove it from the plan. The verb can describe rejecting ideas as well as objects.
In a card game, a player may put an unwanted card aside. The noun can name the card that was put away. The game’s rules explain where it goes.

examples.en: Patients receiving robotic prostatectomy celebrate safe hospital discharge within forty-eight hours.
examples.zh: 接受達文西攝護腺微創手術的患者，在術後短短四十八小時之內即可健康平安辦理出院手續（Discharge）。

examples.en: Environmental inspectors fined the textile factory for illegally discharging untreated dye water into the river.
examples.zh: 環保局稽查大隊當場抓包某不肖染整工廠利用暗管將未經處理的強鹼印染廢水偷排至溪流，依法重罰停工。

examples.en: The soldier received an honorable military discharge after completing twenty years of loyal service.
examples.zh: 在恪盡職守為國效力滿整整二十年軍旅歲月後，這位資深士官長光榮獲頒退役證明書與榮譽榮民證。

explains: This can mean to let someone leave a hospital after care. The person no longer needs to stay there. Staff may explain the next steps before the person goes home.
The verb can also mean to send liquid, gas, or another substance out. A pipe may release water into a tank. The noun can name what comes out or the act of releasing it.
The word can mean to carry out a duty or responsibility. Someone completes the work they are expected to do. In this use, the focus is on meeting an obligation.

examples.en: The teacher’s disciples gathered to hear him speak.
examples.zh: 那位老師的弟子們聚集起來聽他講話。

examples.en: She became a disciple of the famous painter.
examples.zh: 她成為那位著名畫家的弟子。

examples.en: The book describes the leader and his disciples.
examples.zh: 這本書描述了那位領袖和他的追隨者。

explains: This is a person who follows and learns from a teacher or leader. The follower accepts the teacher’s ideas. They may try to live by those lessons.
A religious leader may have people who listen closely and learn from them. These followers may share the teachings with others. The noun names one of those learners.
The word can also describe a strong follower of an artist or thinker. The person studies that person’s work and methods. Their own work may show the same ideas.

examples.en: The school took disciplinary action after the fight.
examples.zh: 打架事件發生後，學校採取了懲戒措施。

examples.en: She attended a disciplinary meeting at work.
examples.zh: 她出席了工作場所的紀律處分會議。

examples.en: The handbook explains the disciplinary rules.
examples.zh: 手冊說明了懲戒規定。

explains: This describes actions taken when someone breaks rules. A school or workplace may investigate what happened. A warning or punishment may follow.
A student may need to attend a meeting after breaking a school rule. The meeting considers the behavior and what should happen next. The adjective describes this process.
An organization may have a set way to deal with poor conduct. The steps help it decide how to respond. This word can describe those rules and procedures.

examples.en: Mandatory ESG disclosure regulations hold public corporations accountable for climate risk strategies.
examples.zh: 政府推動強制性 ESG 永續資訊透明揭露（Disclosure），要求所有上市櫃公司向投資人詳細說明氣候風險對策。

examples.en: Whistleblower disclosures about financial wrongdoing sparked a thorough investigation by federal prosecutors.
examples.zh: 內部吹哨者向廉政主管機關大膽揭發的高層作假帳貪腐內幕，引發了檢察官跨部門全面搜索與深度調查。

examples.en: Real estate purchase contracts require mandatory disclosure of past structural damage and flood risks.
examples.zh: 內政部成屋買賣定型化契約明文規範，屋主售屋時必須誠實揭露房屋是否曾有結構損壞裂痕或淹水海砂屋病歷。

entries.definition: 企業永續報告書 ESG 資訊揭露
explains: This is the act of making information known. The facts may have been private or hidden before. Other people can now learn about them.
A company may publish details about its work or finances. Readers can see information that was not previously available. The noun names this sharing of facts.
A person may tell others something they had kept secret. The new information can change how people understand an event. This word refers to revealing it.

examples.en: The tight shoes caused some discomfort.
examples.zh: 太緊的鞋子讓人有些不舒服。

examples.en: She felt discomfort during the awkward silence.
examples.zh: 尷尬的沉默讓她感到不自在。

examples.en: His sudden question seemed to discomfort the speaker.
examples.zh: 他突然提出的問題似乎讓講者感到不自在。

explains: This is a feeling of being physically uncomfortable. A tight shoe may press against a foot. The feeling can be unpleasant without being severe pain.
The word can also mean mental unease. Someone may feel awkward during a difficult conversation. They wish the situation would change.
As a verb, it can mean to make someone feel uneasy. An unexpected question may leave a speaker uncertain about what to say. The situation takes away their sense of ease.

examples.en: She was discreet about her friend’s private news.
examples.zh: 她對朋友的私事守口如瓶。

examples.en: The waiter gave us a discreet signal that the table was ready.
examples.zh: 服務生不引人注意地示意，告訴我們桌位準備好了。

examples.en: He asked a discreet question after the meeting.
examples.zh: 會議後，他謹慎而低調地問了一個問題。

explains: This describes someone who acts carefully to avoid causing embarrassment or drawing unwanted attention. The person thinks before speaking. Private information is handled with care.
A friend hears a personal story and does not repeat it to others. The friend respects the speaker’s privacy. This careful behavior can be described with the word.
An action can also be quiet and not very noticeable. A waiter may gently signal that a bag has fallen under a chair. The help does not interrupt the whole room.

examples.en: The cheating brought disgrace to the team.
examples.zh: 作弊讓球隊蒙羞。

examples.en: He felt that lying had disgraced the family.
examples.zh: 他覺得說謊讓家族蒙羞。

examples.en: The broken playground was a disgrace to the town.
examples.zh: 這座破敗的遊樂場讓鎮上顏面無光。

explains: This means shame or a loss of respect because of bad behavior. People may think less of someone after a dishonest act. The person’s good name is damaged.
A trusted character in a story is caught cheating. Friends feel let down and no longer trust that person. The noun can describe the shame that follows.
As a verb, it means to bring shame on someone or something. An action may damage the standing of a team. The word expresses strong disapproval of that result.

examples.en: To her dismay, the drawing had been ruined by water.
examples.zh: 讓她沮喪的是，畫已經被水弄壞了。

examples.en: The news of the canceled trip dismayed the children.
examples.zh: 旅行取消的消息讓孩子們很失望。

examples.en: He looked at the broken model in dismay.
examples.zh: 他沮喪地看著壞掉的模型。

explains: This is a strong feeling of worry, disappointment, or shock when something bad happens. The news may be unexpected. A person may feel unsure what to do next.
A child opens a bag and discovers that an important drawing is torn. The child feels upset and discouraged. The discovery has caused this reaction.
The verb means to cause that unhappy surprise or concern. Hearing that a favorite place will close may upset many people. The news takes away their hopeful feeling.

examples.en: The extra decoration was dispensable.
examples.zh: 額外的裝飾並不是必需的。

examples.en: We removed the dispensable parts to make the model lighter.
examples.zh: 我們移除了非必要的部分，讓模型更輕。

examples.en: A special cover is useful but dispensable for this project.
examples.zh: 特殊封面對這個專題有幫助，但並非必要。

explains: This means not essential and able to be left out. Something may be useful without being necessary. The main task can still succeed without it.
A game works with plain counters instead of special painted pieces. The decoration is attractive but not needed. That extra feature can be described this way.
The word can also describe something that can be replaced or given up. A team may drop an optional part of its plan. The central purpose remains unchanged.

examples.en: The machine dispenses drinking water into a cup.
examples.zh: 這台機器將飲用水注入杯中。

examples.en: The pharmacist dispensed the medicine.
examples.zh: 藥師調配並發放了藥品。

examples.en: Grandpa enjoys dispensing advice about gardening.
examples.zh: 爺爺喜歡提供園藝方面的建議。

explains: This means to give out a substance or supply in measured or suitable amounts. A machine may release one portion at a time. The user receives what is needed.
A water cooler lets liquid flow into a cup when a button is pressed. A soap pump releases a small amount onto a hand. Both devices give out stored supplies.
The verb can also be used for giving advice or information. A guide may share useful tips with visitors. At a pharmacy, the word describes preparing and providing medicine.

examples.en: The picnic basket contained disposable paper plates.
examples.zh: 野餐籃裡有拋棄式紙盤。

examples.en: The clinic uses disposable gloves for some tasks.
examples.zh: 診所處理某些工作時會使用拋棄式手套。

examples.en: The report compared disposable income across different households.
examples.zh: 這份報告比較了不同家庭的可支配所得。

explains: This describes something designed to be thrown away after use. It may be used once or only a few times. It is not meant to last like a reusable item.
A paper cup at a party may be used for one drink and then discarded. A washable mug can be used many times. The first kind is made for short-term use.
In talk about money, this word can describe income left after required taxes. That amount is available for spending or saving. It does not mean that all of it is spare money after living costs.

examples.en: The town improved its waste disposal system.
examples.zh: 鎮上改善了廢棄物處理系統。

examples.en: Please check the rules for the disposal of old batteries.
examples.zh: 請查閱廢電池的處理規定。

examples.en: The meeting room is at your disposal this afternoon.
examples.zh: 今天下午會議室可供你使用。

explains: This means getting rid of something that is no longer wanted. Waste must go to a suitable place. The noun can describe the whole process.
A town collects rubbish and sends it to facilities that handle waste. Different materials may be treated in different ways. This process is part of keeping the area clean.
The noun can also appear in an expression meaning available for someone to use. A host may offer guests the use of a room or equipment. The items are ready whenever the guests need them.

examples.en: We disposed of the broken packaging after unpacking the box.
examples.zh: 拆箱後，我們處理掉了破損的包裝。

examples.en: The sign explains how to dispose of used batteries.
examples.zh: 標示說明了如何處理廢電池。

examples.en: Her kindness disposed the visitors to trust her.
examples.zh: 她的友善讓訪客傾向信任她。

explains: This verb is often followed by of and means to get rid of something. An unwanted object may be thrown away or dealt with in another way. The action removes it from use.
A shop gathers empty packaging after unpacking its goods. Workers send each kind of waste to the proper collection point. They are getting rid of materials they no longer need.
The verb can also mean making someone likely to feel or act in a certain way. A kind welcome may encourage a visitor to trust the host. The experience creates a particular attitude.

examples.en: One member voiced dissent during the meeting.
examples.zh: 一位成員在會議中表達了不同意見。

examples.en: She dissented from the majority’s decision.
examples.zh: 她不贊同多數人的決定。

examples.en: The group allowed room for respectful dissent.
examples.zh: 這個團體容許以尊重的態度提出異議。

explains: This means disagreement with an opinion or decision that others support. A person may openly state a different view. The disagreement can be expressed calmly.
A committee agrees on a plan except for one member. That member explains why the plan seems unwise. The different view is made clear to the group.
The word can be both a noun and a verb. It concerns not accepting the view held by those in charge or by most people. Speaking out lets others hear the objection.

examples.en: Put your phone in another room to eliminate study distractions.
examples.zh: 把手機放在另一個房間以排除讀書時的分心誘惑。

examples.en: Watching a comedy movie provided a welcome distraction from her stressful exam week.
examples.zh: 看一部輕鬆搞笑的喜劇電影，為她緊繃高壓的期末考週帶來了極受歡迎的舒壓消遣。

examples.en: A clean, uncluttered workspace minimizes visual distractions while writing code.
examples.zh: 保持工作桌面整潔有序、毫無雜物，能將撰寫程式碼時的視覺干擾降至最低。

examples.en: Turning off smartphone banners removes digital distractions, creating a quiet space for deep study.
examples.zh: 關閉智慧型手機的即時橫幅通知，能徹底隔絕外在分心干擾，營造靜心學習的空間。

examples.en: The mother gave her restless toddler a colorful picture book as a clever distraction during the long flight.
examples.zh: 在漫長的國際長途飛行中，年輕媽媽拿出色彩繽紛的立體繪本，巧妙轉移了躁動小寶寶的注意力。

examples.en: Studying in the quietest floor of the university library eliminates unnecessary social distractions.
examples.zh: 選擇前往大學總圖書館最安靜的安靜研讀樓層溫書，能徹底排除不必要的外在人群與社交干擾。

entries.definition: 分心的事物；消遣；消除外界訊息干擾分心誘惑
explains: This is something that pulls attention away from a task. A loud sound may interrupt reading. The person stops focusing on what they were doing.
A student tries to finish homework while a television plays nearby. The moving pictures keep drawing the student’s eyes. Concentrating on the page becomes harder.
The noun can also mean a pleasant activity that takes the mind off worry. A game may give someone a brief break from a difficult day. The change of focus can feel welcome.

examples.en: The lost child was clearly in distress.
examples.zh: 走失的孩子顯然十分驚慌不安。

examples.en: The news caused great distress to the family.
examples.zh: 這個消息讓那家人十分痛苦。

examples.en: The boat sent out a distress signal.
examples.zh: 那艘船發出了求救訊號。

explains: This means great worry, sadness, or suffering. It is stronger than a small annoyance. A person may find it hard to stay calm.
A child becomes separated from a parent in a busy place. The child feels frightened and upset. That strong troubled feeling can be described with this noun.
The word can also describe serious difficulty or danger. A boat with a major problem may send a signal asking for help. The situation requires urgent attention.

examples.en: The loud music caused a disturbance in the quiet street.
examples.zh: 大聲的音樂打擾了安靜的街道。

examples.en: The teacher asked what had caused the disturbance.
examples.zh: 老師問是什麼造成了騷動。

examples.en: The repairs caused a brief disturbance to traffic.
examples.zh: 維修工作短暫干擾了交通。

explains: This is an interruption to a calm or normal situation. A loud noise can break the quiet. People may stop what they are doing to notice it.
A class is reading silently when shouting begins outside the window. The noise interrupts everyone’s concentration. The noun can name that disruption.
The word can also mean a change that upsets the usual way something works. Road repairs may interrupt the normal flow of traffic. The effect may last until the work is finished.

examples.en: Never put all your eggs in one basket; diversify your investments.
examples.zh: 切勿把所有雞蛋放在同一個籃子裡；務必分散投資標的。

examples.en: The tech firm decided to diversify into healthcare and artificial intelligence solutions.
examples.zh: 該科技大廠決定跨界多元化發展，積極進軍智慧醫療與人工智慧解決方案。

examples.en: Farmers diversify crop varieties to protect against potential seasonal droughts.
examples.zh: 農民多角化種植不同抗旱農作物品種，以有效抵禦潛在的季節性乾旱風險。

entries.definition: 分散（風險、投資）；使多樣化
explains: This means to add more kinds of things instead of depending on only one. A collection or activity becomes more varied. The range grows wider.
A farm that grows only one crop begins growing fruit and vegetables too. It now produces several types of food. The farm has broadened what it does.
A shop may add new kinds of products for different customers. A person may try several hobbies instead of just one. The verb describes increasing variety.

examples.en: The funny story was a welcome diversion during the long wait.
examples.zh: 漫長等待中，這個有趣的故事是令人愉快的消遣。

examples.en: Drivers followed a diversion around the closed bridge.
examples.zh: 駕駛依照改道路線繞過封閉的橋。

examples.en: The loud noise created a diversion that drew everyone’s attention.
examples.zh: 那聲巨響轉移了大家的注意力。

explains: This can mean something that takes attention away from another activity. A sudden noise may make people look in a different direction. Their focus changes.
In road travel, the noun can name an alternate way around a closed route. Drivers follow signs to avoid the blocked section. They return to the main road later.
The noun can also mean an enjoyable activity that provides a break. A short game may help pass a rainy afternoon. It offers something pleasant to do.

examples.en: The workers diverted traffic around the flooded road.
examples.zh: 工人讓車流改道，繞過淹水的道路。

examples.en: A small channel diverted water toward the garden.
examples.zh: 一條小水道將水引向花園。

examples.en: The funny question diverted her attention from the long wait.
examples.zh: 那個有趣的問題轉移了她對漫長等待的注意力。

explains: This means to turn something away from its usual direction. Water may be sent through a different channel. Traffic can be directed onto another road.
A worker places signs where a road is closed. Drivers follow a new path around the problem. Their travel has been redirected.
The verb can also mean taking someone’s attention away from a thought or task. An interesting question may make a worried person think about something else. The focus shifts to a new subject.

examples.en: Stable high-dividend stocks pay regular quarterly cash payouts to investors.
examples.zh: 穩健的高股息股票定期向投資人發放每季度的現金股利。

examples.en: The corporation's board voted to distribute annual profits as shareholder dividends.
examples.zh: 公司董事會投票決議將當年度所獲盈餘以股利形式分派給廣大全體股東。

examples.en: Hard work in school paid dividends when she won a full scholarship to Cambridge.
examples.zh: 求學期間的孜孜不倦最終迎來了甜美回報，她順利榮獲劍橋大學全額獎學金。

examples.en: High-dividend ETFs pay quarterly cash dividends directly into investor bank accounts.
examples.zh: 高股息 ETF 每一季皆會將豐厚穩健的現金股息與收益平準金自動匯入投資人的銀行戶頭。

examples.en: The board of directors voted to increase the company's annual cash dividend by ten percent.
examples.zh: 公司董事會投票通過了最新股利分派案，宣布將當年度現金股利發放金額調升一成以回饋股東。

examples.en: Retirees often rely on consistent stock dividend payouts to cover their monthly living costs.
examples.zh: 許多退休樂齡族群高度仰賴每期按時發放的穩定股票股利配息，作為每個月各項生活開銷的依靠。

entries.definition: 股息；股利；紅利；股票股利；現金股息；分紅
explains: This can mean money a company pays to people who own its shares. It is often paid from profits. The amount and timing can vary.
A business may decide to share part of its earnings with its owners. Each shareholder receives an amount linked to the shares held. The noun can name that payment.
The word can also describe a useful benefit from effort. Regular practice may bring better skills later. People sometimes use the financial idea to talk about that kind of return.

examples.en: The story began with a warning of approaching doom.
examples.zh: 故事以末日將近的警告開場。

examples.en: The lack of water doomed the garden project.
examples.zh: 缺水注定讓花園計畫失敗。

examples.en: The dark clouds gave the scene a feeling of doom.
examples.zh: 烏雲讓這個場景帶有災禍將至的感覺。

explains: This means a terrible fate or an expected end in destruction or failure. Stories often use it to create a sense of fear. The future seems very dark.
A tale may describe a castle that everyone believes will soon fall. Characters sense that disaster is coming. The noun names that threatening fate.
As a verb, it means to make failure or a bad ending almost certain. A plan may be impossible because it lacks something essential. That serious weakness can decide its fate.

examples.en: Living in the university dormitory is a great way to make lifelong friends.
examples.zh: 住在大學宿舍是結交終生好友的極佳途徑。

examples.en: Each dormitory room accommodates four students with study desks and bunk beds.
examples.zh: 每一間學生宿舍寢室配有書桌與上下鋪，供四位學生同住。

examples.en: The resident advisor oversees building safety rules within the dormitory.
examples.zh: 舍監督導負責維護宿舍大樓內部的各項安全公約守則。

explains: This is a building where many students live during their studies. Bedrooms may be shared or private. Residents often share bathrooms or common spaces.
A student moves away from home to attend a distant school. The school provides a room near classrooms and the library. Other students live in the same building.
The noun can also mean a large room with beds for several people. People sleep in the same space instead of separate bedrooms. A camp or hostel may have such a room.

examples.en: Raw material prices experienced a sharp downward trend this quarter.
examples.zh: 原物料價格在該季度經歷了急遽的下滑走勢。

examples.en: The roller coaster plunged downward at dizzying speed, making riders scream.
examples.zh: 雲霄飛車以令人目眩神迷的驚人高速由最高點向下垂直俯衝，令所有遊客放聲尖叫。

examples.en: Poor cash flow can push a struggling business into a dangerous downward spiral.
examples.zh: 長期現金流枯竭且債台高築，極易將一家營運困難的中小企業拖入危險的惡性下滑螺旋。

explains: This describes movement toward a lower place or position. A ball rolls from the top of a hill toward the bottom. Its height becomes lower as it travels.
A person may point toward the ground instead of the sky. An arrow can show that direction on a sign. The word describes where the arrow is pointing.
The adjective can also describe a decrease in an amount or level. A line on a chart may slope toward smaller numbers. The trend shows that the measured amount is falling.

examples.en: Raw material prices experienced a sharp downward trend this quarter.
examples.zh: 原物料價格在該季度經歷了急遽的下滑走勢。

examples.en: The roller coaster plunged downward at dizzying speed, making riders scream.
examples.zh: 雲霄飛車以令人目眩神迷的驚人高速由最高點向下垂直俯衝，令所有遊客放聲尖叫。

examples.en: Poor cash flow can push a struggling business into a dangerous downward spiral.
examples.zh: 長期現金流枯竭且債台高築，極易將一家營運困難的中小企業拖入危險的惡性下滑螺旋。

explains: This means toward a lower level or place. Rain falls from clouds toward the ground. The movement goes from higher to lower.
A climber looks from a high rock toward the valley below. The eyes turn away from the top of the mountain. The word can describe that direction of looking.
It can also describe change toward a smaller amount. A price may fall over several weeks. A graph can show the movement toward lower values.

examples.en: Grandpa dozed in his chair after lunch.
examples.zh: 爺爺午飯後坐在椅子上打盹。

examples.en: I had a short doze during the train ride.
examples.zh: 我在搭火車時小睡了一下。

examples.en: The cat was dozing beside the sunny window.
examples.zh: 貓在陽光照進來的窗邊打盹。

explains: This means to sleep lightly, often for a short time. A person may drift between sleep and waking. Small sounds may wake them easily.
A tired traveler closes their eyes on a train. The traveler sleeps for a few minutes and then looks around again. The sleep is brief and not very deep.
The noun can name a short period of light sleep. Someone may rest in a chair after lunch. They wake without having slept for a full night.

examples.en: The plan required a drastic change to our schedule.
examples.zh: 這項計畫需要大幅更動我們的時間表。

examples.en: The town took drastic measures to deal with the water shortage.
examples.zh: 鎮上採取了大幅度措施來處理缺水問題。

examples.en: There was a drastic drop in temperature overnight.
examples.zh: 氣溫在一夜之間大幅下降。

explains: This describes a change or action that is very large and severe. It goes much further than a small adjustment. The effects can be powerful and noticeable.
A school changes its whole timetable instead of moving just one lesson. Almost every class happens at a different time. The change is wide-ranging.
The word can also describe strong measures taken to deal with a serious problem. A group may decide that minor steps are not enough. It chooses an action with a much bigger effect.

examples.en: A cold draught came through the gap under the door.
examples.zh: 一股冷風從門底的縫隙吹進來。

examples.en: He took a long draught of water after the walk.
examples.zh: 步行之後，他喝了一大口水。

examples.en: The restaurant serves draught beer.
examples.zh: 這家餐廳供應桶裝生啤酒。

explains: This can mean a current of air entering a room. Cold air may come through a gap beside a window. A person sitting nearby can feel it.
The noun can also mean a long drink or the amount swallowed at one time. A thirsty traveler may take a deep swallow of water. This use is often found in stories.
The word can describe drinks served from a large container rather than a sealed bottle. Beer is often served this way. The liquid flows through a tap into a glass.

examples.en: She put her folded shirts in the dresser.
examples.zh: 她把摺好的襯衫放進衣櫃抽屜裡。

examples.en: A mirror hung above the bedroom dresser.
examples.zh: 臥室的抽屜櫃上方掛著一面鏡子。

examples.en: The dresser helped the actor change costumes between scenes.
examples.zh: 服裝助理幫演員在場景之間換裝。

explains: This can mean a piece of furniture with drawers for clothing. It often stands in a bedroom. A mirror may be placed above it.
In some homes, the word names a large kitchen cupboard with shelves for plates and other items. The top may be used to display dishes. Storage space lies below.
The noun can also name someone who helps performers put on and change costumes. This person may work behind the stage. Quick changes between scenes require careful preparation.

examples.en: She poured a little dressing over the salad.
examples.zh: 她在沙拉上淋了一點沙拉醬。

examples.en: The nurse placed a clean dressing over the wound.
examples.zh: 護理師在傷口上覆蓋了乾淨的敷料。

examples.en: The child still needed help with dressing.
examples.zh: 這個孩子穿衣服時仍需要幫忙。

explains: This can mean a sauce added to a salad. It may contain oil, vinegar, herbs, or other ingredients. The mixture adds flavor to the vegetables.
The noun can also mean material placed over a wound. A pad or other covering protects the injured area. It may help keep the surface clean.
The same noun can refer to putting on clothes. A small child learns how to do this without help. It is often part of the morning routine.

examples.en: The camera has a dual lens for wide and close views.
examples.zh: 這台相機有雙鏡頭，可拍攝廣角和近距離畫面。

examples.en: She has dual citizenship in Canada and Taiwan.
examples.zh: 她同時擁有加拿大和台灣的雙重國籍。

examples.en: The school built a dual-purpose room for music and meetings.
examples.zh: 學校蓋了一間兼作音樂教室和會議室的多用途房間。

explains: It describes something with two parts or purposes. A phone may have two cameras. Each one has a different job.
A person with two citizenships belongs legally to two countries. Both connections can matter. The adjective describes this situation.
Some furniture serves two uses. A sofa bed offers a seat by day and a bed at night. This feature saves space.

examples.en: The shopper was dubious about the watch's very low price.
examples.zh: 購物者對這支手錶低得不尋常的價格感到懷疑。

examples.en: His excuse sounded dubious to the teacher.
examples.zh: 老師覺得他的藉口聽起來不太可信。

examples.en: The report made a dubious claim without showing evidence.
examples.zh: 這份報告提出了可疑的說法，卻沒有提供證據。

explains: It describes something that seems doubtful or not fully trustworthy. A claim may lack proof. Listeners may wonder whether it is true.
A person can look unsure about a plan. The face may show doubt, and the answer may come slowly. This adjective captures uncertainty.
A deal may seem questionable when the price is strangely low. Careful buyers may ask for more facts. They do not accept every promise.

examples.en: The flight duration is about three hours.
examples.zh: 這趟航班的飛行時間約為三小時。

examples.en: We stayed inside for the duration of the storm.
examples.zh: 暴風雨持續期間，我們都待在室內。

examples.en: The class has a duration of forty minutes.
examples.zh: 這堂課的時間長度是四十分鐘。

explains: This noun names how long an event or condition lasts. A short song has a brief span. A long trip has a greater span.
A movie ticket may list the running time. That number tells viewers how long the show continues. It measures the event from start to finish.
Some rules apply for a set period. A library card may remain active for one year. That time span is its length.

examples.en: We reached the campsite at dusk.
examples.zh: 我們在黃昏時抵達營地。

examples.en: Bats began to fly as dusk settled over the garden.
examples.zh: 黃昏籠罩花園時，蝙蝠開始飛了起來。

examples.en: The sky turned orange at dusk.
examples.zh: 黃昏時天空變成橘色。

explains: This is the dim time near evening, after the sun has gone down. The sky is not fully dark yet. Streetlights may begin to shine.
Birds often return to their nests as daylight fades. Families may walk home under a purple sky. This part of the day comes before night.
The word can set a quiet mood in a story. Shadows grow longer, and colors become soft. People can still see shapes outdoors.

examples.en: A dwarf guarded the cave in the old tale.
examples.zh: 在古老故事裡，一名矮人守護著洞穴。

examples.en: The bright dwarf star is smaller than the Sun.
examples.zh: 這顆明亮的矮星比太陽小。

examples.en: The new stadium dwarfs the buildings around it.
examples.zh: 新體育場讓周圍的建築顯得格外渺小。

explains: As a noun, this can name a very small person in old tales or fantasy stories. Such characters may live underground. Some tales give them magical skills.
In astronomy, a star of a certain small size may receive this name. It still produces light and heat. Scientists classify stars by their properties.
As a verb, it means to make another thing seem much smaller. A huge tower can make nearby houses look tiny. The size contrast is striking.

examples.en: Many families dwell in the valley near the river.
examples.zh: 許多家庭住在河邊的山谷裡。

examples.en: Please do not dwell on one small mistake all day.
examples.zh: 請不要整天一直想著一個小錯誤。

examples.en: The story says that spirits dwell beneath the old bridge.
examples.zh: 故事說，精靈住在那座老橋底下。

explains: This verb means to live in a particular place. It often appears in formal writing or fixed expressions. A family may live beside a river.
It can also mean to keep thinking or speaking about one subject for too long. A person may focus on an old mistake. Friends might suggest looking ahead.
Writers sometimes use it for creatures in a place. Tiny animals may live among leaves. The word gives a slightly formal tone to their home.

examples.en: The family built a small dwelling beside the lake.
examples.zh: 這家人在湖邊蓋了一間小住屋。

examples.en: Each dwelling on the street has a red door.
examples.zh: 這條街上的每間住宅都有一扇紅門。

examples.en: The cave became a winter dwelling for the fox.
examples.zh: 這座洞穴成了狐狸過冬的棲身處。

explains: This noun means a place where someone lives. It can be a house, apartment, or smaller shelter. The term is more formal than home.
A report about a fire may count every affected residence. The writer may use this word for each place where people sleep and keep belongings. The term names the place itself.
Animals also have places where they live. A nest or den can serve as shelter. This noun can describe a human or animal home.

examples.en: The eccentric artist painted his bicycle bright blue.
examples.zh: 那位古怪的藝術家把自己的腳踏車漆成亮藍色。
