examples.en: Her eccentric uncle wears a different hat every day.
examples.zh: 她那位行事古怪的叔叔每天都戴不同的帽子。

examples.en: They bought an eccentric house with a round doorway.
examples.zh: 他們買了一棟有圓形門口的奇特房子。

explains: This adjective describes behavior or ideas that seem unusual and different from what most people expect. A person may wear bright clothes every day. Others may find the choice surprising.
A character in a book may collect bottle caps and speak to a clock. Such odd habits make the character memorable. The word can describe that person too.
Unusual design choices can also receive this label. A house might have round windows and a purple roof. The style feels original rather than ordinary.

examples.en: Day turned into eerie twilight during totality of the breathtaking solar eclipse.
examples.zh: 在震撼人心的日全食（Solar Eclipse）全食階段，原本晴朗的白晝瞬間化為昏暗神秘的黑夜，太陽日冕如銀環浮現。

examples.en: Observers wore certified solar safety glasses to prevent retinal damage while viewing the partial eclipse.
examples.zh: 現場觀測民眾皆配戴通過國際認證的專用日食觀測眼鏡，以防強烈陽光灼傷視網膜。

examples.en: The newcomer's extraordinary athletic performance completely eclipsed all previous tournament records.
examples.zh: 這位新秀選手在賽場上令人驚嘆的破紀錄表現，完全遮蔽掩蓋了所有前輩留下的賽會輝煌紀錄。

entries.definition: 日全食（黑晝奇景）；月食；遮蔽
explains: This noun describes an event in which one space object partly or fully blocks another from view. During a solar event, the Moon covers the Sun. The sky may grow dim.
The same noun can describe a loss of attention or importance. A new star may outshine an older performer. The older person receives less notice.
As a verb, it means to outshine or overshadow something. A wonderful goal can become the main memory of a game. Earlier moments may seem less important.

examples.en: These berries are edible, but those red ones are poisonous.
examples.zh: 這些莓果可以食用，但那些紅色的有毒。

examples.en: The cake has edible flowers on top.
examples.zh: 蛋糕上面有可食用的花朵。

examples.en: The children checked whether the wild mushrooms were edible.
examples.zh: 孩子們確認那些野生蘑菇是否可以食用。

explains: This adjective means safe or suitable to eat. Some plants look pretty but are poisonous. A guide can help identify which ones people may consume.
A label on a cake decoration may say it is safe to eat. This matters because some decorations are only for display. The word gives useful food information.
Certain parts of a fruit are eaten, while others are thrown away. The soft flesh is food, but a hard pit is not. This describes what may be eaten.

examples.en: The newspaper's editorial called for urgent investments in renewable energy.
examples.zh: 該報今日刊登的重量級社論強烈呼籲各界應擴大推動綠色再生能源投資。

examples.en: She joined the publishing house as an editorial assistant proofreading manuscripts.
examples.zh: 她加入出版社擔任編輯助理，負責校對書稿。

examples.en: The paper's editorial board unanimously endorsed the new educational reform bill.
examples.zh: 該報的社論委員會全票表決贊成並支持這項教育改革新法案。

explains: This adjective relates to preparing written material for publication. An editor checks facts, wording, and organization. Careful review helps a book read clearly.
A newspaper may publish an opinion article written by its editors. The piece states the paper's view on an issue. Readers can distinguish it from a reporter's news story.
The noun can also mean that opinion article itself. It may support a public change or criticize a decision. The writer argues for a position.

examples.en: The electrician rewired the circuit breaker box safely.
examples.zh: 電工技師安全地重新配置了總配電箱電路。

examples.en: Only hire a qualified licensed electrician to install high-voltage equipment.
examples.zh: 僅應聘請合格領有執照的甲級電匠來安裝高電壓設備。

examples.en: The electrician diagnosed why the kitchen power outlets suddenly lost electricity.
examples.zh: 水電電工排查診斷出了廚房插座為何突然無預警斷電。

examples.en: Certified electricians upgraded the main electrical breaker panel to 100 amperes.
examples.zh: 擁有甲級證照的專業水電師傅將全戶總配電盤電箱總安培數擴容升級至 100 安培。

examples.en: An experienced electrician added dedicated circuits for the high-power induction stove.
examples.zh: 經驗老到的水電師傅為廚房大功率 IH 電磁爐拉設了獨立的 220V 專用無熔絲迴路。

examples.en: Never attempt dangerous wiring modifications yourself; always consult a qualified electrician.
examples.zh: 絕不要自行冒險私接高壓強電配線；遇有配電需求請務必洽詢合格持照的水電技師。

entries.definition: 電工；配電技師；水電師傅；甲級電匠
explains: This noun names a trained worker who installs or repairs electrical systems. The job involves wires, switches, and outlets. Proper training helps prevent dangerous mistakes.
A family may call this worker when a wall socket stops working. The worker checks the cause and fixes the problem. This is a skilled trade.
New buildings need electrical systems for lights and appliances. A qualified worker connects and tests them. The work helps power reach rooms safely.

examples.en: The platform will elevate the singer above the crowd.
examples.zh: 升降台會把歌手升到人群上方。

examples.en: Her careful work helped elevate her to team leader.
examples.zh: 她認真的工作讓她升任組長。

examples.en: The bright music seemed to elevate everyone's mood.
examples.zh: 明快的音樂似乎讓大家的心情都變好了。

explains: This verb means to raise something to a higher place or level. A lift can move a box upward. The object ends up above its earlier position.
It can also mean to improve someone's status or importance. A new role may give a worker more responsibility. The change places that person in a higher position.
The word may describe lifting spirits or thought. Kind words can improve someone's mood. A thoughtful book can raise a discussion to a deeper level.

examples.en: The emigrant left Ireland to begin a new life in Canada.
examples.zh: 這名移民離開愛爾蘭，前往加拿大展開新生活。

examples.en: Her grandfather was an emigrant from Italy.
examples.zh: 她的祖父是從義大利移居出去的人。

examples.en: The town held a farewell party for each emigrant family.
examples.zh: 鎮上為每個移居海外的家庭舉辦歡送會。

explains: This noun describes a person who leaves one country to live in another. The viewpoint is the country being left. A family may move abroad for work.
When a town loses many residents to other places, its people may describe those who leave with this term. Their destination may be far away. The direction is from home to abroad.
A person can be this from one place and an immigrant in another. The first label focuses on departure. The second focuses on arrival. Family records may describe that move.

examples.en: They plan to emigrate from Peru next year.
examples.zh: 他們計畫明年從秘魯移居海外。

examples.en: Her parents emigrated to Australia when they were young.
examples.zh: 她的父母年輕時移居澳洲。

examples.en: Some families emigrate to join relatives abroad.
examples.zh: 有些家庭移居海外與親人團聚。

explains: This verb means to leave one's country and settle in another. The move is usually lasting, not a brief trip. People may go for safety or work.
A family that moves from one nation to a new home elsewhere performs this action. The word looks at the departure. Another country becomes their destination.
This action differs from visiting abroad for a holiday. The family plans to build daily life somewhere new. They may learn local customs and language.

examples.en: Emigration from the island increased after the factory closed.
examples.zh: 工廠關閉後，移出這座島的人數增加了。

examples.en: The museum exhibit explains Irish emigration in the nineteenth century.
examples.zh: 博物館展覽介紹了十九世紀愛爾蘭人的移民潮。

examples.en: War caused a wave of emigration from the region.
examples.zh: 戰爭引發了該地區的移民潮。

explains: This noun names the process of leaving one's country to settle elsewhere. It describes movement away from a home nation. Many families may take part.
A history book may discuss a time when many residents moved abroad. The large movement of people is a social trend. This noun describes that process.
The viewpoint differs from immigration. One term focuses on people leaving. The other focuses on people arriving in a new country.

examples.en: We found a clear map in the children's encyclopedia.
examples.zh: 我們在兒童百科全書裡找到一張清楚的地圖。

examples.en: The encyclopedia has an entry about ancient Egypt.
examples.zh: 這本百科全書有一篇介紹古埃及的條目。

examples.en: She used an online encyclopedia for her school report.
examples.zh: 她使用線上百科全書完成學校報告。

explains: This reference work gathers facts about many subjects. Entries are arranged so readers can find information. It may come as books or a website.
A student can use this source to learn basic facts about planets, music, or history. Articles usually explain topics in an organized way. They support research.
A single volume may cover one field, while a large set covers many. Readers look up a subject rather than read every page in order. Entries appear in alphabetical order.

examples.en: Their new garden is a community endeavor.
examples.zh: 他們的新花園是社區共同努力的成果。

examples.en: She will endeavor to finish the model before Friday.
examples.zh: 她會盡力在星期五前完成模型。

examples.en: The rescue endeavor brought neighbors together.
examples.zh: 這項救援行動讓鄰居們團結起來。

explains: As a noun, this means a serious effort to do something difficult. A team may work toward a shared goal. Success is not always certain.
As a verb, it means to try earnestly. A young musician may practice each day to improve. The action shows commitment, even when progress is slow.
This term often sounds formal. A school may praise a student's effort in a project. It highlights determined work rather than an easy result.

examples.en: Her endowment for music became clear at an early age.
examples.zh: 她很早就展現出音樂方面的天賦。

examples.en: The college used its endowment to fund student scholarships.
examples.zh: 這所學院運用捐贈基金提供學生獎學金。

examples.en: A local endowment supports the town's public library.
examples.zh: 當地的捐贈基金支持鎮上的公共圖書館。

explains: This noun can mean a natural quality or ability that someone possesses. A child may have a gift for music. Practice can help that ability grow.
It can also mean money or property given to support an institution. A university may invest a donation and use its earnings. The fund helps pay future needs.
A person may leave funds to a library or school. The gift can continue supporting programs over many years. This lasting donation is another use.

examples.en: Long-distance cycling builds extraordinary cardiovascular stamina and endurance.
examples.zh: 長途公路自行車騎乘能鍛鍊出卓越超群的心肺耐力與堅韌毅力。

examples.en: Ultra-marathon runners push the absolute biological limits of human endurance.
examples.zh: 征戰極限百公里超馬的長跑名將，不斷用驚人意志力挑戰並刷新人類生理耐力的絕對極限。

examples.en: The ceramic brake pads demonstrated remarkable thermal endurance under repeated high-speed stops.
examples.zh: 頂級陶瓷煞車來令片在高頻繁的極速煞停摩擦高溫考驗下，展現出了令人驚嘆的耐熱持久性能。

examples.en: Long-distance cycling builds cardiovascular fitness and muscular endurance.
examples.zh: 長距離公路自行車騎乘能大幅強化心肺功能並鍛鍊腿部核心的深層肌耐力。

examples.en: Mountaineering at extreme altitudes tests human mental and physical endurance to the absolute limit.
examples.zh: 在極高海拔的險峻雪山攀登，將人類的身心極限耐力推向了前所未有的考驗。

examples.en: Swimming continuous laps every morning is a fantastic way to develop total-body endurance.
examples.zh: 每天清晨堅持不懈地在泳池游上數十趟，是鍛鍊全身綜合耐力的極佳運動方式。

examples.en: Multi-day mountain traverses demand exceptional aerobic capacity and cardiovascular endurance.
examples.zh: 挑戰長達一週的中央山脈南二段或能高安東軍高山縱走，極度需要強大的心肺與肌耐力。

examples.en: Long-distance trail running builds extraordinary leg endurance and mental fortitude.
examples.zh: 長期堅持越野山徑跑訓練，能為人體建立起非凡卓越的腿部肌肉耐力與堅不可摧的鋼鐵心理意志。

examples.en: The heroic marathon runner pushed through severe exhaustion through sheer willpower and physical endurance.
examples.zh: 這位英雄般的馬拉松健兒憑藉純粹的鋼鐵意志與頑強體能耐力，在極度力竭狀態下咬牙衝過終點線。

entries.definition: 耐力；持久力；忍耐力；堅韌體能耐力
explains: This noun means the ability to continue through effort, pain, or difficulty. A runner needs strength over a long race. The quality helps the body keep going.
Mental strength can also last through a hard task. A student may keep working on a challenging puzzle. Patience and effort are part of this quality.
A long performance tests how well equipment lasts under strain. A battery that works for many hours shows lasting power. The noun can describe that ability.

examples.en: Soft music can enhance the mood of the dinner.
examples.zh: 柔和的音樂能提升晚餐的氣氛。

examples.en: The new windows enhanced the view of the garden.
examples.zh: 新窗戶讓花園景色更加出色。

examples.en: A short caption enhances the meaning of the photograph.
examples.zh: 簡短的說明文字能增進照片所傳達的意義。

explains: This verb means to improve the quality, value, or appearance of something. Better lighting can make a room look warmer. The change adds to what is already there.
A clear title can make a school project easier to understand. Small improvements help the whole piece work better. The original project remains recognizable.
This idea is about making a good feature stronger. Color can bring out details in a picture. The added effect helps viewers notice them.

examples.en: The historical Enlightenment era championed scientific reason, individual freedom, and democratic equality.
examples.zh: 橫掃歐洲的十八世紀「啟蒙運動」（Enlightenment），大舉確立了科學理性、個人自由與民主平等的思想燈塔。

examples.en: Decades of disciplined meditation under ancient bodhi trees brought the sage to a state of spiritual enlightenment.
examples.zh: 在古老菩提樹下歷經數十年如一日的嚴格打坐參禪與內觀，引導這位高僧最終證悟抵達精神心靈大徹大悟的超脫境界。

examples.en: Reading global history from non-Western viewpoints provided university students with immense intellectual enlightenment.
examples.zh: 跳脫西方中心主義、從多元南方視角研讀全球通史，為這群大學歷史系學子帶來了豁然開朗的知識啟蒙心智覺醒。

entries.definition: 十八世紀啟蒙思潮心智覺醒；啟蒙
explains: This verb means to give someone useful knowledge or a clearer understanding. A teacher can explain a difficult idea. The learner sees the subject in a new way.
It can also describe a sudden improvement in understanding. Reading about another culture may help a person see beyond old assumptions. New facts can change a viewpoint.
As a noun, it names the state of gaining deeper understanding. A class discussion can open students' minds. The result is greater awareness.

examples.en: Immersing oneself in great art offers deep emotional resonance and lifelong spiritual enrichment.
examples.zh: 讓自己沉浸於偉大藝術名作的浩瀚海洋中，能獲得深沉的情感共鳴與終身豐盈的心靈精神富足。

examples.en: The community college offers weekend foreign language and cooking classes for personal enrichment.
examples.zh: 社區大學每逢週末開設多元的外語會話、陶藝及烘焙料理手作課程，提供廣大市民豐富多元的終身學習自我充實。

examples.en: Zoo caretakers introduce puzzle toys and foraging mazes as daily mental enrichment for rescued primates.
examples.zh: 台北市立動物園保育員每天定期在展場投放益智藏食玩具與攀爬繩梯，為靈長類動物提供豐富化行為刺激。

entries.definition: 豐盈充實心靈世界；豐富
explains: This verb means to improve something by adding valuable qualities. A story gains depth when it includes vivid details. Those additions make the experience fuller.
Food may become more nutritious by adding helpful ingredients. The added parts increase its value. The word can describe this kind of improvement.
Experiences can also make a person's life more interesting or meaningful. Meeting new people can broaden someone's view. New knowledge adds depth to daily life.

examples.en: Maya will enroll in the art class this fall.
examples.zh: Maya 今年秋天會報名參加美術課。

examples.en: The school opened enrollment for its summer program.
examples.zh: 學校開放暑期課程報名了。

examples.en: He enrolled his daughter in a weekend dance course.
examples.zh: 他替女兒報名了週末舞蹈課程。

explains: This verb means to officially join a class, school, or program. A student fills out forms and becomes a member. The school records the new name.
A parent may sign a child up for swimming lessons. Once accepted, the child is part of the course. The noun form can describe the act or number of students.
A person can join a club by completing its registration. The process makes the membership official. It often happens before classes or activities begin.

examples.en: The late goal helped equalize the score.
examples.zh: 最後的進球幫助兩隊追平比分。

examples.en: The club added a second bus to equalize travel times.
examples.zh: 俱樂部加開第二輛巴士，讓交通時間更加一致。

examples.en: The new rule aims to equalize access to the school library.
examples.zh: 新規定旨在讓大家都能平等使用學校圖書館。

explains: This verb means to make two amounts, conditions, or chances more equal. A teacher may give each group the same time. The difference becomes smaller.
A sports rule can help balance a contest between teams. The rule gives each side a fairer chance. It does not guarantee the same result.
Numbers may also be adjusted until they match. If one side has more points, a later score can bring the totals level. The action creates equality.

examples.en: Do not equate a high price with high quality.
examples.zh: 不要把高價格等同於高品質。

examples.en: The chart equates one mile with about 1.6 kilometers.
examples.zh: 圖表將一英里換算為約 1.6 公里。

examples.en: She equated his silence with agreement, but he was unsure.
examples.zh: 她把他的沉默當成同意，但他其實還不確定。

explains: This verb means to treat two things as if they were the same. A person may confuse similar ideas. The comparison can hide important differences.
A teacher may compare two fractions by changing their form. The values become the same even though the numbers look different. This is a mathematical use.
People sometimes make unfair comparisons between unlike things. Careful speakers explain why the comparison works. The verb describes that act of comparison.

examples.en: A guide will escort the class through the museum.
examples.zh: 導覽員會陪同全班參觀博物館。

examples.en: The guest arrived with an escort.
examples.zh: 這位來賓由陪同人員一起抵達。

examples.en: Two volunteers escorted the children across the busy street.
examples.zh: 兩名志工陪孩子們穿越繁忙的街道。

explains: As a noun, this means a person who goes with someone for safety or guidance. A child may have an adult nearby on a trip. That person stays close.
As a verb, it means to go along with someone. A guide may lead visitors through a museum. The group moves together from one place to another.
A security worker can accompany a guest at a public event. The guest has help finding the right room. This role is often temporary.

examples.en: The players held their coach in high esteem.
examples.zh: 球員們非常敬重他們的教練。

examples.en: She esteems people who keep their promises.
examples.zh: 她敬重信守承諾的人。

examples.en: His self-esteem grew after he learned the new skill.
examples.zh: 學會這項新技能後，他的自尊心提升了。

explains: This noun means great respect or admiration for someone. A student may look up to a kind teacher. The feeling comes from recognizing good qualities.
As a verb, it means to regard someone with respect. People may value a fair judge. Their view reflects admiration and high regard.
The feeling can also relate to how people value themselves. A person who feels worthy has a positive view of personal value. This is self-respect.

examples.en: Looking across millions of light-years through a telescope is literally looking across space into deep eternity.
examples.zh: 透過望遠鏡凝視數百萬光年外的璀璨星光，實質上正是跨越了無垠的時空深淵凝視著「永恆」（Eternity）。

examples.en: Ancient Egyptian pharaohs constructed stone pyramids to safeguard their immortal souls throughout eternity.
examples.zh: 古埃及法老王耗費傾國之力興建巍峨雄偉的巨石金字塔，期盼庇護其不朽靈魂在永恆時空中長存。

examples.en: In the stillness of the mountain sanctuary, waiting for the storm to pass felt like a timeless eternity.
examples.zh: 在空曠寂寥的高山避難山屋中，等待屋外狂暴山嵐風暴完全平息的漫長過程彷彿度過了一個世紀。

examples.en: With proper maintenance every few decades, a mechanical watch will tick rhythmically into eternity.
examples.zh: 只要每隔數十年細心洗油保養，一枚純機械腕錶將超越佩戴者的壽命，規律滴答「邁向永恆」（Eternity）。

examples.en: The ancient pyramids standing silently beneath desert stars evoke a breathtaking sense of timeless eternity.
examples.zh: 靜靜佇立在浩瀚沙漠星空下的古埃及巨石金字塔群，激起人們心中對超越時空限制、永恆不朽的崇高敬畏。

examples.en: Standing upon the windy mountain peak gazing at endless ridges, ten quiet minutes felt like an eternity.
examples.zh: 隻身佇立在狂風呼嘯的高山之巔極目遠眺綿延山巒，那靜謐無聲的短短十分鐘彷彿跨越了恆久的時光長河。

entries.definition: 凝望群星深處即是凝望跨越時空的永恆；擺輪滴答擺動、超越時間長河的機械永恆
explains: This noun means time without an end. Stories may describe a life continuing forever. It can also express an extremely long time.
People use the word in religious or philosophical ideas about life after death. Different traditions explain this endless state in different ways. It is beyond ordinary time.
In casual speech, someone may say a wait felt endless. The speaker does not mean actual endless time. The phrase simply emphasizes a very long delay.

examples.en: Firefighters helped evacuate the hotel.
examples.zh: 消防員協助疏散飯店裡的人。

examples.en: The school evacuated students during the gas leak.
examples.zh: 瓦斯外洩時，學校疏散了學生。

examples.en: Police asked residents to evacuate the coastal area.
examples.zh: 警方要求居民撤離沿海地區。

explains: This verb means to move people away from danger. A fire may force families to leave a building. Safety is the main reason for the move.
Officials may clear an area before a storm arrives. Residents go to a safer place for a while. The action protects people from possible harm.
The word can also apply to removing something from a place. Workers may empty a room before repairs. The area becomes clear for a new purpose.

examples.en: An evergreen tree stood beside the snowy road.
examples.zh: 一棵常綠樹矗立在積雪的道路旁。

examples.en: They planted evergreen shrubs around the house.
examples.zh: 他們在房子周圍種了常綠灌木。

examples.en: The old children's song remains an evergreen favorite.
examples.zh: 那首古老的兒歌一直深受喜愛。

explains: This adjective describes a plant that keeps its leaves through every season. Pine trees often stay green in winter. They do not lose all their leaves at once.
It can also name a plant with lasting green leaves. Gardeners may choose such plants for year-round color. Some kinds grow as trees or shrubs.
The term is also used for something that stays popular for a long time. A song may remain loved by new listeners. Its appeal does not quickly fade.

examples.en: The song evoked memories of summer camp.
examples.zh: 那首歌喚起了夏令營的回憶。

examples.en: Her letter evoked a feeling of hope.
examples.zh: 她的信喚起了希望的感覺。

examples.en: The old photograph evoked stories from his childhood.
examples.zh: 那張老照片勾起了他童年的往事。

explains: This verb means to bring a feeling, memory, or image into someone's mind. A familiar smell may recall a childhood home. The response can be emotional.
A painting can call up an idea without showing it directly. Dark colors may suggest sadness. Viewers connect the image with a feeling.
A story or song may awaken a memory from long ago. One detail reminds a person of a past event. This verb describes that mental effect.

examples.en: Each examinee received a numbered answer sheet.
examples.zh: 每位應試者都拿到一張有編號的答案卡。

examples.en: The examinee listened carefully to the recorded questions.
examples.zh: 應試者仔細聆聽錄音中的問題。

examples.en: An examinee may ask for extra paper during the test.
examples.zh: 應試者可以在考試時索取額外的紙張。

explains: This noun names a person who takes a test. The person answers questions or completes tasks. The results may show what has been learned.
At a driving test, the person behind the wheel is being judged. A trained worker watches the performance. The two people have different roles.
Schools and licensing groups use this term in formal settings. It focuses on the person being tested. The test can be written, spoken, or practical.

examples.en: The examiner handed out the test papers.
examples.zh: 監考人員發下了考卷。

examples.en: The examiner asked each candidate the same questions.
examples.zh: 考官向每位應試者提出相同的問題。

examples.en: A medical examiner reviewed the report.
examples.zh: 法醫審閱了這份報告。

explains: This noun names a person who checks or judges someone's work or answers. A teacher may fill this role during an exam. The person applies set standards.
A doctor who checks a patient during a formal assessment may also receive this title. The job is to observe and record findings. The setting determines the exact task.
The term is common in schools and official tests. A candidate gives answers, while this worker reviews them. The two roles are distinct.

examples.en: Lena excels at solving number puzzles.
examples.zh: Lena 很擅長解數字謎題。

examples.en: The young pianist excels in classical music.
examples.zh: 這位年輕鋼琴家在古典音樂方面表現出色。

examples.en: Our team excelled during the final round.
examples.zh: 我們隊在最後一輪表現得十分出色。

explains: This verb means to do very well at an activity or skill. A student may be especially strong in science. Practice can build that ability.
People can perform better than others in a particular area. A fast runner may stand out in short races. The verb highlights strong results.
The word can also mean to succeed or surpass a standard. A business may do very well in a difficult year. Its success stands out.

examples.en: The teacher read an excerpt from the novel.
examples.zh: 老師朗讀了小說中的一段節錄。

examples.en: This excerpt gives a glimpse of the poet's style.
examples.zh: 這段節錄讓人一窺詩人的風格。

examples.en: She excerpted one paragraph for her report.
examples.zh: 她為報告摘錄了一個段落。

explains: This noun means a short part taken from a longer text, speech, or piece of music. It gives readers a small sample. The full work remains much larger.
A book review may include a few lines from a novel. The selected passage can show the writer's style. It helps readers understand the larger work.
As a verb, it means to choose and copy a short part. A student may take a passage from a speech. The selection should match the topic.

examples.en: The shop donated its excess bread to a shelter.
examples.zh: 商店把多出的麵包捐給收容所。

examples.en: An excess of salt made the soup unpleasant.
examples.zh: 鹽放得太多，讓湯變得不好喝。

examples.en: The report found excess water in the basement.
examples.zh: 報告發現地下室積水過多。

explains: This adjective or noun refers to more than what is needed or allowed. Too much food may remain after a party. The extra amount is beyond the limit.
A store may have extra items that it cannot sell quickly. The surplus takes space. Careful planning can reduce the leftover amount.
It can also describe behavior that goes too far. Spending far more money than planned is beyond what is necessary. The word signals an unnecessary amount.

examples.en: The exclusion of younger students upset the parents.
examples.zh: 排除年紀較小的學生讓家長很不滿。

examples.en: The club changed its rule to prevent exclusion.
examples.zh: 俱樂部修改規則以避免排斥他人。

examples.en: The report examined the exclusion of rural families.
examples.zh: 這份報告探討了鄉村家庭遭到排除的情況。

explains: This noun means the act of keeping someone or something out. A club may refuse a person entry. The person cannot take part.
A rule can prevent certain people from joining an activity. The policy creates a boundary between included and excluded groups. The term names that separation.
A book may discuss groups that face unfair barriers. Their limited access is part of the problem. The noun describes the act or state of being left out.

examples.en: Children under five are exempt from the entry fee.
examples.zh: 未滿五歲的兒童免收入場費。

examples.en: The coach was exempt from the training requirement.
examples.zh: 教練不必遵守這項訓練要求。

examples.en: Some books are exempt from sales tax.
examples.zh: 某些書籍免徵銷售稅。

explains: This adjective describes someone who does not have to follow a particular rule or pay a fee. A child may enter a museum free. The usual charge does not apply.
A class can excuse certain students from one assignment for a good reason. The teacher states who is not required to complete it. The adjective marks that status.
Some goods may avoid a tax under a specific rule. The exemption applies only to certain cases. This describes being free from an obligation.

examples.en: The hikers exerted great effort on the steep trail.
examples.zh: 登山客在陡峭山徑上付出了很大的努力。

examples.en: She exerted pressure to have the broken light repaired.
examples.zh: 她施加壓力要求修好故障的燈。

examples.en: The players exerted themselves during the final minutes.
examples.zh: 球員們在最後幾分鐘全力以赴。

explains: This verb means to use energy, strength, or effort. A runner may work hard to climb a hill. The body uses power to keep moving.
It can also mean to apply influence or authority. A leader may use pressure to change a decision. The action affects what other people do.
A person might put effort into a difficult task. Careful work requires concentration and time. The verb emphasizes active use of effort.

examples.en: The school reduced its travel expenditure this year.
examples.zh: 學校今年減少了旅費支出。

examples.en: Food is the family's largest monthly expenditure.
examples.zh: 食物是這個家庭每月最大的開銷。

examples.en: The report lists public expenditure on roads.
examples.zh: 報告列出了道路方面的公共支出。

explains: This noun means money spent on something. A family may add up food and travel costs. The total is part of its spending.
A company records payments for rent, supplies, and wages. These costs help show how money is used. The word often appears in budgets.
Governments also report the money used for services or projects. The amount may be compared with income. This noun describes the act or total of spending.

examples.en: Check the expiration date on the milk carton.
examples.zh: 請查看牛奶紙盒上的有效期限。

examples.en: The passport's expiration is listed on its final page.
examples.zh: 護照的到期日列在最後一頁。

examples.en: The form asks for the expiration of your membership card.
examples.zh: 表格要求填寫會員卡的到期日。

explains: This noun can mean the date when something ends or is no longer valid. A ticket may have a final usable day. After that, it cannot be accepted.
Food labels show a date that helps buyers judge freshness. The printed date marks when the item should no longer be sold as fresh. Buyers can use it to choose a fresh product.
The term can also name the act of breathing out in medical language. Air leaves the lungs. The context shows which meaning is intended.

examples.en: My library card will expire in June.
examples.zh: 我的借書證將於六月到期。

examples.en: The coupon expired before we could use it.
examples.zh: 優惠券在我們使用前就過期了。

examples.en: The patient was asked to inhale and then expire slowly.
examples.zh: 病人被要求先吸氣，再慢慢吐氣。

explains: This verb means to reach the end of a valid period. A coupon may no longer work after its final date. The offer is no longer available.
Food or medicine can become too old for its intended use. A label may show the last date for use. Afterward, its stated period has ended.
The verb can also mean to breathe out. A person releases air from the lungs. In this sense, the word appears in medical descriptions.

examples.en: Lyophilized bacterial extract contains all the enzymes needed to synthesize complex proteins in test tubes.
examples.zh: 凍乾保存的「細胞裂解提取物」（Extract），封存了在試管中直接合成複雜蛋白質所需的全部酵素機構。

examples.en: Add two drops of pure Madagascar vanilla extract to the waffle batter for rich confectionery flavor.
examples.zh: 在格子鬆餅麵糊中滴入兩滴純天然馬達加斯加香草精提取物，能烘烤出濃郁撲鼻的甜點香氣。

examples.en: The literary journal printed a fascinating extract from the author’s upcoming historical biography.
examples.zh: 這本文學權威雜誌搶先刊載了這位知名傳記作家即將出版的歷史傳記新書精選節錄。

entries.definition: 含有豐富核糖體與轉譯酵素之細胞裂解提取物；提取物
explains: As a verb, this means to remove something from a larger source. A cook may take flavor from herbs. A researcher may obtain facts from records.
A short passage can be taken from a book for a report. The selected part keeps its original meaning. The source is larger than the copied piece.
As a noun, it can mean a concentrated substance taken from a plant or another material. Vanilla flavoring is one familiar example. Only part of the source remains.

examples.en: She joined an extracurricular chess club.
examples.zh: 她加入了課外西洋棋社。

examples.en: The school offers several extracurricular activities.
examples.zh: 學校提供好幾種課外活動。

examples.en: His extracurricular work included helping at the library.
examples.zh: 他的課外活動包括在圖書館幫忙。

explains: This adjective describes school activities that happen outside regular lessons. Students may join a music group after class. These activities are part of school life.
A team, club, or art program can fit this description. It gives students a chance to practice interests. It is separate from normal classroom study.
Schools often list sports and service groups in this category. Students choose activities based on their interests. The term contrasts them with academic lessons.

examples.en: A tiny raindrop rested on her eyelash.
examples.zh: 一小滴雨水停在她的睫毛上。

examples.en: He brushed an eyelash off his cheek.
examples.zh: 他把一根睫毛從臉頰上拂掉。

examples.en: The doll has long painted eyelashes.
examples.zh: 這個娃娃有長長的彩繪睫毛。

explains: This noun names one of the short hairs along the edge of an eye. These hairs help keep dust away. They also make the eyes look distinct.
Makeup products may be applied to these hairs to make them more visible. A small brush can separate them. The noun refers to the hairs themselves.
Each eye has a row of these protective hairs. They can catch tiny particles before they reach the eye. Their position is right along the eyelid.

examples.en: A speck of dust landed on her eyelid.
examples.zh: 一粒灰塵落在她的眼皮上。

examples.en: He closed one eyelid to wink at his friend.
examples.zh: 他閉上一隻眼皮，向朋友眨眼示意。

examples.en: Her eyelid twitched after a long day.
examples.zh: 忙了一整天後，她的眼皮抽動了幾下。

explains: This noun names the thin fold of skin that covers and protects an eye. It moves when a person blinks. It can close during sleep.
The upper and lower folds meet when someone shuts an eye. A doctor may examine the area during a checkup. The skin helps shield a delicate organ.
A tiny muscle lifts the upper fold to open the eye. A blink spreads moisture across the surface. This body part supports protection and movement.

examples.en: His eyesight is sharp enough to read the small sign.
examples.zh: 他的視力很好，能看清楚那塊小標誌。

examples.en: The eye doctor checked her eyesight.
examples.zh: 眼科醫師檢查了她的視力。

examples.en: Poor eyesight made the distant numbers hard to see.
examples.zh: 視力不佳使遠處的數字難以辨認。

explains: This noun means the ability to see. Glasses can help someone see more clearly. A checkup can measure how well the eyes work.
People may notice that distant signs look blurry. That change concerns their ability to see. The word names this sense rather than the objects used to help it.
Good lighting can make reading easier for the eyes. Some people need lenses for near or far objects. The noun describes the power of sight.

examples.en: The fable teaches children not to boast.
examples.zh: 這則寓言教孩子不要自誇。

examples.en: We read a fable about a clever fox.
examples.zh: 我們讀了一則關於聰明狐狸的寓言。

examples.en: The old fable ends with a lesson about patience.
examples.zh: 這則古老寓言以耐心的重要性作結。

explains: This noun means a short traditional story that teaches a lesson. Animals may speak and act like people. The ending often shows why a choice was wise or foolish.
Parents can read such a tale to children at bedtime. A fox or tortoise may face a problem. The plot makes a moral idea easy to remember.
A made-up story can also be called this when it is not true. The word is often used for a simple, imaginative tale. It can entertain and teach.

examples.en: A faction within the club wanted a new leader.
examples.zh: 俱樂部內的一個派系想換新領導人。

examples.en: The party split into factions over the proposal.
examples.zh: 該政黨因這項提案分裂成不同派系。

examples.en: Each faction argued for a different plan.
examples.zh: 每個派別都主張不同的計畫。

explains: This noun means a smaller group within a larger organization, often with different beliefs. Members may support one plan while others prefer another. Disagreement can divide the whole group.
In politics, people with shared views may form such a group. They try to influence the larger party. Their goals may not match everyone's.
The word can also describe sides in a conflict. Each side may compete for power or resources. The term often suggests disagreement within a larger community.

examples.en: The forecast says it will reach 90 degrees Fahrenheit.
examples.zh: 天氣預報說氣溫將達到華氏九十度。

examples.en: Water freezes at 32 degrees Fahrenheit.
examples.zh: 水在華氏三十二度時結冰。

examples.en: She converted the Fahrenheit reading to Celsius.
examples.zh: 她把華氏溫度換算成攝氏溫度。

explains: This noun names a temperature scale used mainly in the United States. Water freezes at 32 degrees on it. Its numbers differ from those on the Celsius scale.
A weather report may show a reading using this scale. People can compare today's heat with yesterday's. The unit is named after a scientist.
The scale divides the interval between water's freezing and boiling points into 180 degrees. Other countries usually use Celsius instead. Both systems measure temperature.

examples.en: The singer began to falter during the final verse.
examples.zh: 歌手唱到最後一段時開始有些不穩。

examples.en: His voice faltered when he spoke about his friend.
examples.zh: 談到朋友時，他的聲音顫抖了。

examples.en: The tired runner faltered near the finish line.
examples.zh: 疲憊的跑者在終點線附近步伐不穩。

explains: This verb means to lose steadiness or confidence for a moment. A speaker may pause while searching for a word. The interruption can be brief.
A runner may stumble slightly on uneven ground but keep moving. The movement becomes less sure. This verb can describe that small loss of control.
Plans can also weaken when problems arise. A team may lose confidence after a setback. The verb suggests that progress or courage is wavering.

examples.en: Her familiarity with the town helped us find the station.
examples.zh: 她熟悉這座城鎮，因此幫我們找到了車站。

examples.en: He spoke with familiarity about the old theater.
examples.zh: 他談起那座老戲院時顯得十分熟悉。

examples.en: The children gained familiarity with the new classroom.
examples.zh: 孩子們逐漸熟悉了新教室。

explains: This noun means the state of knowing someone or something well. Years of reading give a person knowledge of a topic. Repeated contact builds recognition.
A new student may feel at ease in a building after several visits. The rooms and routines become known. This state can reduce uncertainty.
It can also mean a friendly connection between people. Neighbors who talk often may know each other well. The word can describe either knowledge or a relationship.

examples.en: Her fascination with birds began in childhood.
examples.zh: 她從小就對鳥類著迷。

examples.en: The magician's tricks held the children's fascination.
examples.zh: 魔術師的戲法吸引孩子們看得入迷。

examples.en: He has a fascination for maps and old roads.
examples.zh: 他對地圖和古道非常著迷。

explains: This noun means a strong feeling of interest or attraction toward something. A child may watch ants for hours. Curiosity keeps attention focused.
A person can have a deep interest in stars, puzzles, or old stories. They want to learn more. This feeling makes an activity especially engaging.
The word can also describe the power something has to hold attention. A mysterious painting may draw many viewers. Its appeal keeps them looking.

examples.en: The team found a feasible way to finish the project.
examples.zh: 團隊找到可行的方法完成這項專案。

examples.en: A direct train makes the trip feasible in one day.
examples.zh: 搭直達火車讓這趟旅行一天內完成成為可能。

examples.en: The budget made the small repair feasible.
examples.zh: 這筆預算讓小型修繕得以實行。

explains: This adjective describes a plan that can realistically be done. The available time and tools are enough. It is possible under the conditions.
A school project may seem difficult but still be manageable. Students can finish it with the materials they have. The idea is practical rather than impossible.
Before choosing a route, a group may consider distance and weather. If the trip can be completed safely, the plan is workable. This adjective expresses that judgment.

examples.en: The feeble candle barely lit the dark room.
examples.zh: 微弱的蠟燭幾乎照不亮黑暗的房間。

examples.en: After the long hike, he gave a feeble wave.
examples.zh: 長途健行後，他虛弱地揮了揮手。

examples.en: The story offered a feeble excuse for the mistake.
examples.zh: 這個故事對那個錯誤提出了薄弱的藉口。

explains: This adjective means weak in strength, force, or quality. A faint sound may be hard to hear. It has little power.
A tired person may give a weak push on a heavy door. The effort is not strong enough. The adjective describes limited physical force.
An argument can also be weak if it lacks good reasons. Readers may not be convinced. In that use, the idea has little strength.

examples.en: The costume had a feminine style with soft colors.
examples.zh: 這套服裝採用柔和色彩，風格較為女性化。

examples.en: The poet wrote about feminine beauty in the painting.
examples.zh: 詩人描寫了畫作中的女性之美。

examples.en: The adjective has a feminine form in that language.
examples.zh: 這個形容詞在該語言中有陰性形式。

explains: This adjective describes qualities or styles traditionally linked with women or girls. Clothing colors may receive this label in some cultures. Ideas about it can vary by place and time.
It can describe a gentle or graceful style, though people of any gender may have those qualities. The description concerns a social association, not a rule. Fashion changes over time.
As a noun, it can refer to the female side of a person or a language form associated with female gender. The context determines the specific sense. Grammar books explain such forms.

examples.en: The study examined fertility in several kinds of fish.
examples.zh: 這項研究檢視了幾種魚類的繁殖能力。

examples.en: Good soil fertility helps the garden produce healthy vegetables.
examples.zh: 土壤肥沃有助於菜園長出健康蔬菜。

examples.en: The farmer tested the field's fertility before planting.
examples.zh: 農夫在播種前檢測了田地的肥力。

explains: This noun means the ability to have young or produce fruit. In animals, it concerns having babies. In plants, it concerns making seeds or fruit.
A farm may look at how many healthy young animals are born. The number shows how well they can have babies. The same idea applies to crops that make seeds.
The word can also describe soil that helps plants grow well. Rich earth allows crops to thrive. In this sense, it concerns the land's ability to support growth.

examples.en: Farmers apply natural compost organic fertilizer to enrich soil nutrients.
examples.zh: 農民施用天然堆肥有機肥料來充實土壤中的各項養分。

examples.en: Overusing synthetic chemical fertilizer can cause groundwater pollution and algae blooms.
examples.zh: 過度濫用化學合成肥料容易造成地下水優養化污染與河道藻類過度暴長。

examples.en: Potassium and nitrogen are key chemical components found in agricultural fertilizer.
examples.zh: 鉀與氮元素是各類農業複合肥料中最核心關鍵的化學營養成分。

examples.en: Dilute balanced liquid fertilizer to half strength during peak spring growing season.
examples.zh: 在春夏植物生長旺季，將均衡觀葉液態肥料稀釋至半倍濃度，隨澆水時薄肥勤施。

examples.en: Applying too much concentrated chemical fertilizer will burn delicate root tips.
examples.zh: 一次施用過量或未稀釋完全的高濃度化學肥料，會直接灼傷植物脆弱細嫩的吸收根尖。

examples.en: Foliar fertilizer sprays deliver micronutrients directly through microscopic leaf stomata.
examples.zh: 葉面噴施專用微量元素營養液，能透過葉片上的微小氣孔直接迅速吸收所需微量元素。

entries.definition: 肥料；有機肥；植物肥料；營養液
explains: This noun means a substance added to soil to help plants grow. It may contain nutrients such as nitrogen. Gardeners use different kinds for different plants.
Compost is one natural type made from decayed plant material. It returns nutrients to the earth. Some products are made from minerals instead.
The word can describe a material in solid, liquid, or granular form. Its purpose is to support plant growth. Labels show which nutrients it contains.

examples.en: Her fiancé brought flowers to the family dinner.
examples.zh: 她的未婚夫帶了花來參加家庭晚餐。

examples.en: They introduced her fiancé to their friends.
examples.zh: 他們把她的未婚夫介紹給朋友。

examples.en: My sister and her fiancé chose a wedding date.
examples.zh: 我姊姊和她的未婚夫選定了婚期。

explains: This noun means a man who is engaged to be married. He has agreed to marry his partner. The wedding has not happened yet.
People often introduce this person as their future husband. The feminine counterpart names a woman engaged to marry. Both terms describe a relationship before marriage.
The borrowed French spelling may include an accent mark, but English writing often leaves it out. Pronunciation remains similar. The meaning depends on the engagement.

examples.en: Long carbon-fiber freediving fins deliver powerful thrust with minimal leg fatigue.
examples.zh: 換上一雙超長碳纖維自由潛水長蛙鞋，只需輕輕踢動雙腿即可在水下產生強勁的無聲推進力。

examples.en: Adjust the silicone heel straps of your open-heel fins snugly before stepping into the ocean surf.
examples.zh: 在邁步走進海浪碎浪區前，務必將套鞋式蛙鞋的矽膠後跟調整帶微調至服貼腳踝的緊度。

examples.en: The marine biologist identified the predatory shark species from the distinctive shape of its dorsal fin.
examples.zh: 海洋生物學家僅憑海面上露出的三角形背鰭輪廓與特殊弧度，便精準辨識出該鯊魚的具體品種。

explains: This noun names a flat body part that helps a fish swim and steer. A tail part pushes it forward. Other parts keep it balanced.
Swimmers wear flat blades on their feet to push water backward. The equipment helps them move forward. Long versions are used for diving.
Some machines have flat parts that guide air or release heat. An airplane tail may have one that helps control direction. These parts have a shape similar to the ones on a fish.

examples.en: The room has finite space for extra chairs.
examples.zh: 房間可容納額外椅子的空間有限。

examples.en: Our time for the game is finite.
examples.zh: 我們玩遊戲的時間有限。

examples.en: The list contains a finite number of names.
examples.zh: 清單上的名字數量有限。

explains: This adjective describes something that has an end or limit. A small cup holds only a set amount. It cannot continue forever.
A story with a final chapter has a limited length. The number of pages can be counted. This quality contrasts with something endless.
In mathematics, a set is limited when it contains a countable number of members. Each member can be listed. The adjective describes a bounded quantity.

examples.en: Setting off loud firecrackers is believed to scare off evil spirits.
examples.zh: 燃放震耳欲聾的爆竹被認為能驅逐邪煞年獸。

examples.en: Strings of red firecrackers popped and sparked brightly outside the temple gate.
examples.zh: 一串串紅豔的鞭炮在宮廟大門前劈啪作響、金星四射。

examples.en: Many cities encourage digital audio recordings instead of real gunpowder firecrackers.
examples.zh: 許多都會城市鼓勵以電子鞭炮音效代替傳統實體火藥爆竹以策安全。

explains: This noun means a small explosive that makes a loud pop and bright sparks. It is often used during celebrations. The sound can surprise people.
Families may light these noisy objects during a festival. They are associated with holiday customs in some places. Their popping sound is easy to recognize.
The object contains material that burns quickly and creates a bang. Because it can be dangerous, people should only observe it from a safe distance. The noun names that celebratory item.

examples.en: The laboratory uses fireproof cabinets for important records.
examples.zh: 實驗室使用防火櫃存放重要紀錄。

examples.en: His jacket is made from fireproof fabric.
examples.zh: 他的外套由防火布料製成。

examples.en: They installed a fireproof door between the rooms.
examples.zh: 他們在兩個房間之間裝了一扇防火門。

explains: This adjective describes material or clothing that resists catching fire. A special coating may slow flames. It does not necessarily make an object impossible to burn.
A protective curtain in a theater may use treated fabric. The material helps reduce the chance of a small flame spreading quickly. The adjective describes that property.
Some cabinets are built to protect papers during a fire. Their construction can resist heat for a limited time. The term means resistant to fire.

examples.en: The town's fishery employs many local families.
examples.zh: 這座城鎮的漁業僱用了許多當地家庭。

examples.en: The fishery raised young salmon in clean tanks.
examples.zh: 這座養魚場在乾淨的水槽裡養殖小鮭魚。

examples.en: Careful rules protect the coastal fishery.
examples.zh: 審慎的規範能保護沿海漁業。

explains: This noun means a place or business where fish and other water animals are raised or caught. Workers may sort the catch there. The site supports the fishing industry.
It can also refer to the activity or industry of catching fish. A coastal town may depend on this work. Rules can limit how many fish are taken.
A government may manage a protected area for fish production. The word can name either the location or the larger occupation. Context shows which sense is meant.

examples.en: A flake of snow landed on her mitten.
examples.zh: 一片雪花落在她的連指手套上。

examples.en: The old paint began to flake near the window.
examples.zh: 窗邊的舊油漆開始剝落。

examples.en: He brushed a pastry flake from his shirt.
examples.zh: 他把一片酥皮屑從襯衫上拂掉。

explains: As a noun, this means a small thin piece that has broken off something larger. Snow may fall in soft pieces. Pastry can also break into crumbs.
As a verb, it means to break or peel away in small pieces. Dry paint may come off a wall. The pieces are light and thin.
A small patch on skin can peel away after dryness. The same word describes the bit that comes off. It can name either the piece or the action.

examples.en: The vase has a small flaw near its base.
examples.zh: 花瓶底部附近有一個小瑕疵。

examples.en: A flaw in the plan delayed the trip.
examples.zh: 計畫中的一個缺失延誤了旅程。

examples.en: The cold weather may flaw the paint on the fence.
examples.zh: 寒冷天氣可能使圍欄上的油漆出現裂痕。

explains: This noun means a small weakness or mistake in something. A tiny crack may weaken a cup. A careful check can reveal the problem.
A plan may have a weakness that causes trouble later. People can discuss the problem and improve the plan. The noun identifies what is wrong.
As a verb, it means to crack or split slightly. A stone may break under pressure. The action creates a weak spot.

examples.en: The garden flourished after the spring rain.
examples.zh: 春雨過後，花園裡的植物長得繁茂。

examples.en: She flourishes in a classroom that encourages questions.
examples.zh: 她在鼓勵提問的教室裡如魚得水。

examples.en: The actor ended the scene with a flourish.
examples.zh: 演員以一個俐落的動作結束了那場戲。

explains: This verb means to grow or develop in a healthy, successful way. A plant may produce many flowers. A small business can also do very well.
Flowers can grow richly in warm soil and sunlight. The verb suggests strong, lively growth. It can describe people or ideas doing well too.
As a noun, it can mean a confident or stylish movement. A dancer may add a graceful turn. The movement brings extra energy to a performance.

examples.en: He feared he would flunk the history test.
examples.zh: 他擔心自己會不及格，沒通過歷史考試。

examples.en: The coach flunked the player for missing practice.
examples.zh: 球員因缺席練習而被教練淘汰。

examples.en: A flunk in math meant she had to take the course again.
examples.zh: 數學不及格讓她必須重修這門課。

explains: This informal verb means to fail a test or course. A student may receive very low marks. The student does not pass the required work.
A student may fail a course after earning very low marks. The student does not pass the required work. This informal verb describes failing a class or test.
The word can also name a failing grade. The student may need more practice. It is common in everyday speech.

examples.en: The knight faced his foe across the bridge.
examples.zh: 騎士隔著橋面對敵人。

examples.en: Our team respected its foe after the close match.
examples.zh: 激烈比賽後，我們隊尊重對手。

examples.en: The hero's oldest foe returned in the final chapter.
examples.zh: 主角最老的敵手在最後一章再度出現。

explains: This noun means an enemy or opponent. Two characters in a story may fight against each other. One person is the other person's adversary.
In a game, a player may face a strong rival. The contest is not always about hatred. The noun simply names someone on the opposing side.
A person may describe an obstacle as an enemy in a figurative way. Fear can feel like an opponent. The word can refer to a person or thing.

examples.en: The museum displayed costumes from local folklore.
examples.zh: 博物館展出了當地民間傳說中的服飾。

examples.en: Folklore says a blue bird brings good luck.
examples.zh: 民間傳說認為藍色的鳥會帶來好運。

examples.en: Her book collects folklore from mountain villages.
examples.zh: 她的書收集了山村的民間故事。

explains: This noun means traditional stories, beliefs, and customs shared by a community. The stories may pass from grandparents to children. They often explain local history or values.
Tales about spirits, heroes, or special places can be part of this tradition. Different regions keep different stories alive. They reflect a group's culture.
The term can also refer to common beliefs about a topic. People may repeat ideas without knowing where they began. These shared stories and beliefs form a body of tradition.

examples.en: The climbers faced a formidable peak.
examples.zh: 登山客面對一座難以攀登的高峰。

examples.en: She proved to be a formidable chess opponent.
examples.zh: 她證明自己是個實力強大的西洋棋對手。

examples.en: The castle's formidable walls protected the town.
examples.zh: 城堡堅固高聳的城牆保護了城鎮。

explains: This adjective describes something that inspires fear or great respect because it seems powerful. A huge mountain may look difficult to climb. Its size impresses viewers.
A rival team may have many skilled players. The opponent seems very strong before the game begins. The adjective captures that imposing challenge.
A large task can also feel overwhelming. A long list of work may seem hard to complete. This word describes something impressive and difficult.

examples.en: The class will formulate questions for the visitor.
examples.zh: 全班會為來訪者擬定問題。

examples.en: They formulated a plan to clean the beach.
examples.zh: 他們擬定了清理海灘的計畫。

examples.en: The scientist formulated a clear hypothesis.
examples.zh: 科學家提出了一個明確的假設。

explains: This verb means to create or express a plan, idea, or rule in a clear way. Scientists may write a question to test. The wording guides their work.
A group can develop a method for solving a problem. Members consider facts and arrange their ideas. The verb names the process of shaping a plan.
A speaker may put a thought into exact words. Clear language helps others understand the idea. This action is useful in writing and planning.

examples.en: The hero refused to forsake his friends.
examples.zh: 英雄不肯拋下朋友。

examples.en: She forsook the old path and chose a new one.
examples.zh: 她放棄舊路，選擇了一條新路。

examples.en: The dog was forsaken near the empty station.
examples.zh: 那隻狗被遺棄在空蕩蕩的車站附近。

explains: This verb means to abandon someone or something, especially in a difficult time. A friend may leave another person alone. The action can feel deeply hurtful.
It can also mean to give up a belief or habit. A character may reject an old promise. The verb often carries a serious emotional tone.
A person may leave a familiar place behind forever. The word suggests a strong break with the past. It is more dramatic than simply leaving for a short visit.

examples.en: The forthcoming concert will feature young musicians.
examples.zh: 即將舉行的音樂會將有年輕音樂家演出。

examples.en: Details of the forthcoming book appeared online.
examples.zh: 即將出版的書籍資訊已在網路上公布。

examples.en: She is the author of the forthcoming report.
examples.zh: 她是即將發表的報告作者。

explains: This adjective describes something that will happen soon or is about to arrive. A report may be released in a few days. People can expect it shortly.
A person can also be described this way when they are ready to appear or help. A guest may be prepared to speak. The word suggests something near in time.
In a book, a notice may discuss a new event coming soon. The adjective helps readers know it has not happened yet. It is expected in the near future.

examples.en: Stone walls fortify the old harbor.
examples.zh: 石牆加固了舊港口。

examples.en: The teacher used examples to fortify her explanation.
examples.zh: 老師用例子來強化她的說明。

examples.en: The castle was fortified against attack.
examples.zh: 城堡經過加固以抵禦攻擊。

explains: This verb means to make something stronger or more secure. Builders may add walls or supports to a structure. The added parts help it resist pressure.
A person can strengthen an idea with clear evidence. More facts make the argument harder to challenge. The verb applies to both physical and abstract things.
Food can be enriched with extra nutrients. The added elements increase its value. This use also conveys strengthening or support.

examples.en: The farmer raised fowl beside the barn.
examples.zh: 農夫在穀倉旁飼養家禽。

examples.en: The restaurant serves roasted fowl with vegetables.
examples.zh: 這家餐廳供應搭配蔬菜的烤禽肉。

examples.en: Wild fowl gathered near the marsh.
examples.zh: 野生水鳥聚集在沼澤附近。

explains: This noun names domestic birds raised for eggs or meat, such as chickens and turkeys. Farmers keep them in coops or fields. The term is often used in cooking.
A recipe may ask for a whole bird rather than beef or fish. The meat can come from several farm species. The word refers to those birds as a group.
In older writing, it can mean a bird of any kind. Modern use often points to farm birds used as food. Context helps identify the intended group.

examples.en: The skier suffered a minor leg bone fracture after slipping on ice.
examples.zh: 滑雪選手在冰面上滑倒後導致腿部輕微骨折。

examples.en: A protective fiberglass cast was applied to immobilize the arm fracture.
examples.zh: 醫師為他打上了堅固輕盈的玻璃纖維石膏夾板，以固定手部骨折患處。

examples.en: Disagreements over zoning laws caused an internal fracture within the municipal committee.
examples.zh: 土地分區管制法規上的重大分歧導致該市政審議委員會內部出現了深層分裂裂痕。

examples.en: X-rays revealed a hairline fracture in his left wrist from the scooter slip.
examples.zh: X 光片檢查清晰顯示出他在雨天騎機車打滑摔倒時造成左手腕處有細微骨裂骨折。

examples.en: A compound bone fracture requires emergency surgical intervention to realign bone fragments.
examples.zh: 開放性複雜骨折伴隨骨頭刺破皮膚軟組織，必須第一時間送進開刀房進行骨折復位與內固定。

examples.en: Older adults with advanced osteoporosis face higher risks of debilitating hip fractures.
examples.zh: 患有嚴重骨質疏鬆症的高齡銀髮長輩在日常生活中若不慎跌倒，極易引發致命的髖關節骨折。

entries.definition: 骨折；破裂；折斷；骨裂；使斷裂
explains: This noun means a break or crack in a bone, object, or relationship. A fall may damage a bone. A disagreement can split a group.
As a verb, it means to break or crack something. Cold weather may split a rock. A serious disagreement can also divide people.
The word often appears in medical or technical settings. A small crack in a material can still affect its strength. It can name the break or the act of breaking.

examples.en: The fragrance of jasmine filled the garden.
examples.zh: 茉莉花的香氣瀰漫整座花園。

examples.en: She chose a light fragrance for the evening.
examples.zh: 她為晚上挑選了一款淡雅香水。

examples.en: The soap has a fresh citrus fragrance.
examples.zh: 這款肥皂帶有清新的柑橘香氣。

explains: This noun means a pleasant or noticeable smell. A flower may give off a sweet scent. Perfume is another source of smell.
People may notice a familiar smell when they enter a kitchen. Fresh bread can fill a room with a warm scent. The noun describes what the nose detects.
The term often suggests a pleasant smell, though context matters. A scented candle can make a room feel inviting. It names the smell itself.

examples.en: Fragrant roses grew beside the fence.
examples.zh: 圍欄旁種著芳香的玫瑰。

examples.en: The fragrant bread came out of the oven.
examples.zh: 香氣四溢的麵包剛出爐。

examples.en: We walked through a fragrant herb garden.
examples.zh: 我們走過一座飄著香氣的香草園。

explains: This adjective describes something that has a pleasant smell. A flower may perfume the air around it. The scent can be sweet or fresh.
A soap or candle can have a noticeable smell. People may describe it as pleasant when the scent is enjoyable. The adjective describes that quality.
The word often appears in descriptions of gardens and food. Herbs can give off a fresh smell. It tells the reader how something smells.

examples.en: She made a frantic search for her missing phone.
examples.zh: 她焦急地四處尋找不見的手機。

examples.en: The frantic crowd rushed toward the exits.
examples.zh: 慌亂的人群衝向出口。

examples.en: He sent a frantic message before the train left.
examples.zh: 火車離站前，他焦急地傳了一則訊息。

explains: This adjective describes a person who is extremely worried or rushed. Someone may search wildly for a lost key. Their movements show panic.
A crowd can become noisy and confused during an emergency. People move quickly without a clear plan. The word captures intense anxiety and disorder.
A busy person may make a hurried effort to finish before a deadline. The action seems hurried and almost desperate. The adjective shows urgency.

examples.en: A freak storm flooded the quiet street.
examples.zh: 一場罕見的暴風雨淹沒了安靜的街道。

examples.en: The sudden crash freaked the baby out.
examples.zh: 突然的撞擊聲把寶寶嚇壞了。

examples.en: He called the giant pumpkin a freak of nature.
examples.zh: 他稱那顆巨型南瓜是自然界的奇觀。

explains: As a noun, this informal word can mean an unusual or surprising person or thing. A sudden event may seem very strange. The word can also describe a sudden whim.
As a verb, it means to frighten or upset someone greatly. A loud noise may startle a child. The reaction can be strong.
People sometimes use it for something unexpected, such as a rare storm or an unusual animal. It can be playful or critical depending on context. Context makes the intended sense clear.

examples.en: We took the freeway to reach the airport.
examples.zh: 我們走高速公路前往機場。

examples.en: Traffic moved slowly on the freeway after the rain.
examples.zh: 下雨後，高速公路上的車流緩慢。

examples.en: The hotel is just off the freeway.
examples.zh: 飯店就在高速公路旁邊。

explains: This noun means a major road designed for fast traffic. It usually has several lanes. Cars enter and leave at special ramps.
Drivers enter and leave by ramps instead of crossing streets at level intersections. Long-distance routes can connect towns and cities. Signs show the way to each exit.
In some countries, the name refers to a public road with controlled access. Signs show exits and directions. The term is common in North America.

examples.en: Friction between the two pieces of wood made a squeak.
examples.zh: 兩塊木頭之間的摩擦發出吱吱聲。

examples.en: There was friction between the neighbors over the fence.
examples.zh: 鄰居之間因圍籬問題產生摩擦。

examples.en: Oil reduces friction inside the machine.
examples.zh: 油能減少機器內部的摩擦。

explains: This noun means resistance that happens when two surfaces rub together. Rubbing hands creates warmth. The contact slows movement.
People may also use it for tension between people or groups. A small disagreement can create conflict. The social sense describes difficulty in getting along.
Machines need parts that move smoothly. Too much rubbing can create heat and wear. The word names both physical resistance and social tension.

examples.en: Fumes rose from the hot pavement.
examples.zh: 熱氣從滾燙的路面升起。

examples.en: He fumed when the bus left without him.
examples.zh: 公車沒等他就開走時，他氣得直冒火。

examples.en: The workers left the room when chemical fumes appeared.
examples.zh: 化學氣體出現時，工人們離開了房間。

explains: As a noun, this means thick smoke or vapor, often with a strong smell. A car may release clouds from its exhaust. The air can become unpleasant.
As a verb, it means to show anger or irritation. A person may complain after waiting too long. Their mood is plainly upset.
The noun can also refer to gas from chemicals. A strong vapor may irritate the nose. Context tells whether the word describes smoke or anger.

examples.en: The broken promise filled her with fury.
examples.zh: 失信的承諾讓她怒火中燒。

examples.en: He shouted in fury after losing the match.
examples.zh: 輸掉比賽後，他氣得大喊。

examples.en: The storm's fury shook the windows.
examples.zh: 暴風雨的猛烈威力震動了窗戶。

explains: This noun means very strong anger. A person may feel it after being treated unfairly. The emotion can be difficult to control.
A story may describe a ruler's intense anger after a betrayal. The feeling is stronger than ordinary annoyance. The word signals powerful emotion.
The term can also mean a violent storm or force in older writing. The context makes clear whether it refers to anger or nature. It suggests great intensity.

examples.en: A blown fuse left the kitchen without power.
examples.zh: 保險絲燒斷後，廚房停電了。

examples.en: The glass artist used heat to fuse the pieces.
examples.zh: 玻璃藝術家用熱力將碎片熔接起來。

examples.en: The electrician replaced the fuse in the panel.
examples.zh: 電工更換了配電盤裡的保險絲。

explains: As a noun, this is a small device that breaks an electric circuit when too much current flows. The part helps protect wires. It may need replacement after it works.
As a verb, it means to join separate things together. A craft worker may connect two pieces of glass. Heat can help them become one piece.
A short string can light an explosive in a story. This is another noun sense. The common meanings depend on whether the topic is electricity, joining, or fireworks.

examples.en: There was a fuss about the missing cake.
examples.zh: 大家為不見的蛋糕吵成一團。

examples.en: Please do not fuss over the small scratch.
examples.zh: 請不要為那道小刮痕大驚小怪。

examples.en: Grandma fussed over the baby all afternoon.
examples.zh: 奶奶整個下午都細心照料著寶寶。

explains: As a noun, this means unnecessary worry or excitement about a small matter. A guest may complain about a tiny delay. The reaction seems bigger than the problem.
As a verb, it means to make a lot of noise or worry over something. People may argue about a small change. The action draws extra attention.
A person can also give a child lots of extra care. This sense is affectionate. The word often describes busy concern or unnecessary trouble.

examples.en: The horse began to gallop across the meadow.
examples.zh: 馬開始在草地上奔馳。

examples.en: We heard the gallop of hooves on the road.
examples.zh: 我們聽見馬蹄在路上奔馳的聲音。

examples.en: The pony galloped toward the open gate.
examples.zh: 小馬朝著敞開的大門奔去。

explains: As a verb, this means to run quickly with long, springing steps. A horse may move this way across a field. The motion is smooth and energetic.
The noun names this fast, bouncing way of moving. A rider can hear the animal's feet strike the ground. The pace is faster than a walk.
A story may use the word for a lively horse race. The animals cover ground quickly. It describes a recognizable movement and pace.

examples.en: The detective questioned the gangster in the film.
examples.zh: 電影中的偵探盤問了那名黑幫分子。

examples.en: A gangster appeared as the villain in the old movie.
examples.zh: 一名黑幫分子在老電影中扮演反派。

examples.en: The story follows a young gangster who wants to leave crime.
examples.zh: 這個故事描寫一名想脫離犯罪生活的年輕幫派分子。

explains: This noun describes a member of a criminal group that uses violence or threats. Such groups may control illegal activities. The term is common in crime stories.
A movie may show a person working for an organized gang. The character might collect money or intimidate rivals. The word names that kind of criminal.
The term became well known through stories about city crime groups. It refers to a person involved, not the group itself. The setting may be historical or fictional.

examples.en: High-quality tailored garments last for decades when cared for properly.
examples.zh: 剪裁作工精良的高品質成衣服裝只要平日悉心保養洗滌，穿上數十年依然挺括如新。

examples.en: Each garment undergoes strict quality inspection to check for loose seams and misaligned buttons.
examples.zh: 每一件出廠的成衣服飾都要經過嚴格品檢，仔細檢查是否有脫線或鈕扣縫偏的瑕疵。

examples.en: Read the care label inside the garment carefully before using hot water or bleach.
examples.zh: 在使用熱水清洗或漂白水之前，請務必先仔細閱讀服裝內側的水洗標籤說明。

explains: This noun means one item of clothing, such as a shirt or coat. It is a formal word often used in stores or reports. Each item is counted separately.
A warm item can protect someone from cold weather. People choose clothing for comfort, work, or style. This noun refers to the article itself.
The word can describe clothing made for a particular purpose. A uniform is one example. It is a general term for a piece of clothing.

examples.en: High-speed tracks adhere strictly to the 1,435-millimeter international standard gauge across the whole line.
examples.zh: 全線軌道百分之百嚴格遵循「一千四百三十五公釐國際標準軌距」（Standard Gauge），誤差僅容許一公釐。

examples.en: Check the digital tire pressure gauge before setting out on an extended family highway road trip.
examples.zh: 在開車載全家人展開長途自駕旅行出發前，請務必使用數位胎壓計仔細量測四輪胎壓是否充足。

examples.en: It is challenging to gauge public sentiment accurately based solely on noisy social media discussions.
examples.zh: 若單純僅僅依據社群媒體上的零星喧囂言論，往往很難全面客觀且精準地衡量出真實社會民意。

entries.definition: 1,435 公釐國際標準鐵道軌距；測量
explains: As a noun, this is an instrument that measures an amount or level. A fuel dial shows how much remains. A simple tool can measure width too.
As a verb, it means to judge or estimate something. A teacher may try to understand how well students grasp a lesson. The judgment uses available signs.
The word can also refer to the width between rails or the thickness of material. Context tells which measurement is meant. It concerns size or evaluation.

examples.en: My gay uncle came to dinner with his partner.
examples.zh: 我那位男同志叔叔和伴侶一起來吃晚餐。

examples.en: The film tells the story of a gay teenager.
examples.zh: 這部電影描述一名男同志青少年的故事。

examples.en: She joined a local group that supports gay rights.
examples.zh: 她加入了支持同志權益的在地團體。

explains: This adjective describes attraction to people of the same gender. People may use it for themselves or a community. It is a common identity term.
In older writing, the adjective could mean happy or bright. A story may describe a cheerful mood this way. This use is now uncommon.
As a noun, it can refer to a man attracted to men. Some people prefer identity labels that feel right to them. Respectful usage follows a person’s choice.

examples.en: The report includes a geographical map of the islands.
examples.zh: 報告附有一張這些島嶼的地理地圖。

examples.en: Mountain ranges create geographical barriers between towns.
examples.zh: 山脈在城鎮之間形成地理屏障。

examples.en: The book compares geographical features of two regions.
examples.zh: 這本書比較兩個地區的地理特徵。

explains: This adjective relates to the physical features of a place on Earth. Maps may show rivers, hills, and borders. The term connects information to location.
A report may compare areas by their position or landscape. Mountains can shape how people travel. The adjective describes matters connected with places.
The word is used in science, travel, and history. A description of a region's location is about its place on a map. It focuses on where things are.

examples.en: We used geometry to find the triangle's missing angle.
examples.zh: 我們用幾何學找出三角形缺少的角度。

examples.en: The tiles form a simple geometry on the floor.
examples.zh: 地磚在地面上形成簡單的幾何圖案。

examples.en: Her geometry homework included circles and squares.
examples.zh: 她的幾何作業包括圓形和正方形。

explains: This noun is the study of shapes, lines, angles, and space. Students may measure triangles in class. The subject uses diagrams and logical rules.
A designer may use ideas from this field to plan a room. Measurements and shapes help objects fit together. The subject appears in practical work too.
The word also names the arrangement or shape of something. A pattern on a floor may have repeating forms. Context shows whether it means the subject or a shape system.

examples.en: The glacier carved a deep valley in the mountain.
examples.zh: 冰河在山中刻出一條深谷。

examples.en: They watched blue ice break from the glacier.
examples.zh: 他們看著藍色冰塊從冰河崩落。

examples.en: A glacier moves slowly across the land.
examples.zh: 冰河緩慢地移過陸地。

explains: This noun names a huge mass of ice that moves slowly over land. It forms where snow builds up over many years. The ice can shape valleys.
The ice may look still, but it moves gradually downhill. Cracks can appear on its surface. Cold regions and high mountains contain these formations.
When the ice melts, it can add water to rivers and seas. Scientists study its movement and age. The noun refers to this large moving body of ice.

examples.en: She wore a glamorous gown to the award show.
examples.zh: 她穿著華麗的禮服出席頒獎典禮。

examples.en: The glamorous hotel stood beside the beach.
examples.zh: 那間時尚豪華的飯店矗立在海邊。

examples.en: The magazine showed a glamorous view of city life.
examples.zh: 雜誌呈現了光鮮迷人的城市生活景象。

explains: This adjective describes a person or thing that seems exciting, stylish, and attractive. A sparkling dress may look impressive at a party. The appearance catches attention.
Old movie stars were often shown in elegant clothes and bright settings. The adjective suggests beauty and charm. It can describe a place or event too.
The word can also mean exciting in a polished, fashionable way. A hotel lobby with shining lights may seem impressive. It focuses on attractive style.

examples.en: The old theater still has glamour and charm.
examples.zh: 這座老戲院依然散發魅力與風采。

examples.en: The magazine added glamour to the simple room.
examples.zh: 雜誌讓這間簡樸的房間更顯華麗。

examples.en: She admired the glamour of classic films.
examples.zh: 她欣賞經典電影的迷人風采。

explains: This noun means the attractive quality of beauty, style, or charm. Shiny clothes and elegant settings can create it. People may find a place exciting.
It can also refer to an appealing image created by fashion or publicity. A magazine may present a star's life as dazzling. The image can differ from daily reality.
A person may have a special charm that draws attention. The noun names that appealing quality. It often relates to style and attractiveness.

examples.en: A gleam of sunlight crossed the desk.
examples.zh: 一道陽光掠過書桌。

examples.en: Her eyes gleamed with excitement.
examples.zh: 她的眼中閃爍著興奮的光芒。

examples.en: The polished spoon gleamed under the lamp.
examples.zh: 擦亮的湯匙在燈下閃閃發亮。

explains: As a noun, this means a small, bright flash or shine. Sunlight may reflect from a glass window. The brief shine catches the eye.
As a verb, it means to shine softly or briefly. A metal button may reflect light. The brightness is often gentle rather than strong.
A person's eyes can show a spark of happiness. The word can describe that lively brightness. It can refer to light or an expression.

examples.en: The skater glided across the ice.
examples.zh: 溜冰者滑過冰面。

examples.en: A small boat glided across the quiet lake.
examples.zh: 一艘小船平穩地滑過寧靜的湖面。

examples.en: She watched the dancer glide across the stage.
examples.zh: 她看著舞者優雅地滑過舞台。

explains: This verb means to move smoothly and quietly over a surface or through the air. A swan travels across a lake with little effort. The motion looks graceful.
A skater can move across ice without many visible steps. The body stays balanced and the motion is fluid. The word also names such a smooth movement.
An object can move gently along a track. A drawer may open without sticking. The term suggests easy, steady motion.

examples.en: The glitter on the card caught the light.
examples.zh: 卡片上的亮粉反射出光芒。

examples.en: Her shoes glittered under the stage lights.
examples.zh: 她的鞋子在舞台燈光下閃閃發亮。

examples.en: The decorations were covered with silver glitter.
examples.zh: 裝飾品上佈滿了銀色亮粉。

explains: As a noun, this means many small points of bright light. Stars may shine this way in a clear sky. The effect is noticeable and lively.
As a verb, it means to shine with small flashes of light. Sequins may reflect a lamp. The surface appears bright from many points.
The word can also describe lively excitement. A child's eyes may show energy. It names either sparkling light or an animated quality.

examples.en: The gloom lifted when the sun came out.
examples.zh: 太陽出來後，陰鬱的氣氛消散了。

examples.en: Rain gloomed the sky before the picnic.
examples.zh: 野餐前，雨水讓天空變得陰暗。

examples.en: The room was filled with gloom after the bad news.
examples.zh: 壞消息傳來後，房間裡充滿了憂鬱氣氛。

explains: This noun means darkness or a feeling of sadness and hopelessness. A room without lights may look dim. A person can also feel low in spirit.
As a verb, it means to become dark or gloomy. Clouds may cover the sky. The change can affect a person's mood.
A story may use this word to create a serious mood. A gray day can seem quiet and heavy. It describes darkness in a place or in feelings.

examples.en: The goalkeeper caught the ball near the post.
examples.zh: 守門員在門柱附近接住了球。

examples.en: Their goalkeeper blocked the final penalty kick.
examples.zh: 他們的守門員擋下了最後一記罰球。

examples.en: The young goalkeeper practiced diving to both sides.
examples.zh: 年輕的守門員練習向左右兩側撲球。

explains: This noun names the player who guards a goal in a team sport. The person tries to stop the other side from scoring. Special rules may apply to this position.
In soccer, this player can use hands inside a marked area. Teammates defend other parts of the field. Quick reactions are important.
A team may choose a backup for this position. The main player can rest or be replaced. The noun describes a defensive role.

examples.en: The cultural exchange festival fostered immense international goodwill and friendship.
examples.zh: 這場多元文化藝術交流嘉年華在各國青年之間搭起了滿滿的跨國善意與真摯友誼。

examples.en: The diplomat presented traditional Taiwanese tea as a sincere gesture of international goodwill.
examples.zh: 外交官特地致贈頂級台灣高山烏龍茶禮盒，作為展現兩國深厚邦誼的誠摯善意姿態。

examples.en: Decades of outstanding honest service generated enormous commercial goodwill for the bakery.
examples.zh: 數十年來如一日童叟無欺的誠信經營，為這家百年老烘焙坊累積了無比珍貴的商譽資產。

entries.definition: 善意；親善友好；企業商譽
explains: This noun means friendly feelings and helpful intentions toward others. A neighbor may offer to lend a tool. The gesture shows kindness.
In business, it can mean the value of a good reputation and customer trust. A familiar shop may attract loyal buyers. That reputation has worth.
The term can also describe a positive relationship between groups or countries. Respect and cooperation create trust. This friendly attitude is not a physical object.

examples.en: A gorilla rested beneath a tree at the zoo.
examples.zh: 一隻大猩猩在動物園的樹下休息。

examples.en: The young gorilla held tightly to its mother.
examples.zh: 小大猩猩緊緊抱著母親。

examples.en: Researchers observed a gorilla family in the forest.
examples.zh: 研究人員在森林裡觀察一個大猩猩家庭。

explains: This noun names a very large ape that lives in forests in central Africa. It has dark fur and strong arms. It usually eats plants and fruit.
The animal lives in family groups led by an adult male. It communicates with sounds and gestures. Wild populations need protected habitats.
A character may be compared to this ape because of great strength. The actual animal is generally calm when undisturbed. The noun names the species.

examples.en: The choir sang a gospel song at church.
examples.zh: 合唱團在教堂唱了一首福音歌曲。

examples.en: She read a passage from the Gospel of Mark.
examples.zh: 她讀了《馬可福音》中的一段經文。

examples.en: The book presents a gospel of kindness and hope.
examples.zh: 這本書宣揚善良與希望的信念。

explains: This noun can mean the teachings or message of the Christian faith. It is also the name of the first four books of the New Testament. Churches read these texts.
A singer may perform religious music that shares a message of hope. This style developed in African American church traditions. It often features strong voices and rhythm.
The word can also mean a set of central beliefs about an idea. A group may promote a guiding message. Context indicates whether the sense is religious or general.

examples.en: She ate half a grapefruit for breakfast.
examples.zh: 她早餐吃了半顆葡萄柚。

examples.en: Pink grapefruit tastes sweet and slightly tart.
examples.zh: 粉紅葡萄柚吃起來香甜又帶點酸味。

examples.en: He squeezed fresh grapefruit juice.
examples.zh: 他榨了新鮮的葡萄柚汁。

explains: This noun names a large citrus fruit with a thick yellow or pink skin. Its flavor can be sweet and slightly bitter. People often eat it at breakfast.
The fruit grows on a tree and separates into juicy sections. Some kinds have pink flesh. It can also be squeezed for juice.
The word is a compound name for a fruit. Its peel is thicker than that of an orange. A sharp knife may help cut it open.

examples.en: The sheep grazed on the hillside.
examples.zh: 羊群在山坡上吃草。

examples.en: The horse grazed near the fence all morning.
examples.zh: 那匹馬整個早上都在柵欄附近吃草。

examples.en: Her knee grazed the pavement when she fell.
examples.zh: 她跌倒時膝蓋擦到了路面。

explains: This verb means to eat small amounts of grass while animals move around. Cows may feed in a field. They take bites slowly over time.
A goat can eat leaves from low bushes. It moves from plant to plant. The verb describes this relaxed way of feeding.
Animals may also lightly scrape a surface while moving past it. A knee can brush against a rough path. This is another sense, usually involving a light touch.

examples.en: Grease covered the mechanic's hands.
examples.zh: 機械技師的雙手沾滿了油脂。

examples.en: She greased the pan before baking the bread.
examples.zh: 她在烤麵包前先在烤盤上抹油。

examples.en: The old gear needed grease to move smoothly.
examples.zh: 舊齒輪需要潤滑脂才能順暢轉動。

explains: As a noun, this is a thick, slippery substance used to make parts move smoothly or food taste rich. A mechanic may apply it to a wheel. Cooking can also use it.
As a verb, it means to cover something with this substance. A pan may need a thin layer before cooking. The coating reduces sticking.
