examples.en: The new captain thanked her predecessor.
examples.zh: 新隊長向前任隊長道謝。

examples.en: This model is faster than its predecessor.
examples.zh: 這個型號比前一代更快。

examples.en: His predecessor had led the club for ten years.
examples.zh: 他的前任曾帶領俱樂部十年。

explains: This noun means a person or thing that came before another in the same role. A new principal may learn from the former one. The earlier person held the position first.
A machine may replace an older model. The old version was used before the new one. The word describes the earlier item.
A person taking over a job may respect the work already done. The term can refer to someone or something that came first in a sequence. The sequence may be a list or a line of leaders.

examples.en: The museum displayed prehistoric tools.
examples.zh: 博物館展示了史前工具。

examples.en: Prehistoric animals once lived in this region.
examples.zh: 史前動物曾經生活在這個地區。

examples.en: They found prehistoric footprints in the rock.
examples.zh: 他們在岩石中發現了史前腳印。

explains: This adjective describes a time before recorded human history. Dinosaurs lived during a very distant age. No written records from that time remain.
A fossil or stone tool may come from an age before people kept written records. Scientists study physical evidence to learn about it. Such objects provide clues about the past.
The term can describe animals, plants, or events from that ancient period. The word means earlier than recorded history. Fossils are one source of evidence.

examples.en: Stars walked the red carpet at the grand international movie premiere.
examples.zh: 眾多明星走上紅毯盛大出席國際電影首映典禮。

examples.en: The new fantasy drama will premiere on Friday night at eight o'clock.
examples.zh: 這部全新奇幻影集將於週五晚間八點準時進行全球首播。

examples.en: Critics praised the director's bold narrative choices during the film premiere.
examples.zh: 影評人在電影首映會上對導演大膽前衛的敘事手法讚譽有加。

examples.en: Stars walked the glamorous red carpet at the Taipei world film premiere.
examples.zh: 眾多影視巨星盛裝出席踏上台北全球首映典禮的星光紅毯。

examples.en: The prestigious opera house hosted the global premiere of the composer's latest symphony.
examples.zh: 這座享譽國際的百年歌劇院隆重主辦了這位當代傳奇作曲大師最新交響樂力作的全球首演盛典。

examples.en: Fans waited outside in the freezing rain for hours just to catch a glimpse of their idols at the movie premiere.
examples.zh: 無數狂熱影迷頂著刺骨寒雨在會場外引頸期盼苦守數小時，只為在電影全球首映會紅毯旁一睹心愛偶像的巨星風采。

examples.en: The film made its world premiere at the prestigious Venice International Film Festival.
examples.zh: 這部震撼人心的歷史史詩巨作於享負盛名的義大利威尼斯國際影展進行了隆重的全球首映。

examples.en: Tickets for the midnight premiere screening sold out completely within forty seconds of opening.
examples.zh: 這部超級大片的午夜首映場電影票在開賣系統剛上線四十秒內，便全數被瘋搶一空。

examples.en: The highly anticipated sci-fi sequel is scheduled to premiere in theaters worldwide next December.
examples.zh: 這部備受全球影迷引頸期盼的科幻史詩續集電影，已正式定檔於明年十二月全球院線盛大首映。

examples.en: The world premiere was attended by international critics, dignitaries, and celebrated playwrights.
examples.zh: 這部年度旗艦大戲的全球首演之夜（World Premiere），吸引了無數國際劇評家與文化名流盛裝出席。

examples.en: The indie film premiered at the Golden Horse Film Festival to glowing praise from cinephiles.
examples.zh: 這部由台灣年輕導演執導的獨立長片，在台北金馬影展舉行世界首映，獲得在場資深影迷一致起立盛讚。

examples.en: Cast members walked the glamorous red carpet before the glitzy Asian premiere in downtown Taipei.
examples.zh: 全體主要演員在台北信義商圈繁華影城舉行的亞洲首映會前，盛裝步上星光熠熠的星光紅毯接受媒體拍照。

entries.definition: 首映；首播；初次登場；首映典禮；首演；電影全球首映會；初次上映；旗艦大戲世界首演首映
explains: This noun means the first public showing of a play, film, or performance. The audience may see it before the general release. People often attend a special event.
The word can also mean the first time a performer appears in an important role. The event marks a beginning. It may receive attention from the public.
As an adjective or verb, it can describe a first appearance or showing. The context may be a film, play, or person. It marks something new.

examples.en: The mayor presided over the town meeting.
examples.zh: 市長主持了鎮民大會。

examples.en: A judge presided at the hearing.
examples.zh: 法官主持了聽證會。

examples.en: She presided over the awards ceremony.
examples.zh: 她主持了頒獎典禮。

explains: This verb means to lead a meeting or ceremony. A chairperson may guide discussion and keep to the schedule. The person manages the gathering.
A judge may guide a hearing and make sure each side gets a chance to speak. The role includes keeping order. The verb describes leading the event.
A person in charge may sit at the front of a group. They make sure the activity follows its rules. The word often appears in formal settings.

examples.en: The award added prestige to the small theater.
examples.zh: 這座獎項提升了小劇院的聲望。

examples.en: The school is known for its academic prestige.
examples.zh: 這所學校以學術聲望聞名。

examples.en: She earned prestige through years of careful research.
examples.zh: 多年認真的研究為她贏得了聲譽。

explains: This noun means respect and admiration that a person or organization has earned. A famous university may be highly regarded. Its name carries weight.
A person can gain respect through skill and fair behavior. Others may value their opinion. The word describes a good public standing.
The term can also mean high status or honor. An award may add to a school's standing. It refers to respect from others.

examples.en: Preventive medicine emphasizes annual health screenings, balanced nutrition, and regular aerobic exercise.
examples.zh: 現代「預防醫學」（Preventive Medicine）強調定期成人健檢、均衡原型飲食與規律運動，防患於未然。

examples.en: Regular vehicle maintenance, such as oil changes and tire rotations, serves as effective preventive care.
examples.zh: 養成每半年定期進廠更換機油、檢查煞車皮與輪胎對調的愛車保養習慣，是最行之有效的預防性防範保養作為。

examples.en: The police took preventive security measures, setting up checkpoints around the international summit venue.
examples.zh: 國安特勤單位在國際高峰會會場周邊數公里提前採取嚴密的預防性維安措施，層層設立防暴路障與臨檢崗哨。

entries.definition: 預防醫學早篩早治的；預防性的
explains: This adjective describes something done to stop a problem before it happens. A fence may keep animals away from a garden. The measure keeps damage from happening.
A checkup can find small issues early. Taking action before trouble grows can stop it. The word describes steps taken ahead of time.
A rule may reduce the chance of accidents. People follow it before danger occurs. The adjective emphasizes stopping trouble before it starts rather than repairing damage.

examples.en: We watched a preview of the new film.
examples.zh: 我們看了新電影的預告片。

examples.en: The website offers a preview of the next issue.
examples.zh: 網站提供下一期內容的預覽。

examples.en: She previewed the slides before the meeting.
examples.zh: 她在會議前先預覽了投影片。

explains: This noun means a short look at something before it is fully available. A movie may show a few scenes before release. The sample gives viewers an idea.
As a verb, it means to view something in advance. A student may read chapter titles before a lesson. This early look prepares the person.
A software update may be shown before its final launch. Users can see what is coming. The word describes either the early look or the act of showing it.

examples.en: Her grandmother's letters were priceless to her.
examples.zh: 祖母的信對她來說無價。

examples.en: The old map was a priceless family treasure.
examples.zh: 這張古老地圖是無價的家族珍寶。

examples.en: His advice proved priceless during the trip.
examples.zh: 他的建議在旅途中非常寶貴。

explains: This adjective means so valuable or special that no price can truly measure it. A family photo may hold deep meaning. Its worth is personal.
A helpful friend's support can feel beyond money's value. The word expresses how much something matters. It does not mean that the item is literally free.
A discovery may be extremely useful to science. People may call it beyond price because of its importance. The adjective describes great value.

examples.en: The government voted to privatize the rail service.
examples.zh: 政府表決將鐵路服務民營化。

examples.en: They plan to privatize the water company.
examples.zh: 他們計畫將自來水公司民營化。

examples.en: The proposal would privatize several public services.
examples.zh: 這項提案將把幾項公共服務民營化。

explains: This verb means to transfer a business or service from government control to private ownership. A public company may be sold. The new owner makes decisions.
A city may change who runs a service. The service becomes privately managed instead of publicly owned. The word describes that change.
The process can affect jobs, prices, and public access. People may disagree about its results. The verb names the move to private ownership.

examples.en: The robot probe explored the ocean floor.
examples.zh: 機器探測器探索了海床。

examples.en: Police probed the cause of the fire.
examples.zh: 警方調查火災原因。

examples.en: The reporter probed the mayor about the delay.
examples.zh: 記者追問市長延誤的原因。

explains: As a noun, this is a close examination or search for information. Scientists may explore the ocean floor with a device. They look for details.
As a verb, it means to examine or investigate carefully. A doctor may use a small tool to look inside a space. The action seeks information.
The word can also mean to ask questions to learn more. A reporter may investigate a claim. It suggests a careful search rather than a quick glance.

examples.en: A procession moved slowly through the town square.
examples.zh: 一列隊伍緩緩穿過鎮上的廣場。

examples.en: The wedding procession entered the hall.
examples.zh: 婚禮隊伍進入大廳。

examples.en: A procession of floats passed along the street.
examples.zh: 一列花車隊伍沿街行進。

explains: This noun means a group of people walking together in an organized way. A wedding party may move from a church to a hall. The group follows a route.
A band and dancers may lead a parade through town. The people move in order. The word describes the group or the act of walking together.
At a ceremony, people may walk slowly behind a leader. Their movement is formal. The noun can also mean a series of things in order.

examples.en: Demonstrating high professional English proficiency is mandatory for international marketing roles.
examples.zh: 具備流暢自信的商務英語精通熟練度，是應聘跨國品牌國際行銷主管職位不可或缺的硬性門檻。

examples.en: Technical proficiency with cloud virtualization is a core requirement for our DevOps engineering candidates.
examples.zh: 具備對各類雲端架構與虛擬化容器技術的高度專業熟練度，是我們招募 DevOps 工程師的必備條件。

examples.en: Language proficiency improves exponentially when learners practice active speaking in immersive daily settings.
examples.zh: 當學習者勇於將語言主動應用於沉浸式的日常對話環境中時，外語熟練精通程度將以幾何級數躍升。

explains: This noun means a high level of skill in a subject or activity. A musician may play a difficult piece with confidence. Practice builds ability.
A worker may use a computer program quickly and correctly. They understand its tools well. The word describes skill gained through learning and experience.
A language learner can improve through reading and conversation. Their skill grows over time. The term often appears in school or work settings.

examples.en: The prohibition of smoking applies inside the building.
examples.zh: 大樓內禁止吸菸。

examples.en: The old prohibition lasted for many years.
examples.zh: 過去的禁令持續了許多年。

examples.en: They discussed prohibition laws in history class.
examples.zh: 他們在歷史課討論禁酒法。

explains: This noun means an official rule or law that forbids an action. A town may ban parking on a narrow street. People must follow the rule.
A government may prohibit a product or activity. The restriction applies to everyone covered by the law. The word names the act or state of banning.
The term can also refer to the time when a ban is in place. A country may prohibit a certain drink for years. Context shows the law or period.

examples.en: The engine propelled the boat across the water.
examples.zh: 引擎推動船隻越過水面。

examples.en: Her curiosity propelled her to explore the cave.
examples.zh: 好奇心促使她探索洞穴。

examples.en: A strong gust propelled the kite upward.
examples.zh: 一陣強風把風箏吹向高處。

explains: This verb means to push or drive something forward. A strong wind may move a sailboat. The force sends it ahead.
An idea or event can also push someone to act. A kind remark may give a person courage. The word describes causing movement or action.
A rocket uses engines to move through space. The verb can describe physical motion or influence that leads to progress. The force helps the object continue its path.

examples.en: Her lyrical prose describes everyday life in Tainan with warmth.
examples.zh: 她細膩抒情的散文筆觸溫暖描摹出在台南的市井生活日常。

examples.en: The author's concise, direct prose stands in stark contrast to ornate Victorian novels.
examples.zh: 該作家精準俐落且直截了當的散文文風，與繁複華麗的維多利亞小說形成鮮明對比。

examples.en: Translation requires capturing not only word meaning but also the melodic flow of prose.
examples.zh: 外語文學翻譯不僅要精準傳達字面文意，更需細膩還原散文原本如流水般的音律美感。

explains: This noun means writing that uses ordinary sentences rather than poetry. A story or essay is often written this way. It follows normal speech patterns.
A book may mix this kind of writing with poems. The paragraphs tell events or explain ideas. The word names the style, not a specific subject.
The term can also mean plain or direct language. A person may speak in simple, ordinary words. Context indicates the writing form or style.

examples.en: The state will prosecute the person accused of theft.
examples.zh: 州政府將起訴這名被控竊盜的人。

examples.en: The lawyer prosecuted the case in court.
examples.zh: 律師在法庭上提起訴訟。

examples.en: The firm decided to prosecute the fraud case.
examples.zh: 公司決定對詐欺案提起訴訟。

explains: This verb means to bring a criminal case against someone in court. A public lawyer may present evidence. The judge or jury considers the case.
The word can also mean to continue an activity or plan. A team may carry on with a project. Context shows whether the use is legal or general.
A person accused of a crime may face an official legal process. The verb describes the government's action in court. It is a formal legal term.

examples.en: Prospective students toured the campus.
examples.zh: 準學生參觀了校園。

examples.en: The company met with prospective buyers.
examples.zh: 公司會見了潛在買家。

examples.en: She spoke with her prospective roommate.
examples.zh: 她和未來的室友交談。

explains: This adjective describes something expected or likely to happen in the future. A student applying to a school may be a possible future member. The event has not happened yet.
A company may contact people who could become customers. They are possible future buyers. The word refers to what may come.
It can also mean looking toward a future result. A plan may offer good chances of success. Context tells whether it describes a person or possibility.

examples.en: The engineers tested a prototype of the new bridge sensor.
examples.zh: 工程師測試了新型橋梁感測器的原型。

examples.en: She built a prototype from cardboard.
examples.zh: 她用紙板製作了一個原型。

examples.en: The company showed its first prototype at the fair.
examples.zh: 公司在展覽會上展示了第一個原型。

explains: This noun means an early model made to test a new design. Engineers may build one before making many copies. It shows how the idea works.
A company may test the model with a small group. Problems can be found before full production. The item is an early version.
The term can apply to a machine, product, or plan. The first version may change many times. It helps people test an idea in real form.

examples.en: The proverb reminds us that practice takes time.
examples.zh: 這句諺語提醒我們練習需要時間。

examples.en: Grandpa shared a proverb about patience.
examples.zh: 爺爺分享了一句關於耐心的諺語。

examples.en: The story ends with a proverb about kindness.
examples.zh: 故事以一句關於善良的諺語作結。

explains: This noun means a short traditional saying that offers advice or expresses a general truth. People may repeat it in daily conversation. It is often easy to remember.
A family may share a saying about patience or hard work. The phrase sums up a lesson. The word names this kind of expression.
The saying may come from long experience and be passed across generations. It can guide behavior or comment on life. The term refers to the expression.

examples.en: The provincial museum displays local pottery.
examples.zh: 省立博物館展出當地陶器。

examples.en: He writes for a provincial newspaper.
examples.zh: 他為一份地方報紙撰稿。

examples.en: The provincial office serves several small towns.
examples.zh: 地方辦公室為幾個小鎮提供服務。

explains: This adjective means related to a region outside a country's capital or main city. A local newspaper may cover events in small towns. The word describes the area.
It can also describe a person or view considered limited to one region. The meaning may sound critical. Context determines whether it is neutral or dismissive.
A school system may have local branches in different provinces. The term describes their connection to a region. It can refer to places, customs, or attitudes.

examples.en: They built a provisional bridge while repairs continued.
examples.zh: 維修期間，他們搭建了一座臨時橋梁。

examples.en: The committee made a provisional decision.
examples.zh: 委員會做出了暫時決定。

examples.en: She held a provisional position for six months.
examples.zh: 她暫時擔任這個職位六個月。

explains: This adjective means temporary or intended to last until something permanent is ready. A school may use a short-term plan during repairs. The arrangement will later change.
A worker may hold a position for a limited time. Another person may take over later. The word describes the temporary role or plan.
A government may set up a short-term office after an emergency. It handles immediate needs. The term signals that the arrangement is not final.

examples.en: She is studying psychiatry at medical school.
examples.zh: 她正在醫學院研讀精神醫學。

examples.en: Psychiatry includes the study of mood and behavior.
examples.zh: 精神醫學包含對情緒與行為的研究。

examples.en: He chose psychiatry as his medical specialty.
examples.zh: 他選擇精神醫學作為自己的醫療專科。

explains: This noun names the branch of medicine that studies mental health and behavior. A doctor in this field may help people with serious emotional difficulties. The work includes evaluation and care.
The field also studies how the brain and mind affect feelings. Specialists may work in hospitals or clinics. The word names the profession and area of study.
A person who works in this field has special medical training. The term is used in health care and research. It focuses on the mind and its health.

examples.en: The psychic in the story predicted a storm.
examples.zh: 故事中的通靈者預測了一場暴風雨。

examples.en: A psychic character appeared in the mystery novel.
examples.zh: 推理小說中出現了一個有心靈感應能力的角色。

examples.en: She visited a psychic for a fictional interview.
examples.zh: 她為了一次虛構的採訪拜訪了一位靈媒。

explains: This adjective can describe claimed mental powers beyond ordinary senses, such as knowing something without being told. A story may feature a person who senses distant events. The power is usually presented as unusual.
As a noun, it can refer to a person believed to have such abilities. The belief is common in fiction and supernatural stories. Evidence for these powers is disputed.

The word can also relate to the mind or mental processes in some fields. Context shows whether it means supernatural ability or something connected with the mind. The surrounding sentence clarifies the sense.

examples.en: Psychotherapy helped the character understand her fears.
examples.zh: 心理治療幫助故事中的角色了解自己的恐懼。

examples.en: The novel describes a person's experience with psychotherapy.
examples.zh: 這本小說描述一個人接受心理治療的經歷。

examples.en: Psychotherapy can involve regular conversations with a trained professional.
examples.zh: 心理治療可能包含與受過訓練的專業人士定期談話。

explains: This noun means treatment that uses talking to help a person understand feelings and behavior. A trained professional listens and guides the conversation. It may take place over many visits.
The work can help someone explore worries or habits. Different methods focus on different needs. The word names a kind of mental health care.
A person may meet with a therapist in a private office or clinic. The talks help them consider their experiences. It is a professional form of support.

examples.en: The school will publicize the art fair next week.
examples.zh: 學校下週會宣傳藝術展。

examples.en: They publicized the concert on local radio.
examples.zh: 他們在地方電台宣傳了這場音樂會。

examples.en: The library publicizes free events on its website.
examples.zh: 圖書館在網站上公布免費活動。

explains: This verb means to make information or an event known to the public. A museum may share news about an exhibit. People learn that it is happening.
A company may use signs or announcements to tell people about a new service. The message reaches more people. The verb describes sharing news widely.
A town can make a festival known through posters and radio. The action helps people hear about it. It does not necessarily mean paid advertising.

examples.en: Crispy craquelin cream puffs burst with chilled fresh vanilla bean custard.
examples.zh: 表面覆蓋一層香脆菠蘿皮的脆皮泡芙一口咬下，冰涼爆漿的天然香草籽卡士達內餡四溢。

examples.en: Watch through the oven glass as the balls of choux pastry dramatically puff up with hot steam.
examples.zh: 隔著烤箱玻璃觀察，原本扁平的泡芙麵糊在強烈水蒸氣推擠下不可思議地快速鼓起膨脹。

examples.en: He let out a weary puff of air after carrying the heavy bags of bread flour up three flights of stairs.
examples.zh: 徒手將幾大袋重磅麵包麵粉一口氣扛上三樓之後，他精疲力竭地長長吁了一口大氣。

explains: As a noun, this means a small amount of smoke, air, or dust released at once. A candle may send a thin cloud into the air. The amount is light.
As a verb, it means to swell or become rounded. Dough can rise in a warm place. A bird may also spread out its feathers.
A person may breathe out quickly when upset. The word can describe a brief burst of air, a soft cloud, or a rounded shape. The small burst does not last long.

examples.en: Please be punctual and arrive five minutes prior to the scheduled meeting.
examples.zh: 請務必準時赴約，並於表定會議開始前五分鐘從容抵達會議室。

examples.en: German train systems are well known for being remarkably punctual.
examples.zh: 德國鐵路系統以其高度準時聞名於世。

examples.en: Being punctual shows deep respect for other people's valuable time.
examples.zh: 準時展現了對他人寶貴時間的高度尊重。

explains: This adjective describes someone who arrives or acts at the expected time. A student who reaches class before the bell is on time. The person is not late.
A meeting may begin as scheduled because everyone arrives when expected. The word praises respect for time. It can describe people or events.
The adjective can also describe a regular event that happens at the planned time. A bus may arrive according to its schedule. It suggests reliability.

examples.en: The filter purifies water for the village.
examples.zh: 濾水器為村莊淨化飲用水。

examples.en: They purified the silver before making the necklace.
examples.zh: 他們先提純銀，再製作項鍊。

examples.en: The story says the hero purified his intentions.
examples.zh: 故事說主角淨化了自己的意念。

explains: This verb means to remove dirt or unwanted material from something. A filter can clean water. The liquid becomes safer or clearer.
A person may clean a metal object or remove harmful parts from a mixture. The action leaves the useful material behind. The word means to make clean.
It can also mean to make a person's actions or ideas free from blame. The sense is figurative. Context shows whether the change is physical or moral.

examples.en: Ultra-pure water (UPW) used to rinse delicate wafers undergoes rigorous multi-stage ion exchange for absolute purity.
examples.zh: 用於清洗微細晶圓的「超純水」（UPW），需經過多重逆滲透與離子交換樹脂過濾以達到極致無雜質純度。

examples.en: The diamond appraiser verified the exceptional brilliance and flawless clarity purity of the royal gemstone.
examples.zh: 權威珠寶鑑定專家在顯微鏡下再三確認，該顆皇室典藏藍寶石散發出令人屏息的澄澈火彩與頂級淨度純淨度。

examples.en: Children’s open laughter filled the room with genuine, unpretentious innocence and moral purity.
examples.zh: 育幼院孩子們毫無掩飾的歡聲笑語迴盪在整個客廳，帶給在場所有大朋友一份最真摯純粹、未染塵俗的童真與純潔。

examples.en: Automotive fuel cells require ultra-high hydrogen purity to prevent platinum catalyst poisoning.
examples.zh: 車用燃料電池需要高達 99.999% 的「超高氫氣純度」（Purity），以徹底防範昂貴白金催化劑中毒。

examples.en: Goldsmiths assay gold bullion jewelry to verify its twenty-four-karat physical metal purity.
examples.zh: 銀樓金工金匠嚴格檢驗鑑定純金條塊成色，確保其符合千足金二十四 K 純金的極限金屬純度。

examples.en: Mountain spring water celebrated for its crystal purity flows naturally from pristine limestone aquifers.
examples.zh: 享譽盛名的高山甘冽天然山泉水，源源不絕湧自未受任何污染的天然石灰岩深層清冽含水層。

entries.definition: 晶圓製造超純水極致純度；純潔；達 99.999% 五個九之車規燃料電池級超純氫氣；純度
explains: This noun means the state of being clean or free from unwanted material. A clear glass of water may show physical cleanliness. The idea can also be moral.
A person may value honesty and freedom from wrongdoing. The word can describe that quality. It appears in religious and ethical discussions.
In science, a substance's cleanliness can be measured. The fewer unwanted materials it has, the higher this quality. Context determines the type.

examples.en: A quake shook the town before dawn.
examples.zh: 黎明前，一場地震震動了城鎮。

examples.en: The ground quaked beneath the old bridge.
examples.zh: 老橋下的地面震動起來。

examples.en: She felt a quake of fear when the lights went out.
examples.zh: 燈熄掉時，她感到一陣恐懼。

explains: As a noun, this is a sudden shaking of the ground. Buildings and roads may move. The shaking can last only a short time.
As a verb, it means to shake strongly. A person may shake with fear or cold. A machine can also tremble during use.
The word can also describe a strong shaking feeling or event. It is commonly used for earthquakes. Context tells whether it is literal or figurative.

examples.en: A bachelor's degree in engineering is a minimum qualification for this role.
examples.zh: 工程學系學士學位是該職位的基本必備資格條件。

examples.en: She acquired advanced cloud certification qualifications while working full-time.
examples.zh: 她在全職工作的忙碌之餘，利用公餘時間成功考取了多項高階雲端專業證照資格。

examples.en: Outstanding interpersonal and leadership skills are vital qualifications for management.
examples.zh: 出色卓越的人際溝通手腕與團隊領導統御魅力，是晉升管理階層不可或缺的資格。

explains: This noun can mean a skill, degree, or condition needed for a job or activity. A teacher may need special training. The training meets a requirement.
It can also mean an ability someone has gained through study or experience. A person may know several languages. The word describes that skill.
A document may prove that someone completed a course. The certificate shows they meet a standard. Context shows whether it means skill or a required condition.

examples.en: The radiant moon lit the quiet lake.
examples.zh: 明亮的月亮照亮了寧靜的湖面。

examples.en: She had a radiant smile after the good news.
examples.zh: 聽到好消息後，她露出燦爛的笑容。

examples.en: Radiant colors filled the artist's canvas.
examples.zh: 畫家的畫布上充滿了鮮明亮麗的色彩。

explains: This adjective describes a person or thing that shines brightly or seems full of light. The morning sun may make the snow sparkle. The scene looks bright.
It can also describe someone who looks happy and healthy. A smiling face may seem to glow. The word suggests warmth and brightness.
A painting may show bright colors that stand out. The adjective describes a shining quality, either real or figurative. The light may come from a natural or painted source.

examples.en: The heater radiated warmth across the room.
examples.zh: 暖爐把熱氣散布到整個房間。

examples.en: Her face radiated joy at the reunion.
examples.zh: 重逢時，她臉上洋溢著喜悅。

examples.en: The sun radiates light and heat.
examples.zh: 太陽放射光和熱。

explains: This verb means to send out light, heat, or energy from a central point. A lamp gives light across a room. The energy spreads outward.
A person may give off a feeling of confidence or kindness. Others notice the quality. The word describes how a feeling seems to spread from someone.
Heat can travel from a warm stove into nearby air. The verb applies to energy or emotion. It suggests spreading from a source.

examples.en: The scientist tested the radioactive sample.
examples.zh: 科學家檢測了放射性樣本。

examples.en: Radioactive material must be stored carefully.
examples.zh: 放射性物質必須妥善存放。

examples.en: The lab sign warned that the room contained radioactive material.
examples.zh: 實驗室標誌提醒大家房間內有放射性物質。

explains: This adjective describes material that gives off a kind of energy called radiation. Some elements have this property. Scientists study how it changes over time.
The word can describe substances or places that emit this energy. Special instruments can detect it. The adjective appears in science and safety discussions.
A warning sign may mark material that gives off harmful energy. The term describes the source, not how much can be seen. It is a scientific label.

examples.en: She sliced a radish into the salad.
examples.zh: 她把蘿蔔切片放進沙拉裡。

examples.en: The garden grew crisp red radishes.
examples.zh: 菜園裡長出爽脆的紅蘿蔔。

examples.en: He ate a radish with his lunch.
examples.zh: 他午餐時吃了一根蘿蔔。

explains: This noun names a small root vegetable with a red or white round part and green leaves. It has a crisp texture and sharp taste. People add it to salads.
The plant grows quickly in cool weather. The edible root may be sliced or eaten whole. The leaves can also be cooked.
A bunch of these vegetables may be sold at a market. The word names the plant or its root. It can be eaten raw or cooked.

examples.en: The circle has a radius of five centimeters.
examples.zh: 這個圓的半徑是五公分。

examples.en: She measured the radius of the round table.
examples.zh: 她量了圓桌的半徑。

examples.en: The radius of the planet is shown on the chart.
examples.zh: 圖表上標示了這顆行星的半徑。

explains: This noun means a straight line from the center of a circle to its edge. The line is half as long as the diameter. Geometry uses it to measure circles.
The word can also describe a line from the center of a sphere to its surface. It helps define the size of a ball or planet. The measurement begins at the center.
In anatomy, it names one of the two bones in the forearm. The bone extends from the wrist toward the elbow. Context shows the mathematical or body meaning.

examples.en: He gave a gentle rap on the door.
examples.zh: 他輕輕敲了敲門。

examples.en: The band played a rap song at the festival.
examples.zh: 樂團在音樂節演奏了一首饒舌歌曲。

examples.en: She rapped on the window to get our attention.
examples.zh: 她敲了敲窗戶，引起我們的注意。

explains: As a noun, this means a quick knock or sharp hit. A person may tap on a door. The sound can be repeated to a beat.
It can also name a style of music with rhythmic spoken words. Performers speak in time with a strong beat. The music often uses rhyme.
As a verb, it means to knock lightly or speak rhythmically. Context tells whether it is a sound, action, or musical style. Rhythm helps listeners follow the words.

examples.en: A red rash appeared on his arm.
examples.zh: 他的手臂上出現一片紅疹。

examples.en: She made a rash decision to leave early.
examples.zh: 她草率地決定提早離開。

examples.en: The child showed the doctor a rash on her neck.
examples.zh: 孩子把脖子上的紅疹給醫生看。

explains: As a noun, this is a group of red spots on the skin that appears suddenly. A person may notice it after an illness or reaction. A doctor can identify its cause.
As an adjective, it can mean done without careful thought. Someone may make a quick choice. The decision can be unwise.
The adjective can also describe a person who acts quickly and carelessly. The noun means a skin condition. Context helps distinguish these meanings.

examples.en: The council ratified the new agreement.
examples.zh: 議會正式批准了新協議。

examples.en: Several countries ratified the treaty.
examples.zh: 幾個國家批准了這項條約。

examples.en: The board will ratify the decision next week.
examples.zh: 董事會下週將正式核准這項決定。

explains: This verb means to officially approve or confirm an agreement. A group may vote to accept a plan. The vote makes it formal.
A government may approve a treaty after leaders sign it. The agreement then becomes official. The verb is used in law and politics.
A school board can formally accept a new rule. The decision follows a set process. This action confirms that the group agrees.

examples.en: The realization came to her during the walk.
examples.zh: 她在散步時突然明白了這件事。

examples.en: His realization that the door was open came too late.
examples.zh: 他太晚才發現門是開著的。

examples.en: The team celebrated the realization of its goal.
examples.zh: 團隊慶祝目標實現。

explains: This noun means the moment when someone understands or recognizes something clearly. A child may suddenly see how a puzzle works. The new understanding feels important.
It can also mean the act of making a plan or goal happen. A team may complete a project they imagined. The idea becomes real.
A person may have a sudden insight about their own behavior. They see a truth they had not noticed before. Context shows insight or achievement.

examples.en: The farmers reaped the wheat in late summer.
examples.zh: 農夫在夏末收割小麥。

examples.en: She reaped the rewards of years of practice.
examples.zh: 她獲得多年練習帶來的成果。

examples.en: We reaped a large harvest after the rain.
examples.zh: 雨後我們收穫了大量作物。

explains: This verb means to gather a crop from the land. Farmers cut grain when it is ready. The work follows planting and growing.
It can also mean to gain a result from effort. A student may receive good marks after studying. The benefit comes from earlier work.
The word may describe collecting or obtaining something useful. People can gather information from books. Context shows farming or gaining a result.

examples.en: The reckless driver ignored the stop sign.
examples.zh: 魯莽的駕駛無視停車標誌。

examples.en: It was reckless to climb the icy roof.
examples.zh: 爬上結冰的屋頂是魯莽的行為。

examples.en: A reckless choice put the whole team at risk.
examples.zh: 魯莽的選擇讓整個團隊陷入危險。

explains: This adjective describes someone who acts without thinking enough about danger or results. A driver may race through a crowded street. The behavior can hurt people.
A person may spend all their money without considering future needs. The choice is careless. The word suggests too little caution.
An action may be described this way when it creates avoidable risk. People may feel regret afterward. It means acting with poor judgment.

examples.en: I reckon the walk will take about an hour.
examples.zh: 我估計這段路要走大約一小時。

examples.en: They reckoned the cost before starting the repair.
examples.zh: 他們在開始修理前估算了費用。

examples.en: She reckoned that the team would arrive by noon.
examples.zh: 她估計團隊會在中午前抵達。

explains: This verb can mean to believe or suppose something is true. A person may estimate that a walk takes twenty minutes. The idea may be based on a guess.
It can also mean to count or calculate. A shopkeeper may add up the cost of several items. The word describes a mental estimate.
A person may consider a situation before deciding what to do. The verb can mean think, estimate, or calculate. Context shows the intended use.

examples.en: The sisters reconciled after their argument.
examples.zh: 姊妹倆爭吵後和好了。

examples.en: He reconciled the account with the receipt.
examples.zh: 他核對帳目和收據，使兩者一致。

examples.en: She tried to reconcile with her old friend.
examples.zh: 她試著與老朋友和解。

explains: This verb means to restore a friendly relationship after disagreement. Two friends may talk and forgive each other. They become close again.
It can also mean to make two ideas or facts seem consistent. A person may compare a bank record with a receipt. The figures should agree.
A person can make peace with a past event. They may accept what happened. Context shows whether the word means restoring a relationship or bringing things into agreement.

examples.en: The town built a recreational center for families.
examples.zh: 鎮上為家庭興建了一座休閒中心。

examples.en: They chose a recreational activity for the weekend.
examples.zh: 他們選了一項週末休閒活動。

examples.en: The park offers recreational paths for cycling.
examples.zh: 公園提供休閒自行車步道。

explains: This adjective describes something done for fun, exercise, or rest rather than as a job. A community may have a sports league. People join during free time.
A park may offer activities such as boating or hiking. Visitors take part for enjoyment. The word relates to leisure.
The term can describe facilities, games, or activities used outside work and school. People choose them for pleasure. It means connected with recreation.

examples.en: Dual fiber optic lines provide vital network redundancy against undersea cable cuts.
examples.zh: 雙迴路光纖網絡提供了關鍵的備援機制，能有效防範海底電纜意外中斷危機。

examples.en: Modern passenger aircraft are designed with triple hydraulic control redundancy to guarantee flight safety.
examples.zh: 現代民航大型噴射客機在方向舵控制系統上全面配備了三套相互獨立的液壓控制備援系統，以確保極限飛行安全萬無一失。

examples.en: The merger between the two competing software firms unfortunately led to widespread job redundancies.
examples.zh: 兩家同業競爭的軟體巨頭在宣布強強合併之後，不可避免地在總部行政與重複的業務職能部門中引發了大規模的職位裁撤精簡。

examples.en: Triple hardware redundancy guarantees that critical guidance computers keep operating if one chip fails.
examples.zh: 三重硬體備援冗餘設計，確保導航控制電腦即便在單一晶片損壞時依然能無縫接管運作。

examples.en: The data center installed backup diesel generators to provide electrical power redundancy during outages.
examples.zh: 雲端資料中心安裝了大型備用柴油發電機組，在台電跳電停電期間提供無縫的電力備援。

examples.en: Streamlining the corporate workflow eliminated administrative redundancy and cut operating costs.
examples.zh: 重新梳理與精簡企業日常工作流程，成功消除了行政層面的冗贅重複並降低了營運支出。

entries.definition: 備援機制；多重備份；冗餘設計；雙重備援多重容錯冗餘設計
explains: This noun means an unnecessary extra part or repeated item. A company may remove duplicate steps from a process. The work becomes more efficient.
It can also mean the loss of a job because a role is no longer needed. A worker may be let go after a company changes. The term appears in employment contexts.
The word may describe repeated information in speech or writing. A sentence may say the same thing twice. Context shows extra repetition or job loss.

examples.en: Sinking retired steel vessels creates sprawling artificial reefs that shelter millions of juvenile fish.
examples.zh: 將退役報廢的鋼鐵船隻投放沉入海底打造成人工魚礁，能成為百萬幼魚的避風港。

examples.en: Scuba divers travel from around the world to marvel at the vibrant coral reefs off Green Island and Orchid Island.
examples.zh: 來自世界各地的水肺潛水客專程前往綠島與蘭嶼，驚嘆於五彩繽紛的珊瑚礁生態。

examples.en: Rising ocean temperatures have triggered unprecedented coral reef bleaching events across tropical seas.
examples.zh: 海洋水溫持續攀升，引發了熱帶海洋中前所未有的珊瑚礁大規模白化現象。

examples.en: The vibrant living reef exhibit showcases symbiotic clownfish darting between swaying sea anemone tentacles.
examples.zh: 色彩斑斕的「活體珊瑚礁展示缸」（Living Reef），呈現小丑魚穿梭在海葵觸手間的生動共生畫面。

examples.en: The Great Barrier Reef is the largest living structure on Earth, visible from orbiting satellites.
examples.zh: 澳洲大堡礁是地球上規模最龐大的活體生命結構體，其宏偉輪廓甚至能從外太空衛星軌道上清晰看見。

examples.en: Local diving communities coordinate voluntary cleanup campaigns to remove ghost nets snagged on the reef.
examples.zh: 在地潛水愛好者社群自發組織淨海保育行動，合力拆除纏繞在天然礁岩上的廢棄幽靈沉船漁網。

entries.definition: 人工魚礁聚魚設施；暗礁；萬紫千紅色彩斑斕之熱帶活體珊瑚礁水族缸
explains: This noun names a line or area of rock or coral in the sea. It may rise close to the surface. Fish and other sea life live around it.
The structure can protect a shoreline by slowing waves. Boats must avoid shallow parts. The term refers to a natural barrier in the ocean.
Coral animals build some formations over many years. Bright fish may swim among them. The word can describe the formation or the community around it.

examples.en: The referee blew his whistle to signal the end of the match.
examples.zh: 裁判鳴笛吹響哨音示意比賽結束。

examples.en: Both team captains respectfully shook hands with the match referee.
examples.zh: 兩隊隊長恭敬地與執法裁判握手致意。

examples.en: Academic papers are evaluated by independent referees before peer-reviewed publication.
examples.zh: 學術論文在同儕審查發表前會由獨立審查人進行評審。

examples.en: The basketball referee blew the whistle to signal a foul.
examples.zh: 籃球執法裁判果斷鳴響哨音示意場上球員發生防守犯規。

examples.en: The soccer referee showed a red card to the defender for an intentional hand ball.
examples.zh: 足球場上的主裁判果斷向那名故意手球犯規的後衛出示紅牌、將其驅逐出場。

examples.en: It takes mental toughness to be an impartial referee when home crowds boo your decisions.
examples.zh: 在滿場主場球迷對著判決狂噓鼓譟的巨大壓力下，擔任一名鐵面無私的公正裁判需要極強的心理素質。

examples.en: The referee blew the whistle and awarded a penalty kick for a handball foul.
examples.zh: 主裁判吹響哨音，判定禁區內手球犯規並毫不猶豫判罰關鍵的十二碼罰球。

examples.en: Players must respect the match referee's final calls, even during contentious moments.
examples.zh: 即使在充滿爭議的關鍵判決時刻，場上球員也必須恪守規矩尊重主審裁判的裁決。

examples.en: After reviewing video replay footage, the referee overturned the earlier offside decision.
examples.zh: 在仔細檢視 VAR 慢動作重播畫面後，裁判改判推翻了先前越位犯規的原判。

entries.definition: 裁判；執法裁判；擔任裁判；裁判員；足球主審
explains: This noun names an official who makes sure players follow the rules of a game. The person watches the action. A call can stop play.
A sports official may decide whether a point counts. The decision should be fair to both teams. The term is common in baseball and other sports.
The word can also mean someone who settles a disagreement. The person listens to each side. Context indicates a sports official or a judge.

examples.en: Citizens cast ballots in the national referendum to decide important public policies.
examples.zh: 廣大公民在全國性公投中投下神聖一票以共同決定重大公共政策走向。

examples.en: The municipal government scheduled a referendum to let island residents vote on the construction of the bridge.
examples.zh: 縣市政府特別安排舉行了一場地方性公民投票，由全體離島鄉親自主公決跨海大橋的興建方案。

examples.en: The constitutional amendment will be put forward for approval in a nationwide referendum next winter.
examples.zh: 這項涉及重大憲制調整的憲法修正案，將於明年入冬之際正式交付全民公投進行最後的民意批准。

explains: This noun means a public vote on a specific question or proposal. Citizens choose whether they agree. The result can shape a law or policy.
A government may ask people to vote on a major issue. Each voter selects an answer. The vote is separate from choosing a candidate.
The term describes the process and the vote itself. The question is put directly to the public. It is used in politics and law.

examples.en: The artist refined the clay before shaping it.
examples.zh: 藝術家在塑形前先提純黏土。

examples.en: They refined the plan after hearing feedback.
examples.zh: 聽取回饋後，他們改善了計畫。

examples.en: A final refinement made the design clearer.
examples.zh: 最後的小幅修改讓設計更清楚。

explains: This verb means to make something purer or better by removing unwanted parts. A company may clean a metal material. The finished substance is of higher quality.
An author may improve a draft by making small changes. Unclear parts are removed. The work becomes clearer and more polished.
The noun form can name a small improvement or a pure substance. Context shows whether it concerns cleaning material or making a work better. Both uses involve change or improvement.

examples.en: High-albedo reflective white coatings bounce eighty percent of solar infrared rays back into space.
examples.zh: 在鐵皮屋頂噴塗高反射率隔熱白色冷屋頂塗料（Reflective Coating），能將八成太陽紅外線熱輻射反射回天空。

examples.en: Night joggers wear reflective armbands and neon vests so oncoming drivers can spot them from afar.
examples.zh: 喜愛夜跑的市民在夜間跑步時配戴高係數反光臂帶並穿上螢光背心，確保對向行駛的車輛司機能遠距離看見。

examples.en: He spent a quiet evening in a reflective mood, journaling about his personal growth over the past year.
examples.zh: 在寧靜的週末夜晚，他沉浸在深沉自省反思的心境中，執筆於手帳上記錄下自己過去一年來的心智成長與體悟。

entries.definition: 白色高反射隔熱冷屋頂塗料的
explains: This adjective describes a surface or material that sends light or heat back. A shiny mirror has this quality. It can also describe a person who thinks carefully about experiences.
A student may look back on a mistake and consider what to learn. The person is thinking deeply. The word describes thoughtful behavior.
The term can describe a kind of writing that considers ideas and feelings. The writer examines an experience. Context shows the physical or thoughtful meaning.

examples.en: A 120Hz dynamic refresh rate ensures smooth movement during rapid head turning.
examples.zh: 搭載 120Hz 動態「螢幕更新率」（Refresh Rate），確保在快速轉頭時畫面依然極致流暢無殘影。

examples.en: If the payment gateway stalls, please refresh your web browser tab before re-entering card details.
examples.zh: 若付款金流頁面停滯，請在重新輸入卡號前先重新整理瀏覽器分頁。

examples.en: A crisp walk in the morning autumn air helped refresh her mind after hours of exam preparation.
examples.zh: 在清爽的秋日晨風中散步片刻，讓苦讀備考數小時的她精神為之一振。

entries.definition: 120Hz 超高螢幕更新率 (消除畫面殘影)；刷新
explains: This verb means to make someone feel lively or rested again. A cool drink on a hot day may help. The person feels renewed.
It can also mean to clean or add moisture to something. A breeze may cool a warm room. The noun form can name a short rest or drink.
A person may take a short break after working. Food or water can help restore energy. The term describes renewal or a pause.

examples.en: The hotel provided refreshments after the tour.
examples.zh: 導覽結束後，飯店提供了茶點。

examples.en: We enjoyed light refreshments in the garden.
examples.zh: 我們在花園裡享用了簡單茶點。

examples.en: The club served refreshments during the break.
examples.zh: 俱樂部在休息時間供應茶點。

explains: This plural noun means small amounts of food or drink served to guests. A meeting may offer juice and crackers. The items are usually light.
It can also mean a short break during a meeting or event. People may stretch and talk before returning. The pause gives everyone time to rest.
A school may sell drinks and snacks after a concert. The word can refer to the food and the pause when it is served. The event may offer a chance to rest.

examples.en: The new evidence refuted the old theory.
examples.zh: 新證據駁斥了舊理論。

examples.en: She refuted the claim with a dated receipt.
examples.zh: 她用有日期的收據駁斥了這項說法。

examples.en: The report refutes several rumors about the school.
examples.zh: 報告駁斥了幾項關於學校的謠言。

explains: This verb means to prove that a statement or belief is wrong. A scientist may show that an old idea does not fit the evidence. The facts challenge it.
A person may answer an accusation with records or witnesses. The response shows the claim is false. The word often appears in formal arguments.
A debate team may present reasons against another side's point. Clear evidence supports the response. The verb means to disprove or deny with proof.

examples.en: The center helps rehabilitate injured athletes.
examples.zh: 中心協助受傷的運動員復健。

examples.en: Workers rehabilitated the old library after the fire.
examples.zh: 火災後，工人修復了舊圖書館。

examples.en: The program aims to rehabilitate people after prison.
examples.zh: 這個計畫旨在協助服刑者重返社會。

explains: This verb means to help someone return to health, strength, or normal life after injury or difficulty. A physical program may build movement skills again. Progress can take time.
A place or building can be restored after damage. Workers repair it so people can use it again. The verb describes bringing back usefulness.
It can also mean helping someone return to society after a problem. Support may help them learn skills or find work. Context can concern a person or place.

examples.en: Dancers rehearsed their synchronized routine for four hours daily.
examples.zh: 舞者們每天進行長達四小時的群舞動作同步排練。

examples.en: He rehearsed his keynote presentation multiple times in front of the mirror.
examples.zh: 他在臥室鏡子前反覆演練排練自己即將上台發表的主題簡報演說。

examples.en: The choir gathered on Saturday morning to rehearse carols for the holiday service.
examples.zh: 合唱團成員在週六清晨齊聚一堂，認真排練即將在聖誕崇拜獻唱的讚美詩篇。

explains: This verb means to practice a play, song, or speech before performing it. Actors say their lines and move on stage. Repeated practice helps the show run smoothly.
A musician may play a difficult section several times. The person prepares for a concert. The word describes practice before the real event.
A person can go over a speech before giving it. They check the words and timing. The activity helps them feel ready.

examples.en: The queen's reign lasted for many decades.
examples.zh: 女王的統治持續了數十年。

examples.en: A new king began to reign after his father's death.
examples.zh: 父親去世後，新國王開始統治。

examples.en: The champion reigned over the league for years.
examples.zh: 這位冠軍多年稱霸聯盟。

explains: As a noun, this means the period when a king or queen rules. A ruler may lead for many years. The years form a period of rule.
As a verb, it means to rule a country or kingdom. A queen may lead the nation. The word can also describe a person or feeling being dominant.
A champion may remain the best in a sport for a long time. People may say the champion rules the field. Context shows royal leadership or dominance.

examples.en: The children rejoiced when the school trip was announced.
examples.zh: 校外教學公布時，孩子們欣喜不已。

examples.en: We rejoiced at the team's victory.
examples.zh: 我們為球隊獲勝而歡欣。

examples.en: She rejoiced to see her old friend again.
examples.zh: 她再次見到老朋友時非常高興。

explains: This verb means to feel or show great happiness. A family may celebrate after hearing good news. The emotion is strong.
People may express joy by smiling, singing, or dancing. The word describes the feeling and its outward display. It often appears in formal or literary writing.
A group can be glad about someone's success. Their happiness may be shared. The verb means to be very happy.

examples.en: Our team won the relay at the sports day.
examples.zh: 我們隊贏得了運動會的接力賽。

examples.en: She relayed the message to the next group.
examples.zh: 她把訊息傳給下一組。

examples.en: The runners passed the relay baton quickly.
examples.zh: 跑者迅速傳遞接力棒。

explains: As a noun, this is a race in which teammates carry and pass a baton. Each runner covers one part of the distance. The team works together.
As a verb, it means to pass something from one person or place to another. A worker may send a message along a chain. The item moves onward.
A system may pass a signal from one device to the next. The word can name the race, the handoff, or a device that passes signals. The meaning depends on the situation.

examples.en: The relentless rain flooded the garden.
examples.zh: 連綿不斷的雨淹沒了花園。

examples.en: She showed relentless effort during practice.
examples.zh: 她在練習中展現不懈的努力。

examples.en: The team's relentless attack kept the defenders busy.
examples.zh: 球隊持續不斷的進攻讓防守球員忙個不停。

explains: This adjective describes something that does not stop or weaken, even when it is difficult. A steady rain may continue for days. The word suggests constant force.
A worker may keep trying despite many problems. The effort continues without giving up. The person shows strong determination.
An argument can continue in an intense way. People may keep discussing the issue. The adjective means unending or very persistent.

examples.en: Her reliance on the map helped the group.
examples.zh: 她依靠地圖幫助了整個團隊。

examples.en: The project showed our reliance on volunteers.
examples.zh: 這個專案顯示我們仰賴志工。

examples.en: His reliance on the old bridge worried the engineer.
examples.zh: 他依賴那座老橋，讓工程師感到擔心。

explains: This noun means the act of depending on someone or something for help. A child may trust a parent to provide care. The relationship involves support.
A team may use a map to find a route. They count on it to guide them. The word describes dependence or trust.
A person may need help from others to complete a task. The term can describe that need. It often appears with the word on.

examples.en: The seedlings are reliant on regular water.
examples.zh: 幼苗需要定期澆水才能生長。

examples.en: The town is reliant on tourism for many jobs.
examples.zh: 這座城鎮的許多工作仰賴觀光業。

examples.en: She was reliant on her neighbor for a ride.
examples.zh: 她需要鄰居載她一程。

explains: This adjective describes someone or something that depends on another for support. A young child needs adults for food and care. The child is not fully independent.
A machine may need electricity to work. It cannot operate without that source. The term describes what it depends on.
A person may rely on a friend during a difficult time. The adjective can describe that relationship. It is often followed by on.

examples.en: The museum displayed a relic from the ancient temple.
examples.zh: 博物館展示了一件古廟遺物。

examples.en: A broken cup became a family relic.
examples.zh: 一只破杯子成了家族紀念物。

examples.en: The old rule was a relic of another era.
examples.zh: 那項舊規定是另一個時代留下的遺風。

explains: This noun means an object from the past that remains after its original use is gone. An old coin may be found in the ground. It can show how people lived.
A museum may display a tool from an earlier time. The item may be broken but still important to history. The word describes a leftover object.
The term can also describe a custom or idea that continues from the past. A family may keep an old tradition. Context shows a physical item or old practice.

examples.en: She packed the remainder of the cake.
examples.zh: 她把剩下的蛋糕包了起來。

examples.en: The remainder of the class stayed to help.
examples.zh: 班上其餘的人留下來幫忙。

examples.en: The remainder after division is four.
examples.zh: 除法後的餘數是四。

explains: This noun means what is left after some has been used, removed, or counted. A meal may have a small amount of food left. The rest can be saved.
In math, it is the amount left after subtraction. A student can check the result. The word also appears in division problems.
A book may have a final part left after the main action. It can mean what is left. Context shows what is left.

examples.en: The old song is reminiscent of my childhood.
examples.zh: 這首老歌讓我想起童年。

examples.en: Her dress was reminiscent of a style from the 1950s.
examples.zh: 她的洋裝讓人想起 1950 年代的風格。

examples.en: The scent of pine was reminiscent of winter holidays.
examples.zh: 松樹的氣味讓人想起冬日假期。

explains: This adjective describes something that reminds a person of an earlier time or experience. A song may bring back a summer trip. The memory feels familiar.
A painting may look like the style of an older artist. Viewers can recognize a connection to the past. The word describes that resemblance.
A smell can make someone think of a childhood home. The feeling or detail recalls something. The adjective means suggestive of a memory.

examples.en: The renowned singer performed at the festival.
examples.zh: 這位知名歌手在音樂節演出。

examples.en: The school invited a renowned scientist to speak.
examples.zh: 學校邀請了一位知名科學家演講。

examples.en: The town is renowned for its handmade cheese.
examples.zh: 這座城鎮以手工起司聞名。

explains: This adjective describes someone or something widely known and admired for a good quality. A painter may be famous for bright landscapes. Many people know the work.
A town may be known for its old stone bridge. Visitors come because of that feature. The word describes a respected reputation.
The term is stronger than simply being known. It suggests praise and respect. Context can describe a person, place, or achievement.

examples.en: The printer can reproduce the image clearly.
examples.zh: 這台印表機能清楚複製影像。

examples.en: Some plants reproduce through tiny spores.
examples.zh: 有些植物透過微小孢子繁殖。

examples.en: The artist reproduced the old map by hand.
examples.zh: 藝術家手工複製了這張古地圖。

explains: This verb means to make a copy or create new living things of the same kind. A printer can copy a picture. A plant can grow from a cutting.
Animals and plants make young ones through natural processes. The word describes producing another generation. It can also refer to copying sounds or images.
A person may copy a document for a class. The verb can mean making a duplicate. Context shows whether it means copying or producing young.

examples.en: A reptile rested on the warm rock.
examples.zh: 一隻爬行動物在溫暖的岩石上休息。

examples.en: The zoo has a room for tropical reptiles.
examples.zh: 動物園有一間飼養熱帶爬行動物的展室。

examples.en: The snake is a reptile with smooth scales.
examples.zh: 蛇是一種有光滑鱗片的爬行動物。

explains: This noun names a cold-blooded animal with scales, such as a snake, turtle, or lizard. Many kinds lay eggs. Their skin is covered with scales.
The animal's body temperature changes with the surroundings. Some live on land, while others live in water. The word describes a broad animal group.
A zoo may have a warm house for these animals. Visitors can see them behind glass. The term includes many species.

examples.en: She resented being left out of the game.
examples.zh: 她不滿自己被排除在遊戲之外。

examples.en: He felt resentment after the unfair decision.
examples.zh: 不公平的決定讓他心生怨恨。

examples.en: The siblings resented the unequal rules.
examples.zh: 兄弟姊妹對不平等的規則感到不滿。

explains: This verb means to feel anger or bitterness about something unfair or hurtful. A person may remember being left out. The feeling can last.
The noun form names this unhappy feeling. A worker may feel upset about unequal treatment. The emotion is often quiet but strong.
The term can describe a reaction to a real or imagined wrong. People may talk about what hurt them. Context shows the feeling or its cause.

examples.en: They reside in a small town by the coast.
examples.zh: 他們住在海岸旁的小鎮。

examples.en: The queen resides in the palace during winter.
examples.zh: 女王冬天住在宮殿裡。

examples.en: The answer resides in the final chapter.
examples.zh: 答案就在最後一章裡。

explains: This verb means to live in a particular place. A family may make a home in a village. The word sounds formal.
A person can live in a house or town for a long time. A report may state where someone lives. The verb names that fact.
The term can also mean to exist in a place. A quiet feeling may remain in an empty room. Context shows a home or presence.

examples.en: The fabric is resistant to water.
examples.zh: 這種布料具有防水性。

examples.en: Some plants are resistant to cold weather.
examples.zh: 有些植物耐寒。

examples.en: The old bridge was resistant to strong winds.
examples.zh: 這座老橋能抵抗強風。

explains: This adjective describes something that can withstand damage, pressure, or disease. A strong plant may survive dry weather. The quality helps it last.
A person may refuse to be affected by a certain illness. The body does not respond easily to it. The word can describe protection or opposition.
A material can resist heat or water. It remains useful under difficult conditions. Context shows what it can withstand.

examples.en: The players returned to their respective teams.
examples.zh: 球員們回到了各自的隊伍。

examples.en: Each child sat in their respective seat.
examples.zh: 每個孩子都坐在各自的座位上。

examples.en: The two groups went to their respective rooms.
examples.zh: 兩組人各自前往自己的房間。

explains: This adjective means belonging to each of two or more people or things mentioned. Each student carried a different book. The word connects each one to its own item.
A list may name several towns and their own leaders. The term points back to each town separately. The items correspond in order.
The word is often paired with a plural noun. Each person has a different object or role. It shows that the things match one by one.

examples.en: The Taiwan Film and Audiovisual Institute completed 4K digital restoration of classic Taiwanese-language films.
examples.zh: 國家電影及視聽文化中心戮力完成了數十部珍貴台語經典黑白老電影的 4K 數位修復保存工程。

examples.en: Film restoration involves digitally cleaning dust scratches, stabilizing color fade, and remastering optical audio.
examples.zh: 老電影數位修復是一門兼具科技與匠心的浩大工程，涵蓋逐格數位除塵刮痕修補、色彩校正與老光學音軌重製。

examples.en: Preserving cinematic cultural heritage through meticulous digital restoration ensures that masterpieces inspire future generations.
examples.zh: 透過無微不至的數位修復悉心保存無價的電影文化資產，能確保這些影壇傳世瑰寶持續啟迪未來世代的創作者。

examples.en: Scientific art restoration restores brittle historic manuscripts without altering original brushstrokes.
examples.zh: 結合科學光學檢測的古籍修復揭裱工藝，在絲毫不破壞原始墨跡的前提下賦予脆弱古書全新生命。

examples.en: The historic timber temple reopened to pilgrims following a comprehensive five-year earthquake restoration.
examples.zh: 經歷震災受損嚴重的百年全木構媽祖廟，在歷經長達五年的精心原貌修復後，正式重新開放香客參拜。

examples.en: Restorations must strictly adhere to international heritage conservation charters and reversibility standards.
examples.zh: 所有古蹟修復工程皆必須嚴格恪遵國際威尼斯遺產修復憲章，恪守工法技術具可逆性的最高準則。

examples.en: Furniture restoration preserves the original patina of century-old mahogany dressers while reinforcing loose joints.
examples.zh: 專業古董老家具修復技術，在保留百年風化包漿韻味的同時重新加固鬆脫的榫卯。

examples.en: The wetland restoration project successfully brought back dozens of migratory bird species to the lagoon.
examples.zh: 沿海濕地生態棲地復育計畫取得了巨大成功，重新吸引了數十種珍稀候鳥重返潟湖覓食棲息。

examples.en: Following the devastating typhoon, technicians worked tirelessly to achieve full electrical power restoration.
examples.zh: 在強烈颱風重創電網之後，台電工程人員頂著風雨徹夜搶修，全力爭取全區全面供電復原。

examples.en: The meticulous temple restoration took five years, using traditional lime mortar and natural mineral paints.
examples.zh: 這場耗時整整五年的國寶級廟宇古蹟修繕工程，全程採用傳統糯米灰漿與天然礦物彩繪。

examples.en: Architects examined archival photographs from the 1920s to ensure historical fidelity in the facade restoration.
examples.zh: 建築師團隊反覆研讀一九二零年代的歷史老照片，以確保立面修復工程能忠於原味。

examples.en: Improper past repairs were carefully removed during this comprehensive monument restoration project.
examples.zh: 在這次全面的古蹟修復大工程中，過去不當的水泥修補物被細心剔除清除。

examples.en: Fast frequency restoration reserves provide automated voltage support when large power plants trip offline.
examples.zh: 參與電力交易平台的動態調頻備轉服務，在大型發電機組跳脫時即刻救援電網。

examples.en: Battery assets registered for automatic frequency restoration earn stable returns on the power market.
examples.zh: 投入電力交易平台參與動態調頻備轉（dReg）的民營儲能資產，每月在市場上獲得穩健的容量收益。

examples.en: Frequency restoration mechanisms kicked in within two seconds of the generator trip, averting a blackout.
examples.zh: 當大型發電機組意外跳脫瞬間，自動調頻備轉機制在短短兩秒內瞬態介入注入電力，化解了大停電危機。

examples.en: Replanting native broadleaf trees accelerates the ecological restoration of abandoned hilltop betel nut orchards.
examples.zh: 在廢棄檳榔園山坡地重新廣植台灣原生闊葉大樹，全面加速淺山丘陵的「生態棲地復育」（Restoration）。

examples.en: Mangrove restoration projects buffer vulnerable shorelines against storm surges while trapping blue carbon.
examples.zh: 紅樹林沿海復育工程不僅能抵禦強烈風暴潮的侵襲，更能長效固存大量的海洋藍碳。

examples.en: Soil restoration methods eliminate chemical residues and revitalize microscopic fungal mycorrhizae.
examples.zh: 友善土壤修復工法能有效消除土地殘留的農藥化肥，全面喚醒地底微生物與菌根真菌的蓬勃生機。

entries.definition: 老電影數位修復；修復重建；古籍書畫揭裱修復；復原；百年古董老家具細心翻新修復；百年國寶古蹟慎重修繕修復工程；台電電力交易平台 dReg 動態調頻備轉；淺山退化棲地生態復育與原生樹種造林
explains: This noun means the act of bringing a building, object, or system back to good condition. Workers may repair an old bridge. The structure becomes useful again.
It can also mean returning something to its earlier state. A museum may fix a damaged painting. The work preserves its history.
A community may rebuild after a flood. People restore homes and services. The word describes the process of making things whole or active again.

examples.en: The guard restrained the dog near the gate.
examples.zh: 守衛在大門附近控制住那隻狗。

examples.en: She restrained her anger during the meeting.
examples.zh: 她在會議中克制了怒氣。

examples.en: The police restrained the crowd at the entrance.
examples.zh: 警方在入口處控制人群。

explains: This verb means to hold someone or something back from acting freely. A parent may stop a child from running into the street. The action limits movement.
A person may control a strong feeling before speaking. Taking a breath can prevent an angry response. The verb describes keeping something in check.
The word can also mean to keep information or an impulse from being expressed. Someone may stay quiet during a meeting. Context shows physical or emotional control.

examples.en: He showed restraint when the argument became heated.
examples.zh: 爭論變得激烈時，他保持了克制。

examples.en: The law places a restraint on how fast cars may travel.
examples.zh: 法律限制了汽車可以行駛的速度。

examples.en: Her restraint helped the group stay calm.
examples.zh: 她的克制幫助大家保持冷靜。

explains: This noun means control over actions or feelings. A person may wait before speaking while upset. The pause shows self-control.
It can also mean a rule or limit that keeps someone from doing something. A safety bar holds a rider in place. The word describes a boundary.
A person may show calm behavior in a difficult moment. The quality keeps strong feelings from taking over. Context points to self-control or a limit.

examples.en: He made a retort about the muddy shoes.
examples.zh: 他對那雙沾滿泥巴的鞋子回了一句尖銳的話。

examples.en: She retorted that the room was already clean.
examples.zh: 她反駁說房間早就打掃乾淨了。

examples.en: His quick retort made the class laugh.
examples.zh: 他迅速回了一句，讓全班都笑了。

explains: As a noun, this is a quick, sharp answer, often made in an argument. A person may respond with a clever sentence. The reply can sound rude.
As a verb, it means to answer sharply. Someone may speak back after being criticized. The response is quick and pointed.
The word can describe a short comment that shows anger or wit. Context tells whether it names the reply or the act of giving one. It can sound sharp or amusing.

examples.en: The dog retrieved the ball from the pond.
examples.zh: 狗從池塘裡把球叼了回來。

examples.en: She retrieved her coat from the classroom.
examples.zh: 她從教室取回了外套。

examples.en: The search team retrieved the lost backpack.
examples.zh: 搜救隊找回了遺失的背包。

explains: This verb means to get something back after it was lost or left behind. A search team may find a missing bag. The owner receives it again.
A computer user can bring a saved file back onto the screen. The information was stored earlier. The word describes finding or getting it again.
The term can also mean to bring back an idea or memory. A smell may remind someone of a childhood home. Context shows a physical item or thought.

examples.en: The revelation changed how she understood the story.
examples.zh: 這個揭露改變了她對故事的理解。

examples.en: The letter brought a revelation about the family's past.
examples.zh: 這封信揭開了這個家庭過去的一件事。

examples.en: His sudden revelation surprised everyone.
examples.zh: 他突然說出的真相讓大家都很驚訝。

explains: This noun means the act of revealing something that was hidden or unknown. A letter may show a secret plan. People learn new information.
It can also mean a surprising new understanding. A student may suddenly see how a story ends. The idea becomes clear.
In religion, the term can refer to a message believed to come from a divine source. Context determines whether it means disclosure, insight, or a sacred message. The message may be private or public.

examples.en: The old theater enjoyed a revival after repairs.
examples.zh: 整修後，老戲院重新受到歡迎。

examples.en: There was a revival of interest in folk music.
examples.zh: 民謠音樂重新受到關注。

examples.en: The town planned a revival of its summer festival.
examples.zh: 鎮上計畫讓夏季節慶重新舉辦。

explains: This noun means a return to life, activity, or popularity after a quiet period. A town may bring an old theater back into use. People come again.
A singer's career may become popular again after years away. The renewed attention is a return. The word describes a fresh start.
The term can also name a religious ceremony or belief about coming back to life. Context shows whether it means renewed activity or a faith idea. The exact sense depends on the setting.

examples.en: The rain revived the dry garden.
examples.zh: 雨水讓乾旱的花園恢復生氣。

examples.en: The coach revived the team's confidence.
examples.zh: 教練重振了球隊的信心。

examples.en: They hope to revive the old community theater.
examples.zh: 他們希望讓舊社區劇院重新活絡起來。

explains: This verb means to bring something back to life, health, or activity. A doctor may help a patient regain strength. The person becomes active again.
A team can bring back a plan that was paused. Members may decide to continue it. The word describes restarting something.
A garden can become lively again after receiving water. Plants begin to grow. The verb can refer to restoring energy, interest, or function.

examples.en: The revolt began after years of unfair rule.
examples.zh: 多年不公平的統治後，反抗行動開始了。

examples.en: The people revolted against the cruel king.
examples.zh: 人民起來反抗殘暴的國王。

examples.en: The workers planned a revolt against the new policy.
examples.zh: 工人們計畫反抗新政策。

explains: As a noun, this is an open fight against a ruler or government. People may oppose unfair control. The conflict can be political or military.
As a verb, it means to oppose authority or refuse to obey. A group may rise against a king. The action is often forceful.
The word can also describe a strong refusal to accept a condition. A person may react against an unfair rule. Context shows organized conflict or personal resistance.

examples.en: The moon revolves around Earth.
examples.zh: 月球繞著地球運行。

examples.en: The dancers revolved slowly around the room.
examples.zh: 舞者在房間裡緩緩旋轉。

examples.en: The discussion revolved around school lunch.
examples.zh: 討論一直圍繞著學校午餐打轉。

explains: This verb means to move in a circle around a central point. A planet moves around a star. The path repeats over time.
A wheel turns around its center as a bicycle moves. The motion is circular. The word describes this kind of movement.
The term can also mean to focus conversation on one subject. A meeting may keep returning to the same question. Context shows physical turning or repeated attention.

examples.en: The lab follows rigorous safety rules.
examples.zh: 實驗室遵守嚴格的安全規則。

examples.en: She completed a rigorous training course.
examples.zh: 她完成了一項嚴格的訓練課程。

examples.en: The team used rigorous testing for the new design.
examples.zh: 團隊對新設計進行了嚴謹的測試。

explains: This adjective describes work or rules that are exact and demanding. A science test may require careful measurements. Mistakes can change the result.
A training plan may follow a firm schedule. People must pay attention to every step. The word means thorough and strict.
A proof or study may be carefully checked in every detail. The process is systematic. The adjective describes precision and discipline.

examples.en: A ripple crossed the surface of the pond.
examples.zh: 一道漣漪掠過池塘表面。

examples.en: The news caused a ripple of excitement.
examples.zh: 這消息引起一陣興奮。

examples.en: The breeze rippled the water.
examples.zh: 微風吹皺了水面。

explains: As a noun, this is a small wave that spreads across water after something touches it. A pebble makes circles in a pond. The movement moves outward.
It can also mean a small effect that spreads through a group. One kind act may encourage others. The result grows beyond the first action.
As a verb, it means to form small waves or spread gently. A breeze can disturb a pond. The word describes water movement or a growing effect.

examples.en: The rivalry between the schools lasted for decades.
examples.zh: 兩所學校之間的競爭持續了數十年。

examples.en: Their friendly rivalry made practice exciting.
examples.zh: 他們友善的競爭讓練習變得刺激。

examples.en: The rivalry for the top prize grew stronger.
examples.zh: 爭奪首獎的競爭越來越激烈。

explains: This noun means a situation where people or groups compete against each other. Two teams may want the same trophy. Each side tries to do better.
A long disagreement between families or schools can continue for years. The competition may be friendly or hostile. The word describes their relationship.
The term can also mean the feeling of wanting to win against another person. Runners may try to beat one another's times. It focuses on competition.

examples.en: The horses roamed across the open field.
examples.zh: 馬群在空曠的田野上四處走動。

examples.en: We roamed through the old market.
examples.zh: 我們在老市場裡四處逛。

examples.en: His thoughts roamed during the long meeting.
examples.zh: 漫長會議中，他的思緒飄到別處。

explains: This verb means to travel around without a fixed route or plan. A family may walk through a forest path. They explore as they go.
An animal may move freely across a wide area. It does not stay in one small place. The word describes wandering.
A person's thoughts can move from one subject to another. Their attention is not fixed. The verb can describe walking or thinking without a set path.

examples.en: The hikers carried robust backpacks.
examples.zh: 登山客背著堅固耐用的背包。

examples.en: She remained robust and active in old age.
examples.zh: 她年長時仍然健康又活躍。

examples.en: The robust table held all the heavy boxes.
examples.zh: 這張堅固的桌子承住了所有重箱子。

explains: This adjective describes something strong and healthy. A sturdy plant can survive wind and dry weather. It grows well despite hardship.
A person may have a strong body and good energy. The word describes physical health. It can also describe a strong business or system.
A piece of equipment may be built to last. It can handle rough use without breaking. The adjective means sturdy and dependable.

examples.en: The fan rotates slowly above the table.
examples.zh: 風扇在桌子上方緩慢旋轉。

examples.en: The dancers rotated partners during the lesson.
examples.zh: 舞者在課堂中輪流更換舞伴。

examples.en: Earth rotates once each day.
examples.zh: 地球每天自轉一圈。

explains: This verb means to turn around a center or change direction in a regular way. A wheel turns as a car moves. The movement repeats.
A worker may turn crops or tasks from one person to another. The order changes over time. The word can describe turning or changing positions.
The Earth turns around its axis once each day. The verb describes this circular motion. Context can also mean taking turns or changing direction.

examples.en: Earth's 24-hour axial rotation causes the natural cycle of day and night.
examples.zh: 地球二十四小時的地軸自轉運轉造就了大自然晝夜交替的循環規律。

examples.en: The smooth rotation of the giant windmill generated enough electricity to power the nearby farmhouse.
examples.zh: 巨型風車扇葉在海風吹拂下平穩順暢的旋轉轉動，所產生的綠色電能足以供應鄰近農舍全部用電。

examples.en: The basketball center demonstrated quick footwork and a sharp pivot rotation toward the basket.
examples.zh: 籃球隊主力中鋒在禁區內展現了無比輕盈靈巧的腳步變換，一個俐落的轉身自轉突破輕鬆上籃得分。

examples.en: Crop rotation between nitrogen-fixing legumes and corn prevents soil nutrient depletion.
examples.zh: 在田區實施固氮豆科作物與甜玉米的輪作休耕制度，能有效防止土壤特定單一養分耗竭。

examples.en: Hospital nurses work on a scheduled monthly night shift rotation to ensure adequate rest.
examples.zh: 醫學中心護理團隊嚴格落實排定好的每月大夜班輪班輪調機制，確保醫護人員享有充分休養。

examples.en: The continuous rotation of the turbine generates clean electrical power for nearby homes.
examples.zh: 水力發電渦輪機日夜不息的持續高速旋轉，為鄰近村落數千戶家庭輸送源源不絕的純淨綠電。

examples.en: Practicing systematic crop rotation prevents soil nutrient depletion and breaks pest reproductive cycles.
examples.zh: 實施科學的作物輪作制度，能有效打破連作障礙並切斷特定害蟲的繁殖溫床。

examples.en: The earth's axial rotation every twenty-four hours creates the regular rhythm of daytime and night.
examples.zh: 地球每二十四小時繞自身地軸自轉一圈的旋轉運動，創造出大自然日出而作、日入而息的晝夜節律。

examples.en: Medical interns undergo clinical rotation across internal medicine, pediatrics, surgery, and emergency care.
examples.zh: 醫學系實習醫學生必須依序在內科、小兒科、一般外科與急診醫學部等各大核心專科進行輪調實習。

entries.definition: 自轉；旋轉；輪值；作物輪作；輪流更替；豆科輪作打破連作障礙；輪流
explains: This noun means the act of turning around a center. A wheel makes one full turn as it rolls. The movement follows a circular path.
It can also mean taking turns in an arranged order. Players may change positions after each round. The order is shared among them.
A machine may use a turning motion to do work. The word describes the motion or a repeated change of place. This process may happen once or many times.

examples.en: Songwriters receive monthly royalties whenever their music is streamed.
examples.zh: 每當歌曲被串流播放時，詞曲創作者都能收到相應的版稅收入。

examples.en: Authors usually earn a percentage of book royalties on every copy sold.
examples.zh: 作家每賣出一本書通常可獲得一定比例的版稅抽成。

examples.en: British royalty attended the solemn memorial service at the cathedral.
examples.zh: 英國王室成員出席了大教堂舉行的莊嚴追思儀式。

examples.en: Songwriters receive quarterly music royalties each time their songs stream.
examples.zh: 詞曲創作人每當其原創歌曲在串流平台被播放時，每季皆可收取音樂版稅。

examples.en: The publishing house paid the best-selling author a 15% royalty on all paperback book sales.
examples.zh: 這家知名出版大社按合約向該名暢銷作家支付了每本實體平裝書定價一成五的版稅酬勞。

examples.en: Members of the British royalty attended the prestigious charity gala in London last night.
examples.zh: 英國皇室家族的多位主要核心成員於昨晚親臨出席了在倫敦舉行的年度盛大慈善晚宴。

entries.definition: 版稅；專利權費；王室；權利金；皇室成員
explains: This noun means kings, queens, and members of their families. They may have special titles and duties. Some countries still have royal families.
It can also mean a payment made to an author or artist when copies of their work are sold. The amount depends on the agreement. The payment is tied to sales.
The word can refer to royal status or earnings from creative work. Context shows whether it concerns a royal family or money paid for sales. The surrounding topic makes the sense clear.

examples.en: Please put the rubbish in the blue bin.
examples.zh: 請把垃圾丟進藍色垃圾桶。

examples.en: The yard was covered in rubbish after the party.
examples.zh: 派對過後，院子裡滿是垃圾。

examples.en: He called the rumor rubbish.
examples.zh: 他說那個謠言是胡說八道。

explains: This noun means waste or things that are no longer useful. A bin may hold food scraps and packaging. The material is thrown away.
In British English, the term can mean nonsense. A person may call a silly idea nonsense. The tone may be informal.
The term can also mean a broken item that has little value. A person may clear old objects from a garage. Context shows waste or an informal judgment.

examples.en: The hikers crossed rugged mountain terrain.
examples.zh: 登山客穿越崎嶇的山地。

examples.en: He grew up in a rugged coastal village.
examples.zh: 他在一座崎嶇海岸旁的村莊長大。

examples.en: The truck handled the rugged road well.
examples.zh: 這輛卡車順利行駛在崎嶇道路上。

explains: This adjective describes land that is rough, rocky, and difficult to cross. A mountain trail may have steep slopes. Travelers need sturdy shoes.
It can also describe a person who is strong and able to handle hard conditions. Life in a remote place may require toughness. The word suggests resilience.
A coat or surface may look coarse and uneven. The term describes a rough natural quality. Context can refer to land, people, or appearance.

examples.en: The ruthless ruler punished anyone who disagreed.
examples.zh: 那位冷酷的統治者懲罰所有持不同意見的人。

examples.en: The team faced a ruthless opponent.
examples.zh: 這支隊伍面對一個毫不留情的對手。

examples.en: Her ruthless decision ended the project.
examples.zh: 她無情的決定讓專案結束。

explains: This adjective describes someone who has no pity and is willing to hurt others. A story's villain may ignore other people's pain. The behavior is cruel.
A competitor may continue trying to win without showing mercy. The word suggests a hard and uncaring attitude. It is strongly negative.
A policy can be described this way if it causes suffering without concern. The adjective can describe a person, action, or rule. The harm can be physical or emotional.

examples.en: The soldiers gave a salute to the flag.
examples.zh: 士兵向國旗行禮。

examples.en: She saluted the captain as he entered.
examples.zh: 船長進來時，她向他致敬。

examples.en: The crowd offered a salute to the fallen hero.
examples.zh: 群眾向犧牲的英雄致敬。

explains: As a noun, this is a formal greeting or sign of respect. A soldier may raise a hand to a commander. The gesture follows a rule.
As a verb, it means to greet or honor someone. People may raise a hand or give a short speech. The action shows respect.
The word can also mean a signal to show respect to a flag or person. It is used in military or ceremonial settings. Context shows the action or gesture.

examples.en: The crew salvaged tools from the damaged boat.
examples.zh: 船員從受損的船上搶救工具。

examples.en: Workers salvaged old bricks from the building.
examples.zh: 工人從建築物中回收舊磚。

examples.en: She tried to salvage the friendship after the argument.
examples.zh: 爭吵後，她試著挽救這段友誼。

explains: As a verb, this means to save useful material from something damaged or unwanted. A crew may collect wood from a wrecked boat. The parts can be used again.
The noun can mean the goods or materials saved from a wreck or old building. Workers may sort them for reuse. The items can still have value.
A team may save a project after many problems. The word can describe recovering something useful or important. It can name the act or the saved goods.

examples.en: The town improved sanitation near the public market.
examples.zh: 鎮上改善了公有市場附近的衛生環境。

examples.en: Good sanitation helps protect community health.
examples.zh: 良好的衛生措施有助於保護社區健康。

examples.en: The camp needs better sanitation facilities.
examples.zh: 營地需要更完善的衛生設施。

explains: This noun means keeping places and equipment clean to protect health. A restaurant follows rules for safe food handling. Clean surfaces help stop illness.
Schools need clean toilets and washing areas. Good practices lower the spread of germs. The word concerns public cleanliness and health.
A city may collect waste and provide clean water. These services help keep residents safe. The noun describes systems and habits that support cleanliness.

examples.en: The story described a savage battle.
examples.zh: 故事描寫了一場殘酷的戰鬥。
